author: mnot
body:
`make i18n-extract` scans the whole repository root. This changes the input directory from `.` to `$(PROJECT)` in the `i18n-extract` target, so only the `httplint` package is scanned. No issue to close.

## Why

I extracted `origin/main` twice in scratch copies (once from `.`, once from `httplint`), same options, using Babel 2.18 with the one-line `list(extra_keywords)` workaround in the scratch copy of `tools/i18n/extractors.py`:

- From `.`: 747 msgids. From `httplint`: 716.
- 31 msgids come only from `test/` (for example "Note A", "Parent.", "bad", "x"; from `test_note_escaping.py`, `test_thread_safety.py`, `test_cli_output.py`, `test_hsts_set_cookie.py`, `test_delta_seconds.py`). They would be sent to translators.
- 3 more msgids ("ahead", "header", one field-name message) also come from `httplint/` but pick up extra `test/...` location lines, which make the template change whenever a test file changes.
- `tools/` contributes no msgids or locations.

## Verification

- Scanning `httplint` instead of `.`: the msgid set loses exactly those 31 test-only entries and gains none. For the remaining 716, flags and strings are unchanged, and the locations are exactly the old ones minus the `test/` references (checked per msgid with Babel's PO reader, 0 mismatches). Locations keep the `httplint/` prefix (for example `httplint/util.py:249`, not `util.py:249` or `./httplint/...`).
- Ran the real `make i18n-extract` against a scratch copy of the tree that also contains `.claude/worktrees/x/` (copies of `httplint/` and `test/`): exit 0, 165 files read, none under `.claude`, and the output is byte-identical to the `httplint` extraction above.
- `--ignore-dirs` from #342 is kept; it still protects against dot-directories inside the package.
- `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test` all exit 0.
- No `.pot`/`.po`/`.mo` files are changed here; the checked-in `messages.pot` is stale and is regenerated in separate i18n commits.

## Notes

- Other open PRs: `refactor/i18n-no-fuzzy` edits the `i18n-update` target and the header comment of the same file; this PR touches only the `i18n-extract` command line.
- On Babel 2.18 `make i18n-extract` fails on main until `fix/i18n-extractor-babel-2-18` merges; this PR does not touch `tools/i18n/extractors.py`.

Drafted by Claude (an AI agent). It was reviewed by a second AI reviewer agent (its comment is on this PR and its items are addressed), and has not yet been read by a human.

author: diegoudistrital
body:
## ¿Qué cambia?

- API_KEY obligatoria (43 a 128 caracteres base64url, al menos 10 distintos; el valor de ejemplo se rechaza al arrancar).
- Toda ruta exige Authorization: Bearer con la key salvo /health. Si falta, está mal formada o no coincide, responde un 401 genérico igual para todas las causas, antes de cualquier 404/405 y sin leer el cuerpo ni consultar la base de datos.
- La key se compara por su resumen SHA-256 con timingSafeEqual; nunca aparece en logs ni respuestas.
- helmet (versión exacta) y Cache-Control: no-store en las respuestas de las rutas protegidas.
- Ayudantes de test que envían la key; ninguna expectativa de los tests de las specs anteriores cambia.

## ¿Por qué?

La API ya no debe ser accesible sin autenticación de aplicación. Denegar por defecto hace que cualquier ruta futura nazca protegida.

## ¿Cómo probarlo?

Añade API_KEY a tu .env (node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64url'))"). En backend/: npm test, npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm run build. A mano: npm start; sin cabecera, GET /api/tasks responde 401; con Authorization: Bearer <key>, responde 200; /health responde 200 sin key.

## Cobertura

99,84 % en líneas y 99,85 % en sentencias (1327 tests).

**Avisos importantes:**
- Protegida por key pero SIN límites por IP, SIN CORS y SIN tope en la lista; no debe exponerse a ninguna red hasta cerrar el siguiente PR (límites, CORS y tope).
- No hay login: la key autentica a la aplicación, no a la persona.

## Checklist de seguridad

- [x] No se han subido secretos (`.env`, claves, credenciales)
- [x] La entrada está validada (tipos, longitudes, UUID, campos desconocidos)
- [x] El SQL está parametrizado
- [x] Los errores no exponen detalles internos al cliente
- [x] Se aplican permisos mínimos
- [ ] La API key no se expone al navegador

## Checklist de calidad

- [x] `test` con cobertura >= 95 % en verde
- [x] `lint` en verde
- [x] `typecheck` en verde
- [x] `build` en verde
- [x] Commits convencionales en español
- [x] README actualizado

author: agentgabo
body:
Build 772 crashed twice at launch on an iPad. Both crash reports stop at `EXC_BREAKPOINT` in Swift's main-actor check, on SwiftUI's `AsyncRenderer` thread, inside a sheet's `LazyView` body. That was when the new alerts offer appears, about 3 seconds after the list loads.

The alerts offer is the only sheet in the app with `presentationDetents([.medium, .large])`. To size a medium sheet, SwiftUI lays out its content off the main thread. The content closure belongs to the main actor, and the runtime check traps.

**Fix:** the offer opens at full height, like the other 25 sheets.

**Check:** CI builds it. On device: sign in, or relaunch with alerts off, wait for the offer, then tap Not now. The app must not crash.

author: neantonii
body:
Fixes a config error introduced in #104. GitHub's validation of `.github/dependabot.yml` has failed on `master` since #104 merged:

```
The property '#/updates/3/cooldown/semver-major-days' is not supported for the package ecosystem 'docker'.
The property '#/updates/3/cooldown/semver-minor-days' is not supported for the package ecosystem 'docker'.
The property '#/updates/3/cooldown/semver-patch-days' is not supported for the package ecosystem 'docker'.
```

While the file is invalid, Dependabot version updates are likely paused for every ecosystem. Security updates are a repo setting and unaffected.

## Change
The `docker` entry gets `default-days: 30` only, the single setting it supports (same as `github-actions`). 30 rather than 90 because most docker updates are new digests of the same tag carrying Debian security patches. A runtime major bump (e.g. `node:27`, `python:3.14`) fails `tests/test_deploy.py` until `ui/.nvmrc` / CI follow, so it can't land silently.

`uv` and `npm` keep their per-release-type waits; GitHub accepted those in #89.

## Verification
GitHub's dependabot.yml validation didn't run on #104's PR, only after the push to `master`. If it doesn't show on this PR either, check the `.github/dependabot.yml` check on `master` after merging.

author: rmorozov
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"rmorozov"} -->
_Requested by **Ruslan** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01K6bYgd3V5q5ifGJ57oJs1t?thread=cmsg_01K6bYgd3V5q5ifGJ57oJs1t5GLthUWtCidzXvkM8SRpgn)_

Rebased onto master c39c06a, which includes #672 (0318).

## Problem

This is phase P2 of the approved 0049 plan (`/mnt/project-files/release-2.0/0049-plan.md` §2.1, decisions D1 and D2).

In Python these are all names of one object:

- `y = l`;
- a macro's argument;
- a loop variable over `messages`;
- `messages[0]` read twice.

Jinja2C++ lent the host's data as read-only views. The first write made a private copy and stored it back only where the receiver came from, so every other name kept the old view. For example, `{% set y = l %}{% do y.append(9) %}{{ l }}` printed `[3, 1, 2]`. A bound method of host data raised "this list cannot be changed".

## Behaviour now

- **Cell link.** The adapters of the host's data carry a `CellLink` (src/borrowed_cells.h). These are `ValuesListAdapter`, `ValuesMapAdapter`, `GenericListAdapter` and `GenericMapAdapter`.
- **First write.** The first write copies the data once into a `BorrowedCell`. The write goes through `methods::MakeMutable`, also at call time for a bound method. The cell is registered by the data's identity in the render's registry. From then on, the writing adapter and every other adapter of the same data read and write the cell.
- **Epoch.** A global epoch tells the other adapters that a cell may exist. The checks cost:
  - a loop over a host list: one compare per step (`CellStep`);
  - random item reads: one relaxed load and a compare.
- **Host data is never written (D2).** The registry lives in the render's `CycleCollector` notes and is made on the first write. It detaches its adapters before the collector walks.
- **Globals.** The thread's globals outlive renders (0211), so they read their own data again in the next render.
- **Modules.** A template module keeps one registry across its calls.
- **`list()`.** `list()` of host data now copies it, as Python's `list()` does.
- **Exports.** While the render has cells, an export copies the containers it reaches into a `GenericList` or `GenericMap` of its own. This applies, for example, to a user callable's argument, which the host may keep. Without the copy, a kept container would read the host's data again after the render, and a nested write would revert (review finding). The copy is a snapshot taken at the export.
- **Tests.**
  - Closes the divergences `methods.context_alias` and `methods.operand_changed_by_call`.
  - Adds 16 `methods.alias_*` corpus rows.
  - Adds test/borrowed_cells_test.cpp: aliases narrow and wide, globals across renders, nested render, host callable, self-append, module calls, and 4 threads over shared host data.
  - Adds an allocation-failure row.

## Remaining limits (recorded in docs/tasks/0049)

- The loop rows are P3: `pop` in a loop over context data, and `loop.length` after an append.
- A JSON value read twice gives two accessors, so its aliases stay split until P5's `IJsonNode` identity (the plan's open point). The verifier found that 52 of 270 probe templates differ on JSON data, and none on `ValuesList` or `ValuesMap`.
- The write-back in `EvaluateMutableRoot` and `EvaluateIndices(forMutation)` stays for containers that are not host data. For a cell, it stores the same value back.
- A nested render over the same host data has its own cells. This is documented and pinned by a test.

## Validation

- **Debug GCC `-Werror`:** ctest 5/5 on 4588321.
- **ASan+UBSan, clang-18 RelWithDebInfo:** ctest 5/5 on 4588321.
- **`scripts/preflight.sh --perf`:** all checks pass.
- **CI on 8df3730 (before the rebase):** all 50 checks green, including MSVC and Apple Clang.
- **`bench/count.py` against master c39c06a** (tables in `/mnt/project-files/0049-p2/`):

author: ivanwng97
body:
The JSONL watcher's attach state was never reconciled against the filesystem. Three symptoms shared that one seam:
- **A root that appears mid-run was seen only at the next 60 s poll.** This happens when the user installs or first runs a CLI while pixtuoid is open. Measured: first sight after 58.15 s.
- **A deleted-and-recreated root silently lost its watch on inotify and Windows** for the rest of the run.
- **A failed mid-run `watcher.watch(..)?` killed the whole source.** That breaks AGENTS.md's JSONL-watcher log-and-continue rule.

## The fix: one owner of "the root is watched exactly when it exists"
Established practice is to watch through the parent. notify's docs say "If you want to receive an event for a deletion of folder `b` for the path `/a/b/..`, you will have to watch its parent `/a`", and that events may be incomplete ("not a 100% reliable source"). chokidar says "a missing path is still watched through its parent".

`jsonl/root_watch.rs` owns the reconcile:
- **Anchor.** A non-recursive anchor watch sits on the nearest existing proper ancestor of the root. A filesystem root never anchors, and falls back to the poll.
- **Reconcile.** Events only nudge. The reconcile re-reads the filesystem and loops until the anchor is stable, bounded at one round per ancestor. The existing 60 s poll stays the backstop and the one cadence authority.
- **Identity.** A replaced root or anchor is detected by directory identity: the id plus the birth time (`Metadata::created`). On Unix the id is `(dev, ino)` from plain metadata; no fd is held, so the anchor's own `IN_DELETE_SELF` isn't delayed. On Windows it is the file index from `winapi_util::file::information`, already in core's graph via walkdir. The birth time disambiguates an id reused on ReFS, whose 64-bit ids are "not guaranteed to be unique", or on FAT, whose ids are position-derived.
- **Watchers.** Linux and Windows host the anchor and root watches on one notify watcher, routed by path; both backends report the spelling they were given (`inotify.rs:217-219`, `windows.rs:395-398`). An ancestor's own `.jsonl`, such as `~/.claude/history.jsonl`, only nudges and never reaches `walk_jsonl`. Instances go from 6+P to 7+P, not 14+2P, against the per-user default of 128.
- **macOS anchor.** On macOS the anchor is a small rustix `EVFILT_VNODE` watcher that opens only the anchor directory, with `O_EVTONLY`. A `notify` watcher was ruled out:
  - notify 8.2.0 can't build FSEvents and kqueue together (`lib.rs:186-205`).
  - Its KqueueWatcher recursively watches each new child (`kqueue.rs:173-187`, `290-292`).
  - A $HOME FSEvents stream's TCC behaviour is undocumented: Apple's FSEvents security guide and the TCC protected-folders write-ups don't cover it, and this machine lost Desktop access during this work.

  `exit_watch` shares the kqueue wake helper.
- **Failures.** The root is watched before the anchor. A mid-run attach failure is latched, warned once and retried by the poll. An anchor failure degrades to the poll. A boot root failure stays fatal (#157).
- **omp profiles.** omp's profile discovery rides the same primitive, so a profile created mid-run is watched at once.
- **No directory creation.** Nothing creates a directory (#1258), and nothing scans history.

## Tests that fail before and pass after
- **`tests/watcher/attach.rs`:** the root is two levels absent with a 3600 s poll. At base it fails after 5.33 s; at head it passes in 0.65 s.
- **`tests/watcher/sources.rs`:** an omp profile is created mid-run with a 3600 s rescan. It fails at base and passes at head.
- **`tests/native_watch.rs`:** a recreated root is re-watched, and an empty anchor that is rmdir'd and then recreated is caught.
  - The file-level `#![cfg(unix)]` moved onto the one test that needs it, so windows-test runs the rest.
  - On macOS these already pass at base; their fail-before shows only on CI's linux and windows lanes.
- **Unit tests on the reconcile:** the anchor walk, a fixpoint after an anchor switch (the reviewer's race probe), detach, identity replacement, a latched attach failure, and router routing.

## Verification
- **Gates, all exit 0:** `cargo fmt --check`, `just clippy`, `just test -p pixtuoid-core` (1556 passed), `just check-windows`, `just check-other-unix`, a Linux cross-clippy of core, `just deny`, `just arch`, `just doc-check`, `just preflight`.
- **Must-run Probe:** the #104 stress ran 25 times under 8 CPU hogs with 0 failures, on exactly the committed code.
- **Real release binary, root absent at boot:** first sight takes 0.24 s at head, against 58.15 s at base.
- **`just hermetic codex`:** 5/5 Pass.
- **Residuals.**
  - Shared-watcher mode first runs natively on CI's linux and windows lanes; macOS never selects it.
  - A persistently failing anchor rebuilds the watch set every poll.
  - Identity can still collide on a filesystem without birth time where an inode is reused (e.g. NFS).
  - A TCC check on a fresh macOS account is undone. The anchor only opens `$HOME` itself and never reads inside it.

## Local review
A correctness reviewer and a design reviewer ran. They raised 12 findings, 1 of them blocking: the hand-rolled unsafe Windows identity, against AGENTS.md's reuse rule. Seven distinct items, each dispositioned in its own thread:
- Six are fixed in abb703605.
- One is refuted: replacing the macOS kqueue anchor with FSEvents.

author: soyeonp92
body:
Fixes BUG-089 (#bug-reports: "Lightning hawk summon is not working").

## Cause

The Lightning Hawk Summon (`SKILL_CH_BOW_CALL_D`) draws `res/npc/animal/lighthawk.bsr`. In the v1.150 data that resource is the **Black Hawk's own mesh and material** (`hawk01/02.bms`, `hawk.bmt`, the same as `blackhawk.bsr`) plus an **ambient** modifier: `skill\china\bow_bird_a.efp` on `Bip01 L Hand` and `Bip01 R Hand`. That's what makes it look different. `coldhawk.bsr` (the Frost Hawk) is the White Hawk plus `bow_bird_b.efp`, and `firehawk.bsr` carries its own ambient set too.

The build publishes those modifiers correctly: `skillfx/manifest.json` lists `lighthawk.bsr`'s two `kind: 2, "ambient"` entries. But `effects.ts`'s `SCT_MOVER` (hawk) branch pushed the hawk actor and `continue`d **before** the stage path that turns a model's ambient particles into attached effect actors. So the wing effects never drew, and the Lightning Hawk looked exactly like the Black Hawk; its built `.glb` is byte-identical to `blackhawk.glb`, as the source says it should be.

The report also said "low level damage". That's the look, not the numbers: the server strikes with the summoned skill's own `summ` row (`CALL_D_01` physical 1297, `CALL_D_05` 1883, against `CALL_B_01`'s 255), so nothing server-side changes.

## Fix

`effects.ts`: after the hawk actor, push one effect actor per ambient particle of the hawk's model, attached to the hawk's gid (`modelParticleAttachment(hawkGid, …)`), looping and kept for as long as the hawk is. That's the same construction the ordinary stage path uses for every other model. The particles ride the hawk as it flies, attacks and returns, and leave with it.

## Tests

`tests/runtime/hawk.test.mjs`, "all 17 SCT_MOVER rows …" (NATIVE_ONLY, real data):
- row 0 stays the hawk;
- every further row is one of that model's ambient effects, with the right program, attached to the hawk's gid, and the row count equals 1 + the ambient count;
- the Black Hawk has none, and the Lightning Hawk has exactly `bow_bird_a.efp` on both wings.

**Mutation:** with `effects.ts` reverted to main, the test fails ("lighthawk.bsr ambient effects").

## What ran

- `node --test tests/runtime/hawk.test.mjs`: 9/9.
- `pnpm exec dprint check` on both files: clean.
- **`pnpm --filter @sro/client-next check`: PASS (12 gates, 459.6 s).**

Old tab: safe, since this is client-only and there's no wire change.

author: dikeckaan
body:
Follow-up to #361 and the review of #387.

**Problem.** The lock helper (`unisoc-modem/lock`, behind the LuCI locks page, the Ubuntu panel and `mu300dash`) only knew the F50's LTE table (`LTE_SUP = 1,3,5,8,34,38,39,40,41`). On the U30 Air you couldn't lock B2/B4/B7/B12/B17/B20/B28/B42/B43/B66. On top of that, with the U30 on automatic, `get` listed all 19 bands as `locked`. The page still said "Automatic" only because it counts candidates.

**Change.**
- The LTE table is now picked per board with `mu300-device`. `u30air` gets `1,2,3,4,5,7,8,12,17,20,28,34,38,39,40,41,42,43,66`, which is the U30 Air's cleared read-back `0,2018,2057,2271,2` on W25.30.2. Every other board gets the F50's table, as before.
- That one table drives `caps.lte` (the panel's candidates and the rpcd "supported" check), the apply filter, the replay filter, and the automatic test that reset and replay run on their read-backs (`lte_full`: every table band present, or an empty mask).
- `get` shows the modem's read-back as it is. The one exception: a read-back that holds the whole table is reported as `locked: ""`. A lock the panel didn't save, such as `0,450,0,149,0` sent by hand, still shows as that lock.
- Nothing is written to flash on a read.

**Design choice: a fixed table per board, not one learned from a read-back.** Any learned table can be poisoned. If the helper learns from a read-back while a lock sits in the modem's NV (left by Android, the stock UI, a hand-sent AT command or a wiped state dir), that lock becomes "the table". From then on it reads as automatic and passes every reset and replay check. That is what #387 does on the U30 Air with `0,450,0,149,0`. Learning only right after an explicit clear plus radio restart avoids that, but has two problems. The learned file sits in the state dir on the SD card or eMMC, which can move to the other board. And the U30's bands would only appear after a reset. A fixed per-board table has neither problem and needs no flash write. The cost is a new table entry when a new board or firmware has a different table. FINDINGS 223 records this.

**#387.** This PR doesn't fully cover #387's case. That report is a modem whose *cleared* read-back is `0,450,0,149,0`, maybe one that ignores a zero mask. If such a firmware exists, it would show as an 8-band lock here and the reset would fail. That fails loudly rather than passing silently, but it is still unresolved until we have that board's AT output (requested in the review). So #387 stays open. No code was taken from it; its finding prompted the "a lock set outside the panel still shows" test.

**Tests.** `test_unisoc_plugin`: U30 table and an automatic modem read as nothing locked, with nothing written to the state dir; a hand-set lock still shows on the U30, including a lock on all of the F50's bands; the F50 table is unchanged; B20+B7 on the U30 send `0,0,8,64,0`, are saved and pass the replay check, a lost lock fails it, and the F50 refuses them; the replay check for a saved automatic needs the whole table on both boards. The four new tests fail on main. `test_panel test_luci_i18n test_mu300dash_security test_early_replay_hook test_api test_static test_package test_atd_dash test_unisoc_plugin`: 346 OK.

**Device check.**
- **U30 Air** (OpenWrt 25.12.6, 6.18.58, v2026.10.26.1, modem W25.30.2, this helper installed):
  - Automatic reads `locked ""`, raw `0,2018,2057,2271,2`, 19 candidates.
  - `ubus call mu300dash lock_set {"kind":"lte","val":"20,7"}` sent `0,0,8,64,0` and read back `20,7`. CEREG showed the modem registered.
  - A reboot replayed the lock: `replay done (early)`, and `lock verify` passed.
  - Panel `lte ""` saved automatic. After a reboot the early check accepted `0,2018,2057,2271,2`.
  - A hand lock `AT+SPLBAND=1,0,450,0,149,0` read back as `34,39,40,41,1,3,5,8`, not as automatic.
  - Reset from the panel lock and from the hand lock: `state ok` both times. It ended with an empty state dir and the modem on automatic (mode auto, EN-DC on, no cells).
- **F50-B** (Ubuntu, 7.3.0, W25.39.4):
  - The table and the cleared read-back `0,482,0,149,0` are unchanged.
  - `20,7` was refused (none supported). `3,7` locked B3, leaving B7 out.
  - `lock verify` passed. Reset `ok` brought it back to automatic with nothing saved.
- Both boards are back on their installed helper.

author: rachelnhuang
body:
## What this adds
- `src/data/features.py`: past-only tabular features for each prediction point (user, window t): recency, frequency, clicks, cost, conversions so far, time of day. Built with a backward as-of merge, so nothing from window t+1 or later can leak in.
- `src/models/baselines.py` + `scripts/run_baselines.py`: non-sequential baselines, evaluated on both the chronological and user-disjoint splits.
  - Conversion: recency/frequency score, logistic regression, gradient boosting. Trained on all positives plus 2% of negatives, with probabilities corrected back afterwards. The F1 threshold is chosen on validation and applied to test.
  - Campaigns (top 10): popularity, repeat the user's last window, user history.
- `src/data/dataset.py`: per-user sequence dataset for the LSTM / Transformer: inputs [T, 6], campaign bags for `nn.EmbeddingBag`, next-window conversion and campaign labels, and split masks. Includes a PyTorch DataLoader. Inputs cover all T windows, so **models must use causal attention** (`causal_mask(T)` is provided).
- `src/data/io.py`: shard readers. `metrics.py`: top-K ranking metrics without dense [N, 675] score matrices.
- Thread cap: scripts limit BLAS/OpenMP threads to the Slurm CPU allocation. Zaratan login nodes cap each user at 256 threads, and numpy was starting 128 per process.
- Tests: leakage checks for features and campaign baselines, dataset shapes, the PyTorch collate, and an end-to-end script run. 37 pass on Zaratan.

## Full-data results, 12h windows (test split)
Job 23587289: 21 min on 4 CPUs, 18.4 GB peak.

| Task | Best baseline | Chronological | User-disjoint |
|---|---|---|---|
| Conversion (base rate 0.19%) | Gradient boosting | PR-AUC 0.023, ROC-AUC 0.843, top 10% captures 53% | PR-AUC 0.025, ROC-AUC 0.847, 54% |
| Campaigns | User history | HitRate@10 0.895, NDCG@10 0.833 | HitRate@10 0.873, NDCG@10 0.819 |

Full tables: `results/tables/baselines_criteo_w12h.md`

## Implications for the Transformer
- **Conversion is where there is room to improve.** Gradient boosting (PR-AUC 0.023) is the number to beat.
- **Campaign prediction is close to saturated.** About 90% of next-window campaigns are ones the user has already seen (Criteo is a retargeting platform). The Transformer's opportunity there is the ~10% of new-to-the-user campaigns, so we should report those separately.

## How to run
    pytest -q
    python scripts/run_baselines.py --data-dir data/processed/criteo_w12h_smoke   # 2% sample, ~20 s
    sbatch scripts/zaratan/run_baselines.sbatch                                   # full 12h

body:
## Scope: shared POS infrastructure + canonical financial and history rules

### Shared infrastructure
- `PosNavigation`, `PosUi.showRootWithBack()`, and `PosBarcode` centralize navigation/layout entry points and barcode scan result handling.
- `PosDatabase.findProduct()` centralizes active-product lookup.
- `PosTransactions` gives multi-table operations one atomic commit/rollback boundary.
- `PosRecords` centralizes schema writers for `stock_history`, `sales_ledger`, `sales_ledger_items`, `price_history`, and `payment_history`.

### Canonical business rules and event records
- `PosBusinessRules` is the shared source for credit-fee calculation, the 24-hour fee-waiver/payment-due rule, return/cancel eligibility window and status checks, and reversal ledger arithmetic.
- `PosEvents` is the canonical event contract for sales, line items, debt payments, fee waivers, returns/cancellations, price changes, stock changes, stock-limit changes, product creation, barcode registration, and customer-profile changes. Business-state updates and their ledger/audit records must share the same `PosTransactions` transaction.
- Sale item, sale stock movement, return/cancel item, and return/cancel stock movement writes now route through `PosEvents`, not directly from the screens.
- Money remains integer satang with overflow-checked arithmetic.
- `PosBusinessRulesTest` covers fee rounding, payment-window boundaries, cash/credit differences, reversal arithmetic/status, and non-destructive retention policy. CI is configured to run `testDebugUnitTest` before `assembleDebug`.

### History and retention integrity
- `PosHistoryPolicy` is the canonical retention policy.
- Routine retention is now deliberately non-destructive: it does not delete bills, bill items, payment rows, `stock_history`, `price_history`, `payment_history`, `sales_ledger`, `sales_ledger_items`, or `audit_log`.
- Age-based deletion remains disabled until a verified archival/export workflow exists, because these rows are inputs to historical reports and customer-account history.

### Compatibility and validation
- `MainActivity.java` remains unchanged in this PR.
- Earlier CI run [#926](https://github.com/preechaphukthaisong65-arch/ma-yai-on-pos/actions/runs/40260492681) passed for an earlier commit. Newer commits require a fresh CI run before this branch can be called build-verified.
- Build success does not prove runtime behavior. Return/cancel, credit-fee waiver, payment, stock, reports, and retention still need scenario tests and physical-device review before merge.
- This PR remains separate from `main`; it has not been merged.

author: sensorylog
body:
## Why this is needed
The website tracker PR writes to `analyticsEvents`, but the current repository `firestore.rules` has no matching rule, so the final deny-all rule rejects those writes. This PR adds the narrow rule required for the tracker to function.

## Security properties
- Authenticated users can create only events whose `userId` matches their own UID.
- Event keys are strictly allowlisted and required; platform, event name, session ID, app version, timestamp and details are bounded/validated.
- `timestamp` must equal `request.time` (compatible with Firestore `serverTimestamp()`).
- Only the configured dashboard admin UID can read analytics events.
- Updates and deletes are denied; the existing catch-all deny remains intact.
- No anonymous Firestore writes, no public collection reads, no Cloud Functions or Blaze dependency.

## Before merging
Deploy rules to a staging/test Firebase project or use the Firestore Rules Emulator to verify: authenticated owner create succeeds; mismatched `userId`, missing/extra fields, invalid platform, client timestamp, anonymous create, non-admin read, update and delete all fail. Confirm the admin UID is still correct for this project. This repository change does not itself deploy Firestore rules.

L'agenda de reunion.fr n'est plus lu. À la place, une mention datée le dit, avec les mots de marketing.

**En attente** : les mots attendent la validation avant la mise en file. Le jour de « Non repris depuis le … » (`non_lue_depuis`, 26/10 ici) est à mettre au jour de la mise en ligne.

Une sous-requête de moins par vue froide : outil 34 → 33, /evenements 55 → 54, ses sous-pages 37 → 36, /enfants 38 → 37. Registre et BUDGET.md régénérés. agenda 12, enfants 7, chiffres 4.

body:
Fixes from a second-opinion review of #92 and #93. Stacked on #93; merge that first.

## Kicked casts
The generator measures a spell's intervals across completed casts only. In the matcher, though, a kicked cast re-anchored the spell's track. So when a mob recast a kicked spell sooner than its cooldown, the interval check rejected that cast, and NarrowByHistory could hand it to the spell's same-length sibling. A track now remembers that its last start was kicked, and neither check rules the spell out on that gap. test_core.lua has a case that fails on #93's head (the recast went to the other spell).

author: dmpl6454
body:
## What

Owner: *"connect the all sub-domain to each other as per requirement"*.

Before this, the portals barely reached each other: the staff portal linked out only from its login page (and never to Sales), HR linked to nothing, Sales only to the website, and every staff portal asked for its own sign-in even though all three use the same account.

### One-click switching between the staff portals
The staff portal (portal.), HR (hr.) and Sales (sales.) all sign in the same `users` row, so switching needs no second password.

- **API** `apps/api/src/services/portal-handoff.service.ts` (routes in `auth.routes.ts`):
  - `GET /auth/portals`: the directory each switcher renders. It marks which staff portals this account may enter: staff and HR for every active employee, Sales when the account holds `sales:view`, the same check the `/sales` routes make. It also lists the public sites, with URLs from the `*_APP_URL` env the CORS list already reads.
  - `POST /auth/handoff {target}` returns `<portal>/login#handoff=<code>`: a 256-bit one-time code, valid 60 s, bound to its target, held in memory (the API is one pm2 fork process; a restart just voids pending codes). The code rides in the **URL fragment**, which browsers never send to a server, so it stays out of nginx and Cloudflare logs and out of `Referer` headers.
  - `POST /auth/handoff/exchange {code}` returns that portal's own session: an `hr` token for HR, an `employee` token for staff and Sales (`issueEmployeeSession` / `issueHrSession` are now exported). Staff tokens only; a client token is refused by type.
- **Staff portal**: "Switch portal" block at the foot of the DS rail (icons with tooltips when collapsed). The login header now links Sales too.
- **HR portal**: "Other portals" block in the sidebar footer.
- **Sales portal**: "Portals" menu in the header; `adoptSession` added to its auth context.
- Each `/login` page exchanges the code on mount, strips it from the URL, and falls back to the form with a clear message on a used or expired code (410 `HANDOFF_INVALID`).

### Public sites
- digitalsukoon.com footer: Client portal · Creators · Careers · Staff (its own row on phones). The client, creators and jobs sites already link back to the website; every switcher lists the public sites too.

body:
## Summary

### Item 1 — Which tool changed `config/risk.yaml` and why the hook did not block it

The change was made in commit `5b3ff88` using the **Edit tool** (Claude Code built-in). The diff shows lines appended at the end of the file — the Edit tool matched the last existing line as `old_string` and replaced it with `old_string + new price_shock block`.

The hook did **not** block it for two reasons:
1. **`risk-config-guard.yml` did not exist yet** at the time of the edit. The workflow file was created in that same session and committed together with the `risk.yaml` change. A GHA workflow cannot enforce itself retroactively on the commits that create it.
2. **GHA workflows only run on PRs**, not on local `git commit`. The pre-commit hooks (ruff, mypy, pytest, secrets) have no rule covering `config/risk.yaml` changes — that gap is exactly what this workflow is designed to close.

Going forward, any PR touching `config/risk.yaml` or `config/live_approval.yaml` will fail `risk-config-guard / guard` unless the repo owner adds the `owner-approved-risk` label.

---

### Item 2 — Changes to the workflow

- Replaced `python3 -c ... json.load` label parser with GitHub's native `contains()` expression — no subprocess, no JSON quoting edge cases.
- Added `labeled` / `unlabeled` trigger types so the check re-runs immediately when the label is added or removed (without requiring a new push).
- Added an 8-step comment with exact click-path to configure this as a required status check on master.

---

### How to make `risk-config-guard / guard` a required status check (exact steps)

1. **Merge this PR** to master so the workflow file is on the default branch.
2. **Trigger a first run**: open any test PR that touches `config/risk.yaml` (or push a dummy change). GitHub only surfaces a check in the branch-protection UI after it has run at least once on master.
3. Go to **https://github.com/tahirbaba/ai-trader/settings/branches**
4. Under *Branch protection rules*, click **Edit** next to the `master` rule (or **Add rule** if none exists; set *Branch name pattern* = `master`).
5. Check **Require status checks to pass before merging**.
6. In the search box type: `risk-config-guard / guard` — select the entry that appears.
7. Optionally check **Require branches to be up to date before merging**.
8. Click **Save changes**.

The exact required check name is: **`risk-config-guard / guard`** (workflow name / job id).

> **Note:** Do NOT add the `owner-approved-risk` label yourself. Only the repo owner should add that label.

## Test plan
- [ ] Verify workflow YAML is valid (`act` dry-run or push to a test branch)
- [ ] Open a PR touching `config/risk.yaml` without the label → check fails
- [ ] Add `owner-approved-risk` label → check re-runs and passes
- [ ] Open a PR NOT touching those files → check is skipped (satisfies required check)

author: ingridmorstrad
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** A Slack voice reply that is still being synthesised is kept alive until it finishes, and gateway shutdown cancels it.

`_reply_by_voice` in `src/kiro_crew/slack/handler_runtime/voice.py` started the spoken reply with a bare `asyncio.create_task(_safe_voice_reply(...))` and dropped the task. The event loop holds only a weak reference to a task, so nothing kept the reply alive while it ran, and it was never added to the handler's `_background_tasks` set that `cancel_background_tasks()` clears at shutdown.

## Why it matters

Every user who turns on Slack voice replies goes through this path. A reply collected mid-synthesis is lost with no audio and no error. A reply still running at shutdown is skipped by `cancel_background_tasks()`, the shutdown step that exists to stop such tasks. The same package already names both outcomes as defects in `track_background_task`'s docstring.

## Not a goal

- The other untracked fire-and-forget tasks in `slack/` (listed under Sibling sweep).
- Changing what the voice reply does, when it triggers, or how it reports a failure.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

Symptom: an in-flight voice reply is held by nothing and outlives `cancel_background_tasks()`. Root cause: `_reply_by_voice` discards the task `create_task` returns. Change: the task goes through `track_background_task`, the helper in `handler_runtime/access.py` that `delivery.py` and `transport_dispatch.py` already use. It holds the task in `_background_tasks` until it finishes, and `cancel_background_tasks()` can then stop it. The name is resolved through the handler module's namespace like every other owner function, and `voice.py` lists it in its `TYPE_CHECKING` import block.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: the reply runs exactly as before; it is now also held in `_background_tasks` until it finishes, and cancelled at shutdown.

Removes nothing: the change adds a registration and takes away no path, key or reader.

## Tests

New file `test/test_slack_voice_reply_tracked.py`. Each test parks the reply on an `asyncio.Event`, so the in-flight state is observable without a sleep. Every wait the test must unblock goes through `slack_handler_helpers._within_lost_run`, so a reply that never starts fails by name instead of hanging the worker:

- `test_in_flight_voice_reply_is_tracked_until_it_finishes`: the parked reply is in `_background_tasks` while it runs, and the set is empty once it finishes. Red on `origin/main` with `assert set() == {<Task pending ... _parked() ...>}`.
- `test_shutdown_cancels_an_in_flight_voice_reply`: `cancel_background_tasks()` requests cancellation of the parked reply, and the reply ends cancelled. Red on `origin/main` with `assert 0 == 1` on `replies[0].cancelling()`.

Both pass 20/20 at `-n0`, 10/10 at `-n 4 --dist loadgroup` beside `test_slack_handler_coverage_delivery.py` and `test_slack_stream_held_tail.py`, and in a shuffled order (seed 18529, 25 ids with `test_slack_handler_coverage_delivery.py`).

Proof: PROVEN test/test_slack_voice_reply_tracked.py (head cd4e3587afdb)

Gates run locally: black, isort, flake8, mypy, `check_black_formatting.py`, `check_sync_io_in_async.py`, `check_subprocess_encoding.py`, comment-history, brand-name, `test_flake_pattern_ratchet.py`, and semgrep 1.78.0 `--config semgrep/` diff-scoped (clean). `local-gate.py` backend related set: 7911 passed, 48 skipped. Its frontend related set could not start because this worktree has no `website/node_modules` (`Cannot find package 'vite'`); the diff touches no frontend file.

## Manual verification

N/A — unit coverage sufficient: the tests drive the real `_reply_by_voice` and the real `cancel_background_tasks`; only the synthesis call is replaced.

## Related Issues

Closes #24220

## Sibling sweep

Swept: `git grep -nE "^\s+(asyncio|loop|_loop)\.create_task\(" -- src/kiro_crew/slack/`
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/slack/handler_runtime/voice.py:203 -- changed here
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/slack/handler_runtime/delivery.py:838 -- not affected -- already wrapped in track_background_task
Sibling: src/kiro_crew/slack/transport_dispatch.py:1202 -- not affected -- already wrapped in track_background_task

Same defect, not changed here and not yet tracked (each is its own fix in another file):

- `src/kiro_crew/slack/interactions_approvals.py:507`: `asyncio.create_task(_do_revise())` on the review-revise submit drops its task.
- `src/kiro_crew/slack/gateway_runtime/service_boot.py:1335`: `asyncio.create_task(_start_bg_session())` drops its task.

## Pattern harvest

Rule candidate: semgrep
Pattern: an expression statement `asyncio.create_task(...)` whose result is neither bound nor passed to a tracker such as `track_background_task`.

## Checklist

- [x] At most two commits (one is the norm), with a Conventional Commits title (`feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|ci|build|revert: ...`)
- [x] Existing tests pass and new tests added for new functionality
- [x] Self-review completed; code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or internal references in the diff

author: zerojunz
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"zerojunz"} -->
_Requested by **Dan** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01CxLicvn5y4tRRpJxVUdpgo?thread=cmsg_01CxLicvn5y4tRRpJxVUdpgo7ALFsYen3CQ1ayUrwv2Q6T)_

Before: a 3D scene was exposed the same way whatever it showed. A camera walking from a dark tunnel into daylight saw the daylight burn white, and nothing like Godot's `CameraAttributesPractical` existed, so Godot projects lost their exposure settings on import. Emission energy was applied before the color was made linear, so a material's `emission_energy_multiplier` of 6 shone about 66 times white rather than 6.

After: a camera's `CameraAttributesPractical` (or the `WorldEnvironment`'s, for cameras without their own) exposes the 3D world as Godot 4.6's does. `exposure_multiplier` brightens lights, emission, the background and the sky. With `auto_exposure_enabled`, Forward+ measures each frame and adapts to it over game time, so daylight starts white and settles to its blue in a few seconds, and stepping back into the tunnel goes dark before the eyes adjust. Emission is the linear color times its energy, as in Godot, so the glow examples now shine as brightly as their READMEs say.

How:
- **Component.** `CameraAttributesPractical` with Godot's fields and defaults: `exposure_sensitivity`, `exposure_multiplier`, `auto_exposure_enabled`, `auto_exposure_scale`, `auto_exposure_speed` and the min and max sensitivities. `scene3d::camera_attributes` picks the camera's own, else the first `WorldEnvironment`'s. `scene3d::environment` applies the multiplier where Godot's exposure normalization does (lights, sky suns, the background and sky energy, emission), and not to ambient color or fog, and turns the sensitivities into brightnesses (sensitivity × 0.125 / `exposure_sensitivity`). A zero `exposure_sensitivity` is reported and auto exposure is skipped.
- **Measuring.** `forward_post.hlsl` gains Godot's `luminance_reduce.glsl` passes: each pixel's brightest channel averaged in 8×8 blocks, then the blocks, down to one R32F value that the device keeps between frames. The last pass moves `auto_exposure_adjust` of the way from the previous brightness and clamps it to the min and max. The tonemap and glow's first level are exposed by scale over brightness. `luminance_plan` and `run_luminance_pass` are the CPU twins. Vulkan, Metal and Direct3D 12, WebGPU and the software device run the same passes.
- **Game time.** `Renderer::prepare` takes the game time and turns `auto_exposure_speed` into each frame's adjust. A new version starts the measurement over when auto exposure turns on, when the camera follows other attributes, or when time goes back (as after a restore). `frame.capture`'s `time` carries it from one capture to the next.
- **Emission.** `mesh.hlsl` and its CPU twin in `mesh.cpp` make the emission color linear and then multiply by the energy. The glow tests' dim square is now 2.5 times white, which is about what it drew before.
- **Import.** A Godot `WorldEnvironment`'s `camera_attributes` and a `Camera3D`'s `attributes` that are a `CameraAttributesPractical` become the component. `CameraAttributesPhysical` and the depth of field fields are reported.
- **Tests.** `test_forward_post.cpp`: block reduction and the final pass's smoothing and clamping; dark frames brightened and bright ones darkened; smoothing, new versions, the floor and ceiling and exposed glow on every Forward+ device; and the GPUs matching the software device over three frames. `test_scene3d.cpp`: which attributes win, the multiplier, sensitivities, the zero-sensitivity problem and versions over time; a captured frame adapting over game time. `test_import_godot.cpp`: both import paths.
- **Examples.** The new `examples/auto-exposure-3d` walks from a torch-lit tunnel into daylight and back, then changes `auto_exposure_scale`. `glow-3d`, `post-processing-3d` and `fbx-models` outputs change where emission is above 1, and the glow-3d and post-processing-3d READMEs quote the new colors.
- **Docs.** scene-format.md's new `CameraAttributesPractical` section and the emission row, godot-import.md, AGENTS.md and the roadmap.

## O que este PR faz e por quê

Esta alteração configura o ambiente da API do SalonBooking para utilizar o Prisma ORM na versão 7.10.1, conforme os requisitos da Atividade 08. Foi configurado o gerador `prisma-client`, com saída para `../generated/prisma`, e criado o arquivo `prisma.config.ts`, responsável por carregar as variáveis de ambiente e configurar o acesso ao schema do Prisma. Também foi adicionado o Docker Compose com PostgreSQL 16, utilizando o banco `appdb`, o usuário `app` e a porta `5432`. O `ConfigModule` do NestJS foi configurado globalmente, e as dependências necessárias para o Prisma e a conexão com o PostgreSQL foram adicionadas. Os arquivos `.gitignore` e `.env.example` foram ajustados para manter as variáveis de ambiente locais fora do controle de versão, permitindo o compartilhamento de um exemplo de configuração. O schema permanece sem modelos de negócio e sem migrations, conforme solicitado. O arquivo `docs/prd.md` não foi alterado.

## Validação

- **Testes:** executados com sucesso para a API e a aplicação web.
- **Lint:** executado com sucesso.

C++ byte oracles for the document commands of #105, and the cause of the white mmegold `post` images.

## script3

`--mds-script` gains verbs that run the real C++ handlers. 8 scripts under `tests/fixtures/rust/script3/` exercise them:

- the timeline key drag, in model mode and in camera mode;

author: lprimak
body:
Fixes #15407.

Keeps `bean-discovery-mode="all"` and leaves MyFaces behavior as it is. Adds one conditional exclude so that PrimeFaces classes are not CDI-discovered unless MyFaces' `CdiAnnotationProviderExtension` (the `USE_CDI_FOR_ANNOTATION_SCANNING` path the `beans.xml` was introduced for in #13702) is on the classpath:

```xml
<exclude name="org.primefaces.**">
    <if-class-not-available name="org.apache.myfaces.config.annotation.CdiAnnotationProviderExtension"/>
</exclude>
```

**Why:** on Mojarra, `all` makes Weld run `ProcessAnnotatedType` and bean creation for all 1,829 classes on every deploy. PrimeFaces has no `jakarta.enterprise.*` / `jakarta.inject.*` annotations on any class, field or method, so nothing is lost as beans. Measured on Payara 7.2026.10-4 / Mojarra 4.1.16.payara-p1 with PF 16.0.1 as a shared library: ~1.2 s -> ~0.3 s deploy (details and profile in #15407).

**Class name check:** `org.apache.myfaces.config.annotation.CdiAnnotationProviderExtension` exists on `apache/myfaces` `4.0.x` and `4.1.x`; it is a CDI extension that observes `ProcessAnnotatedType` for the Faces annotations.

**Alternative:** switch to `annotated` (what was discussed in #14846 for Faces 5). This change gets the same speed today without touching the MyFaces path.

**Not verified by me (please run before merging):**
- Integration tests on Mojarra, on MyFaces, and on MyFaces with `org.apache.myfaces.annotation.USE_CDI_FOR_ANNOTATION_SCANNING=true`.
- Showcase deployment on Payara, WildFly and Quarkus (no unsatisfied-dependency errors).
- I measured only the Payara shared-library setup (warlibs)

_Requested by **Ryan**_

**Swap panel** for 0.59.1. Ryan's feedback on 0.59.0: in Studio > Film there was nowhere to put a video and a picture of the person to swap in. Swap was only a right-click action, or a Video-mode button that used the gallery selection. This PR adds the panel from his mark-up: a **Swap** chip after the film chips, and two big drop boxes under it, **Video** on the left and **Person** on the right.

**What it does**
- **Film** gets a **⇆ Swap** chip after *Short film ⇄* and the film list. **Video** mode's **⇆ Swap a character** chip now opens the same panel. It's one shared component (`#swap-panel` in the create bar, with `initSwapPanel` / `renderSwap` / `runSwap` in studio.ts). The chip toggles the panel. While it's open, the prompt, reference slot, settings and warning are hidden.
- **Video box**:
  - Takes a drop from Explorer, a drop from the Renders gallery (video cards can now be dragged, using their own drag type `application/x-prestige-video` so chat and the picture drop targets ignore them), a paste, or a click to choose (the PC's file dialog, so the video is read where it is).
  - Shows the video with its name, length and size. It plays muted on hover, and **×** clears it.
- **Person box**:
  - Takes a picture dropped from Explorer or the gallery, a paste, or a click to choose. **Or a character** picks a saved Character's face.
  - Shows the picture, and **×** clears it.
- **Under the boxes**: *Who to replace* (defaults to *person*), Draft/Standard, the time estimate for this video, the consent note with the minors line, and a big **Swap** button. The button reads "Swap (add to queue)" while something is rendering.
  - It queues the same SCAIL-2 job as 0.58 (`swapInto`: render queue, chat model unloaded, source sound muxed back on).
  - The result lands in Renders and the panel links it. **Add to "film"** then puts it at the end of the open film (or the latest one) as a new shot, with the swap as its take (`filmMode.addClip`, using the existing `addTake`).
- Right-click a video → **Swap a character…** opens the panel with that video in the Video box. It switches to Video mode unless Film is showing. A gallery video dropped anywhere on the create bar does the same.
- A video dropped from Explorer reaches the page as bytes with no path. The new `swap_video_save` command writes it to `comfy-output\swap.frames\<safe name>`, which the gallery skips, so `video_info`, the upload and `mux_swap` work as they do for a render.
- The old `#swap` dialog is removed. Film's per-shot **Swap…** dialog (a cast member into a take) is unchanged.
- Styles: `.swap-box` joins the Molded lists in mesa.css next to `.ref-add`, and `.opt.swap.on` gets the gold "on" look like ⚙ Settings. The boxes stack into one column below 640 px.

**Tested**
- `tsc --noEmit` clean, `vite build` OK, `cargo test` 62 passed. That includes a new `dropped_videos_keep_a_safe_name` test, which covers path separators, odd characters and non-videos.
- Dev build with the test app profile, driven over WebView2 DevTools:
  - **Explorer drops**: a real OS-style file drop (CDP `Input.dispatchDragEvent` with file paths) of an MP4 onto Video and a JPG onto Person. The video was saved to `swap.frames`, and both previews and names showed.
  - **Gallery drag**: a video card dragged onto the Video box filled it with that render. One dropped on the create bar in Image mode opened the panel in Video mode with it.
  - **Right-click**: from Music mode, Swap a character… switched to Video with the panel open and prefilled. Toggling the chip off brings the prompt back.
  - **One Draft swap end to end** from the Film tab: a 3.4 s 768×512 clip (81 frames, 1 part) with a full-body picture. Estimated 9 min; it took **8 min 53 s** (sampling ~95 s a step).
    - Output `scail2-swap_00006_.mp4`: 81 frames with sound, the woman in the green coat walking in place of the man in red.
    - **Add to "The Last Letter"** added it as shot 4 with the swap as its take.

author: codesensedev
body:
Code and anything aligned with spaces lost its indentation and its lines in a `<text>`, which collapses white space. `<code>` is a box that keeps them, wraps what is too long and splits across pages, and `<code-span>` is a run of code inside a `<text>`.

## What changes
- `<code>`: a column around one text that keeps its spaces and lines. The box is padded and tinted and fills the width, in Courier unless `font` says otherwise. It takes the attributes of a box, `tab-size`, `line-height`, `widows` and `orphans`. A line longer than the box wraps at a space, and a word with none breaks at the last character that fits. A `<span>` in it colors a stretch of the code.
- `<code-span>`: a run of code in a `<text>` or `<text-at>`, in the code font on a tint.
- The kit tree path, `kit_to_xml` and the SDK code generator know both, and the generator escapes the lines and tabs of a code in each language.
- `scripts/gen-sdk-api.mjs` and `scripts/check-sdk-parity.mjs` list the two elements.
- Two showcase fixtures: `showcase-code` and `showcase-code-split`, a listing of 182 lines over four pages.

## How it was checked
`make test-all`: core, WASI and the four SDKs pass, with new tests for parsing, wrapping, tabs, splitting across pages, kit trees, data binding, the generator and an embedded font. No existing snapshot hash changed. The two new PDFs were looked at page by page. The VS Code extension needs no change: its tests pass against the new schema.

author: eugenioenko
body:
Closes #1152

## Why

With word wrap on, Up/Down jumped between buffer lines, so a long wrapped line (Markdown prose) could only be crossed with Left/Right. VS Code, Sublime, JetBrains, Emacs, nano and Helix all move by screen row under soft wrap; this makes it the default with no setting.

## What changes (word wrap on only)

- Up/Down and Shift+Up/Down step one screen row, including within a wrapped line.
- PageUp/PageDown move by the viewport height in screen rows instead of buffer lines.
- A sticky screen column is kept across shorter rows and reset by any other cursor move or edit.
- Diff phantom rows (deleted lines, fillers) are skipped, as before.
- Multiple cursors move by screen row (without the sticky column).
- Past the end of a row that continues on the next, the cursor stops on the row's last rune, since the position after it is drawn at the start of the next row.

Unwrapped movement is unchanged.

## Tests

- `internal/ui/editor_widget_wrapmove_test.go`: rows within and across lines, edges, sticky column and its reset, fullwidth runes and tabs, Shift selection, PageUp/PageDown, phantom rows, multi-cursor, `colAtX`, and an unwrapped regression.
- `tests/e2e/word_wrap_test.go`: arrows, Shift+Down and PageDown through the full app.
- `tests/e2e/inline_diff_test.go`: Down in a wrapped unified diff skips the deleted row and walks the wrapped edited line.

`make test`, `make lint` and the functional suite pass. The new tests fail without the key handler change.

## Run

`bin/ttt --size 70x14 prose.md --exec 'wait-for Notes; exec "Toggle Word Wrap"; key Down; key Down; key Right; key Right; key Right; key Down; key Down; screenshot s.txt; quit'`

Before: `Ln 5, Col 1` (jumped past the paragraph). After:

```
│  1  # Notes                                                        │
│  2                                                                 │
│  3  This is a long paragraph of Markdown prose that keeps going w  │
│     ell past the edge of the editor so that word wrap has to spli  │
│     t it across several screen rows, which is exactly the case re  │
│     ported in the issue.                                           │
│  4  Short line.                                                    │
│  5                                                                 │
╰────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
                    Ln 3, Col 126   Spaces: 4   UTF-8   LF   Markdown
```

## Not in this PR

- Home/End to the start/end of the screen row first (VS Code style).
- Unwrapped Up/Down keep the rune index rather than a goal column, so the column drifts after a short line or across tabs/fullwidth text.

author: aheimowitz
body:
Closes #31.

## Changes

**PIN unlock after Lock.** The popup only looked up whether a PIN was set when it opened on a locked vault. If it opened unlocked, pressing Lock showed the password field even with a PIN configured. It now reads `hasPIN` on every open.

**Pop-out window.** A new header button opens the popup in its own resizable window (`?popout=1`). It's hidden once you're in the window. Two follow-on fixes:
- QR scan now captures the last-focused *normal* window. Before, it captured the "current" window, which would be the pop-out itself.
- The background now also broadcasts `AUTH_STATE_CHANGED` to extension pages via `runtime.sendMessage`. The popup listens and drops to the unlock or login screen. Without this, a long-lived pop-out would keep showing codes after an idle or system lock.

**Form draft restore.** Edits in the add/edit form are saved to session storage (`src/shared/popup-draft.ts`) and restored when the popup reopens.
- Opening a form without changing it doesn't create a draft, and reverting your edits clears it.
- Cleared on save, cancel, delete, lock and logout. A draft for a code that has since been deleted is dropped.
- On Firefox MV2 without `storage.session`, it uses the existing `session_`-prefixed local fallback, the same as the codes cache.

**Scrollbars.** The code list and the form use thin scrollbars that are only visible while hovering.

## Testing
- `tsc --noEmit` passes, and the Chrome and Firefox builds succeed.
- Not yet tested by hand in a browser. Worth checking:
  - [ ] PIN → close and reopen → Lock asks for the PIN
  - [ ] Pop-out on Chrome and Firefox (sizing, QR scan from the window, auto-lock while it's open)
  - [ ] Close the popup mid-add, reopen, and the form is restored
  - [ ] Scrollbar appears only on hover

author: hogan-yuan
body:
Cut **v0.15.0**. Bumps `0.14.0` → `0.15.0` (minor: new tools and output changes for Longbridge US accounts, listed below).

## Included since v0.14.0
- **Longbridge US accounts** (#173), built on longbridge SDK 5.3.0:
  - `account_balance`, `stock_positions`, `cash_flow`, `exchange_rate`, `today_orders`, `history_orders` and `order_detail` call the US asset and order APIs for US accounts and return the same shape as for AP accounts.
  - `today_executions` / `history_executions` work on US accounts; `side` is filled from the account's orders.
  - AP-only tools (`fund_positions`, `margin_ratio`, ...) are hidden for US accounts, and a direct call returns an error whose hint names the alternative.
- **`fx_rate`** (#175): public ECB reference exchange rates via Frankfurter (latest, a past date, or a daily series), separate from Longbridge's account-conversion rates in `exchange_rate`.

## Behaviour changes for API clients
- On US accounts, the tools above now return the AP shape instead of the raw US payloads; US-only fields stay alongside the AP keys.
- `cash_flow` on US accounts returns a signed `balance` plus `direction`.
- `today_orders` on US accounts covers the overnight session (from 20:00 ET the previous day); `history_orders` / `history_executions` read date-only bounds in New York time for US accounts.

Only `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` and `server.json` change.

author: wadakatu
body:
## Summary

A reboot or OS update kills every agent running in Orca. Orca restores the tabs and scrollback but not the processes ("What doesn't get restored" in Orca's `model/session-restore.mdx`), so each session had to be reopened by hand with `claude --continue`.

Now a SessionStart hook leaves a marker for each interactive Claude session in an Orca terminal, and a LaunchAgent reopens the sessions that were still alive when the machine went down, with `claude -r <session id>` in a new Orca tab. How it resumes depends on how the transcript ends:

- waiting on an AskUserQuestion answer: asks the same question again
- in the middle of a turn: checks `git status` and the conversation, then continues
- idle: only reopens the conversation (no prompt, so no tokens)

## Changes

- `agents/claude/hooks/session-marker.sh` (SessionStart): writes `<boot time> <claude pid> <Orca worktree id> <cwd> <transcript>` to `~/Library/Application Support/agent-resume/sessions/<session id>`. Skips `claude -p` (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-cli`) and sessions outside Orca. After `/clear`, the previous marker of the same process is dropped.
- `home/scripts/agent-resume.sh` + `home/agent-resume.nix`: runs at login and every 3 minutes. Markers from an earlier boot are resumed; markers from this boot whose `claude` process is gone are removed. Nothing happens while Orca is unreachable, so a run during shutdown cannot erase the markers.
- `agents/claude/settings.json`: register the hook.
- `README.md`: list the job.

Markers are removed by pid instead of a SessionEnd hook because Claude runs its exit handlers when the host shuts down (transcripts got `cost-state` / `last-prompt` records at reboot), so SessionEnd would likely remove the markers that the resume needs.

## Not covered

- Codex sessions.
- An Orca daemon crash without a reboot: the processes die in the same boot, so their markers are cleaned up as normal exits.
- Sessions started before the hook was installed have no marker.

## Test plan

- [x] shellcheck on both scripts, `nix flake check --no-build`, and `nix eval` of the LaunchAgent (`RunAtLoad`, `StartInterval = 180`)
- [x] Transcript classification on real sessions: AskUserQuestion pending → question, mid-turn → work, end_turn / `/clear` / interrupted → idle, missing file → idle
- [x] Live resume after today's reboot: a hand-written old-boot marker for the infra session opened a new Orca tab, the session re-asked its AskUserQuestion, and the hook wrote a fresh marker (`CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli`)
- [x] Cleanup in a scratch state dir: live claude pid kept, dead pid and non-claude pid removed, old-boot marker with a deleted worktree moved aside without resuming

author: yysskk
body:
## Summary

A type with nothing for `copying` to replace was told to add a type annotation:

```swift
@Copying            // error: @Copying requires at least one stored property with an explicit type annotation
struct Session {
    let id: Int = 0
    lazy var cache: [String] = []
}
```

Both properties are annotated, so that advice cannot help. Both are rejected because a copy skips them: a `let` with an initial value and a `lazy var`. A property that really lacks an annotation is already reported by its own `missingTypeAnnotation` error, so this diagnostic never fires for one.

The message now reads:

> @Copying requires at least one stored property that 'copying' can replace; computed, 'static', and 'lazy' properties and 'let' constants with an initial value are not copied

## Changes

- `CopyingDiagnostic.noStoredProperties` has the new message. The ID is unchanged.
- The Limitations article links the rule to the list of skipped properties, and the changelog has an entry.

## Test plan

- [x] Updated the two existing expansion tests, for an empty type and a type with only static or computed members.
- [x] New expansion test for a type whose only stored properties are a `let` with an initial value and a `lazy var`.
- [x] `swift test` and `swift format lint --strict` pass locally.

author: kaishi00
body:
Carries malaiwah's #1242 with main merged in, plus the last round of review fixes. This merges with a merge commit, so #1242 shows as merged.

## Carry fixes
- Signing out of or removing the open dashboard now runs `forgetPredictiveState()`. It cancels the pause and follow-up waits and resets every predictive field, the store's draft included. Before, cleanup ran only when everything was wiped.
- A `.queued` follow-up keeps "Hermes followed up" and its push hold. Only `.steered` and `.redirected` drop them.
- Answers asked before the cleanup are dropped (`predictiveGeneration`), and the hidden turn's send keeps nothing once it runs. Delete Saved Chats leaves predictions be, as it leaves the chat in use.
- The sidebar, a room or Conduit in the background drop a follow-up's tag and hold, as leaving for another chat does, and a paused draft or a hidden turn isn't sent once the chat is covered.
- A follow-up queued behind another client's turn tags its own reply, not that turn's.
- The plugin needed is 0.80 (0.79.0 went to Linked Rooms' room rules).
- `Predictive.date(fromTimestamp:)` uses the chat's own `MessageTimestampFormatter.date(from:)`, so epoch timestamps are read too.

## Summary

Settings > Chat > Predictive: three switches, all off by default and kept on the device. They need the plugin's new `predict` capability (plugin 0.80, kaishi00/hermes-conduit-notifier#363, carried in kaishi00/hermes-conduit-notifier#382). Without it, the page says so and nothing is asked.

- **Suggested replies.** After a reply, the messages the user will most likely send next (1, 3 or 5, best first) show as chips above the composer. Tap sends; touch and hold puts the text in the composer to edit. Each reply is asked about once.
- **While I pause.** When the user stops typing (0.8 to 5 s, default 1.2 s), dashed chips offer the next words of the draft (tap inserts them, and they follow the draft as it's typed), plus whole messages the draft might become. Typing folds the row behind a ✦ button instead of making it vanish.
- **Hermes follows up.** While a chat is on screen, Hermes is waiting and the user isn't writing, Conduit asks, from 1 min (configurable), whether Hermes has something useful to add. It sends the durations it measured (since the reply, on screen, local time, check N of 4), so the model does no arithmetic. Hermes answers either take a turn, or ask again in 30 s to 15 min, or never. A turn is a hidden `prompt.submit` (`display_kind: "hidden"`) carrying the why, with `[SILENT]` as the way out. There's at most one per message the user sends, and its reply is tagged "Hermes followed up" (tap shows why).
- Model: the host's fast model (`auxiliary.conduit_predict`) or the chat's own.

Predictions go to the plugin's quiet `/predict` route, not `prompt.btw`. They run on a tool-less fork that saves nothing, and they aren't broadcast, so Hermes Desktop shows no `[btw]` notes.

## Siblings

FEATURE_MAP: new entry "Predictions".

- Notifier `/predict` route, README and CHANGELOG: done in kaishi00/hermes-conduit-notifier#363.
- Settings captions and the 33 new strings in all 14 languages: done.
- The reply push hold (AppState+ChatOnScreen): done. A follow-up turn while the chat is watched is held like an engaged one, and the Notifications entry's ruling says so.
- Group rooms, Apple Watch: gaps left open in the entry.
- Voice modes, CarPlay: not needed. There's no composer to suggest into, and the entry rules them out by design.
- Step summaries still ask over `prompt.btw`; moving them to `/predict`'s quiet path is a gap left open.
- The "Hermes followed up" tag lives in memory only; it's gone after a relaunch (gap).
- Chats, project chats and Bot Chat: done, one row above the composer in each.
- Hermes Desktop and the TUI on the same chat: not needed. The guesses come from a fork answered only to the asking device, and the hidden turn is marked so other clients don't show its prompt.
- The composer's draft and Send: done. A guess sends, edits or inserts through the composer's own request.

## Testing

- ConduitTests/ChatTypographyTests+Predictive.swift: defaults, request bodies, ranking, the turn-answer clamp, continuation remainders, local time, the row's fold and unfold, and the tap guard.
- Fork CI (macOS build, tests and smoke) is green.
- `check-feature-map.py`, `check-l10n-coverage.py`, `plan-tests.py validate` and the scripts tests pass.
- testSigningOutForgetsWhatPredictiveKnewOfTheChats covers the sign-out cleanup.

_Requested by **Steven**_

Part of the Mage skill effect audit. **Builds on #132 (Cold Bolt) and #122**; merge those first.

## What changes
How the official client (kRO 2020-12-29) shows Fire Bolt (MG_FIREBOLT, skill 19). It is the Cold Bolt effect with a fire look:
- As the damage packet arrives: effect 31 on the target with the hit count n, 160 ticks.
  - Tick 12: one `EF_FireArrow1-3.wav`, picked at random.
  - One fire bolt on tick 12, then every 10 ticks, n in all, dropping from the upper right like Cold Bolt's. Two crossed quads 28 x 7 units, animated through `불화살1-6.tga`, one frame a tick. Each sticks in the ground, then fades.
  - Each landing opens a `ring_yellow.tga` ring at the feet (same numbers as Cold Bolt's ring).
  - Every 4 ticks a `particle4` spark leaves the newest bolt (where it flies or where it stuck) and flies back up its line, 20 degrees either side and 10 up or down, at 0.6-1.5 units a tick slowing to a third, for 6-29 ticks, shrinking from scale 0.2-0.49 to nothing.
- When the damage lands: 49 (fire hit) once per packet.

roBrowser played `ef_firebolt` once per hit, each a straight drop with its own sound, then 49 once per hit (ten fire hits at level 10).

How: `BoltRainSim.planSparks` plans the sparks; `BoltRain` hands each to a callback on its tick, and effect 31 spawns it as a `3D` sprite effect (straight-line flight; the client's slowing is folded into the end point). Row `{ damageEffectIdOnTarget: 31, hitEffectId: 49, hitEffectOnce: true }`.

Not covered: the client also sheds two sparks at the feet before the first bolt (ticks 4 and 8, aimed nowhere in particular); left out.

Spec: `effect-port/bolts.md`. Preview (software render, 5 bolts, sparks as dots): `effect-port/fire-bolt-preview.png`.

## Checks
- `npx vitest run`: all pass (`tests/renderer/BoltRainSim.test.js` extended)
- eslint clean, prettier clean on the new files, `npm run build:online` ok

author: dnslin
body:
关联任务：修复PR #301合并后main的CI阻塞；main全绿后继续清理PR #301分支/worktree并同步主仓库，保留其他未提交改动，不发布部署。

## 问题与最终行为

本PR修正两处隔离回归的夹具/就绪判定问题，**没有修改生产健康接口、S3交付、统计、调度、依赖或CI配置**。

1. **健康启动就绪。** Next16.4.1先输出Ready，再加载请求处理器。旧健康测试把提前的日志当成真实就绪，使后续2秒请求承担了初始化时间。现于原15000ms启动预算内观察真实200/no-store/精确JSON，随后继续全部原检查；Ready日志仍断言。
2. **S3已发布资产夹具。** 夹具实际上传文件但未记录内容摘要，被后台识别成待回填旧资产；合法后台GET干扰了交付测试“签名不产生远端预检”的全局请求数。现填入实际上传Buffer计算的SHA-256，符合正常上传元数据。另用明确的未摘要旧资产/等待回填重试状态验证相同交付合同，不关闭后台功能或改变产品行为。

## 未放宽的要求

- 原启动等待仍15000ms，未串联额外启动预算。
- `requestHealth`原样保留：2000ms同时覆盖响应头和完整正文；原有两次正常请求继续执行。
- 原健康用例30000ms总期限、200/no-store/精确JSON、全部表/default/empty数据、产物隔离、无外部连接观察、关库/卡头/卡正文、IPC/SIGTERM/秘密不外泄断言全部保留。
- S3原request helper及四个原交付用例逐字保留，精确远端请求数、权限、统计和请求期限没有改动或过滤。
- 没有skip、全局回填开关或用例重跑规则变化。历史摘要回填测试完整执行。

## 失败先行与回归

- 真实子进程router延迟2500ms：原4项过/新增用例TimeoutError；修复后健康5项全过。临时注入有checkpoint，保留no-strip-types与入口前安装的网络观察器，不替换真实响应。
- 原S3夹具：新回归稳定收到null，而非实际字节SHA；修复后严格摘要一致且默认不制造回填任务。
- 明确旧资产：摘要null、真实后台任务等待重试，仍要求302/签名前零额外远端请求/摘要保持null/签名返回真实字节。该数据状态用于分开后台与交付测量，不增加测试期限。

## 实际本地验证

| 命令 | 结果 |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm exec vitest run --project integration tests/integration/runtime/health.test.ts --maxWorkers=1` | RED 1失败/4通过；GREEN 5通过 |
| health、logging、secret-preflight、standalone定向，`--maxWorkers=2` | 4文件26项通过 |
| `pnpm exec vitest run --project integration tests/integration/delivery/s3.test.ts tests/integration/delivery/s3-fixture-cancel.test.ts tests/integration/delivery/s3-races.test.ts tests/integration/media/fingerprints.test.ts --maxWorkers=2` | 4文件40项通过 |

author: garyjob
body:
## Why

On 2026-10-26 I filed a CONTRIBUTION EVENT, then swept all 38 tabs of the Main Ledger looking for it, found nothing, and wrongly reported that the contribution had "not reached the ledger" — implying a pipeline failure. It was working exactly as designed: submissions land in a staging sheet first and only reach `Ledger history` at the quarterly consolidation. This PR writes the pipeline down so no agent repeats that false alarm.

Verified against live sheets on 2026-10-26.

## What's added

`CONTRIBUTION_LEDGER_PIPELINE.md` — the three stages, sheet/tab IDs, the column-L foreign key, service-account permissions, and the explicit rule that absence from `Ledger history` is expected for up to a quarter.

## No code changes

Docs only.

body:
## Ce que ça change

Une nouvelle rubrique **Tableau de bord** (`#/accueil`, `admin/tableau.js`) ouvre l'administration : un hub sur ce qui presse et ce qui vient, chaque ligne menant au geste en un clic (la fiche s'ouvre sur le champ à remplir, `data-viser`).

**Les tuiles**
- **Actions rapides** : nouvelle date, proposer des dates, nouvelle fiche, nouveau lieu, séance d'atelier, inviter une salle, opportunité de diffusion, tableur, modifier sur le site, rechercher… (on choisit lesquelles).
- **À traiter** : demandes de devis à répondre, relances de diffusion en retard, notes de frais à valider, options à confirmer, dates sans horaire, contrats à suivre, feuilles de route à publier, propositions de dates en attente, invitations pro qui échoient, portraits sans accord (au choix).
- **À compléter avant la tournée** (le même compte que le bloc de Représentations), **Prochaines dates**, **La saison en chiffres** (à côté de la saison d'avant), **Qui part bientôt** (téléphone à appeler d'un geste), **Diffusion** (pipeline, montants, devis, alertes), **Propositions de dates**, **Séances d'atelier à venir**, **Dernières modifications** (chacune vers sa fiche), **Spectacles** et **Mémo** (masqués d'office).
- Une tuile dont la base n'a pas les tables (scripts 3, 4, 5, 7) ne se montre pas.

**Entièrement personnalisable** (« Personnaliser ») : l'ordre (glisser-déposer par le titre, ou ← →), la largeur (1, 2 colonnes ou toute la largeur), masquer / remettre, réduire, les réglages de chaque tuile (période, nombre de lignes, ce qu'elle suit), les colonnes de la grille, la page d'ouverture (tableau de bord ou Représentations), réinitialiser. Gardé avec le compte (`crescite_preferences`, clé `accueil.tableau`) ; sans le script 6, sur l'appareil, puis repris dans la base.

Le temps réel redessine les tuiles ; le journal se relit (au plus toutes les 5 s). Fait pour l'écran d'ordinateur (3 ou 4 colonnes), une colonne au téléphone, clair et sombre.

**Branchement** : rubrique et route dans `admin/index.html` (douze rubriques dans l'en-tête, CSS ajusté), la marque mène au tableau de bord, `build.py` copie `tableau.js`, `docs/admin/` publié, README et commentaire du script 6.

## Vérification

`node maquettes/tableau.mjs` : Chromium hors ligne, REST Supabase simulé sur une base fictive, 60 vérifications (les tuiles et leurs comptes, les liens visés, la personnalisation et sa persistance dans `crescite_preferences`, le repli sur l'appareil sans le script 6, le téléphone, le sombre) — toutes passent ; captures dans `maquettes/dist/shots-tableau/`.

Aucun script SQL à lancer : la clé `accueil.tableau` s'ajoute dans la table des préférences existante.
