author: astrogilda
body:
This adds a definition of an independent run to SHARED-DECISIONS.md. It applies to the 48-hour tier that covers verified progress and standing changes.

This lets a standing change rest on reproducible evidence that anyone can check from a public run record. A project other than the claim's owner runs the check, and whoever runs it wrote neither the fixtures nor the verifier. Any pinned verifier qualifies, the owner's included, and the run record says whether it was written without reading the owner's implementation.

The authorship rule is the one proposed for independent records in the boundary map, open as #179. It replaces closed #208 and carries both edits @aeoess asked for there.

author: dweej-patel
body:
Follow-up to #25, which didn't fix the case it described. Six review rounds shaped this; the history is in the commits.

## Bugs
1. **Squished terminal in a new tab.** Starting a full-screen program (e.g. `claude`) in a new tab squished its input box onto one line until you left the tab and came back. The phone sends `open` with the first layout's grid, then the keyboard comes up and shrinks it. That resize never reached the new session:
   - the screens dropped resizes while no session was active;
   - with another tab open, the resize went to the old session, and the Mac refused it, showing an error banner on a working tab.
2. **Switching tabs while a new one opens** (predates #25). The phone sent `open`, then `attach A`. The Mac opened B, attached it, then attached A, but `opened` made B current on the phone and switched the screen to it. Typing then went to a session the Mac had left (refused, error banner), and A's output went unshown.
3. **A new tab asked for while connecting** (most "New shell" buttons allow this). The queued `open` was overtaken by the reattach of the old tab on ready.

## Fix
- **Mac `resize`:** applies to whatever session the connection has attached when the line is read. Lines are handled in order and wait behind an `open`, so a resize sent before `opened` sizes the new session, including after several opens or an unrelated refusal. With nothing attached it's ignored, not refused. A `session` it names is ignored; phones still send it for older Macs.
- **`open` / `ref`:** an `open` carries a `ref` that the Mac echoes in `opened` or in the error refusing it, and every `open` is now answered (including while the listener stops). An `attach` sent while opens are unanswered marks them overtaken. Their sessions join the tabs while the screen and typing stay on the attached tab (`openedDetached` / `OpenedDetached`). Both clients decide this as `opened` reaches the app, in order with its own `attach` calls: on the iPhone client's delivery queue, and in Android's `events` flow as the app collects it. It's never decided on the network queue, where an answer could be judged before an attach the app had already made. One number per client tracks it, so a missing or untagged answer affects only its own open. A refused open is its own event (`.openFailed` / `Failed` with `ref`). Each client also says whether an open is still pending. A new session that ends or is taken over before its `opened` reaches the app leaves nothing current, so typing goes nowhere. Keys typed while an open is pending are dropped; the Mac would refuse them for the old tab. A refused open leaves the old tab current.
- **Models** (`ShellModel`, `ShellViewModel`): a new session asked for while connecting, or while waiting to redial, is opened on ready. The active tab is re-attached only if that open is refused and no other open is pending, so neither the old shell nor the new one gets the other's keystrokes. The request is dropped in any state but connecting and ready (unreachable, locked, another Mac…), or when a tab is chosen.
- **Android rotation:** a rebuilt terminal doesn't re-attach (which would overtake the open) while a new tab is opening; it re-attaches once, and only if that open is refused. On both phones, a refused open is no longer mistaken for "timeline unsupported".
- **Phone clients:** `resize` isn't sent before ready (`attach` carries the size). Both screens pass resizes on even with no session active or an ended tab shown; every tab shows in the one view, at its size.
- #25's resends are removed. `protocol/README.md` is updated.

## Testing
- `ShellListenerTests`, over the wire against the real listener with `stty size`:
  - a resize while opening reaches the new session;
  - with a tab already attached, no refusal;
  - after two quick opens, it reaches the last;
  - with an unrelated refusal first, it still reaches the new session;
  - with nothing attached, it's ignored;
  - attaching before `opened` gives `openedDetached`, and typing reaches the attached tab;
  - an attach made before `opened` is delivered to the app still overtakes it. The test is deterministic: a test hook confirms the client has read `opened` while delivery is held back;
  - a new session that ends before its `opened` is delivered takes no input;
  - keys typed while an open is pending are dropped, not refused for the old tab;
  - a refused `open` (session limit) doesn't make a later one look overtaken.

  The new-behaviour tests fail with their part of the fix removed.
- Android `ShellConnectionTests`, against the fake Mac: resize waits for ready and goes out while an open is unanswered; an attach before `opened`, or before it's delivered, leaves the new session detached (deterministic: a ping/pong proves the client read `opened` while the collector is held); a session ended before delivery takes no input; typing while an open is pending is dropped; a refused open is answered; `openPending` follows the delivered answers. These tests hold the app's collector, so they're deterministic.
- Neither phone has view-model tests, so the reconnect and rotation changes are covered by builds and code reading only.
- Full `swift test` passes. The iPhone and Mac apps build. Android is covered by CI.
- Not yet tried on a device.

## Compatibility
Update the Mac and phones together. A new phone with an old Mac behaves as before this PR: no `ref` echoed, so nothing is marked overtaken, and resizes still name a session. An old phone works with a new Mac.

author: awaliuddin
body:
Built from `feat/claim-meter` (0886cd9, never merged). `origin/main` is merged in; conflicts in `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/INTEGRATION.md` and `routes/report.ts` were resolved keeping main's behaviour. The branch was then reshaped to the agreed contract.

**Nothing changes in production when this merges.** The meter is off unless `FAULTLINE_CLAIM_METER=1` is set. With it on, only keys that have `metered: true` are metered. Admin keys, the server key and every existing key behave exactly as on main.

## What changed against main

- **Billable unit.** One claim that got a provider verdict, `unverified` included. The rule comes from the engine's `isBillableVerdict` (`packages/cli/lib/verdict-guard.ts`); the API's own copy is deleted.
- **Usage record** (`packages/api/src/store/claim-meter.ts`). An append-only `claim-meter.jsonl` on the ledger volume, rebuilt from the file at start like `provider-spend.ts`. The first line is a header holding `ledgerId`, written with the first row. Reads never create the file.
- **Seq without gaps.** Assigning `seq`, writing the line and indexing the row happen in one synchronous section (`appendRow`) with no await in between. That section is the lock: no other commit can run inside it, so `seq` is never reused and readers see rows in order. A row whose write fails gets no `seq`. It still counts against the cap in this process and shows as `claimMeter.ledgerWriteFailures`.
- **The read.** New `GET /admin/usage-records` (`routes/usage-records.ts`).
- **Key fields.** Keys gain `metered` and `scopes` (`usage:read`, `keys:write`) next to `claimCap` and `stripeCustomerId`. There are new helpers `hasScope` and `requireScope(name)`; admin keys pass every scope.
- **Idempotency.** `POST /keys` accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header:
  - First call: 201 with the plaintext key.
  - Replay with the same value: 200, the same `id`, and `key: null`.
  - Empty or longer than 200 characters: 400.
  - `POST /keys/:id/rotate` still issues a fresh plaintext key.
- **402 bodies.**
  - `claim_cap_reached` now also carries `period` and `resetsAt`.
  - A metered key with no `claimCap` gets `402 {"error":"claim_cap_unset"}`. The `FAULTLINE_DEFAULT_CLAIM_CAP` fallback is gone, as are the suite-wide env defaults in `vitest.config.ts`, which is back to main's.
- **Revocation.** A disabled, expired or deleted metered key makes no new reservation. Work it queued earlier fails with `key_revoked` and calls no provider. Deleted metered keys are remembered in memory, like the keystore itself. Rows already committed stay.
- **Voids** for full-scan jobs (details below).
- **Stripe sender removed.** Deleted: `store/claim-meter-sync.ts`, its sync ledger, `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` / `FAULTLINE_STRIPE_METER_EVENT` / `FAULTLINE_CLAIM_METER_SYNC_LEDGER`, its tests, `meterSyncLagRows` and the other `sync` fields, and the doc text about it. This API makes no Stripe call.
- **Docs.** Updated `docs/INTEGRATION.md` §1, `packages/api/docs/openapi.yaml`, the claim-meter section of the operating runbook, and one `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` line.

## Route coverage

I found every caller of the engine's verify path by grepping `packages/api/src` for `scan(` / `verifyClaim`. `tests/claim-meter-route-table.test.ts` also finds the verifying routes by behaviour, and has a red-control route that bypasses the meter to prove it can catch one. It now also asserts that every verifying route wrote rows and that no row was refused for a malformed scanId.

| Caller | Coverage |
|---|---|
| `POST /scan`, `POST /scan/template/:id` | `reserveClaims(planVerifyCap)` before any provider call, `commitClaims` on delivery, cached hits included |
| `GET` and `POST /scan/stream` | Reserve before the stream opens; each verdict commits as it is sent; release in `finally` |
| `POST /scan/deep`, `/scan/upload`, `/scan/report`, `/scan/eu-report`, `/scan/compliance/:template`, `/scan/compliance-gate` | Reserve at the engine cap (8), commit on delivery |
| `POST /scan/batch` | Reserve 8 per text |
| `POST /scan/diff` | Reserve 16; the two scans commit under two new UUIDs (the response has no scanId) |
| `POST /scan/full/estimate` | Extracts only, verifies nothing, reserves nothing (asserted) |
| `POST /scan/full` (the job) | Reserves the estimate's `factClaims`; served claims commit when the job ends |
| `POST /jobs`, `/queue/scans`, `/schedules`, `/schedules/:id/trigger`, `/scan/bulk` | Headroom check at submit; each run reserves again through `meteredScan` when it runs |
| `POST /admin/verify-claims`, GraphQL `scan` / `scanBatch` | Admin only, so not metered by rule (GraphQL is also off unless `FAULTLINE_GRAPHQL=on`) |

Every error path releases its reservation in the server's `onResponse` hook. `tests/claim-meter-abort.test.ts` shows that on Fastify 5.12.5 this hook also runs when the client disconnects mid-scan; without the release that test goes red.

## The row

```
{ seq, ts, period, kind: 'usage'|'void', keyId, stripeCustomerId: string|null,
  scanId, claimId, verdict: 'supported'|'contradicted'|'mixed'|'unverified',
  provider, identifier, voids? }
```

- **identifier.** For usage rows it is `scanId:claimId`, at most 36 + 1 + 58 = 95 characters. A claimId over 58 characters is not recorded; the count is logged (never the value) and shown as `claimMeter.refusedIdentifiers`. The 58 was not lowered. For void rows it is `void:` + the usage identifier, so at most 100 characters.
- **scanId.** Main issues scan ids as `scan-<uuid>`, not bare UUIDs, so rows carry the bare UUID. A full-scan job id `fsj_<time>_<32 hex>` becomes those 32 hex characters as a UUID, which lets the void path find a job's rows from its id after a restart. Anything that is not a UUID is refused at commit.
- **stripeCustomerId.** Read from the key at commit time; rebinding the key never moves past rows. A void row copies the customer from the usage row it cancels.
- **period.** The UTC month of `ts`. `used` counts usage rows minus their void rows, and a void subtracts from the month of the row it cancels.
- **Duplicates.** A duplicate identifier is written once and counted once, also across a restart.
- **Contents.** No claim text, evidence or key material.

## The read

`GET /admin/usage-records?after=<seq>&limit=<1..1000>` (default `after=0`, `limit=500`)

- Answers `{ ledgerId, records, nextAfter, hasMore }` in seq order, with header `X-Usage-Record-Version: 1`.
- Needs scope `usage:read`. The route is declared `access: 'key'` rather than `'admin'` so that a non-admin key holding the scope gets through. Without the scope: `403 {"error":"scope_required","scope":"usage:read"}`.
- Read only. It also works with the switch off. Before the first row it answers `ledgerId: null` and creates no file.
- Admin `GET /usage` adds `usageRecords { ledgerId, lastSeq, rowsThisPeriod }` plus `claimMeter` fleet totals. Both appear for admin even with the switch off; these are the only additive changes visible when the meter is off.

## Voids

- **Served mark.** The first GET of `/scan/full/:jobId` that returns served verdicts to the owner marks the job served. The ledger is append-only, so this appends a copy of the job's terminal row with `resultServedAt`; on reload the last row for a job wins, so the refund report is not double counted. The mark is written only for metered jobs, so unmetered full-scan ledgers stay identical to main (main's `full-scan-routes.test.ts` pins this).
- **When voids are written.** When the owner later gets `resultAvailable: false`, or `404 job_lost`, for a job that was never served, every usage row that key committed for the job gets a void row. This happens once, deduplicated by void identifier. Served results are never voided, and other keys reading the id void nothing.
- **job_lost.** Commits happen when a job ends, so `job_lost` only has rows to void when the job's terminal row never reached the disk. That is the same case the web app already refunds in full.

- **Idempotency map storage.** The ke

author: dbtsai
body:
### What changes were proposed in this pull request?

Share immutable logical-plan and expression nodes instead of recursively cloning
their ancestors while building DataFrames and Columns.

- Store DataFrame roots and logical-plan child edges as `Arc<LogicalPlan>`.
- Make `Expression` an immutable shared handle around `ExpressionNode`.
  Common builders use `Expression::literal`, `Expression::column`, and
  `Expression::function`; other nodes use the `From<ExpressionNode>` conversion.
- Remove redundant boxes around expression handles in `DirectShufflePartitionId`
  and `CaseWhen::else_expr`.
- Preserve structural equality (including NaN), Debug/render output, protobuf
  output, argument order, and execution-time plan-ID assignment.
- Keep focused sharing, branch-immutability, serialization, and self-join plan-ID
  tests. Add a Rust API migration note in `docs/compatibility.md`.

CI follow-ups type-check documentation snippets without linking an executable per
block, constrain Spark 4.2 tests and workers to pandas 2.x, and retain per-file
pytest diagnostics. Benchmark code lives in
[pyspark-connect-benchmark](https://github.com/dbtsai/pyspark-connect-benchmark).

### Why are the changes needed?

Extending and reusing a plan or expression currently copies existing subtrees.
Sharing immutable nodes avoids that repeated work. Expression and Column clones
become O(1) with respect to subtree size.

Fresh benchmark rerun on 2026-10-27 UTC, after the review cleanups, using
separately built release wheels from base `c41ff82` and PR head `ff6fddd3`.
The separate
[pyspark-connect-benchmark](https://github.com/dbtsai/pyspark-connect-benchmark)
harness is pinned to
[1bbdec9](https://github.com/dbtsai/pyspark-connect-benchmark/tree/1bbdec9f3665fcd2ec2ee5129bbcdb95ee4b00c4).
These results supersede the earlier measurements of `b45e5d6`; old samples are
not pooled with this rerun.

The breadth stage covered 39 cases with six attempts per client/case. A separate
confirmation stage repeated eight selected cases with 18 attempts per client/case.
Each stage used two rounds with the Rust baseline/candidate execution slots
swapped. The tables compare the two Rust builds, not Rust against official Python.

Confirmation wall-time medians (18 samples per Rust version):

| Case | Before | After | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `chain-withColumn-256` | 7.969 ms | 0.326 ms | 24.46x faster |
| `linear-expression-64` | 0.664 ms | 0.084 ms | 7.95x faster |
| `increment-filter-depth256` | 40.728 us | 0.241 us | 168.97x faster |
| `core-outbound-rpc-expression-10` | 15.044 ms | 10.149 ms | 32.5% less time |
| `core-outbound-rpc-deep-10` | 5.557 ms | 5.372 ms | 3.3% less time |
| `core-outbound-rpc-deep-100` | 6.329 ms | 5.614 ms | 11.3% less time |
| `core-outbound-rpc-expression-5` | 6.488 ms | 6.480 ms | About unchanged |
| `prebuilt-schema-depth256` | 2.826 ms | 2.857 ms | 1.1% more time |

The earlier 15.3% wall-time slowdown in `core-outbound-rpc-deep-10` was not
reproduced: both confirmation rounds favor the PR, but their ranges overlap
widely, so this is not evidence of a statistically significant speedup.
The schema-depth256 timing remains mixed (-0.9% and +2.2% across rounds), rather
than a convincing timing regression. Expression-5 outbound also reverses
direction between rounds. These are not direct old-head/current-head comparisons,
so differences from the earlier run cannot be attributed solely to review cleanups.

Two cold-construction slowdown signals remain in the breadth stage:

| Case | Before | After | Wall-time change | CPU-time change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `core-construct-deep-10` | 5.189 ms | 6.048 ms | +16.6% | About unchanged |
| `core-construct-expression-5` | 4.987 ms | 6.220 ms | +24.7% | +7.2% |

Both have higher wall-time medians in both breadth rounds. Each has only six
samples per Rust version and overlapping ranges; neither was included in the
confirmation stage. They need targeted confirmation, and should not be dismissed
as noise or interpreted as established regressions.

Memory measurements (before -> after, MiB):

| Case / stage | Absolute sampled peak RSS | Additional peak RSS |
|---|---:|---:|
| `core-construct-expression-10` / breadth | 105.148 -> 101.242 | 5.039 -> 1.289 (-74.4%) |
| `core-outbound-rpc-expression-10` / confirmation | 116.609 -> 112.695 | 14.219 -> 10.164 (-28.5%) |
| `prebuilt-schema-depth256` / confirmation | 104.727 -> 104.258 | 1.688 -> 2.031 (+352 KiB) |

Additional peak RSS is the median of each sample's sampled peak minus its own
post-setup baseline, not the difference of two medians or total process memory.
Memory improvement is not universal: the schema case uses more incremental RSS
despite its slightly lower absolute process peak. RSS sampling targets 2 ms and
can miss short spikes; zero observed growth does not mean zero allocation.

These are client-side measurements against canned localhost gRPC responses on
an Apple M3 Max (64 GiB), macOS arm64, Python 3.12.14 and Rust 1.99.1, using
identical release build settings and dependencies for the two Rust versions.
Core one-shot cases include imports/first-use work inside timing; outbound cases
also include plan construction, encoding, transport, and response handling.
Matched warmups and RPC counters were checked for all Rust pairs, and source,
wheel, native-extension, dependency, and harness identities were audited.

Results measure plan and expression sharing together, not either Arrow-handoff
experiment or isolated protobuf encoding. They do not establish real-server
performance, statistical significance for small changes, API parity, or universal
gains. Breadth and confirmation samples are reported separately. Raw reports have
not been published in the harness repository.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

Yes, for direct Rust users of the public representation:

- `Expression` becomes a shared handle; its enum variants move to
  `ExpressionNode`. Construct nodes using the common constructors or `.into()`,
  and match through `expression.node()`.
- `LogicalPlan` child fields change from `Box<LogicalPlan>` to
  `Arc<LogicalPlan>`. Plan helpers accept owned/shared nodes through
  `Into<Arc<LogicalPlan>>`.
- `DirectShufflePartitionId` takes `Expression` and `CaseWhen::else_expr` takes
  `Option<Expression>`.

The 4.3 migration note in `docs/compatibility.md` includes a construction and
matching example. Ordinary Column, DataFrame, and Python APIs are unchanged.
The wire protocol is unchanged: serialization still expands shared occurrences
into independent protobuf trees. Recursive serialization/destruction limits
remain, and flat CASE/window containers can still copy collections of handles.

### How was this patch tested?

Benchmark rerun at `ff6fddd3`:

- 1,134 fresh measured attempts: 1,122 passed and 12 failed.
- All 756 Rust samples passed. The 12 failures were exclusively the official
  PySpark 4.2.0 reference's known `Exceeded upb_DecodeOptions_MaxDepth` failures
  in `plan-expression-32-schema-first` and `plan-expression-32-collect-empty`.
  The benchmark launcher retained exit status 1; the full run is not reported
  as green.
- All 11 harness unit tests and all nine pilot attempts passed. Pilot samples
  are excluded from the measured results.
- Warmup/RPC matching, execution-order balance, and provenance audits passed.
  No additional live-server or official parity suite was run for this benchmark.

After the review cleanup:

- 424 Rust tests passed: 368 core unit tests and 56 selected integration/golden
  tests, including seven expression-sharing tests. The selected golden target
  also reports 12 explicitly ignored tests; these are not counted as passes.
- All core integration-test targets compiled, with and without `wasm-udf`.
- The native Python extension built in release mode. A before/after snapshot of
  its 108 exported classes showed no changed members or text signatures.
- All 52 Rust documentation snippets type-che

author: sramireddy2
body:
Fixes #310.

### Problem
Two refactors in 2022 renamed parameters stored in checkpoints, so checkpoints saved before them (including pretrained models linked from the docs) fail to load with "Missing key(s) / Unexpected key(s)":

| Change | Old key | New key | Example model that breaks |
|---|---|---|---|
| 521b7edc ("V75"): `ConvEncoderImpl.fc_layers` → `mlp_layers` | `…enc.fc_layers.0.weight` | `…enc.mlp_layers.0.weight` | `andrewzhang505/sample-factory-2-doom-battle` (this issue) |
| #198 (`MultiInputEncoder`) | `encoder.mlp_head.0.weight` | `encoder.encoders.obs.mlp_head.0.weight` | `andrewzhang505/sample-factory-2-mujoco-ant` |

### Fix
`upgrade_legacy_state_dict()` in `sample_factory/model/model_utils.py`, called from `enjoy.load_state_dict()` and `Learner._load_state()`, so both evaluation and resuming training work.

A key is renamed only if the model doesn't expect the old name, does expect the new one, and the checkpoint doesn't already contain it. As a result:
- up-to-date checkpoints are returned unchanged (the same object);
- a custom model that legitimately has an `fc_layers` layer isn't affected;
- real mismatches are still reported by the strict `load_state_dict()`.

A warning is logged when something is renamed. The optimizer state needs no change, since it's stored by parameter position.

### Tests
New `tests/algo/test_legacy_checkpoints.py`:
- old-style checkpoints load through `enjoy.load_state_dict` with identical weights, for `fc_layers` (conv), the pre-#198 prefix (mlp), and both renames combined;
- `Learner` resumes training from an old-style checkpoint (MuJoCo, skipped if unavailable);
- controls: current checkpoints still load, and an unrelated unexpected key still raises.

The legacy cases fail on master with the same error as the issue and pass with this change.

Full suite (Linux, CPU): 153 passed / 9 failed with the change, vs 149 / 13 on master. The 4 newly passing tests are the new ones. The remaining 9 failures and 1 collection error are identical on master and come from optional packages I don't have installed locally (`onnxscript`, `pettingzoo`). `black`, `isort` and `flake8` pass.

### Checked with the real HF checkpoints
| Model | master | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `sample-factory-2-doom-battle` | RuntimeError | all keys match (2 renamed) |
| `sample-factory-2-mujoco-ant` | RuntimeError | all keys match (4 renamed) |
| `doom_deathmatch_bots` (already current) | loads | unchanged |

For `doom-battle` I also checked that the saved optimizer state lines up with the current model (same 20 parameters, same order and shapes), so resuming training from it works too.

### Not covered
Old `cfg.json` files use settings that were later replaced (`encoder_extra_fc_layers`, `hidden_size`, …). They're still ignored. For the models above, today's defaults give the same layer sizes, but an older model with non-default sizes would report a size mismatch. Happy to look at that separately if useful.

I used Claude (an AI assistant) to help investigate and draft this. I reviewed every change and ran all the tests and checks myself.

author: pangjiping
body:
## Summary

Deserializer failures in the Kotlin SDK could silently lose the server's actual response, leaving nothing to diagnose the real error with. Two gaps:

1. **LinkageError escaped every handler.** A kotlinx-serialization serializer/runtime version mismatch surfaces as `AbstractMethodError` at decode time. It is an `Error`, not an `Exception`, so plain `catch (e: Exception)` blocks never saw it: SSE event decoding dropped every event (silent stream death), and JSON response decoding escaped without any response context.
2. **Response body discarded on decode failure.** Handwritten adapter decode paths read the body and passed it straight to the decoder; when decoding threw, the body was gone.

### Changes

- `ExecdEventSupport.decodeEventLine` now catches `LinkageError` separately: the raw SSE line is reported through `onError` (adapters already log it at ERROR) and then **rethrown** — a systemic incompatibility affects every event, so skipping them all would turn the failure into a silent stream death. Regular `Exception`s keep the existing log-and-skip behavior.
- New shared helper `Json.decodeResponseBody(serializer, payload, operation)` wraps both `Exception` and `LinkageError` decode failures into `SandboxInternalException` whose message keeps the raw body (truncated to 2048 chars) with the original error as cause.
- All 8 handwritten response decode paths switched to the helper: 7 in `IsolatedSessionsAdapter`, 1 in `SandboxesAdapter` (patch sandbox metadata).
- `onError` callback widened to `Throwable` (`ExecdEventSupport` is documented as not part of the stable public API).

### Motivation

In production, an execd error response carrying `ErrorData` triggered `AbstractMethodError` during deserialization; the original error body was unrecoverable and the session died silently. This change guarantees that even if a serializer incompatibility reappears, the raw server payload is logged and surfaced for diagnosis. The root cause (serializer/runtime version alignment) is handled separately by upgrading to a compatible serialization stack.

### Tests

- `ExecdEventSupportTest`: LinkageError is reported with the raw line and rethrown
- `ResponseBodyDecodingTest` (new): well-formed decode passthrough, `Exception` wrapping, `AbstractMethodError` wrapping, oversized payload truncation
- `./gradlew spotlessCheck :sandbox:test :code-interpreter:test`: green (one pre-existing, unrelated `PoolWarmupLoggingTest` failure exists on a clean tree)

author: harmengrossedeters
body:
Follow-up to HarmenGrosseDeters/geometry3Sharp#97, from the final runs of the analysis benchmark (`BENCH_REPAIR=analysis`, 400 Thingi10K meshes: none, meters, geo).

## Meshes far from the origin
**The problem, with geo coordinates (offset 5e6):**
- `DMeshAABBTree3`'s float boxes round by 2⁻²⁴ of the coordinates, which is 0.3 units at 5e6.
- The analysis took twice as long (median 11.1 s vs 5.4 s per mesh, 29 timeouts), and up to 30 % of the NaN pattern differed from the origin.

**The fix:**
- For a mesh more than 10 diagonals from the origin, and when the caller sets no spatial structure, `MeshWallThickness` and `MeshDeviation` now run on a copy moved to the origin. The copy keeps the same IDs (`MeshWallThickness.FarFromOrigin`).
- The certified Hausdorff bound runs on copies of both meshes, moved by the same offset.
- A tree passed by the caller is used as it is.

**After the fix:** ray and inscribed-ball thickness and their NaN shares are identical to the origin on all 400 meshes. There are the same 3 timeouts as at the origin, at about the same time (median 6.2 s vs 5.7 s).

## Review (CLAUDE.md)
The independent review found two stale-cache bugs in this PR. Both are fixed, with tests that fail before the fix:
- `MeshDeviation` used the previous reference after `Reference` or `ReferenceSpatial` changed.
- `MeshWallThickness` keyed its caches by `ShapeTimestamp` only, which two meshes built the same way share.

The robustness findings and nits are fixed too; see the review comment. While checking the geo run, it also turned out that `AnalysisBench` passed its own tree and so bypassed the copy path. The benchmark now lets the library build its trees.

## LO-RANSAC, measured
`LocalOptimization` on vs off over 400 meshes:
- **Time:** about the same median time (−13 % to +7 % per primitive).
- **Quality:** somewhat better models (better / worse by more than 1 % of the points: sphere 32/15, cylinder 46/42, cone 52/44).
- **Rotation:** a rotated input reaches another quality slightly more often (27/29/23 instead of 21/16/16 meshes).
- The 2–3× time against the first version comes from the sample changes.

The code doc and the README now say this; #97's description claimed more stability.

## Benchmark README
Final results of all three runs (none, meters, geo), including the before/after numbers for geo.

Local CI steps of CLAUDE.md: all green.
- geometry3Sharp.Tests 1160 passed
- g3cli.Tests 40 passed
- pack + package smoke test
- net48 build
- all benchmark builds

CI on GitHub: green.

body: Coaches can mark up a play with a red marker, hide the marks while talking to the team, and find the same marks after closing the modal or reloading. ## What changed - **Dibujar** turns the pen on. Strokes are freehand, one red marker width, round caps and joins, and stored in normalized coordinates so they stay aligned when the modal resizes. The overlay matches the rendered video, including letterboxing on a native file. Drawing does not pause playback. With the pen off, clicks pass through to the video controls and existing strokes stay visible. - **Mostrar dibujos / Ocultar dibujos** is a separate eye toggle. Turning the pen on shows the drawings. - **Borrar** clears only the current play, after a short confirm, because the drawing is stored. - Switching plays shows that play's strokes. Coming back shows them again. Nothing is kept in localStorage. ## Who can edit Camila's decision for now: drawings are public. Anyone who can view the team library can read and edit them. The site has no account or edit-permission model. A clip in a library is treated as viewable. `clips.visibility` still only gates the media file, not the drawing. The row is shaped for later per-account ownership. Each drawing has its own `id`, `play_id`, nullable `owner_id` (NULL is the anonymous public drawing), timestamps, and a versioned strokes document. Rows are indexed on `(play_id, owner_id)`, not keyed by play alone. Partial unique indexes keep one public drawing per play and, later, one drawing per account per play. Reads and writes go through `lib/clip-drawings.ts` and `GET`/`PUT /api/clips/[clipId]/drawings/[playOrd]`. `resolveAuthor(request)` returns null. The modal never talks to D1. Version 1 is a single red layer: `{ version: 1, strokes: [{ points: [{ x, y }] }] }` with `x` and `y` in 0–1. A later color or extra layers should bump `version`. This client refuses to rewrite a version it does not understand, so old rows do not need a migration. ## When accounts exist Only `lib/clip-drawings.ts` should change: 1. `resolveAuthor` returns the session account id. 2. `getDrawings` filters to that owner, and can also return drawings explicitly shared with them (owner row first). 3. `saveDrawing` sets `owner_id` from the session and rejects edits from anyone else. No login UI in this change. ## Cloudflare setup Apply migration `migrations/0007_clip_drawings.sql` before relying on saves. Wrangler records it in `d1_migrations`. ```bash pnpm run db:migrate:local # wrangler d1 migrations apply carpeta-de-clips --local pnpm run db:migrate:remote # wrangler d1 migrations apply carpeta-de-clips --remote ``` `db:migrate:remote` needs `wrangler login`. If the site is deployed before the remote migration, the drawings route returns 503 and the pen cannot save. Playback is unchanged. `play_id` is `clip:{clipId}:play:{ord}` (`ord` matches `clip_instances.ord`). A clip with no instances uses ord `0` for the whole file.

body:

body:
Adds a dedicated opt-in sequential critic diagnostic without changing the approved probe, SAC implementation, main configurations or active pilot. The alternative-only runner uses the real training lifecycle and never constructs RunProbes; disabling the alternative delegates the existing entrypoint unchanged.

A starts from the checkpoint's current critic and carries weights across targets1–8; B carries the exact saved fresh initialization through the same sequence; C restarts fresh for each current target. All arms use identical stored targets and phase minibatches, fresh probe AdamW state per phase, and2,000 updates/target. The architecture-specific fresh-derived offset stays frozen. Raw errors, source scores,2,000 minibatch losses, full-pool milestones, hashes and phase receipts are preserved.

### Runner and resume
The runner captures fresh weights immediately before the first SAC update, preserves ordinary actor/environment evaluation and training, and saves complete recovery boundaries before diagnostics. Resume verifies committed phases without refitting. Supported dtype/configuration checks fail closed; source, backend, precision and package versions bind the identity. The legacy combined hooks remain compatibility APIs, not the dedicated pilot path.

Invocation and explicit request schema: `main/docs/sequential_alternative_probe.md`. Alternative arrays/trajectories are local artifacts; ordinary SAC W&B logging is preserved. No automatic alternative artifact publisher is claimed.

### CPU verification
Tested implementation: `545008f4b447bebd6c9b1b9291548b7cfdb751fd`.
Final head: `a6958337f411c30f6ebe1a1b3d5c5a0403287780`; subsequent changes are documentation/receipts only.

- 141 pytest cases pass,0 failures/skips,231 dependency warnings:50 alternative-core,13 runner lifecycle/rejection,6 alternative mutation and72 existing regression cases.
- Complete existing74-case mutation suite passes twice: every mutant detected and every restoration passes; zero unexpected failures.
- All65 CPU simulator restoration cells pass (13 tasks ×five seeds), including exact next-transition/action-RNG restoration.
- Tiny real-critic example and independent reload pass:16 phase receipts/48 arm archives, initial A=B, K1 B=C, cross-checkpoint B/C invariance and target/index/carry hashes. No new fit during independent reload.
- Black, Pyflakes, compileall and diff checks pass. All default experiment/probe/trainer/SAC/pilot source bytes remain unchanged relative to the PR base.

Tiny real-trainer tests cover startup, warmup, two later evaluations, complete state isolation, checkpoint restoration, and interruptions at initial/later phase boundaries. Their final parameters, optimizers, replay, normalizer, counters, RNGs and simulator state match the disabled-probe baseline bit-for-bit (W&B run ID excluded). These are CPU engineering fixtures, not campaign results.

Receipt: `main/diagnostics/sequential_validation_receipt.json`; original49-test receipt retained as `.v1.json`. Exact commands, counts, warnings, source/runtime hashes and evidence checksums are recorded. Evidence bundle SHA256: `e90a5b3471a689ebd7e91d6537b6b7189eded0e81368203817aee84dba43960c`.

### Base and remaining limits
PR17 remains based on draft PR16 at `57d2beb78be7cf0e1145f4a9479082a07924cd16`. Shared main was `087feab341b9be1f377697668f2d1c750ec0467f`. Alternative runtime does not import PR16's pilot adapter/launcher; adjacent PR16 adapter tests are included as regressions. Earlier unmerged trainer/probe/diagnostic dependencies are source-bound in `main/diagnostics/sequential_base_dependencies.json`. Approval to restack that dependency stack onto main remains unverified, so the base/history is preserved.

The existing30-parent proposal and separate five-job engineering smoke remain unapproved/non-executable. Environment eligibility, seed allocation, teacher, bank producer, cadence and resource choices were not adopted or changed. Five jobs cannot establish balanced scaling. GPU/full-size performance, memory/storage, long-horizon qualification and artifact transport remain unqualified. No GPU/Slurm execution, campaign launch, merge or force push occurred.

The sequential extension is a new diagnostic inspired by Lyle2023, not a paper-validated method or proof of plasticity loss. A favorable contrast alone cannot establish the mechanism.

author: paradauxio
body:
## Why

Workstream Q of the Economy Explorer redesign (spec §1.4, §3 rules 5 and 8, §4.3, §13; Tesks PAR-535). This PR fixes the small defects that don't depend on the redesign, makes money arithmetic exact, hardens the shared cache against cold-start stampedes, and removes duplicate per-request access queries. It also publishes two Wave 0 contracts (§13.2): `lib/money.ts` and `lib/pagination/cursor.ts`.

## How

### Exact money (§1.4 item 9, §3 rule 8)
- New `lib/money.ts`. It parses DB decimal strings to integer cents (`bigint`), rounding half away from zero beyond 2 dp. It also provides `add`, `sub`, `sum`, `sumBy`, `negate`, `abs`, `sign`, `compare` and `divRound`, plus `formatMoney` (full or compact K/M/B/T, sign modes, tenant currency from `lib/currency.ts`) and `toDbString`. `toNumber` and `ratio` exist only for chart coordinates and percentages.
- `fmtAmt` and `fmtAmtFull` keep their signatures but now delegate to `formatMoney`. DB strings format exactly; numbers are rounded to the cent first.
- These `parseFloat`/`Number` money sums now use cents:
  - `/government`: Gov treasury
  - `/money-flow`: total, sent, received and net
  - `/me/market`: spent, earned, net, and the item and partner rollups
  - `/market/activity`: volume and average sale
  - `/chestshop/items/[itemKey]`: 30-day volume and average price
  - `/economy/wealth`: average balance
  - `/firms/[firmName]`: accounts total
  - `/admin/firms`: swept total
  - `/accounts/[accountId]`: the balance and in/out chart series (the sum is done in cents; only the finished points become numbers)
- `lib/taxation.ts` used its own `cents()` helper, which mis-parsed negatives with a zero whole part (`"-0.50"` became +50). It now uses `lib/money.ts`.
- `/me/market` CSV and JSON exports now write amounts as decimal strings (`"12.50"`) rather than doubles.
- Left as `Number` because they are display-only (Wave 1 owners may move them):
  - posting sign classes in `PlayerDashboard.tsx:160`, `accounts/[accountId]/page.tsx:339` and `transactions/[txnId]/page.tsx:105`
  - unit-price series and price-change ratios in `lib/sql/market.ts:232`, `lib/derived.ts:117` (candles) and the item page
  - `lib/sql/health.ts:98` activity volume (a SQL `SUM`, converted for the compact KPI and the percentage change)
  - `lib/sql/stats.ts:73` balances fed to Gini
  - `lib/taxation.ts` per-day chart values
  - `lib/shopPrice.ts` per-item price
  - chart coordinates in `components/charts/*` (DS)

### Defects (§1.4)
- **Item 1, wealth Share 0.0%: not present on `develop`.** `aa3ee597` (PAR-340) removed the Share column. On production the denominator was `getTotalSupply()`, the net of every balance including the minting accounts. A closed ledger nets to zero, so the column was always 0. Production returns `SUM(balance) = 0.00` against $252,557,030.47 of positive balances. Nothing to fix here; the production symptom goes away when `develop` ships.
- **Item 2:** removed `getFineCategorySummary` and `FineCategoryRow`. Nothing in the UI or services called them any more. The fines list is untouched.
- **Item 10:** `getViewer`'s error path returned `permissions: []`. It now returns the live `player` baseline from `permissionsForRoles(['player'])`. If the database is down, it falls back to `SEEDED_PLAYER_PERMISSIONS`, the V31 seed. It never grants anything elevated.
- **Item 11:** the Government tab now shows only for `government.read` or `government.read.all`. `pickSubNav(path, permissions)` takes the client permissions. The client viewer carries no ReBAC scope, so a `government.read` holder with no in-scope account still sees the tab. `/government` keeps its server-side gate. The user guide notes this.

### Cache hardening (`lib/cache.ts`, §4.3)
- **Bounded L1:** an in-house LRU on `Map` order, capped at 5,000 entries and about 64 MiB (measured as serialized length). `lru-cache` is in the tree only as a dev-only transitive dependency, so it would have to become a new runtime dependency for about 40 lines of code.
- **Cross-pod lock on cold misses:** the first pod takes `lock:<key>` and computes. Other pods poll Redis for the published value until the lock goes away or its TTL ends, then compute themselves. In-pod concurrent requests share one run. Lock release compares a token, so a pod that overran its TTL can't drop another pod's lock. Default `lockMs` is 20 s, past the 15 s statement timeout.
- **`maxStaleMs` per key:** defaults to 60 windows (1 h for 60 s windows). Entries now record when they were computed (`at`); older Redis values without it are read as computed at the start of their window. A value past `maxStaleMs` is recomputed before it is served. If that recompute fails, the old value is served rather than a page error.
- **Failures are never stored.**
- `memo(key, windowMs, producer)` is unchanged. A fourth `options` argument is optional. Background refresh failures go through one `reportRefreshFailure` function, so D0 (PAR-531) can add its `refresh_fail` counter in one place.

### Request dedupe (§4.3)
- `lib/auth/access.ts` exports React `cache()` wrappers of `findAccount`, `canReadAccount`, `findFirmByDisplayName`, `findFirmById`, `isFirmMember` and `hasFirmFinancialAccess`. The account page, firm pages and `accountContext` service import these.
- Identity lookups were already deduped through the cached `getViewer`. The second `findIdentityBySub` after an upsert must stay fresh, so it is not wrapped.
- New `readableAccountIds(viewer, ids): Promise<Set<number>>` with the same RBAC + ReBAC rule as `canViewAccount`. It is backed by one `lib/sql/ledger.ts` query, `findReadableAccountIds` (ownership OR `account_read_access_web`). It replaces the N+1 in `PlayerDashboard` and in `canViewTransaction`.
- The firm page runs `canViewFirmInternals` and `canViewFirmFinancials` together. `canViewFirmInternals` runs its membership and finance lookups in parallel.

### Cursor helper
- `lib/pagination/cursor.ts`: `encodeCursor({ at, id })` and `decodeCursor(token)`. The token is opaque, versioned base64url. Decoding a missing, malformed, non-canonical or out-of-range token returns `null`. Encoding an invalid date or id throws `InvalidCursorError`. No pages use it yet.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` (`--max-warnings=0`) are clean.
- `npm run coverage` with `RUN_INTEGRATION=1` against a scratch MariaDB 11.8: 50 files, 607 tests passed. Overall coverage is 48.25% lines and 84.05% branches. `money.ts` 100%, `cache.ts` 94%, `cursor.ts` 96%.
- `npm run test:e2e`: 302 passed.
- New unit tests:
  - `money.test.ts`: negatives, half-away rounding, values past 2^53 cents, malformed input, every format mode.
  - `cache.test.ts`, using a fake Redis shared by separate module instances that stand in for pods: LRU eviction by count and bytes, single-flight, cold lock with three pods, holder failure, lock TTL expiry, fleet-wide stale refresh, `maxStaleMs`, refresh failure, older entries without `at`, Redis errors.
  - `cursor.test.ts`, `viewer.test.ts`, the `readableAccountIds` cases in `access.test.ts`, and Government-tab cases in `navigation.test.tsx`.
- Two mutation checks:
  - Removing the cold-path lock wait fails the cross-pod and TTL tests.
  - Removing the per-byte oversize guard does not fail any test, because the eviction loop then drops the entry anyway. The guard is an early exit.
- New integration test: `findReadableAccountIds` agrees with ownership + `canReadAccount` for every seeded account and player.
- **Not verified:**
  - The dev server (economy.dev.paradaux.io) has not been run with this branch.
  - The 18 s cold `/` failure has not been reproduced. The scratch seed is too small. The fix is covered by the cross-pod unit tests only.
  - No before and after timings against `ops/perf-baseline.md` (D0 has not published it yet).
  - No screenshots: the only visible change is the Government tab being hidden, which `navigation.test.tsx` covers.

## Size

33 files, +1,426 / −275.
- Source: +750 / −265.

author: centuryglass
body:
This updates the AGENTS.md rules for how agents work with harness defaults, CI and local test runs.

**Harness overrides.** Some rules contradict the instructions coding harnesses give, and the file didn't say which one wins. Agents settled it differently from session to session.
- **Branch naming:** a branch the harness assigns doesn't count as the maintainer asking for that branch. The rule now counts as permission to push to the branch the agent names, overriding a harness rule to use only its own branch. If the remote refuses that push, the agent pushes to the assigned branch.
- **Opening PRs:** the existing override now also names the harness's default, not just the agent's.
- **PR subscriptions:** no longer forbidden. Subscribing to your own PR's activity is now optional.
- **CI failures:** a failure your diff has no plausible path to isn't yours to diagnose, even where a harness says every red check is yours. Spend only the effort it takes to tell which case it is. If an open issue tracks the failure, add anything new to that issue. If none does, open one with the test, the output and the commit. Then re-run the failed job.

**Scoped test runs.** The PR checklist asked for a full `pytest` run before every PR, but CI already runs every test on every push. A new Testing rule, "Run the tests a change can reach", replaces it:
- Changes confined to files no test imports run no tests: Markdown, `doc/`, `scripts/`, `.claude/`, `.opencode/` and `.github/`.
- A change under `src/` runs the matching `test/` directory, plus every test file that names a changed module. A change under `src/ui/` runs all of `test/ui/`.
- The full suite runs when a change touches shared foundations (`src/config/`, `src/util/`, `src/ui/theme.py`, `resources/`, the test base classes, the requirements files), when lowering the cycle baseline, and when the scope is unclear.

`scripts/markdown_lint.py` passes. This is a Markdown-only change, so it runs no tests.

author: munkycdev
body:
## What

Google Drive joins OneDrive and Dropbox as library storage on the web, with read-only access (`drive.readonly`).

- `GoogleDriveClient` and `GoogleDriveDrive` in Bibliotaph.Storage. Google is ID-based, so the drive resolves `/googledrive/<account>/<path>` by walking named children from the root, with a one-minute listing cache. Names that hold a slash, or that appear more than once in a folder, get stable names: `∕` and `∖` for slashes, and " (2)" before the extension, oldest first. Google Docs, Sheets and other native files are skipped. Shared drives are supported, and 429, 5xx and rate-limit 403 responses are retried.
- `GoogleDriveProvider` handles OAuth with offline access, and identifies the account by its permission ID. `GoogleDriveChanges` polls changes.list every five minutes and feeds the same change path that OneDrive and Dropbox use.
- The reader reads Google Drive books through the server's time-limited read links, as it does for Dropbox.
- `infra/setup.ps1 -GoogleClientId` stores the secret and prints the redirect URI, plus the note to publish the consent screen.
- Docs: the web guide, features.md, architecture.md, the privacy page's Limited Use sentence, and the CHANGELOG.

## Tests

GoogleDriveTests: connect, listing with paging and naming, indexing and reading a range, and change polling. Uses a fake Google API. The full server suite passes (133).

body:
## Summary

```text
Flushed export snapshot → atomic replacement → bounded retry on transient refusal
                                            → cleanup and error on persistent failure
```

The clean DEV-03 package failed when Windows temporarily refused an atomic export replacement. Keep the flushed snapshot and retry only sharing/lock violations and error 1175, at most five times with 200 ms between attempts. Other errors still propagate.

## Evidence

- The actual save-path probe reproduced 37 failures in 1,000 attempts before the fix; every original destination survived and an immediate repeat succeeded. The fixed implementation had zero failures in 1,000 attempts.

author: theciege23
body:
Three waiver features in one PR (all in the waiver area, to avoid conflicts). Follows #2719, #2728 and #2732.

## 1. Sleeper-style free agency (commissioner option)
`waiverEngineConfig.free_agency_mode = 'after_run'` ("Waivers until each run, then free agents"). It is a mode on the existing add/drop decision (`lib/waiver-wire/after-run-free-agency.ts`), not a second system. Claims, the run and its order are the league's own.
- Before the league's first waiver run after its draft, every player is on waivers, so an add becomes a claim (`WAIVER_REQUIRED`, and the screen opens the claim form).
- After a run, every unclaimed player is an instant first-come add. A run counts as cleared at its scheduled time even when the processor wrote nothing, because it records no run when nothing was pending.
- A player whose game started since the last run is back on waivers until the next one. Kickoffs come from the lineup lock's `buildWeekKickoffMap`, for this week and last week.
- The dropped-player waiver period (#2719) and "a pending claim wins at the run" (#2728) still apply.
- A failed read fails closed: the player needs a claim, never a free add. The mode has no effect in FCFS leagues or while the per-day schedule is on.
- Settings: web hub (`WaiversTab`) and the in-league commissioner panel (`WaiverLeagueSettingsPanel`). Validated in `parseHubWaiverOptions` (settings patch) and the commissioner waivers API schema.

## 2. FAAB at season rollover
`faab_rollover_rule: reset | carry_over` (`lib/waiver-wire/faab-rollover.ts`).
- Read by every renewal path: `renewRedraftLeague`, `renewNativeRedraft`, the renew route's legacy reset, and keeper/dynasty renewals that choose `reset`.
- When unset, each path keeps its old behaviour: redraft resets, keeper/dynasty carries over.
- Saving the setting moves no balance. Only the next renewal applies it.

## 3. Lineup warning on a drop or claim
A drop through add/drop or a claim that leaves a starting slot unfillable (for example dropping the only C) gets `409 LINEUP_WARNING` once.
- The web (`WaiverWirePage`) and native (`NativeWaiversScreen`) screens ask the manager to confirm. A retry with `confirmLineupWarning: true` goes through, so this is a warning and not a block.
- The check is a maximum matching of active players (IR, taxi and devy excluded) to the league's starter slots, using lineup validation's slot eligibility.
- It only fires when the move makes the lineup worse. An unknown position or a failed read means no warning.

EN and ES strings are in their own `waiverFa.*` block, using «reclamos» and never «waiver». No migration.

## Tests
- New: `waiver-after-run-free-agency` (18), `waiver-lineup-fill-warning` (17), `waiver-faab-rollover` (6), `waiver-fa-settings-ui` (9). Extended: `renew-redraft-league` (+2), `commissioner-renew-redraft-route` (+3).
- Related suites (waiver*, daily schedule, settings hub, i18n/Spanish rulings, renewal, post-draft lock routes): 68 files, 595 tests, all passing.
- Mutation controls: flipping the game-start rule fails 4 tests, and disabling the warning fails 5.
- Scoped tsc over the 21 changed source files: 22 errors, identical to the base commit (all known noise, none in changed files).

## For the owner
- Run days for NBA/NHL/MLB stay on the sport default (Mon/Wed/Fri) unless the commissioner changes them. Sleeper's own default there is a daily run.
- FAAB rollover for keeper/dynasty leagues defaults to carry over, which is today's behaviour, not reset. Reset is opt-in there.
- Not built: the one-time mid-season FAAB top-up week.

## Task ORB-18453 — Dashboard rail: the sticky host block hides the lower Settings sub-views, including the active and keyboard-focused one, at 1440×900 ### Description **View:** dashboard left rail, Settings section (also the bottom of Analytics). **Width/theme:** 1440×900, dark (the dashboard's only theme). **Steps** 1. Open `#config/hosts` (or `#config/machine`, `#config/all-keys`) at 1440×900. 2. Look at the rail: under Settings only *Workflow* and *Execution* are visible. *Review, Crews, Machine, Hosts* (the active one) and *All keys* sit behind the sticky rail foot (HOST readings block plus clock). 3. From *Workflow*, press Tab through the sub-views. **What the user sees:** the selected sub-view is invisible in the rail, so nothing shows where they are. Keyboard focus on Review, Crews, Machine, Hosts and All keys is fully covered by the rail foot: `elementFromPoint` at each focused sub-tab's centre lands in `.rail-foot` (sub-tabs at y 679–845, foot at 681–866). That fails WCAG 2.4.11 (Focus Not Obscured). The rail does scroll (`nav.rail` scrollHeight 997 vs clientHeight 810), but nothing signals that, and the reveal on load never brings the active item into view. On Analytics › Agents the active *Agents* item is half covered too. **What it should be:** the active and the focused rail item is always fully visible above the rail foot. **Evidence:** `screenshots/dashboard-rail-settings-hosts-dark-1440.jpg`, `screenshots/dashboard-rail-settings-focus-hosts-dark-1440.jpg`, `screenshots/dashboard-settings-machine-throttle-dark-1440.jpg`, `screenshots/dashboard-agents-implementer-detail-dark-1440.jpg`. **Code pointers** - `crates/orbit-web/assets/dashboard/css/shell.css` `.rail-foot` (~225–235): `position: sticky; bottom: -8px` overlays the `nav.rail` scrollport, and the rail has no matching `scroll-padding-bottom`. - `crates/orbit-web/assets/dashboard/js/router.js` `revealActiveRailSelection()` (~407–416): `scrollIntoView({block: "nearest"})` treats the covered sub-tab as already visible. It then scrolls the top-level tab into view, which undoes any reveal. - The foot grew when the host readings moved into it (ORB-17933). Evidence screenshots are attached to the ux-review task ORB-18441 (spawned_from relation) under the paths named below. ### Acceptance Criteria - At 1440×900 (dark), a direct load of Settings › Hosts and of Settings › All keys shows the active sub-view in the rail fully above the host block without scrolling the rail by hand; screenshots attached. - Tabbing through every Settings sub-view at 1440×900 leaves each focused item and its focus ring fully visible, not covered by the rail foot; a screenshot of a focused lower sub-view is attached. - Analytics › Agents at 1440×900 shows its active sub-view unobscured, and the 375px horizontal rail behaves as before; screenshots attached. ## Screenshots | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | dashboard-rail-analytics-agents, 1440 | | | | dashboard-rail-analytics-agents, 375 | — | | | dashboard-rail-config-all-keys, 1440 | | | | dashboard-rail-config-all-keys, 375 | — | | | dashboard-rail-config-all-keys-focus, 1440 | | | | dashboard-rail-config-hosts, 1440 | | | | dashboard-rail-config-hosts, 375 | — | | ## Execution Summary
Click to expand Implemented the rail visibility repair on starting HEAD 69643af2d3e8564577574c80fff230688d8112e0; the initial worktree was clean and HEAD is unchanged. Changes are uncommitted for pipeline delivery. The desktop rail reserves the sticky footer's measured height using scroll padding and leaves room for the focus outline. The existing layout observer now watches the rail/footer, so wrapping host readings and viewport changes update that reservation. Desktop routing reveals the selected leaf once; the phone retains its existing parent/sub-view scroll behavior. Acceptance evidence: 1. PASSED: fresh Settings Hosts and All keys loads at 1440×900 dark show the active lower edge at 673.25px above the footer at 681.25px, without manual scrolling. 2. PASSED: Tab through all seven Settings sub-views and Shift+Tab back retain unobscured items and full focus rings. The focused All keys screenshot shows the lower ring clear of the foot; focus also remains clear after a wrapped verdict enlarges the foot. 3. PASSED: Analytics Agents lower edge is 672.75px above the footer at 681.25px. Hosts, All keys and Agents at 375px retain visible parent/selected sub-view, no page overflow and the existing horizontal rail behavior. Browser QA: Chromium 156.0.8078.4, shipped HTML/CSS/router and host renderers served on disposable loopback HTTP. Populated host/workspace pickers, Health attention counts and Linux I/O readings reproduce the original obstruction. The new public browser regression FAILED as expected against unmodified HEAD production assets (Settings active/focused items and Analytics Agents were covered), then PASSED against the candidate: seven-width count/label geometry, 18 indicator route transitions and 21 active/focused visibility checks, including footer resizing. Before/after asset replacement was restored in finally. ## Verifikasi ulang P2 — temuan kedua

Item **tombol tahun anggaran di topbar** ternyata baru menangani satu arah batas rentang.

`layouts/app.blade.php`:

```
@for($y = 2023; $y <= max(2028, (int) $tahunAktif); $y++)
```

Plafon sudah dinamis (sekolah dengan tahun anggaran 2031 tetap dapat opsinya), tetapi **lantainya dipaku 2023**. Kalau sesi berada di tahun anggaran lama — arsip 2021/2022, yang memang ada untuk sekolah dengan data BOSP lama — tidak ada `<option>` yang cocok, jadi tak ada yang `selected` dan topbar menampilkan tahun yang salah. author: rosylilly
body:
## Summary

The participant operations of the voice chat rooms (ADR-0100 §4, §5, §7, §11; ADR-0101 §2), on top of #1374.

- Participants: become a speaker (`voice.CanSpeakFreely`, otherwise 403 `voice-cannot-speak`) and go back to listening; raise and lower a hand.
- Host and co-hosts: grant the permission to speak (with or without a raised hand), dismiss a hand, revoke (back to listener and the explicit grant removed), mute (`Transport.Mute` through `voice.apply`), remove with a re-entry ban, invite as a listener or a speaker (100 per room per hour through the KeyValueStore rate limiter; 422 for blocked, banned, non-local, or inactive accounts; 409 for a second invitation) and revoke, and list the invitations.
- Host only: assign co-hosts (at most 3; participants in a block relation with the new co-host leave as `blocked`) and remove them. Co-host status ends with the participation and a co-host who becomes host stops being one (#1345 answer 44), covered by tests.
- Blocks during a room: `graph.blocked` between two participants of the same room enqueues `voice.check_block`, which takes out the one who is not the host or a co-host.
- Every change writes its event rows and emits its event in a transaction that locks the room first (`roomTx`); role changes reach the transport as `voice.apply` `speak` (`SetSpeaking`), mutes as `mute`. New events `voice.speak_grant_changed`, `voice.invited`, `voice.invitation_revoked`, `voice.banned` (no projector reads them; #1361 can subscribe to `voice.invited` for the notification).
- Client API: `/voice/rooms/{id}/speaker`, `/hand`, `/participants/{account_id}` (DELETE removes), `.../grant`, `.../hand`, `.../mute`, `.../cohost`, `/invitations`, `/invitations/{account_id}`.

Tests: `testkit.VoiceRoomsContract` gains cases for each operation's permission (host / co-host / participant), the ban, the block rules, co-hosts, invitations, and the invitation rate limit, on SQLite and PostgreSQL; client API routing and problem tests; a platform test through the API with a real block.

Closes #1358

## Changes

- feat(voice): add the participant operations, co-hosts, invitations, and bans

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Tests for each operation's permission (host / co-host / participant) and for the block and ban rules
- [x] `scripts/task.sh check:changed` passes

## Decisions and assumptions

- A grant gives the permission only; the participant then becomes a speaker with Speak (vision: 'ホストから明示的に許可された時発話開始できるようになる'). Becoming a speaker lowers a raised hand; a grant on a raised hand records 'granted'.
- Nobody operates the host or themselves; the host and co-hosts may grant, revoke, mute, and dismiss co-hosts, but nobody removes a co-host (§5 'ホストと共同ホストは互いを退出させられず').
- Block between two participants: if one is the host or a co-host, the other leaves; between two co-hosts, the blocked one leaves; between two plain participants, nobody leaves (§11 covers only host/co-host).
- Assigning a co-host: every other non-host participant in a block relation with them leaves (co-hosts included, literal §11); assigning someone in a block relation with the host is a 422.
- Revoking an invitation as a speaker also revokes the current explicit grant; a participant keeps their current role and stays.
- The rate limit counts an invitation that passes validation (100/hour/room, sliding window); a second invitation of the same account (even after a revocation) is a 409 voice-already-invited.
- SetSpeaking's reconnect is only logged in voice.apply; sending the new grant over the room stream belongs to #1359.
- The invitation rate-limit token is taken before the transaction and not refunded when the invitation then fails (accepted in review).
- The relations of other modules (follows, blocks, limits) are read before the room transaction, because their ports take no transaction; the transaction re-reads what the voice module owns and fails with ErrConflict (409, retryable) when the host, a co-host, or a participant it did not read appeared meanwhile.
- The invitation list (GET /voice/rooms/{id}/invitations) is keyset-paged by invitation ID and visible to the host and co-hosts only.

## Documentation

No user or operator document describes the changed paths.

## Checklist

- [x] `scripts/task.sh check` passes locally
- [x] Docs / i18n catalogs updated where needed
- [x] No secrets, no unrelated changes

author: 28ns30
body:
Students in Taiwan share by LINE. A just-filed report used to share as the generic site badge, there was no share control anywhere, and a search for the project's own name returned nothing.

**Sharing**
- **A share button** on the receipt (once the record is public), the record page, species pages and /season.
  - It uses `navigator.share` where it exists.
  - Otherwise it offers a LINE share link and copy-link, which also covers LINE's own in-app browser.
  - It has 44 px targets and a live confirmation.
- **A record share card**, `reports/[id]/opengraph-image`: the species name, the date on Taiwan's calendar, and the collection.
  - The record's own already-stripped photo appears only for a published, exact, non-test record that has one.
  - It never shows a map or coordinates.
- **Each record page has its own description**: species, date, collection, and a plain blur note when it is blurred.

**Findability**
- **Indexing:** the 46,305 imported GBIF record pages are `noindex, follow`, because they are thin copies of a published dataset. Reports filed here are indexed, and paged lists are self-canonical.
- **Structured data:**
  - WebSite and Organization on the home page.
  - A schema.org Dataset on /attribution: CC BY 4.0 for the whole, CC0 for the reports filed here (`hasPart`), `isBasedOn` the TaiRON GBIF dataset, Taiwan's coverage, and the dates the public records span.
- **Sitemaps:**
  - one predicate (`INDEXWORTHY`) decides both a species page's robots tag and the sitemap;
  - per-locale sitemaps with no 5,000 cap behind an index at `/sitemap.xml`, and their counts are cached.

**Merged with main** after #166:
- record metadata reads the page's own shared record;
- the two `rewrites` are one;
- the species page shares its own slug.

**Review follow-ups made by me**
- The share button sits outside the receipt's live region.
- The button reports its panel when a native share falls back to it.
- A made-up sitemap id costs no queries.
- The Dataset test no longer races other files' reports.

No migration.

author: pwntato
body:
Restores the one-off CreatedAt backfill Lambda (the #254 shape) so the accepted residual from #259 can be cleared before real users arrive. Refs #258.

## What changes
- Brings back `internal/backfill`, `cmd/backfill`, `terraform/backfill.tf`, the `deploy_backfill` grants, the zip build steps and the README section, exactly as at 6eed1fe.
- `removeTypes` now also covers `Admission`, `GenerationKey` and `Rotation`: rows written before #259 that still carry a second-resolution `CreatedAt`. Nothing reads it.
- A Rotation's `StartedAt` is a separate attribute and is never touched (the test pins it).
- `User` (real accounts only), `Recovery`, `UsernameClaim`, `Group`, `RoleGrant` and MEMBER# truncation are unchanged, so any row written between the first backfill and #259 is also picked up.

## Safety
- Dry run by default (`backfill_dry_run = true`). The invoke payload can force a dry run but never turn writing on.
- Every write is conditional on the `CreatedAt` the scan saw, so a concurrent change is counted as raced and skipped. Reruns are idempotent.
- Its own role: `dynamodb:Scan` and `UpdateItem` only, pinned to the code by `iam_test.go`.

## Verification
- `go build ./...` and `go test -p 1 ./...` pass against DynamoDB Local; `terraform validate` and `fmt -check` pass.
- Mutation runs (committed first, each failed on its own assertion in `TestRunBackfillsEachRowType`): dropping `Admission`, `GenerationKey` or `Rotation` from `removeTypes`; changing the update to also remove `StartedAt`.

## Plan after merge
1. Merge deploys the Lambda in dry-run mode. Jimmy invokes it and reads the counts.
2. A second PR sets `backfill_dry_run = false`; Jimmy invokes again, a third run should be all zeros.
3. A third PR removes the Lambda again (the deploy role already has `iam:ListInstanceProfilesForRole` from #257).

body:
## 🧭 작업 영역
- [ ] AN
- [x] BE
- [ ] AN/BE 공통 설정

## 🚀 변경 사항
FCM HTTP v1 발송기와 컬렉션 발급 가능 알림, 23시 리마인더를 추가한다. 최소 동작을 목표로 동기적으로 보낸다.

| 알림 | 언제 | 대상 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 컬렉션 발급 가능 | 처음 발급 가능한 것을 확인하고 1시간 뒤 | 그때도 받지 않은 카드가 있는 기기, 기기마다 하루 한 번 |
| 컬렉션 리마인더 | 매일 23:00 KST | 받지 않은 카드가 있는 기기 |

- 발급 가능은 오늘 어떤 감정이든 스탬프 1개 이상, 프레스 100회 이상이고 그 감정 카드를 받지 않은 상태다. `CollectionProgressRepository.findClaimableDeviceIds` 가 카드 수령 조건과 같은 기준으로 조회한다
- 5분마다 발급 가능한 기기를 조회하고 처음 확인한 시각을 메모리에 둔다. 1시간 안에 카드를 받으면 기록을 지우고, 이후 다른 감정이 발급 가능해지면 다시 센다. 날짜가 바뀌면 비운다
- 토큰이 있고 `collectionClaimableEnabled` 가 ON 인 기기에만 보낸다. 한 기기 발송이 실패해도 나머지에는 보낸다
- FCM 은 Google 클라이언트 라이브러리 없이 직접 호출한다(ADR-0014 방식). `GoogleAccessTokenProvider` 에 범위를 받는 생성자를 추가해 재사용하고, Play Integrity 동작은 그대로다. `RestClient` 빈은 추가하지 않는다
- FCM 이 404 이면서 `errorCode` 가 `UNREGISTERED` 일 때만 그 토큰을 지운다. 다른 오류는 로그만 남긴다
- `FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_BASE64` 가 비어 있으면 발송기가 꺼진다. 운영은 아직 배선 전(#915 뒤)이라 보내지 않는다
- data 는 `type`(`COLLECTION_CLAIMABLE`, `COLLECTION_CLAIM_REMINDER`)과 `date` 다. 앱 연동 문서 `BE/docs/client/push-notifications.md` 에 추가했다
- #933 범위 리팩터링을 함께 넣었다. 푸시 토큰 등록의 `TransactionTemplate` 을 빼고 `DevicePushTokenRegistrationService.updatePushToken` 의 `@Transactional` 로 옮겼다. 23505 와 토큰 유니크 제약일 때 1회 다시 하는 동작은 그대로다

## 🔗 관련 이슈
- Closes #934

## 🧪 검증 방법
- [x] `./gradlew test` 전체 통과(2,932개, 실패 0)
- [x] 발급 판정의 같은 감정, 같은 날짜 조건, 날짜 변경 시 하루 한 번 기록 초기화, FCM 요청의 `message` 래퍼를 각각 일부러 빼면 해당 테스트가 실패하는 것을 확인
- [ ] 개발 서버 배포 뒤 토큰을 등록한 Debug 빌드 기기에서 실제 수신 확인(FCM 실호출은 아직 확인하지 못함)

## 👀 리뷰 포인트
- `CollectionNotificationService.notifyClaimable` 의 대기와 하루 한 번 처리
- `FcmPushSender.isUnregistered` 의 무효 토큰 판정

## 📝 특이 사항
- 순위 변동 알림은 #935 에서 같은 발송기를 쓴다

body:
A placed image is fitted into 1000 px on its longer side. When working on an interface, the size is the point: I paste screenshots of a live web page next to the design they came from and compare spacing, type and layout, which works only when they line up 1:1. In Figma they do; in FigCraft a 1440 px page came in at 1000 px and nothing matched.

Figma places an image at its pixel size and scales down only a side past 4096 px. A macOS screenshot also records 144 dpi, and Figma reads that as 2x: a 400 × 300 pt selection, saved as 800 × 600 px, comes in at 400 × 300.

**What changes**
- `image.place` (dropped files, Place image, paste) places at the pixel size divided by the PNG's screen density, fitting only a side past 4096 px. Density counts only when the `pHYs` chunk is a whole 2x–4x multiple of 72 dpi, so a 300 dpi scan keeps its pixel size. The image data is untouched, so 2x exports stay sharp. An explicit `width`/`height` still wins.
- On macOS, paste reads the clipboard's `public.png` as is. arboard's decoded pixels drop the density and the colour profile. Other platforms keep the decoded image.

**Testing**
- `engine/placed_image_size_tests`: pixel size, a 144 dpi PNG at half size, a 300 dpi PNG at pixel size, the 4096 px fit, explicit sizes, and bytes that aren't a PNG. The first fails without the change (1000 × 500 instead of 2400 × 1200).
- `ui-egui/paste_image_tests`: a 2x screenshot on the clipboard pastes at 400 × 300, centred in the view.
- With a real macOS screenshot (2318 × 1200 px, 144 dpi) through `figcraft-cli run`: placed at 1159 × 600, the size of the selection on screen. The same file saved at 72 dpi is placed at 2318 × 1200.
- `cargo xtask ci` passes here except `clipboard_fence_tests::a_synthetic_copy_shortcut_leaves_the_system_clipboard_alone`, which fails on this Mac on a clean `main` too, and the wasm step, which I can't build locally.

author: nigelblount
body:
#942 and #954 have merged, so this PR's diff against develop is now only its own work: the comments' undo and the save-only fix.

## Problem

Three problems with Návrh's comments (spec navrh D8, artifact-design **DSN14**, W1):
- A comment's × removed it at once, with no way back. Every other removal on Návrh offers Vrátit.
- In the workbench, "Uložit komentáře" set `plan_changed26`. Porozumění then read "Upraveno podle vašich komentářů" before anything had been reworked: the comments had only been saved for the Lead.
- The section's hint said "Všechny komentáře AI zapracuje najednou", which is not true in the workbench.

## Approach

- **Undo.** A removal goes through the stage's one undo offer, named like the narrative's removals ("Odebráno: „…“"). Vrátit puts the comment back where it stood (`restoreComment`, plan.ts). It restores only while the list holds fewer equal comments than before the removal, so one of two identical comments can be taken back, and a reloaded copy still gets no duplicate.
- **Batch save clears the offer.** Saving or processing the comments clears the offer, because the comments leave as one batch. Without that, a comment taken back after a save would replace the next batch's `review_comments`.
- **No false "upraveno".** In the workbench, saving marks nothing changed.
- **Workbench copy.** The hint says where comments go, and the section says "Komentář nic nemění. Změnu udělá Vedoucí až na vaši žádost."
- **Classic layout.** The hint names Hypotézy as a section a comment can quote.

## Trade-off accepted

The board's "lišta nahoře" wording is left out of the note. The Lead's edits bar (D9) isn't built, so the note doesn't promise it.

## Measured

n/a

## Deliberately not done

- **A comment's target and author** ("k sadě … · Jana Malá"). The store is `{quote, comment}` in `ui_state`, and the author must come from the session, never the browser. That needs a backend field, so DSN14 stays open. The plan file records what's built and what's left.

## Doc follow-up

none (no module, route or key the docs describe changed)

## Checks

- [x] `make lint` (one pre-existing warning), `make typecheck`, `make layer_check`, `make web_design`, `make web_unused`, `make test-web` (4028 passed, after merging develop)
- [x] `workbench_journey.mjs` on a fresh workbench: the comments section's note at 1440 / 1100 / 768 / 390, nothing paid; `proposal_prompt_journey.mjs` passes, `paidJobs: 0`
- [x] `/code-review high`, with its findings applied:
  - the offer cleared on save;
  - no duplicate restore;
  - the workbench hint;
  - the shared "Odebráno" toast;
  - the test asserting order by text.
- [x] Stand-in reviews on a4e023df and 3c1f30f9: no findings. Both optional points were taken in 3c1f30f9.
- [x] Security review by hand: no new request or field; nothing read from the browser as an author
- New tests:
  - `ResearchScreen.workbench.test.tsx` "a removed comment comes back with Vrátit; saving comments marks nothing changed" (spec D8's name);
  - `plan.test.ts` for `restoreComment`, including one of two equal comments.

  The existing workbench test now expects no `plan_changed26` after a save-only. That is the spec's change, not a loosening.

author: amindhouib
body:
## What was wrong

The 2026-10-26 release bumped all 8 public packages. Lerna was not misconfigured and upstream `@argos-ci/*` tags were not involved. The baseline lerna diffed against was wrong because of one lightweight tag:

- In independent mode lerna uses ONE baseline for the whole repo: `git describe --first-parent --match '*@*'` from HEAD. That lookup only sees annotated tags.
- `@snapvisor/storybook@7.0.1` (commit c755c56, the manual `from-package` release) is a lightweight tag (`git cat-file -t` prints `commit`; every lerna-made tag prints `tag`). Lerna ignored it and fell back to `@snapvisor/puppeteer@7.0.0` (b27308a), 11 commits back.
- Everything since b27308a counted as changed: the cli `--wait` feat, the sharp `^0.35.4` bump in core and webdriverio (#9, never released for those two), and the storybook fix/docs already shipped in 7.0.1. lerna then bumped the dependents of cli (devDependency of puppeteer, storybook, webdriverio) and of core (cypress, playwright, storybook, vitest).

Other findings:
- All 21 `@snapvisor/*` tags exist locally and on origin and are reachable from main. Nothing needs pushing.
- 191 `@argos-ci/*` tags are on the first-parent chain, but all are older than `@snapvisor/*@7.0.0`, so they never win the describe. Latent only.
- Current main is clean: HEAD is the `Publish` commit 60252cc, which carries the annotated tags, so `lerna changed` reports nothing to publish.
- Side effect to know: had lerna honored storybook@7.0.1, core's sharp advisory patch (#9) would NOT have been published (baseline after #9), so the wrong baseline happened to ship it.

## Fix

`scripts/check-release-baseline.mjs`, run first by `npm run release`. It compares the nearest tag lerna sees (annotated only) with the nearest tag including lightweight ones and throws when they differ, naming the offending tag. No lerna.json change is needed. `release-canary` (`--force-publish`) and `from-package` do not use the change baseline, so they are untouched. `release.yml` is not edited (avoids conflicting with #15).

## Dry run (nothing published, no tags created)

Before, `lerna@9.0.7 changed` at ba87b17 (the commit the release ran from):

```
lerna info Looking for changed packages since @snapvisor/puppeteer@7.0.0
@snapvisor/cli  @snapvisor/core  @snapvisor/cypress  @snapvisor/playwright
@snapvisor/puppeteer  @snapvisor/storybook  @snapvisor/vitest  @snapvisor/webdriverio
lerna success found 8 packages ready to publish
```

`lerna ls --since @snapvisor/storybook@7.0.1` at the same commit (the baseline lerna should have used): cli, puppeteer, storybook, webdriverio. Direct changes only (`--exclude-dependents`): cli.

After, at main (60252cc):

```
lerna notice Current HEAD is already released, skipping change detection.
lerna info No changed packages found
```

Guard at 60252cc: `Release baseline OK: lerna will diff against @snapvisor/cli@7.1.0`, exit 0.
Guard at ba87b17: `Release baseline mismatch: lerna would diff against @snapvisor/puppeteer@7.0.0 because @snapvisor/storybook@7.0.1 is a lightweight tag...`, exit 1.

Not merged, release.yml not dispatched, nothing published.

Claude Code has no built-in way here to scan the repository, or a branch's changes, for vulnerabilities. Claude Security does that and suggests patches that are applied only on request.
