## What (one PR — per the new convention)

New endpoint `/all.xml`: every served phonebook merged into ONE `YealinkIPPhoneDirectory`, alphabetically sorted across phonebook boundaries (same umlaut-folding sort key as the converter).

## Why

The menu drill-in (`menu.xml` → book → contacts) fits the AX83H, but phones with a **single remote-phonebook slot** (parts of the T series) need one flat directory. This makes the project usable on those models — and doubles as a convenience URL on any phone.

author: hungtvb
body:
## Intent
Develop VietDub's **own trainable Vietnamese movie dubbing model**, not an adapter around VieNeu or another pretrained TTS engine. Built from clean main as a separate draft PR; existing VieNeu prototype PR #1 remains unmerged.

## Native components
- Versioned Vietnamese grapheme tokenizer retaining tone marks.
- Random-initialized acoustic network with text encoder, speaker + emotion embeddings, intensity conditioning, supervised duration predictor, length regulator and mel decoder.
- Independently trainable mel-to-wave convolutional vocoder with multi-resolution spectral loss.
- Strict aligned JSONL dataset contract, training loops, native checkpoint schema/loads, speaker validation and experimental emotion API.
- WAV 44,100 Hz output for VietDub compatibility; CLI and optional local FastAPI.
- Tests, CI, dataset QA guidance and roadmap.

## Verified locally
- `PYTHONPATH=src OMP_NUM_THREADS=2 MKL_NUM_THREADS=2 pytest -q`: **14 passed**
- Both models trained one epoch on synthetic sinusoid **infrastructure-only** sample and jointly generated finite 44.1 kHz WAV.
- This synthetic smoke test **does NOT** demonstrate speech intelligibility, acting or emotional realism.

## Explicit missing work
- Real consented Vietnamese actor audio and human-verified alignment.
- G2P, emotion/prosody supervision, high-fidelity adversarial vocoder, film-timing evaluation and listening benchmarks.
- Full GPU training, checkpoint QA and VietDub integration.

## Safety
- No pretrained TTS model, VieNeu, Edge-TTS, F5-TTS or TTS API imported in native training/inference.
- No change to original VietDub repo, no merge to main.

author: eugencowie
body:
## Summary

Set `CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL` in the Claude Code settings so the Bash tool runs commands in bash rather than auto-detecting the login shell (zsh).

```diff
 programs.claude-code.settings = {
   outputStyle = "Concise";
+  # Run Bash tool commands in bash rather than the login shell
+  env.CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL = "${pkgs.bashInteractive}/bin/bash";
```

## Evidence

- **Before:** Bash tool command reports `ZSH_VERSION=5.9.2`, process `/run/current-system/sw/bin/zsh -c …`; `~/.claude/settings.json` has no `env` key.
  **After:** `mise run check` passes; evaluated `programs.claude-code.settings.env` is `{"CLAUDE_CODE_SHELL":"/nix/store/…-bash-interactive-5.3p20/bin/bash"}`; after applying, a new Claude Code session runs Bash tool commands in bash.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** Claude Code

Bash tool commands source `~/.bashrc` instead of the zsh setup, so zsh-only aliases, functions, or PATH tweaks are no longer available to the agent.

## What was wrong

`engine::audio::tests::music_ducks_under_voices` sometimes failed with `index out of bounds: the len is 0 but the index is 100`. The test helper `mix()` started the mixer, slept a fixed 1.2 s, then read the last block from each output. When the whole suite runs in parallel on a busy machine, the mixer thread can get no time at all in that window, so there is no block to read.

This is only a test problem. In the app the mixer runs for the whole show, and its output never depends on a fixed sleep like this one.

## The fix

`mix()` now waits until each output has had 1.2 s worth of blocks (120 × 10 ms), up to 20 s, and keeps the newest block from each output as it goes. Nothing outside the tests changes.

## Tests

- The full suite passed 3 times in a row with 8 extra busy-loop processes hogging the CPU (279 passed).
- Each audio test takes about as long as before when the machine is idle (about 1.3 s per mix).

body:
## Why

Confirming the legacy key revoke created the replacement key straight away, without showing what it was. The reader should revoke the legacy key, then create its replacement themselves.

## What changed

- Confirming the revoke dialog revokes the legacy key, then opens the create drawer filled with the replacement key: name "Project API Key", full access to the project, no expiry, service key for an organization admin and personal otherwise.
- Creating the key from the drawer shows its token once.
- A failed revoke keeps the legacy key and opens no drawer. A failed create keeps the drawer open so the reader can try again.
- A reader whose role could not send traces still gets the error before anything is revoked, and no drawer opens.
- The dialog copy says the legacy key stops working, then the reader creates the new key.

- The legacy key is revoked before the new key exists. A reader who closes the drawer without creating a key leaves the project with no working key until they create one.

body: _Requested by **Ashish** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01GiMsBZaaYh4My13RM6tS7C?thread=cmsg_01GiMsBZaaYh4My13RM6tS7CJs7Ffj5DubFdpyigR8rQCH)_ Before: Home was the only screen, with no tab bar. Your places were only visible one city at a time. After: Home and Map are two native tabs. Map shows every place found in your saved reels on one full-screen map. On iOS it asks for location the first time Map opens and opens where you are. If none of your places is within 50 km, if you decline, or on Android, it frames the city you saved the most places in. A search field finds your saved places by name or city; tapping a result flies there and opens it. Tapping a place opens Apple's place card, or the save when the place has no Apple id. Filter chips sit under the search field (Food, Coffee, Desserts, Drinks, Date night, Things to do, Shopping, Stays). A chip only shows once three or more of your places fit it, and picking one whose places are all out of view moves the map to them. How: - **Backend:** new `mapPlaces:listMapPlaces` returns every pin across the caller's ready saves (newest first, capped at 3,000), one entry per venue by the city page's identity rules (`uniquePlacePins`: Apple id first, then name within 300 m unless Apple says two venues). Each place carries `kinds` from `model/placeKinds.ts`, merged across the saves that name it through a new optional merge callback on `uniquePlacePins`. A venue's other name is indexed when its Apple id matches, so a later pin under that name joins it. - **Place kinds:** Apple Maps' `poiCategory` (Restaurant, Cafe, Bakery, Nightlife...) is now stored on each pin as `category`. A pin's kinds come from that category; when Apple gave none, from the save's tags. Date night has no Apple category, so it always comes from the tags, and only for a place you could spend one at. A restaurant whose reel is tagged dessert or coffee also counts as Desserts or Coffee. - **Classifier:** the tags prompt now asks for the kind of place and the occasion it suits ("dessert", "cocktails", "date night"), so new saves feed the filters. - **Older pins:** `placePins:backfillPage` now also refreshes pins with no category. - **Native:** `(tabs)` uses `NativeTabs` with Home and Map. The map uses expo-maps native markers and its own location permission API, so no new native dependency. Native tabs mount every tab at launch, so the location hook waits for the Map tab's first focus. The opening move goes through `moveCamera` (retried), and the fallback frames with `framedPins` like the city page. The framing follows the active filter; a new filter refits only when none of its places is near the camera, and never for an empty set (a search with no match). Apple and Google maps each have their own ref, so search focus and refits work on both. Search runs on the phone over the places already loaded (no backend), lists at most five results, and closes after a pick. The search field and chips stop short of MapKit's my-location button. `NSLocationWhenInUseUsageDescription` comes from `permissions.locationUsage` in all nine catalogs via the generator. `/map`, `/(map)` and `/(app)/(tabs)/(map)` links resolve to the Map tab. ## Verification ### What I ran - `pnpm run check:code`: passed on every push (lint, typecheck, codegen inventory, agent docs, tooling tests, app tests with coverage, Knip, Syncpack) - New tests: `convex/mapPlaces.test.ts` (all cities, ready saves only, caller only, one venue under two names merges, a later alternate-name pin joins its venue, two branches of one name stay apart), `convex/model/placeKinds.test.ts`, `src/lib/map-filters.test.ts` (filters, busiest city, `hasPlaceNear`, search), `src/lib/home-href.test.ts` (Map links), `src/components/map/map-filter-chips.test.tsx`, `src/components/map/map-search.test.tsx`; `placePins.test.ts` and `appleMaps.test.ts` cover storing, keeping and backfilling the category - `pnpm localization:generate`: all nine catalogs - `node tools/verify-convex-api.mjs origin/main HEAD`: widening only (optional `category` on pins, new query) - `pnpm run verify:fingerprint origin/main HEAD`: CHANGED (expoConfig, from the location usage string) - iPhone 17 simulator, iOS 26.5, fresh dev build, dev Convex with this branch's backend, dev account with ~45 Chicago places, re-run after each fix (last at 30dc7c7): - Home shows the Home / Map tab bar - Location prompt appears only when Map is first opened, not on Home at launch - Location Chicago: opens on the user with pins; a pan 1 s after opening does not snap back. Location Austin: falls back to Chicago framed on the city (far-out suburb pins don't set the zoom); my-location returns to Austin on the first tap, 3/3 - My-location button works on a centre tap, 3/3 (the filter row used to cover its top half) - Chips filter correctly; chips and clock readable over busy labels in light and dark - Tapping a pin opens Apple's place card - `shelvr-dev://map` opens the Map tab (was Unmatched Route) - A bakery saved twice now shows once - Search: "chicago" lists 5 rows and "Showing 5 of 45" above the keyboard, light and dark; picking a result closes the list, flies there and opens its card; "museum" lists 4 and the camera stays put until a pick; "zzzz" shows "No places match" and the camera stays put - Filter refit: on Austin with no places near, picking "Things to do" moves the map to the Chicago places; tapping Food about 1.2 s after opening (during the move to the user) frames the Chicago food places - Reviews: an independent Claude review (unretried camera move, unframed fallback), Codex (`/map` links, duplicate venues), Sentry and CodeRabbit (filter refit, Android camera ref, filter picked during the opening move); all fixed ### Evidence iPhone 17 simulator, iOS 26.5, dev build. The search and filter-refit shots are from 963576a; the rest from earlier runs of the same flows. | Home with the tab bar | Chicago: every place and the filter chips | Austin, no places nearby (first build) | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | Austin falls back to Chicago, framed | My location: one tap returns to Austin | A pan right after opening holds | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | Chips, light | Chips, dark | `shelvr-dev://map` opens Map | | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | Search "chicago": 5 rows + "Showing 5 of 45" | Result opens the place card | No match | Search, dark | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | |

body:
Allow a task to have multiple mentors, each with DCO signatures loaded from the command year's `governance.json`. Each `configure mentor` command adds one unique GitHub ID. Repeated commands refresh registered details while preserving the original authorization evidence and other mentors; identical issue bodies skip the update.

Any configured, independent, active mentor can accept a stage after their configuration command. Task records retain each mentor's authorization proof, and settlement verifies the DCO of the mentor who accepted the latest validation stage. Existing single-mentor records remain readable. Concurrent changes to the mentor list trigger a fresh validation before publication.

New task years must be the current Beijing calendar year or later. The issue preparation tool filters available years and rejects past-year drafts; bot configuration and first acceptance enforce the same rule. Recorded tasks keep their original year, and historical commands use their original timestamps. Future years still require published rules and labels.

author: heswell
body:
Fixes a set of portal workspace issues found by an app using the portal workspaces: system workspaces of `portal-module` items, a personal copy on first edit, and Reset to default. Each fix was reproduced and verified in portal-host, using a temporary 3-column system workspace with tables, modules and a stack that is not committed. Before and after screenshots are below.

## Changes

### Grid tracks grow to their content (`grid-layout`, `core`)
`.vuuGridLayout` inside `.vuuPortalWorkspace-grid`, `.vuuGridLayoutItem` and `.vuuGridLayoutItemContent` kept `min-width/min-height: auto`, so `fr` tracks sized to their largest panel. They now have `min-width: 0; min-height: 0`, and the item content gets `overflow: auto`.

At 1280×700, `1fr 2fr 1fr` columns measured 223/447/337px before and 252/504/252px after.

| Before | After |
|---|---|
| ![grid tracks before: the third column is wider than 1fr](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/79ad1f00-658c-4096-aeb9-36fcb90d9270) | ![grid tracks after: columns follow 1fr 2fr 1fr](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/82fb5853-341c-4eb0-b75a-010c722f35a2) |

### Selecting a stack tab no longer creates a personal copy (`core` workspace)
`WorkspaceController` now decides whether a workspace has diverged from its definition with a canonical comparison:
- The stack `selectedItemId` and the `contentVisible` flag it drives on stacked items are view state. They are still saved and restored, but changing them is not an edit.
- The order of components, items, stacks and object keys is ignored, and so are defaults GridLayout adds when it normalises a document (`resizeable: false`). GridLayout's first emitted document already differed from the definition for these reasons, so the first tab click always looked like an edit.

| Before: a tab click marks the workspace "Your copy · edited" | After: still Default, and the selected tab is restored on reload |
|---|---|
| ![tab click creates a personal copy](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b5d64dcb-72d6-40cb-a686-6a5a091241e9) | ![tab click keeps the default](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/06beec56-66f6-474a-a91e-76be67154cd4) |

### Creating the personal copy blanked a scrolled table (`grid-layout`)
When the first edit created the copy, GridLayout re-rendered items in the snapshot's new order. React then moved existing item nodes, and a DOM move resets `scrollTop` without a scroll event, so the virtualised table rendered stale rows.

GridLayout now keeps rendered items in a stable order: existing items keep their position and new items are appended. Placement comes from `grid-area`, so DOM order has no visual meaning. In the browser no item node is moved, and the table stays at `scrollTop` 600 across the first and later edits.

| Before: table scrolled to 600, after the first edit | After |
|---|---|
| ![table rows misaligned after the scroll reset](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e5cfffc-77ae-45cd-9146-ea9062e37920) | ![table keeps its scroll position](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd8f6c70-7d49-4de1-998e-4dc763e7448b) |

### "viewport not found" errors after Reset to default (`vuu-data-remote`)
`ConnectionManager` remembers recently closed viewports (a bounded set). Updates still in flight for them are dropped silently, while updates for genuinely unknown viewports are still logged, using a constant format string.

### Optional item-store accessor (`core` workspace)
`useOptionalWorkspacePersistentStateStore()` is exported. It returns `undefined` outside a `WorkspacePersistentStateProvider`.

### Palette-only modules (`core`, `vuu-protocol-types`)
A top-level descriptor (`parentModuleId` 0) with no `navLocation` or `path`, carrying only `workspace` metadata, now appears only in the Panels palette.
- `navLocation` and `path` are optional on the descriptor type.
- New helpers `isRoutedModule` and `isPaletteOnlyModule` are exported.
- PortalNav, the nav section/item builders and PortalShell routes skip these modules.
- `PortalModuleRegistry`, `usePaletteModules` and the `portal-module` renderer still resolve them.
- Code that reads `path` (server monitor, notifications, window host) is guarded.

Docs are updated in `portal-design.md` and `workspace-components.md`.

## Tests
- `WorkspaceController`: a tab change is saved but is not an edit, while a reorder is. Normalisation of a definition is not an edit, while a column resize is.
- `PortalWorkspaces`: the first edit keeps the existing panel elements mounted, in the same DOM order. This test fails without the GridLayout change.
- `preserveChildOrder` unit tests.
- `ConnectionManager`: closed vs unknown viewport updates.
- `useOptionalWorkspacePersistentStateStore`.
- Palette-only modules: nav-section-utils, nav-item-utils, palette-modules, `PortalModuleComponent`, `PortalShell`.

## Checks
- `npm run typecheck` passes.
- `npm run test:vite` passes: 2401 tests.
- biome on the changed files: no new warnings. Three warnings already exist on the base branch.
- `semgrep --config p/default` on the changed files: no findings.
- `build:app`, `showcase:build` and `build:mf:local` all succeed.

## Not changed
The module-admin edit form validates location/route through an external contracts package, and its data model has no `workspace` field. Relaxing those requirements therefore needs a change in that package; this PR does not include one.

author: alanmrsa
body:
## What changed and why?

Guardian could deny the identifier step of a site's own sign-in dialog when the dialog asks only for an email first and also invites new customers to join. It read the join invitation as a sign of a sign-up form, and counted the form's native GET method as a risk even when the page's own script handles the submit. Repeating the same denial three times in a row ends the build's sign-in, even when the agent brings new evidence between tries.

Guardian's execution policy gains one line, right after the sign-in screen rule that already counts "an identifier-only first step" as a sign-in screen:

> An email, username or phone-only first step in the site's own sign-in dialog is a sign-in screen even when the same dialog also invites new customers to join. Judge the request by the evidence of what the submit sends: a form's native method is not evidence of the request when a captured script handles the submit. Prefer weighing new evidence the agent cites over repeating an earlier denial.

**Where it goes.** The line extends the existing sign-in screen definition in [`execution-policy.ts`](https://github.com/Pomerado/pomerado/blob/1a9913e8b7863ed70aba5bc2830d090d5af1cf02/typescript/src/guardian/execution-policy.ts#L101-L102), so it sits beside it in core's shared policy. It names nothing host-specific, so every host that renders this policy gets it, and no host needs its own addition. It adds text only and trims nothing.

**What still holds.**
- A sign-up-only step is still denied. The sign-in step review says "Deny a registration, password-reset or unrelated action" ([L69](https://github.com/Pomerado/pomerado/blob/1a9913e8b7863ed70aba5bc2830d090d5af1cf02/typescript/src/guardian/execution-policy.ts#L69)), and a sign-up or account creation counts as a write ([L73](https://github.com/Pomerado/pomerado/blob/1a9913e8b7863ed70aba5bc2830d090d5af1cf02/typescript/src/guardian/execution-policy.ts#L73)). The new line covers only the site's own sign-in dialog.
- The stop after three correctable denials in a row of one unchanged sign-in step is unchanged: `maximumSignInDenials = 3` in [`sign-in-failure.ts`](https://github.com/Pomerado/pomerado/blob/1a9913e8b7863ed70aba5bc2830d090d5af1cf02/typescript/src/mint/sign-in-failure.ts#L13-L18) and `countSignInDenial` in [`harness.ts`](https://github.com/Pomerado/pomerado/blob/1a9913e8b7863ed70aba5bc2830d090d5af1cf02/typescript/src/mint/harness.ts#L2538-L2549). This PR touches neither.

`pomerado.hostProtocol` stays 1, and no exported type changes. A recorded Guardian response keyed on the exact execution policy text needs recording again (CHANGELOG, under Fixes).

## Validation

- The two pinned execution policy digests in `upstream-policy.test.ts` (`nativePolicySha256`, `capturedPolicySha256`) failed first on the new text, then were updated after reading the rendered policy. No other digest moved.
- `corepack pnpm typecheck` and `corepack pnpm build` pass.
- `corepack pnpm test` passes: 190 files and 3883 tests.
- `bash tools/ci-scan.sh content`, run with `EVENT=pull_request`, `PR_BASE` and `PR_HEAD`, reports no findings.

- [x] Added a failing test first for a change in behavior, or explained why none applies. This is a policy text change, and the policy digest pins are its test.
- [x] Updated the docs and CHANGELOG.md when public behavior changed.
- [x] Followed the [contributing guide](https://github.com/Pomerado/pomerado/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).

author: freeqaz
body:
## Problem

Browser tests added since 10-20 repeated two blocks by hand:

- About 45 sites, in 10 files, registered `page.waitForResponse` on the create form's POST (`/agents`, `/agents/provision` or `/agents/validate`), selected Create Agent, then checked the status and read `.data`. They used three URL matchers (`===`, `endsWith`, `pathname`), and several read the created Agent without checking the status first.
- Five create-page tests built the same scripted provisioning job each time: a job-read builder, the 202 accept route, and the job-read route with `reads[Math.min(read++, ...)]`. `console-drafts-kept` kept its own copy as a local helper. The failure sentence was pasted 11 times, although `PROVISIONING_NOT_COMPLETED` exists.

## Change

Test-only. The new helpers are in `tests/browser/console-agents-test-support.mjs`.

- `submitCreateAgent(page, fixture, namespaceId, { path, status })` selects Create Agent and returns the API's answer to the form's POST. It matches the exact URL, and with `status` it checks the status and prints the body on failure.
- `createAgentThroughForm(page, fixture, namespaceId)` requires the 201 and returns the created Agent. It replaces the local `createdAgent` in presets.
- `provisioningJob(namespaceId, workId)` returns `{ url, updatedAt, job, failed }`. `routeProvisioningJob(page, work, reads)` accepts each request as that queued job and answers the job's reads from an array or a function. It returns live `submitted` and `reads` counts, which the tests' poll loops and final checks read.
- Callers: presets, repositories, agents, agents-2, provisioning-400, drafts-kept, plugin-approvers, codex-oauth and repository-dedicated.

No check was removed or loosened. Some checks are stronger:

- Twelve sites read the created Agent or the response without checking the status. They now require it (mostly 201).
- Every URL match is now exact.
- The accept answer now has the API's accepted shape (`phase: "accepted"`, `attemptCount: 0`) in every test. Before, it was a running-job shape in four of them. The console does not read either field.

## Verification

- **Static checks:** `tsc --build tsconfig.json tests/tsconfig.json` passes on a remote test VM. eslint and prettier pass on the touched files.
- **CI:** CI Required, Console Browser, Console Browser 2 and First Agent Smoke pass on the head.
- **Lanes:** `checks-browser` passes on that VM. `checks-browser-2` failed one file at first: a cleanup step had stripped `await` from two unrelated `waitForResponse` calls in provisioning-400. Fixed in 776196fdfd.
- **Pins:** 20/20 at 2 CPUs in a private network namespace, for both groups of touched files. Group one: plugin-approvers and repositories. Group two: presets, agents, agents-2, codex-oauth, provisioning-400, drafts-kept and repository-dedicated. Both ran on the PR head after merging main.
- **Mutants:** 4 of 4 product mutants of `apps/controller/src/console/agents/create.mts` are killed:
  - **M1** drops `configurationId` from the Agent create body. `createAgentThroughForm`'s status check fails and prints the API's 400 (drafts-kept, repository-dedicated).
  - **M2** labels a queued job "Provisioning Agent…" (finding 1424). The label test on `routeProvisioningJob` fails.
  - **M3** skips the handed-off deployment read. All three quota and named-wait tests on `routeProvisioningJob` fail (agents-2 and provisioning-400).
  - **M4** keeps a draft after a failed job that names its Agent. The drafts-kept test on `routeProvisioningJob(page, work, [...])` fails.

## Risks

Test-only. The two browser lanes run these files. Files held by #3734 and #3746 were not touched, so no merge conflicts with them are expected. The ranking of the remaining duplication clusters and why they were left: `clusters.md` in the workspace analysis (not in this repo).

A wrong passphrase or locked master password stops the import before anything is written. Version-1 files still import.

author: amanthanvi
body:
## Summary

D26 step 9.3, the third step of the Settings lane: search. A **Search settings** field at the right end of the Settings header (Ctrl+F from anywhere in the window) narrows every page to the settings whose name, label, caption, help or keywords contain every word typed. `@modified` narrows it to the settings 9.2 marks as differing from their defaults, alone or with words (`@modified font`). The header line under the page title says how many settings match, and screen readers hear it as a polite live region once typing pauses. Enter in the field goes to the first setting found, and Escape in the field clears it.

### Design choices

- **Results stay on their pages.** Every page is filtered, and each page's rail button shows how many settings the search found there (a number drawn on the button, its label dimmed at zero, and its UIA `ItemStatus`: "2 settings found" / "no settings found"). The shown page does not change while you type. Why not one list across sections:
  - one list would need every section's rows at once and a heading per section. The windows of all sections plus a Reset button for every changed row is past the USER budget, which 9.2 left with no room;
  - switching pages under the keyboard while typing moves what the user is reading, and a first visit to a page makes its windows inside the keystroke;
  - per keystroke the cost is matching every row plus laying out the one shown page and showing or hiding what changes on it.
- **An empty page says where to look.** A page with nothing found shows, in place of its rows, "Nothing on this page matches "clip". Found on Terminal (2), Privacy (4). Enter in the search field goes to the first, or choose a page on the left." With no match anywhere it says what the search looks in and how to clear it. The spoken header line names the first page with matches too ("6 settings match: none on this page, 2 on Terminal.").
- **Keywords come from the field descriptors** (`win32_settings_fields.zig`): the name the command palette gives the field and the palette's keywords, less the three words every palette entry starts with ("settings preferences configuration"), which would make "settings" find every row. The two button rows (Keybindings, Advanced) got keywords of their own. Matching is case-insensitive for ASCII letters and needs every word, each anywhere in the row's text.
- **`@modified` uses 9.2's `rowDiffersFromDefault`**, including for pages whose rows have not been made yet. Its list is taken when the search runs (typing in the field, or a page being shown): an edit, a reset, Discard or a reload leaves the rows where they are, so a row never disappears under the user.

### The change

1. **Room for the field** (first commit). The search field is one more window in every state, so room had to be won permanently; creating hidden windows lazily does not lower the worst case, which shows them. Two windows that are never shown together became one each:
   - the status line's window also says the close prompt's question, and gets the status line back, with whatever changed meanwhile, when the prompt goes;
   - one "Discard changes" serves the action bar and the close prompt. While the prompt is up it moves after "Save and close" in z-order (which is Tab order) and carries the prompt's own id, so it acts as the prompt's Discard; when the prompt goes it moves back after "Use disk" and takes the bar's id again. A UIA Invoke posts its click with the id the button has at that moment, so an Invoke queued on the bar's Discard before the prompt opened cannot confirm the prompt (Greptile caught that the merged button allowed it).
2. **The filter** is `formItems()`: while a search is typed it returns the shown page's found rows. Layout, visibility, the Reset buttons and their pool, the markers, the clip flags and the row hit-tests all read it, so hidden rows leave the Tab order, the arrow-key groups and the UIA tree with their windows.
3. **The field** is a text field like the form's (`makeEdit`, `settingsEditProc`'s frame, themed colours, a cue banner "Search settings (Ctrl+F)"), first in the Tab order, a group of its own, with a `SettingsControlProvider` (Edit, "Search settings", HelpText) and the same MSAA name.
4. **Keys** go through `handleAccelerator`, ahead of `IsDialogMessageW`:
   - Ctrl+F (not Ctrl+Shift+F or AltGr) focuses the field and selects its text. Only keys for the Settings window reach this, so the terminal's own bindings do not change.
   - Enter in the field focuses the first enabled setting found, on the shown page or else on the first page in rail order. A setting Windows does not support is passed over; a page whose found settings are all unsupported gives the focus to its rail button. With `@modified`, a page the last counts named but that has nothing by the time Enter gets there sends it on to the next page with a match, and with none left the focus stays in the field.
   - Escape in a non-empty field clears it. In an empty field, or while the close prompt is up, Escape does what it does elsewhere in Settings.
   - Ctrl+F and Enter clear `UISF_HIDEFOCUS` (`WM_CHANGEUISTATE`): the dialog manager never sees them as navigation keys, so the field Enter focuses would otherwise show no focus rectangle.
5. **The count** is the header line (`searchSummaryText`), made a `live_text` provider (LiveSetting Polite), announced through `events.zig` 500 ms after the last change (`search_announce_timer_id`), and not when Enter has moved the focus. The rail's counts are `SettingsSectionProvider.setSearchCount`.
6. **Jumps that must show a field** (the palette's `openField`, Save or Save and close with a value Settings will not take, `revealControl`) drop a search that hides it. They ask the search as it is now (`searchFinds`), not the last pass, and the drop makes no layout of its own: the page switch lays out and paints once, and moves the focus once (`showSection(.., focus_follows)`). A caller that asks for a page itself (`openSection`: the palette's Config problems opens Advanced) drops a search outright, whether or not it finds rows there, since a page cut down by an earlier search, or one that only says nothing on it matches, is not the page asked for. It moves the focus to the rail button before the switch, so the focus moves once.
7. **One paint per search pass** (last commit, adopted at the lead's request after the 200-row measurement below found the pass over budget). `runSearch` turns the viewport's drawing off (`WM_SETREDRAW`, `suspendViewportRedraw`) while the Reset pool, the layout and the visibility pass move, show and hide rows; a deferred `resumeViewportRedraw` turns it back on and invalidates the whole viewport, its frame and children included, before the pass's existing `RDW_UPDATENOW`. Only the call that turned drawing off turns it on, and the `defer` covers every path out of the block. While drawing is off no window in the viewport counts as visible, so the focus check moved ahead of the pass: `keepFocusShown` now asks which rows the search shows (`activeFormRows`) and moves the focus from a row it is about to hide to the search field. That also fixes a dead end the old check had: Windows hands the focus of a hidden field to its parent, the viewport, which the old check (after the pass, by `IsWindowVisible`) did not look at, so a search changed while a row had the focus (UIA can set the field's value) left the focus where no key reaches. A focused Reset button of a hidden row now goes to the search field too, not the rail.

Docs: `docs/windows.md`, `docs/windows-capability-matrix.md`, `docs/accessibility-inventory.md`, `docs/accessibility-matrix.md` (a "Settings search" row with what was measured). Test pins: `Contracts.50-Accessibility.ps1` (the header's descriptor ids) and `interactive-win11-accessibility.ps1` (each page's controls) now include the search field and the merged Discard.

## Validation

- **Full suite (local, under the loc

body:
[VXG RealForever]

# Interface Refinement V4 — ordinary Browser Conversation rollover-plan composition

PR #938 accepted the effect-free V4 continuity-rollover planner as current source. This slice composes that accepted planner into the ordinary Browser Conversation path without introducing checkpoint persistence or successor-lease effects.

## Why this slice exists

Current source already has the exact ingredients, but they stop one boundary short of composition:

```text
Browser Prompt Context Runtime
  -> exact per-turn Context Lease
  -> exact read-only Continuity Stream projection

Lived Companion
  -> independently validates the projection at provider boundary
  -> returns the prompt materialization receipt

Browser server
  -> resolves exact Companion availability
  -> projects V3 resource/context pressure

accepted V4 planner
  -> pressure + exact continuity projection
  -> effect-free continuity rollover plan
```

The missing product seam is carrying the already-validated continuity projection through the completed turn **in memory only**, then composing the V3 pressure projection with that exact object.

## Candidate behavior

For the ordinary durable Conversation route:

1. Browser Companion captures the exact `selected.continuityProjection` that formed the consumed prompt materialization.
2. The returned receipt must bind the same projection ref + semantic fingerprint.
3. The projection is carried transiently on the bridge result and is never written into Home events/context/head records.
4. `serve-browser-core` strips that internal field before HTTP/NDJSON output.
5. After V3 pressure is formed, the server calls accepted `formContinuityRolloverPlan({ resourceContextPressure, continuityStream })`.
6. The public turn carries `resourceContextPressure` and `continuityRolloverPlan`, but not the internal projection body.

Fresh first turns remain truthful:

```text
no prior completed head
-> promptContextMaterialization = null
-> no pressure projection
-> no rollover plan
```

Context-bearing turns compose:

```text
current prompt receipt + exact continuity projection
-> current pressure
-> NO_ACTION_REQUIRED | CHECKPOINT_READY | ROLLOVER_READY | HELD_*
```

## Boundaries

```text
PROMPT_CONTINUITY_PROJECTION != HOME_PERSISTENCE
PRESSURE_OBSERVATION != CHECKPOINT_EFFECT
ROLLOVER_PLAN != SUCCESSOR_CONTEXT_LEASE
CHECKPOINT_PLAN != CHECKPOINT_PERSISTENCE
CHECKPOINT != SEMANTIC_MEMORY_PROMOTION
RESOURCE_ATTENTION != PROCESS_KILL_AUTHORITY
```

This slice performs no checkpoint persistence, Context Lease issuance, semantic Memory acceptance, cleanup/process kill, model/training/weight, or publication effect beyond this source candidate itself.

## Exact source membrane

Authored:
- `src/core/browser-companion-bridge.mjs`
- `scripts/serve-browser-core.mjs`
- `test/browser-companion-bridge.test.mjs`
- `blueprint/module-registry/browser-prompt-context-runtime.json`
- `test/browser-prompt-context-runtime.test.mjs`

Generated Source Manifest buckets:
- `source-manifest-parts/bucket-92.json`
- `source-manifest-parts/bucket-3b.json`
- `source-manifest-parts/bucket-dd.json`
- `source-manifest-parts/bucket-8a.json`
- `source-manifest-parts/bucket-a4.json`

Accepted V4 planning source: `github.commit.vexlife.96f95d57857423d8e4ea554cad28a77d216b1d7d`.
V3 lived product evidence remains `artifact.vexlife.interface-refinement.v3.lived-pressure.a005.return.sha256.1812d529d99ad89b368e84939835f355065adcb6d96d6c7bda5d975edb6ff6f3`.

<!-- [VXG RealForever][VEXLIFE][INTERFACE-REFINEMENT][V4][BROWSER-ROLLOVER-COMPOSITION][A006] -->


## Formation recovery

A001 stopped before source mutation because its Relay WRITE operations omitted the SDK-required `lineEndingInvariant: true` declaration for multiline `REPLACE_TEXT`. A002 corrected that invariant but stopped before inner task formation because a stale copied SDK blob literal falsely reported source drift. A003 replaced per-file SDK blob constants with one exact provider-observed SDK commit, then exposed a stale PR-body member digest before inner task formation. A004 derived the PR-body digest from exact copied bytes and entered source mutation, then stopped on an ambiguous bridge preimage. A005 narrowed that preimage and reached focused product proof: 55 of 58 tests passed, including the new V4 server pressure→rollover composition test, all V4 planner tests, and all V3 pressure tests.

The three A005 failures shared one exact cause. `materializeLivedCompanionPromptContext(...)` is async. Accepted source previously returned its Promise directly from an async helper, so async-return flattening yielded the exact WeakMap-keyed materialization object. A005 wrapped that unresolved Promise inside `{ materialization, continuityProjection }`, so Lived Companion received a Promise instead of the exact in-process materialization capability and rejected it with `prompt-context inference requires the exact in-process materialization capability`.

A006 changes only that source semantic: `await materializeLivedCompanionPromptContext(...)` before forming the wrapper. The non-enumerable continuity-projection boundary, server ref/fingerprint cross-check, V3 pressure composition, accepted V4 planner call, and all held effect boundaries remain unchanged. No prior attempt produced a committed or remote V4 Browser composition candidate.

body:
## What changed and why

Settings › Accounts › Azure (1.0 slice S1b, the Accounts board's Azure group).

- **One row per tenant**, built from the Key Vaults of their own plus `az account list`:
  - the tenant's name (`tenantDisplayName`, sanitized), or its id while not signed in;
  - the saved vaults by subscription ("Example Production · 2 vaults").
- **A signed-in tenant** shows ● Signed in and Choose Vaults…. Any other tenant shows "Not signed in" with `az login --tenant <id>` and Copy. The tenant id is used only after `isValidTenantID`; otherwise plain `az login`.
- **Sign out of Azure:** an `az logout` row with Copy, then a Check Again note.
- **No user name or email** is ever shown or kept: decoding never reads `user`.
- **Choose Vaults…** is Connect Azure's list for one tenant in a sheet. `AzureVaultChoicesView` is shared with Connect. Vaults already in FX Vault are shown checked and disabled, and are never imported again.
- **Lock:** a lock resets the group and closes the sheet. An import in progress is cancelled. The import compares `lockCount`, so a quick unlock doesn't import the rest, and a sheet opened later is left alone.
- **Display names:** subscription and tenant names are sanitized (`DisplayNameSanitizer`: no control, bidi or invisible characters) at decode, and also when stored.
- **Shared pieces:**
  - `CommandRow` gets an inline style with a Copied state, so there is one command row everywhere;
  - `CommandCheckSteps` (the note, an optional command, Check Again) is used by `GHLoginSteps` and by Azure.
- **No new az command:** Settings runs only `az account list`, and the sheet runs Connect's existing `az keyvault list`.

## Decisions

- A signed-in tenant with no saved vault is listed, so Choose Vaults… works after onboarding.
- Only Key Vaults of their own count, not a repository's runtime destinations.
- Vaults are grouped by subscription id.
- Choose Vaults… starts with nothing checked.

## Tests

- New tests:
  - app: `AzureAccountsTests` (the group, lock, a lock during Add Vaults, the tenant id check, the subscription grouping);
  - package: `AzureDiscoveryTests` (tenant and subscription names cleaned), `DestinationRepositoryTests` (a stored name cleaned);
  - UI: `AccountsUITests.testChooseVaultsAddsAVaultOfTheSignedInTenant`.
- Seen failing before each fix:
  - the tenant-name parsing;
  - the saved-vault guard;
  - the lock during an import (3 issues);
  - both name sanitizations;
  - the tenant id check.
- The UI test failed in the first run: the Sign out row's id hid its children's ids. It now uses `.accessibilityElement(children: .contain)`.

## Waivers, parity, contract

- No waivers. Manual check: RELEASING.md #69.
- Parity: FX Vault is macOS only.
- Contract: no change.

## What was run

- `xcodebuild test`: AzureAccountsTests, ConnectAzureTests, AccountsSettingsViewModelTests, MainWindowLayoutTests, PreferencesViewModelTests and ConnectViewModelTests. 69 passed.
- `swift test` (the whole package): 0 failures.
- `xcodebuild test -scheme FXVaultUITests`: AccountsUITests 2/2 and SettingsUITests 3/3.

body:
## Pourquoi

Clément a demandé si le QR pouvait être « un peu stylisé ». Le 25 octobre, la forme actuelle avait été gardée sans être mesurée. Cette fois, la mesure a été faite.

**Le banc d'essai**
- 20 formes, chacune avec 8 liens, sur t-shirt noir et blanc.
- 9 situations : de près, de 1 à 4 m, de biais, sur un pli, sur un pli fort, dans la pénombre.
- Au total 2 880 images, passées dans 5 lecteurs : jsQR (celui du projet), ZXing C++ et ZXing JS, OpenCV, WeChat.

**Les résultats**
- **Fluide** (modules reliés) : les 5 lecteurs le lisent aussi bien que les carrés arrondis.
- **Yeux ronds, en feuille ou en galet** : OpenCV ne les trouve plus (0 à 4 %). Même un peu plus arrondis qu'aujourd'hui, il recule (66 %, puis 40 %, puis 8 %, contre 90 %). Les yeux restent donc tels quels.
- **Écartés** : la pupille ronde (jsQR à 50 %) ; les points, perles et barres (jsQR échoue de près : 0 à 38 %).

Choix de Clément : « Fluide ».

## Ce qui change

- **`generate-qr-svg`** : nouvelle forme `fluid`, désormais le défaut.
  - Les modules sont soudés à leurs voisins.
  - Seuls les coins extérieurs sont arrondis (0,35 module), et les angles intérieurs sont adoucis d'un congé du même rayon.
  - Le tout forme un seul tracé, donc sans liseré entre deux modules.
  - `shape: 'squares'` garde les carrés arrondis.
  - Les yeux et le ( • ) ne changent pas.
- **La forme de tous les t-shirts**
  - `QR_STYLES` contient `fluid` (le défaut), plus les trois formes d'avant, qui restent pour les commandes déjà passées.
  - `QR_STYLE_SHAPES` remplace `QR_STYLE_CORNER`.
  - Le sélecteur de forme n'était plus affiché nulle part : il est retiré.
  - Une réimpression garde la forme de sa commande (fulfillment).
- **Migration 076**
  - La contrainte `orders_qr_style_valid` accepte `fluid`, qui devient la valeur par défaut de `orders.qr_style`.
  - `schema_version()` passe à 76.
  - Si la 076 n'est pas appliquée : le paiement retombe sur `rounded` au lieu d'échouer, Sentry le signale, et /admin affiche « migration 076 à appliquer ».
  - Ajoutée aussi à `verify-migrations.sql`, à `fresh-setup.sql` (76 migrations) et à DEPLOY_CHECKLIST.
- **Fichiers refaits**
  - `public/print` : `qr-back-{dark,light}.svg` et la feuille de test A4.
  - Les photos du dos de la boutique : le QR fluide est posé à la même place et avec la même encre, et se lit (vérifié).
  - Sur Vercel, le cache des images optimisées dépend du contenu du fichier : les nouvelles photos s'affichent dès le déploiement.
- **Docs** : MISE_EN_PRODUCTION (076) et TESTER_DE_A_A_Z (la forme n'est plus choisie à l'achat).

## Tests

- **Lecture** (`qr-decode`) :
  - 12 liens courts lus sur les deux t-shirts ;
  - lecture à 5 pixels par module (environ 2,5 m pour le QR de 25 cm) ;
  - aucun liseré entre deux modules voisins. Le test a un témoin : des carrés séparés, même sans écart, en laissent un ;
  - yeux et ( • ) identiques à avant ;
  - les formes d'avant se lisent toujours.
- **Paiement**
  - Unitaire : la commande reçoit `fluid` ; sans la 076, elle passe en `rounded` et Sentry est prévenu.
  - Intégration sur une vraie base : la base accepte `fluid` et le donne par défaut ; `dots` est refusé ; avec l'ancienne contrainte, la commande passe en `rounded`.
- **Autres** : /admin (076 absente, signalée) ; fulfillment (forme de la commande).
- **En local**
  - 1 524 tests unitaires passent (dont 3 de moins dans `security-client`, qui passait en revue le sélecteur retiré).
  - 182 tests d'intégration passent.
  - 97 tests E2E passent.
  - Une base neuve reçoit les 76 migrations, et le contrôle SQL de la 076 donne `t | t | 76`.

## Après la fusion

- Appliquer la migration 076 avant la commande d'essai.
- Les fichiers d'essai Printful (dos A et B) sont refaits avec le QR fluide (hors du dépôt).

author: simonvanlierde
body:
Most strings, keys above all, end before a 16-byte block can start, so they went byte by byte through a `match` with a dialect check in each arm. This swaps that for a 256-entry byte-class table, like serde_json's `ESCAPE` table.

- Each string builds a mask of the classes it stops at: its quote, a backslash, a line break, a control character outside JSON5, and past-ASCII bytes when that rule is on. A plain byte then costs one load and one test.
- The first 16 bytes go through the table, and only a string that is still plain after them reaches the block compare.
- Output is byte for byte the same on the 438 corpus files in every dialect, with text and json output.

| callgrind instructions | main | this PR | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8.9 MB generated pretty JSON through `check` | 338.5M | 292.8M | -13.5% |
| 10,000 small config documents of short strings, one `check` each | 609.0M | 559.1M | -8.2% |
| one array of 20,000 strings of 70 to 250 bytes | 81.6M | 81.3M | -0.3% |
| `bench` cases | | | -2.0% (json5) to -7.5% (config file) |

Wall time, `hyperfine -N` medians of 30 runs on one pinned core, load under 0.9:

| file | main | this PR | change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 9 MB of short keys and values | 27.49 ms | 25.27 ms | -8% |
| `\u` escapes | 10.31 ms | 9.27 ms | -10% |
| strings of 40 escapes | 6.91 ms | 5.41 ms | -22% |
| JSON5 strings with a tab every 8 bytes | 6.41 ms | 4.83 ms | -25% |
| 8.7 MB pretty JSON | 24.06 ms | 23.44 ms | -2.6%, within noise |
| 5,000-character strings | 8.13 ms | 8.14 ms | 0% |

The `scripts/bench.py` cases land between +0.1% and -6%, so the 5% in ADR 0004 holds on string-heavy files only. I've kept it on that basis and written it into the ADR: past 5% on one kind of file counts, as long as no other kind gets slower.

Tests: a unit test for where the scan stops for every byte class in every dialect, and one that a raw CR or LF in a JSON5 string is an error (both failed with CR dropped from the table). A third runs every ASCII character plus `é`, U+FFFE and U+10FFFF through short and long strings in every dialect, so a table entry with no match arm hits the `debug_assert`; it failed with DEL marked as a control character. `just check` passes, and the `check` fuzz target ran for an hour without a crash.

author: jasperblues
body:
Fixes #342. Port of liberation-data/drivine4j#294.

Oracle's `SIGN` gives 0 for a positive number from 1.0E-130 up to just under 1.0E-128. On Oracle that made `sign(1.0E-129)` give 0 where Neo4j gives 1, and `round(1.0E-129, 2, 'UP')` give 0.0 where Neo4j gives 0.01.

The fix adds a `signOf(number)` hook, `SIGN(n)` by default, which both `roundTo` and `sign()` now use. Oracle's version is `SIGN(GREATEST(LEAST(n, 1), -1) * 1000)`:
- The number is clamped to [-1, 1] first, so the ×1000 can't overflow.
- That puts a tiny positive number at 1E-127 or more, where SIGN is right.
- 0 stays 0 and null stays null.
- The number is read only once.

Postgres compiles exactly as on master; 33 statements were compared byte for byte.

**Tests:** `CypherSpec.spec.ts` runs drivine4j's assertions on Postgres and Oracle, with every value checked on Neo4j. They fail on Oracle without the fix. They cover:
- every mode, and `sign()`, on numbers near 1.0E-129;
- the same numbers read from a row and under an aggregate;
- numbers near NUMBER's maximum.

`CompiledSize.spec.ts` checks that a nested `sign()` compiles to about the size of `ceil()`.

author: adalinxx
body:
- **Header-rule exclusions (§9.9):** a block whose `spec` or `prevState` breaks the header rule is weighed and excluded in the same step (`HeaderBad`). The new model `MCHierarchy_HeaderBad.cfg` shows two effects:
  - a header-excluded carrier still credits its child;
  - a header-excluded child stops the canonical descent.

  New invariants: `HeaderExcludedOnAdmission` and `NothingValidatedBelowExcluded`.
- **Declared prevState:** each block's declared prevState is now a constant (`PrevState`). A carrier that breaks the prevState rule anchors the child it commits at the state it declared (§5.3 step 3), not at its parent's. The review of adalinxx/Lattice#38 found this: the model had assumed every anchor was the carrier's parent.
- **Three-level traces:** `TraceHierarchy` and `hierarchy_trace_check.py` now replay three chains. The replay compares both lower chains' continuity and each admission's header-exclusion flag. All 20 traces from adalinxx/Lattice#38 at `8c60c39` conform: 2,400 events, 59 header-excluded admissions, and merged grinds on every proof path. The self-test adds three corruptions, all caught. Planted model bugs fail the traces:
  - with no recursion, 6 of 20 fail;
  - with the header exclusion recorded only after execution, 20 of 20 fail.
- **`NothingStuck`** (Hierarchy and ForkChoice): no reachable state is stuck with a fact undelivered, so the quiescence oracles can no longer pass vacuously. The planted bug where a header-rule violation is dropped instead of weighed survived `ExpectedAnswer` until this was added.

Locally: 9 models pass, all 20 mutants are killed, the 2-level and 3-level traces conform, and both self-tests pass.

author: serhii-chernenko
body:
Fixes the false positives that the delta verification of #534 found (NEW-2 and NEW-3) and the residual #11 normalisation gaps. It also makes the 422 for an entry whose saved text a rule now rejects explain itself. There are no migrations and no schema changes.

### NEW-3: card separators

`/` and `_` now count only inside a whole, isolated card layout: 4-4-4-4 (up to 19 digits) or the 4-6-5 Amex layout, with the same separator throughout. The number must still pass Luhn and start with 2-6. Commas are no longer card separators. Spaces, dots and hyphens work as before the audit.

I measured this with the verifier's method: random inputs, 5000 trials each, run through `detectNeverStore`.

| Input | Before (#534) | After |
|---|---|---|
| 6 comma-joined ints 0-9999 | 19.5% | 0.0% |
| 6 comma-joined 4-digit numbers | 15.2% | 0.0% |
| 6 comma-and-space-joined 4-digit numbers | 15.7% | 0.0% |
| 16-digit numbers with comma thousands | 15.2% | 0.0% |
| 3 y/m/d dates | 32.1% | 0.0% |
| 3 zero-padded y/mm/dd dates | 39.3% | 0.0% |
| 4 space-separated 4-digit numbers | 5.9% | 6.1% (a real card layout, unchanged since before the audit) |

Every original evasion dummy is still blocked: Arabic-Indic digits, `/` and `_` cards, dotted and slashed IBAN/NRB, spaced PESEL, NIP after the keyword and in 3-2-2-3 groups, AWS secret, `hasło to`, `password for my bank is`. A 4-6-5 Amex written with slashes is also caught. The one change in behavior: `4111,1111,1111,1111` (a comma-separated card) is now allowed.

### NEW-2: topical false positives

- **Street rule:** it now needs a house number plus a capitalised street name, checked on a case-preserving view. An address cue also counts: "my address:", "I live at", "mieszkam przy" followed by a capitalised name, "мешкаю за адресою", or the `ul.`/`вул.` abbreviations.
- **Status terms:** permit, temporary protection, refugee status, green card, visa status, immigration status and asylum terms need a first-person or possessive status statement, for example "my work permit expires" or "I have temporary protection". The Polish and Ukrainian status terms follow the same rule.
- **Criminal records:** these terms need a possessive or "has a criminal record". Narrowed the same way: the standalone "convicted of", Polish "karalność" and Ukrainian "судимість".

All of the verifier's ordinary strings now pass: "I walked 5 miles down main street", "2 blocks from Wall Street", "Wants a work permit template for building site", "Reads a book about criminal records", "temporary protection for the plant", "visa status check app". Every true positive from the previous spec still fails. New true positives were added as well: "My work permit expires in March", "I have temporary protection in Poland", "Lives on 12 High Road, London", "Mieszkam przy Długiej 4", "Мешкаю за адресою Шевченка 5".

### #11: classifier residuals

- Accents are now stripped from Latin letters after decomposition, so `diabétes` is caught, precomposed or decomposed. Polish diacritic letters and Cyrillic letters (`й`, `ї`) are kept.
- Look-alikes inside a mixed-script word are folded to the word's main script in both directions: `hіv` with a Cyrillic `і`, `prеgnаnt` with Cyrillic letters, and `дiабет` as before.
- The `heroinę` escape still works: `Brał heroinę` is blocked and `Heroine of the story` is allowed.

### Entries whose saved text a rule now rejects

Every write is still checked, so editing such an entry is a 422, even for a title-only change.

- The `why` names the match and says it is in the text already saved in the entry.
- The `fix` says to edit the saved text, or to cancel and delete the entry.
- The 422 message and the copy for an edit that adds the flagged text itself are unchanged.
- Delete never runs the gate.
- The DetailModal already renders `message`, `why` and `fix`. A spec confirms the new copy shows and that Delete is one Cancel away.

### Specs

- `tests/unit/utils/memory/compliance-evasion.spec.ts`:
  - The verifier's exact false-positive strings are negatives.
  - A deterministic, seeded 2000-trial generator per number-list shape asserts 0 flags. Nine cases failed with the #534 separators.
  - New tables for the topical and classifier positives and negatives, and for the folding helpers.
- `tests/unit/utils/memory/entries.spec.ts`: the saved-text 422 copy for a never-store kind and for a sensitive topic, the edit that removes the text succeeds, delete always works, and the plain copy is kept when the edit adds the text.
- `tests/unit/components/Profile/Memory/Entries/DetailModal.spec.ts`: the UI shows the new copy, and Delete is reachable after Cancel.

### Checks

- `pnpm run format`: 0 errors.
- `pnpm run typecheck`: clean.
- Full `pnpm vitest run`: 568 files, 12502 tests passed.
- `docs/memory-architecture.md` 3.17 has a follow-up note.

body:
Stacked on #268. Merge that first, and GitHub will retarget this PR to `main`.

## Summary
Applies the rules of thumb now written up in `docs/backend-dev.md` ("Large records: group or build").

**Group related fields**
- `GetProfileContestListsResult` takes two `ContestPage(contests, total, pages, from, to)` values instead of ten positional fields. `ContestPage.of` owns the page arithmetic that was previously written out twice. The controller keeps its model attribute names, so the template is unchanged.
- The five `renew*` fields duplicated on `ContestSummary` and `PrivateContestRowDto` become one shared `usecase/contest/shared/RenewalOptions`. It also replaces the private `RenewalInfo` copy in `GetUserContestSummaryUseCase`. `contest/index.html` and `profile/my-contests.html` now read `row.renewal.*`.

**`@Builder` on wide records** (8+ components with a run of 3+ same-typed neighbours), with every positional `new` call converted, tests included:
`MatchSyncResult`, `GetLeaderboardResult`, `LatestResultResponse`, `ContestSummary`, `PrivateContestRowDto`, `GeneralContestRowDto`, `ContestPreviewDto`, `SegmentNodeDto`, `ContestSupport.SprintOption`, `LeaderboardEntryDto`, `AdminMatchesData.MatchEntry`, `WhatIfRecap.Line`, `WhatIfMatchDto`, `SeasonPhase`, `RoundResultsPayload` (+ `SprintPlacement`, `SeasonPlacement`), `SegmentResultsPayload` (+ `SegmentPlacement`).

`MatchSyncSchedulerTest` shows the payoff: its `// allMatchesComplete` comments, which only existed to label positional booleans, are replaced by a shared `lockedResult()` builder base.

**Left as they are:** records with no same-typed runs (`GetPrivateContestResult`, `GetPredictionResult`, `FinalTableLeaderboardData`, `GetRoundAdvancementStatusResult`), the football-data `MatchDto` (it mirrors the external API), and private pipeline `Ctx` records.

The JSON shape is unchanged everywhere. `@Builder` only adds a static factory, and the grouped records are rendered by Thymeleaf only.

## Not in this PR
`GetUserContestSummaryUseCase.resolveRenewalOptions` repeats the current-season branch of `GetContestRenewalOptionsUseCase`. Merging the two changes behaviour, so it should be a separate change.

## Test plan
- [x] `mvn test` (api): 1288 tests, 0 failures

Each of these returned 200 with no template or log errors: `/contests`, `/profile/my-contests`, contest detail, join preview, `/leaderboard`, `/api/contests/main/leaderboard`, latest-result banner, `/admin/matches/data`, what-if

body: ## What was blocked Search Console (domain property `doubleyellowsquash.com`, 26 Oct 2026) reports one URL as **Blocked by robots.txt**. That URL is `https://www.doubleyellowsquash.com/booking/success`. Googlebot’s rules on both the apex and www `robots.txt` files disallow only: - `/admin/` - `/en/admin/` - `/booking/success` - `/en/booking/success` The other Page indexing rows (14 not found, 6 redirects, 3 canonical alternates, 1 crawled currently not indexed) are URLs Google was able to fetch, so this is not a sitewide block. The public booking page loads the BookingGood embed, and that document publishes `bookingSuccessRedirectUrl` as `https://www.doubleyellowsquash.com/booking/success`. That is the one disallowed URL Google can discover. Admin is not linked from the sitemap or public pages. The confirmation page is a real public URL (HTTP 200) and should stay out of the index. Bulgarian and English versions already send ``. A `Disallow` stops Google from seeing that tag, so the URL stays on “Blocked by robots.txt”. ## What changed Removed the `Disallow` lines for `/booking/success` and `/en/booking/success`. `Allow: /` is unchanged, so Bulgarian and English public pages stay crawlable, including `/booking` and `/en/booking`. `/admin/` and `/en/admin/` stay disallowed. Local `robots.txt` after the change: ``` User-Agent: * Allow: / Disallow: /admin/ Disallow: /en/admin/ Host: https://www.doubleyellowsquash.com Sitemap: https://www.doubleyellowsquash.com/sitemap.xml ``` ## Left alone - Admin paths stay blocked on purpose. They are not public pages. - Cloudflare still prepends its managed block (training crawlers, `Google-Extended`, `GoogleOther`, and others, each `Disallow: /`). That comes from Cloudflare Bot Preference Sync, not this repo, and those rules do not apply to Googlebot. They are not the one blocked URL. - The sitemap lists 42 public Bulgarian and English URLs. None of them are disallowed, and it does not list the confirmation page. No sitemap change. - Did not chase the 14 historical 404s, the 6 redirects, the 3 “alternative page with proper canonical tag” URLs, or the 1 “crawled - currently not indexed” URL. None of those match a path we disallow. ## After merge and deploy This PR does not change the live site. Merge it and let GitHub Actions deploy, then in Search Console for the domain property **doubleyellowsquash.com**: 1. Open **Page indexing**. 2. Open **Blocked by robots.txt**. 3. Click **Validate fix**. After Google recrawls `https://www.doubleyellowsquash.com/booking/success`, that row should clear. The page should then be excluded by its noindex tag, not indexed.

body:
p1-expense-claims task 6.1 (FR-AP-17; UC-EXP-03; design D8). Cash advances are recorded under "Payment batches" (the owner's decision of 26 Oct 2026, rev 0.148).

## What changes

- **Posting rule `cash_advance@1`** (LEDGER-38):
  - An advance posts Dr the advances account · Cr the money account.
  - The advances account comes from the new setting `claims.advances_account`: 1250, under dual control. Its guide section is compiled into `kb/`.
  - The refund posts the other way, with an allocation to the advance. It takes If-Match with the advance's ETag, and refunds at most what is open (CLAIM-30).
- **Recording and voiding (Payment batches):**
  - `recordCashAdvance` and `recordCashAdvanceRefund` record by hand.
  - `voidCashAdvance` voids with a reversing entry. In Founder mode, voiding needs another person's approval: `requestCashAdvanceVoid`, approval object `cash_advance.void` (CLAIM-33).
  - An advance that claims or refunds have settled is not voided (CLAIM-31).
- **Reading (Expense claims):**
  - `listCashAdvances` and `getCashAdvance` are read under "Expense claims". An Employee sees only their own.
  - Each shows what claims settled, what was refunded and what is open.
  - ⚠ shows when an advance is still open more than the claim deadline after it was paid.
- **A claim settles an advance** (`advance_id`):
  - It settles the least of its total and what is open on the advance, credited to 1250. The rest is owed on 2150 and reimbursed.
  - The allocation is recorded when the claim posts, with the advance locked.
  - The approval envelope carries the split, so if it changes, a pending request goes void.
- **Bank import** matches a bank line to an advance or a refund, as money recorded by hand.
- **Replay** reproduces advances, refunds and claims that settle an advance (ENG-06).
- **Migrations 000168/000169:**
  - `allocation_guard` lets a claim or a refund settle an advance (FY171).
  - `bank_match_posting` accepts `cash_advance` (FY228).

author: frevan14
body: ## Description Brancher le front web sur l'API d'authentification réelle (`POST /register`, `POST /login`, `POST /logout`) et faire arriver l'utilisateur connecté sur la page principale. * Page principale `/app` : en-tête avec navigation, nom du compte et déconnexion, puis tableau de bord en quatre blocs (tournois en direct, mes pronostics, classement général, mes groupes). Les blocs affichent « Bientôt disponible » en attendant les API correspondantes, sans données simulées. * Inscription : seul un statut 201 est accepté comme succès. Un autre 2xx (proxy mal ciblé, ancien squelette de l'API) est traité comme une erreur inattendue, ce qui évite un faux « Compte créé ». Les erreurs 400 sont rattachées aux champs (`errors`), le 409 signale le nom d'utilisateur déjà pris. * Connexion : 401 → « identifiants incorrects », 400 → erreurs par champ, autres erreurs → message inattendu. Suppression du message « connexion pas encore disponible ». * Redirection : après connexion, retour vers la page visée avant la connexion, sinon vers `/app`. Un utilisateur déjà connecté qui ouvre `/login` ou `/register` est renvoyé vers `/app` (nouveau `GuestRoute`). * Déconnexion : appel à `POST /logout` pour révoquer le refresh token côté serveur. La session locale est fermée immédiatement et un échec de la révocation ne bloque pas la déconnexion. * Tests (53 au total) : statut 201 attendu, erreurs 400/401/500, révocation à la déconnexion (y compris en cas d'échec), redirections `GuestRoute` / `ProtectedRoute`, page principale et en-tête. * Mise à jour de `web/README.md` (contrat d'API, redirections, limites de session). Known limitations: * Les tokens sont gardés en mémoire uniquement : un rechargement de la page déconnecte l'utilisateur. `POST /refresh` existe côté API mais n'est pas encore utilisé par le front. La persistance de session reste à trancher (cookie httpOnly posé par l'API, ou stockage navigateur). * Les blocs du tableau de bord sont des états vides tant que les API de tournois, pronostics, classements et groupes ne sont pas livrées. * Pas d'audit d'accessibilité automatisé (axe / Lighthouse) pour l'instant. Closes #33 ## Composants touchés - [ ] backend - [ ] db (migrations) - [x] web - [ ] mobile - [ ] deploy (Helm / Ansible) - [ ] docs ## Vérifications - [x] Tests ajoutés ou mis à jour - [ ] `make lint` et `make test` passent en local - [x] Aucun secret dans le diff - [x] Documentation / ADR mis à jour si nécessaire

body:
## Type of Change

<!-- Put an `x` in the boxes that apply -->

- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Enhancement
- [ ] Refactoring
- [x] Dependency updates
- [ ] Documentation
- [x] CI/CD

## Description

Moves CI and local development off Node 20, which is end-of-life and has no patched release, onto patched Node 24 (24.22.1). `.nvmrc` is now the single place to set the Node version.

**`.nvmrc` as the source of truth**
- Added `.nvmrc` with `24.22.1`. Running `nvm use` / `nvm install` in the repo picks it up.
- All workflows now use `actions/setup-node` with `node-version-file: ".nvmrc"` instead of a hard-coded version:
  - `CI-Action.yml` (also moves `setup-node` from `@v2` to `@v4`)
  - `stable-release.yml`
  - `playwright-pr-checks.yml` (removes the `NODE_VERSION` env)
  - `playwright-live-e2e.yml` (removes the `NODE_VERSION` env)
- Future Node upgrades only need a change to `.nvmrc`, plus the Dockerfile ARG defaults below.

**`engines`**
- `package.json` / `package-lock.json`: `>=20.11.0` → `>=22.23.4 <23 || >=24.22.1 <25 || >=26.12.1`
- Only patched releases of the supported Node lines (22, 24, 26) pass. Node 20, odd-numbered releases (23, 25) and unpatched 22/24/26 releases get an `EBADENGINE` warning on install. The warning doesn't block the install.

**Downstream**
- The orca-elements Jenkins build copies this repo's files over its own workspace, so a release tag with this `.nvmrc` will build on Node 24.22.1 automatically.

**Action needed for developers**
- `nvm install` from the repo root, or `nvm install 24.22.1 && nvm alias default 24.22.1`.

author: mutaaf
body:
## What changed
Ticket: [0060](docs/backlog/0060-paused-resize-audio-and-wake-lock.md). It is the rest of [0042](docs/backlog/0042-pause-background-and-return.md), the lowest-id ready ticket under the lockdown focus, so this PR closes both.

- **Audio goes quiet when paused** (`src/audio.js`, `src/main.js` `syncLife`).
  - The AudioContext is suspended in these cases:
    - the pause sheet (a run, Free Drive or the Sandbox);
    - a hidden tab;
    - the title left with no tap, key or pad input for 60 s.
  - It resumes when none of those holds.
  - Each gesture builds the audio graph if it doesn't exist yet. It resumes the context from any state that isn't running (iOS `interrupted` included), but only when the page shouldn't be quiet.
  - `ctx.state` changes only when the promise settles. So suspend and resume track the latest wanted state and re-apply it if it flipped while a call was in flight. Without this, a tap on the pause sheet turned the sound back on (found in self-review).
- **A resize while paused redraws** (`redrawPaused`). The frozen frame is drawn again on `resize` and again when the drawing buffer is reallocated (`stage.onResize`). Before, a rotation while paused left a blank canvas.
- **Screen wake lock** (`src/wake.js`, new).
  - Held during countdown, live, results (judging) and replay.
  - Released on the title, when paused or when hidden, and asked for again on the way back.
  - Requested 250 ms after it's wanted, so the request stays out of the Jump tap's first frame.
  - Once refused, it isn't asked for again until it has been released.
- `pollPads()` now returns whether a pad is in use, so a gamepad also resets the title's idle timer.
- AGENTS.md system map: adds `src/wake.js`.

## How it was verified
- `npm run check:fast`: backlog OK, lint OK, unit tests all pass (456 before this PR, plus the new `tests/unit/audio-life.test.js`), build OK. The backlog check needs the PR number in the tickets, which comes in the next commit.
- New e2e tests in `tests/e2e/lifecycle.spec.js`, run locally with the sandbox's Chromium:
  - pause → 'suspended', resume → 'running', at 390×844 touch and 1280×720. Another key or a tap on the pause sheet keeps it suspended. A hidden tab goes quiet and stays quiet until Resume.
  - Resize while paused, 1280×720 → 390×844: frames are drawn again and the canvas's pixel spread is above 30, so it isn't blank.
  - Wake lock, with `navigator.wakeLock` stubbed: held in a run, released when paused, asked for again after hidden → visible, held through results, released on the title.
- Test first: the resize and wake-lock tests fail without the change (no frames after resize; wake count 0). The audio tests fail without it (the `life` hook doesn't exist). The new unit test fails 2 of 4 on the first commit's `audio.js` (the in-flight suspend/resume race).
- The rest of `lifecycle.spec.js` and all of `build.spec.js` pass locally.
- One test fails locally: the phone @perf "first Jump" test, with a 60–90 ms long task. Its local bar is 50 ms; CI's is 150 ms. On main it gave 0 ms and 53 ms (it failed once there too). Plain taps on this box produce 80–200 ms long tasks, so these numbers are noise. CI is the judge.
- Self-review by a fresh subagent: the race and the pause-gesture bug are fixed and tested; the wake lock is no longer asked for again on every key after a refusal; the gamepad now resets the idle timer. The reviewer confirmed: no per-frame allocations in `syncLife`; `redrawPaused` is safe before the stage is ready and when the GL context is lost; nothing runs before the module finishes loading.

No sim change. No new hosts. No layout change (hud-audit and title-audit are unaffected).

author: joshuahayeswashere
body:
## Why
To push jview toward a 9/10 UI, each job in the view needs a measure of whether it got faster.
This keeps local events of what the page does: view opened, route, item opened, action taken, and the seconds from page load to the first of each.
`jbus view pace` turns them into a median per route and action, this week against last.

## What changed
- `jbus.view.usage` keeps one line per event, `{at, kind, name, project, route, seconds, headless}`. Kinds are `open | route | item | action` (was `route | drawer | click`), and lines are kept 90 days, with a 16 MiB cap (was 256 KiB).
- `page.html` posts every event from one `note()`. It is fed by one capture click listener on `[data-open]`/`#helpme` and one hook in `ask()` on `/answer` and `/steer`, so no panel posts its own. Routes now include `triage`.
- New `jbus view pace`. `jbus view usage` counts a person's loads only and says how many headless lines it left out.

## Scope
- Covers the `/usage` write, the page listener and hook, both commands, their docs and the `--help` snapshot.
- Leaves out time the tab spent hidden: seconds from page load include it, and the median dampens it.

## Tradeoffs
- Actions come from the write in `ask()`, not from a click table over `data-opt`/`data-steer`. The controls that commit are ids that drift as panels change, while `ask()` counts what was really sent and needs no panel change. An action counts when sent, even if the server then refuses it.
- Built on jv-usage-counts' record in place (same file, same write, same origin rule). Old `drawer`/`click` lines still count under `usage` by name, and `pace` ignores them.

## Blast radius
Every write the page sends (answers, steers, approvals, batch) now passes through the `ask()` hook. The hook only reads the body and calls `note()`, whose post is fire-and-forget with its own `.catch`, so a write's request and answer are unchanged. The gates and routes browser suites drive real answers through the hooked `ask()` and assert the exact write bodies.

## Verification
- `uv run pytest features/jbus/tests/view/test_view_usage.py`: 35 passed. It covers the line shape, 22 refused bodies (content, slugs, thread ids, an `ip` field, bad routes, seconds or headless) that write nothing, the 90-day drop, the cap, and `pace`'s table with headless and old lines left out.
- `pytest -m browser` over `test_view_page_usage.py`, `test_view_page_gates.py`, `test_view_page_routes.py`: 41 passed. The listener gives `item <panel>` with first-of-name seconds, routes stack/triage/project, a batch answer gives one `action answer`, and the write bodies are unchanged.
- Sandbox drive (verify-jstack, the real `jbus view` at this head under headless Chromium): the page kept 10 lines, all `headless: true`, e.g. `item you` at 2.6 s and `route triage`. `jbus view usage` printed `0 since ..., and 10 headless left out`. gh, T3 Code, the webhook and systemctl were stand-ins, so they are not verified here.
- `make check-fast BASE=origin/main` selected all, so lint only here: ruff check and format passed, "0 problems". CI runs the full suite.

author: gandalfix
body:
## Summary

Installing on a host that enforces an application-control policy failed with a raw PowerShell stack:

```
iex : Program 'saife.exe' failed to run: An Application Control policy has blocked this file
at line:145: $reported = ((& (Join-Path $unpacked 'saife.exe') --version) -join ' ')
```

The download was fine (SHA256 matched, archive extracted); the **execution** of the unsigned binary was refused — Smart App Control / AppLocker / WDAC, very commonly for user-writable paths such as `%TEMP%`, which is exactly where the staged copy lives.

### `install.ps1`

- **A refused execution is diagnosed, not dumped.** `Show-ExecutionBlocked` reports the host condition, names the policy families, prints three diagnosis commands (`Win32_DeviceGuard`, `Get-AppLockerPolicy`, the CodeIntegrity event log) and the three options (policy exception / code signing / different host) — detection keys on the *exception* rather than on English text, because the message is localized.
- **The staged (`%TEMP%`) probe no longer decides the install.** If the staged copy cannot run, the installer warns and defers the version probe to the **installed** copy, which is checked *before* the user Path is touched. If that copy is refused too: files stay copied, nothing is added to Path, exit 1 with the diagnosis.
- The pre-flight "existing version" probe is wrapped too — a previous blocked install used to abort the updater before it downloaded anything.

### Docs

- FAQ entry: cause, diagnosis commands, options, and the installer's exact behaviour on a blocked host.

## Test plan

- [x] `Parser::ParseFile` clean (pwsh 7)
- [x] `-WhatIf` → resolves 0.3.1, would replace 0.3.0, changes nothing
- [x] real install to a scratch destination (`-NoPathEntry`) → hash ok, version probe ok, `setup --check-only` ok, new `MXC tier (probe)` line present
- [x] blocked-host pre-flight simulated (unrunnable `saife.exe` at the destination): prints `replacing an existing build this host will not execute`, then installs correctly
- [x] test artifacts removed afterwards
- [ ] On-policy host verification — needs a machine with Smart App Control/AppLocker/WDAC (the reporter's), not available here

author: andypalmi
body:
## What
- **Teardown wedge**: Secret Manager 403 `SERVICE_DISABLED` is now a distinct error (`GcpError::ServiceDisabled`) instead of a generic permission error. Teardown treats it as "no secrets" only when no VM existed in any recorded zone; with a VM present it stays an error telling the user to enable the API. A plain 403 on a secret delete keeps the record and names `secretmanager.secrets.get` / `secretmanager.secrets.delete`.
- **Preflight** (read-only, before any write): Secret Manager API enabled (skipped with `insecure_metadata_secrets`), `default` network exists, and `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs` on the configured service account via `testIamPermissions`, naming `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser`. Failures print the `gcloud` command. Permission-denied on a check is inconclusive and passes. amicu never enables APIs or changes IAM.
- **IPv6 CIDRs** in `allowed_source_cidrs` are rejected with a diagnostic (AMICU-CAP-016).
- **Idle shutdown**: opt-in `idle_shutdown = "30m"` in `gcp {}` (5m or more, shorter than `max_run_duration`). A systemd-run watchdog on the VM polls vLLM `/metrics` with the API key from the root-only env file (running+waiting requests, or the success counter changing) and runs `shutdown -h now` after the window. The clock starts at the first metrics answer, so model loading never counts.
- Refresh notes now say a stopped VM keeps billing its boot disk until the next apply or destroy deletes it (both already delete a TERMINATED VM).
- Docs: GCP provider page and examples/gcp-t4-spot.

## Notes
- Idle shutdown is opt-in: an unexpected shutdown is a surprising default, and `max_run_duration` already bounds cost.
- Whether `instanceTerminationAction=DELETE` applies to a guest-initiated shutdown is not something I could confirm, so the design assumes it does not: the VM ends TERMINATED, and apply/destroy delete it. The VM does not delete itself, so its service account needs no compute permissions.

## Testing
Mock-transport tests for each item (preflight failures write nothing, teardown with API disabled with and without a VM, denied delete keeps state, IPv6, idle script rendering, HCL round trip). fmt, clippy (stable, -D warnings) and tests for core, hcl, engine, gcp and cli pass.
