### Type of Change

## FT812 video modes
Only two modes are left, both with the FT812 within its 60 MHz:

| `video_mode` | Mode | FT clock / pclk | Timing |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0` | 640x480@60 | 48 / 2 = 24 MHz | VESA line (800 clocks), 500 lines |

author: m64github
body:
pi's and Claude Code's channels: a turn the harness runs without a served prompt (typed at the terminal; in Claude Code also a custom command, `/loop`, a background subagent's report, a message from another session) is a **local turn**. Extensions hear its start and end, and its agent-tool calls run inside it. Claude Code's channel now follows Claude Code's turns by their `prompt_id`. An API error ends a served prompt at once.

## Why

The channels gave extensions a turn only for a prompt served over NATS. A turn typed at the terminal had no headers on its model calls and no scope around its agent tools: its calls were filed one by one, and the agents it prompted named no parent.

## The extension contract (all four copies, `agents/EXTENSIONS.md`)

- `LocalTurn { id, local: true, sessionId? }`.
- `localTurnStarted(turn, atMs)` and `localTurnEnded(turn, outcome, atMs)`.
- `aroundToolCall` and pi's `providerHeaders` take a served request or a local turn.
- Claude Code's `promptStarted(request, atMs, sessionId?)`.
- pi's and OpenClaw's copies gain `promptEnded`'s `reason`.

## pi

- A local turn opens at `agent_start` when no NATS prompt is active, and closes at `agent_settled`, before the queue drains.
- The headers and the agent tools are given the active request, else the open local turn.
- The NATS queue also waits while a local turn is open: pi reads idle a moment before `agent_settled` reaches the channel.
- `extensions/local-turns.ts` with its own tests; three smoke steps.

## Claude Code: turns by `prompt_id`

Measured on Claude Code 2.1.310:
- Typed text and channel messages share one first-in, first-out queue.
- A waiting message is **folded into the running turn at its next tool result**; else it starts the next turn after the `Stop`.
- A turn is one `prompt_id`, which is on `PreToolUse`, `Stop` and `StopFailure`.
- A channel message's `UserPromptSubmit` fires when Claude Code takes it, with the id of the turn it lands in.
- Several waiting channel messages each fire a submit, then run as **one** turn under the last id.

The change:
- **Hooks:** `UserPromptSubmit` and `StopFailure` are added. The hooks append submits, stops and failures to one log, `<pid>.events`, never the prompt text. `.tools` records carry `prompt_id`.
- **A turn tracker** (`src/turns.ts`) in two modes. Binding mode starts at the first submit line with a `prompt_id`; before it, fallback mode keeps the old rules exactly.
  - A channel submit binds its request to the turn it carries: its own, or the running one (a fold).
  - A typed submit with a new id opens a local turn.
  - Typed text that waited, and turns Claude Code starts itself, surface by an unannounced id, stamped at the last `Stop`.
  - Channel submits with nothing of the turn between them (no tool call, `Stop`, failure or other submit) are one batch, with 30 s as a bound against a lost `Stop` line.
  - A channel message of an earlier server (request ids restart) binds nothing.
- **Ownership by binding:** a request owns the turn its submit named. A request still waiting owns nothing.
  - So a turn's `Stop` is never refused for a request queued behind it, and that request never gets the turn's final text (measured before: it did).
  - The `Stop` hook decides alone, from `.open` and the log, since a short turn's `Stop` comes before the server's next poll.
- **A served prompt starts when Claude Code takes it** (`promptStarted`), not at delivery.
- **Agent-tool calls** run in the request named by `request_id`; else in the call's own turn (its last open bound request, a folded one included; else the local turn; none for a served turn whose requests all finished); else the current turn; else the last active request.
- **An API error (`StopFailure`) ends the served prompt at once**, in both modes, with an error frame naming it, e.g. `the turn failed on a model API error: billing_error`. Before, the caller waited for its timeout.
- The hook records are read at every tool call, and from a mark taken before the service starts.
- The default state folder comes from one constant (from the review of the PR before this one).

## Tests

- **pi:** unit 88 (`local-turns.test.ts` new); smoke 25/24/20.
- **Claude Code:** typecheck 0, 183 unit tests, both roundtrips ALL PASS, including new cases 9 (reply before the poll), 10 (a batch of three) and 11 (the startup gap). Three CI-job runs in a row and six more roundtrip runs, all green.
- **OpenClaw:** 103 on both versions.
- **End to end** against Claude Code 2.1.310 and a mock model:
  - a typed turn alone;
  - a NATS prompt folded into a typed turn (its own reply, never the typed text);
  - a NATS prompt queued behind one (its own turn, no refusal);
  - two and three batched prompts (all answered; before the batch rule, 2 of 3 got a 500);
  - a 400 `billing_error` (the caller's error frame within 0.13 s).
- **The bundle:** `runtime/server.js` was rebuilt with bun 1.3.14 from the packed SDK artifacts; a fresh export at the head rebuilds it byte for byte, and `verify:bundle` is green.
- **Reviews:** independent code reviews of each part, with mutations: 17 of 18 caught on the first Claude Code pass; every survivor since then has its test.

## Stated honestly

- Typing during a running turn joins that turn.
- A channel message folded into a typed turn takes that turn's later calls; its reply is written there.
- One call at a turn boundary may land in the neighbouring turn (served records are in whole seconds).

author: massimo-sandboxaq
body:
## Problem

When a Slack message carried several files, some never reached the agent. The cause was the file name, not Slack. Console fetches each attachment from the agent media download, which put the filename straight into `Content-Disposition`. Headers are latin-1 on the wire, so any name with a character outside that set failed with a 500. Examples are an em dash ("Device profile — SSH host.png") and the narrow no-break space in a macOS screenshot name. Plainly named files in the same message came through, which made it look like "only the first attachment arrives".

## Fix

- New `switch_core/content_disposition.py`: the RFC 6266 header builder the template download already had, moved out of `gateway/templates.py` so both routes share it. It puts an ASCII skeleton in `filename` and the real name, percent-encoded, in `filename*`.
- The agent media download (`GET /agents/{id}/rooms/{room}/media`) now uses it.
- The template download's output is unchanged.

## Tests

- `tests/switch_core/test_content_disposition.py`: em dash, narrow no-break space, curly apostrophe and CR/LF-injection names all produce a header Starlette can send, and the real name round-trips. ASCII names are kept as they are, and the fallback stem is used when nothing ASCII is left.
- The existing template download tests cover the refactor. They need Postgres, which I couldn't run locally, so they run in CI.

All providers are in `src/main/llm.js`. `ollama.js` is unchanged and is still used for Ollama. Claude Code gets its prompt on stdin, so text from the chat never reaches a shell command line (`shell: true` is needed for an npm `claude.cmd` on Windows).

author: massimo-me
body:
## Cosa cambia

`AcceptByToken` carica la proposta tramite il link e poi costruisce la vista pubblica rileggendo la prenotazione. Se nel frattempo la cassa ha accettato e confermato il rinnovo, la vista nega l'accettazione e il cliente riceveva `410 renewal_expired` («proposta scaduta») invece di `409` («non più aperta»). Ora, quando la vista nega l'accettazione, l'errore si decide con `AcceptRefusal` (funzione pura in `plan.go`) sullo stato attuale della proposta e sulla prenotazione letta dalla vista: proposta chiusa o prenotazione già confermata (dalla cassa, dal webhook o con il credito, prima che la proposta risulti convertita) → `ErrNotOpen`; scadenza, blocco scaduto o prenotazione chiusa altrimenti → `ErrExpired`. Un errore di lettura della proposta viene restituito com'è. I dati erano già corretti (una sola conversione); cambia solo l'errore restituito.

Emerso da un fallimento raro di `TestConcurrency_RenewalProposalAccept/sqlite` nella CI della #8 (`renewal: proposal expired`, `ok 1 refused 98`).

## Come è stato testato

- `TestAcceptRefusal_Scenarios` (unitario, tutti i casi).
- `TestRenewal_CampaignLifecycle`: dopo il webhook e prima della conversione, una seconda accettazione dal link deve dare `ErrNotOpen`; fallisce sul codice di `main` (`renewal: proposal expired`), passa con la correzione.
- `go test -tags integration -race -count=3 ./internal/domain/renewal/` e `make check`: verdi.

## Domande aperte

Nessuna.

author: epenet
body:
## Proposed change

Follow-up to #188133. Device registry entry snapshots currently replace `via_device_id` with `<ANY>`, so a snapshot can't show which device a device is connected through.

This PR reuses the device reference added in #188133 for `via_device_id`:

```diff
-    'via_device_id': <ANY>,
+    'via_device_id': <DeviceEntry identifiers=[('homewizard', '5c2fafabcdef')]>,
```

Devices without a via device still snapshot as `None`. If the via device can't be found, the value falls back to `<ANY>`.

The wmspro hub identifier is built from the config entry id; #188723 gave the wmspro tests a fixed `entry_id` so these snapshots are stable.

author: simonebonato
body:
## In plain words

A first pass at the drawn explanations you asked for: **26 hand-drawn diagrams** across all sections, in the textbook style. They show in Colab as soon as the notebook opens, because they are saved outputs like the callout boxes, so nothing has to run.

- **The map** (section 0, after "The plan"): learning from incomplete labels as three families, each with the question it answers: *change the loss?* (Path 1), *fill in the labels?* (Path 2), *skip training?* (Path 3). The section numbers that try each one are on the cards, with floor and reference above. A small "you are here" version opens sections 5, 6 and 7.
- **How methods work:** how SAM works (encoder once, prompt + decoder per hint), patches → linear head → mask, IoU as a pixel picture, one click / three possible objects, the patch vs a thin vessel, the half-finished label file, recall vs precision, why missing = background goes wrong, the ladder rungs with costs to scale, partial cross-entropy, the one-shot prototype recipe, **three readings of the same label file** and **the PU loss in three steps**, the masked loss' catch, teacher → pseudo-label → student, SAM from stroke clicks, Grad-CAM, train-once vs prompt-every-image, the three prompts side by side, how to read the trade-off plot, the disagreement map, and the six questions as a flow.
- **Nothing is deleted.** Text a diagram covers is folded into a "The same in words" block under it, so you decide what goes (N-047). Formulas learners code (`pu_background`) stay visible.
- **How it works:** a markdown cell starting `<!-- diagram: name | Title -->` shows `assets/diagrams/name.svg`, with the rest of the cell as its caption. The build makes it a hidden form cell; the lint checks the file exists.

## What to look at first
`s00-method-map`, `s05-pu-loss`, `s05-three-readings`, `s01-how-sam-works`. Tell me the style you want changed and it applies to all of them.

## Evidence
`just check` green (lint 0 problems, smoke 11 passed). Every SVG rendered to PNG and checked by eye.

## Merge danger
- It touches the same section files as PR #30 (new markdown cells only). Merge #30 first; I rebase this one.
- Notes from the agents, not changed (content is yours): the order "rung 0 → rung 2 → rung 1 (go-deeper)" confuses people. The 1.1 theory bullet says SAM "learnt from a billion masks" (that was SAM 1's dataset, SA-1B; worth checking for SAM 2.1). Path 1 starts from the half-painted file while Paths 2 and 3 start from scribbles, and the text never says so outright.
- `just version` before merging. The template in the vault gets the diagram support once you keep it.

author: arielpetit
body:
## Problem

Keycloak's **built-in** email templates (`org-invite.ftl`, `email-test.ftl`, …) call `@layout.emailLayout` **without** a title, but the custom theme's `template.ftl` declared `<#macro emailLayout title>` (required). Every such email failed to render:

```
freemarker.core._MiscTemplateException: When calling macro "emailLayout",
required parameter "title" (parameter #1) was not specified.
```

This broke invitation emails and the Realm Settings → Email **Test connection** button.

## Why it reappeared

A server-side fix of this line was applied during the invite-email incident, but the theme is mounted from the server's repo checkout — the next deploy's `git reset --hard` restored the original file. The fix belongs in the repo.

## Fix

`<#macro emailLayout title>` → `<#macro emailLayout title="">` — one line. The theme's own templates (email-verification, executeActions, password-reset) all pass `title=` explicitly, so they render identically.

## Test plan

- [ ] After merge + Keycloak restart (or next deploy): Realm Settings → Email → Test connection succeeds; invitation emails send.

body:
**Every property is supported at 5 of 5** for placing (all eight fixtures), placing with a precedent, and connecting. No fixture needed a redraw.

## Summary
- **Placing's candidates come from mentions.** They are the Stories with a Development whose Item mentions an Entity the Item being placed mentions. The storage adapter's `CandidateStories` returns at most 20, ranked by the Entities each Story shares with the Item. Each Entity is weighted by how few Stories it is in (IDF over Stories), and ties go to the Story with the newest Development. Every Fact of the Item has the same candidates. The request gives them once, each with a `Shares:` line naming what it shares, and the check refuses a placing in any Story outside them. Per-Fact `Entities:` lines and per-Fact candidate lists are no longer shown.
- **The batch hold-back and connecting use mentions too.** In a batch, an Item waits while an earlier Item awaiting placing mentions an Entity it mentions (`ToPlace.Mentions`). Connecting's `FactsNear` (at most 30) now takes the `ToConnect`. It returns the Facts whose Items mention an Entity the Item mentions, plus the Developments in one of its Facts' Stories.
- **Re-recorded:** placing and placing with a precedent, over their own frozen copies, and connecting, which the free check showed stale. No `inputs/` copies were refreshed.

Closes #103

Merges on green with every property supported. The yield shift is for the Owner's review, which gates #104.

## Yield

Before is `main`; after is this PR. Reading and the Briefing are unchanged (not re-recorded).

Connecting's agreement is a fresh draw on new requests, with more nearby Facts in some of them. It is down a little, from 0.93 to 0.90, but still well above reading's 0.69 from #101. The Owner may want to watch this against the #101 refutation line. It doesn't cross it: connecting is higher than reading on every fixture.

## Stale before recording

The free check was `go test ./internal/editor` with no `-record`, run once the code was final. These failed:
- `TestRecordedPlacings`: stale from the first fixture.
- `TestRecordedPlacingPrecedent`: stale.
- `TestRecordedConnectings`: stale from the Commons statement on. Its nearby Facts now include Facts whose Items mention a shared Entity, where before only Facts tied to one counted.
- `TestAChainedFixtureIsCarriedOnByItsFirstSampleToPass`: it replays placing's samples, so it was green again once placing was re-recorded.

These replayed green over their own frozen copies, so none was re-recorded: reading, reading with a precedent, the Briefing, the chain replay, the Sunday read and the compatibility check.

## Calls made

- **IDF is smoothed:** each shared Entity weighs log(1 + N/n), for an Entity mentioned in n of the N Stories with a live Development. Plain log(N/n) gives an Entity in every Story a weight of 0, so a Story sharing only that Entity would rank by recency alone, level with a Story sharing nothing. The smoothed form keeps the order by rarity and gives every shared Entity some weight. A Story's Entities are those mentioned by the Items of its live Developments (withdrawn ones are left out, as the acts see a Story). The final tie-break is the newest Story.
- **Candidates show what they share, not per-Fact Entities.** Placing no longer sees `Entities:` per Fact. Those lists are reading's (or #102's bridge to every mention), and they no longer choose anything. Each candidate instead shows `Shares: …`, the reason it is there, which the design says is kept with the call.
- **The instructions changed in one paragraph only:** where the candidates come from, that every Fact has the same ones, and that each is shown with what it shares. Nothing else changed.
- **`Store.StoriesSharing` is gone.** `CandidateStories(ctx, Item, limit)` replaces it. `FactsNear` takes a `ToConnect` so it can read the Item's mentions. `ToPlace` gains `Mentions`, filled by `FactsToPlace`, and `toConnect` reuses it.
- **Placing's precedents are left as they are** (`PlacingPrecedents` still matches Entities through the Facts' ties): the issue doesn't name them. That works today only because of #102's bridge, so I drafted a follow-up for the orchestrator, needed before #112.
- **Spend** (claude-haiku-5-5, estimated at $1/$5 per million tokens):
  - placing: 8 fixtures × 5 samples, about 111k input and 34k output tokens, about $0.28;
  - placing with a precedent: 5 samples, about $0.02;
  - connecting: the 7 stale fixtures × 5 samples (the US–Russia samples were kept), about 102k input and 59k output tokens, about $0.40.

  That is about $0.70 of the $3. The Sunday read was not stale, so it wasn't recorded ($0 of its $2). No redraws.

## Hypotheses this makes Due

Cheap: none.

# Draft-step launch cuts on i34-9's promoted 8340b5de: fused draft router, fused post-verify Q/K/V, direct paged gather, one-launch accept walk and row picks, second draft's K/V row written in place, and znan2's lazy seed K/V

Effort: Claude Opus 5.5 at max effort, one Claude Code session.

## Base

- i34-9's promoted submission `8340b5de-694a-4776-8a72-215492d1ec4c`. Its editable tree is carried byte for byte except for the items below.
- `mtp-head.manifest.json` is unchanged: native MTP head, `source: pinned`, depth 2, verify width 3.
- Target weights, quantization, the offline transform, the MTP head weights, `Package.swift`, `Package.resolved`,
  the ahead-of-time Metal sources and the generated kernel twins are unchanged.

## What changed

| # | Change | Author | Files | Switch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Lazy seed K/V gathers for the device-picked first draft | znan2 (`7bd1f11a`) | `NemotronH35MTP.swift` | `NEMOTRON_MTP_LAZY_SEED_KV=0` |
| 2 | Draft router: the head's gate and top-six selection in the one fused launch the draft already requests | terrapinelf (`6a3850f9`) | `NemotronH35MTPExactRows.swift`, `NemotronH35MTPLoading.swift` | `NEMOTRON_MTP_DRAFT_ROUTER_FUSED=0` |
| 3 | Post-verify draft rows: Q/K/V in the verify's fused Q/K/V launch | terrapinelf (`6a3850f9`) | `NemotronH35MTPModule.swift`, `NemotronH35MTPLoading.swift` | `NEMOTRON_MTP_DRAFT_ROWS_QKV=0` |
| 4 | Paged single-segment gather into a real kernel output | terrapinelf (`6a3850f9`) | `ContinuousBatchingV2/CBv2CriticalPathCuts.swift`, `ContinuousBatchingV2/Paged/PagedSegmentTransfers.swift` | `CBV2_PAGED_READ_OUTPUT=0` |
| 5 | Device-picked first draft: accept walk, masks and row picks in one launch | terrapinelf (`6a3850f9`) | `NemotronH35MTP.swift`, `NemotronH35MTPLoading.swift`, `ContinuousBatchingV2/MTP/EngineLoopV2+MTPFinalize.swift` | `NEMOTRON_MTP_DRAFT_ROW_PICK=0` |
| 6 | Second device draft writes its own K/V row into the snapshot's spare row instead of a K/V concat | terrapinelf (new) | `NemotronH.swift`, `NemotronH35MTP.swift`, `NemotronH35MTPExactRows.swift`, `NemotronH35MTPLoading.swift`, `NemotronH35MTPModule.swift`, `ContinuousBatchingV2/Paged/*` | `NEMOTRON_MTP_SECOND_DRAFT_KV_ROW=0` |

### 1. Lazy seed K/V gathers for the device-picked first draft (znan2 `7bd1f11a`)

`speculateNextFirstDraft` queues the next round's first draft right behind the verify for the row the device's own
accept walk picks. It builds that row's draft id, draft hidden and its projected K/V (`take(spec.keys, row, axis: 2)`
and the value twin), and submitted all four. The K/V pair is read only by `prestageFirstDraft` when
`readvanceTrusted` cannot re-expose the row `speculateAfterVerify` already stored; with the retained seed row (the
default) that re-exposure succeeds and the two gathers' outputs are dropped. They now stay lazy: they are built as
before but no longer submitted with the draft, so they run only when that fallback reads them. Carried as znan2's
diff over the record, unchanged. `NEMOTRON_MTP_LAZY_SEED_KV=0` submits them again.

### 2. Draft router in one launch (ours, `6a3850f9`)

The draft's one-token MoE tail already asks for the fused router and top-six selection launch
(`NemotronMTPRouterRowsSelect.run(..., draft: true)`), but the head's gate was never recorded as row-major, so every
draft step fell back to the stock gemv plus the selection kernel (two dependent launches). Load now records the
head's gate too and qualifies the R = 1 launch on the draft counter against the head's stock gemv + selection, bit
for bit in gates, indices and weights on seeded rows; the draft takes the one launch only after that check.

### 3. Post-verify draft rows: Q/K/V in one launch (ours, `6a3850f9`)

`frontRows` (the R = 3 post-verify draft rows) projected the attention norm through three launches: the prepared wq
QMV and the wk and wv multi-row QMVs. It now takes the verify's fused Q/K/V launch (`NemotronTargetQKV.apply`,
captured rows, fed the norm's prepared rows) on the head's wq, wk and wv: one launch whose Q, K and V tiles keep each
projection's row body. Load qualifies it against the three launches on the head's weights and attention norm, bit
for bit in q, k and v on seeded rows (R = 3 with and without the prepared rows, R = 4); the three launches remain the
fallback.

### 4. Paged single-segment gather into a real kernel output (ours, `6a3850f9`)

The MTP head pool is one segment per request, so its snapshot gather is one read launch whose records cover every
(token, head, lane) of both planes. That launch now stores into its own output `[2, 1, H, count, D]` instead of a
zero-filled in-place destination: the zero fill, the completion launch and the `Depends` alias go away, and
`gather()` returns slice views of the output instead of one take per plane. Same elements; the multi-segment path is
unchanged. `NEMOTRON_KERNEL_SELFTEST=1` compares every direct gather with the in-place gather bit for bit.

### 5. Accept walk, masks and row picks in one launch (ours, `6a3850f9`)

The device-picked first draft ran the accept walk, the two-mask launch and four take gathers (fused, queries, keys,
values) before its attention. The engine now also hands the drafter the walk's operands (acceptance packet and
offsets; the walked count stays a lazy array nobody launches), and one launch repeats the engine's integer walk,
writes both masks with the masks kernel's statements and copies the walked row of the four post-verify tensors
through their strides. Same values and layouts; the attention keeps its kernel. Load-time qualification compares
the launch with the masks launch and the four gathers bit for bit for accept counts 0...2 in both packet argument
spaces.

### 6. Second device draft writes its K/V row in place (new)

The device second draft attended the head cache snapshot concatenated with its own projected K/V row (four copy
launches per round). The snapshot is now gathered with one spare row; the first draft attends views of the first L
rows, and the second draft's Q/K/V launch is a twin of the fused Q/K/V kernel that also stores its K/V row into the
spare row, ordered before the second attention by a `depends`. The second attention reads the whole snapshot, which
holds the same values at the same positions as the concatenation did. A load-time check on the head's own weights
requires q, k, v and the stored row to be bit-identical and no other row to change.

## Contract and scope

- No prefill before `free_decode_begin`, no decode work inside it beyond the seed, no keep-alive between requests
- Target weights are read as they are; no target array is copied, re-encoded or re-laid out by these items.
- The timed prefill requests run the runner's teacher-forced stepper, which never reaches these decode paths.

## Why emitted tokens cannot change

- Every changed target kernel keeps the record's values, order and rounding points, inside the load-time
  bit-for-bit qualifications described above. The 2-bit draft screen and its chunk size can change which token a draft proposes;
  every proposal is still verified by the target, which decides every emitted token. The acceptance rule and the
  prefill graphs are the base's. The 2-bit records are a draft-only re-quantization of head values used by the
  MTP draft head's screen (the MTP head is the contract's quantization exception); the target's head reads its
  own arrays unchanged.

## Reproduce

```bash
swift build -c release --force-resolved-versions --scratch-path .build-worker --product benc

The changes are organized as follows:

author: fadhlillah-dli
body:
## Why

The owner decided ADR-0041's open decision on 2026-10-26: option **A, OpenCode Go** ($10/month subscription) for broker-served WORKER routes. The provider allows Go from other clients ("Yes, you can use Go with any agent"). Free-tier Zen models return 403 to non-OpenCode clients. Separately, no paid route could run end to end: the planner never sets `max_cost_usd`, so the scheduler answered `COST_UNKNOWN`.

## What

- **Routes.** `opencode-go/*` CANDIDATE routes, PERSONAL only. WORKER: glm-5.3-flash, mimo-v2.6-flash, minimax-m3.1-flash, hy3 (tools UNKNOWN, so not eligible for tool tasks), kimi-k2.7-code. The rest are WATCHLIST; DeepSeek is PUBLIC only (Global region; its ZDR agreement expires 2026-10-31). OpenAI chat-completions at `https://opencode.ai/inference/go/openai/v1`, host-pinned to `opencode.ai`, credential `workers/opencode-go`. No client restriction. The Zen free pilots stay restricted.
- **Broker.** For Go, an own User-Agent plus an opaque `x-opencode-session` (a sha256 prefix of the run id). The Go catalog source is `/inference/go/v1/models`; it reports UNKNOWN (never MISSING) without a key or on errors.
- **Subscription accounting** (ADR-0080 amendment). `pricing.billing = SUBSCRIPTION`:
  - the BUDGET decision covers the plan fee;
  - the ledger records the provider's marginal cost (0 within the plan) and the reported allowance, or an ESTIMATED upper bound, and never charges the reservation as invented dollars.
- **Admission and windows.** The trailing 5-hour window blocks. The week and month windows are advisory (`WARN_EXHAUSTED`). AEOS counts only calls made through this instance, so Go's own limit stays authoritative.
- **Fail closed on provider-side paid fallback.** A charge, a non-plan billing source, or an unreadable cost or source gives `SUBSCRIPTION_BEYOND_PLAN` until the owner re-activates the route. The probe may target a subscription route (ADR-0111 amendment).
- **Docs.** ADR-0041/0080/0111 amendments; OWNER_ACTIONS 1.8, 1.11 and 2.12 (option C corrected: only the WORKER pool is served); OPERATIONS; CHANGELOG.

## Proof

- Three independent adversarial reviews, then a fix round and an independent verification. The last three low findings are fixed in 985d30c.
- Tests: 1,384 targeted tests at the fix round, and 1,052 affected tests after merging current `main` (xdist -n 8), all passing. ruff clean, mypy darwin and win32 0 errors, secret scan clean.

## NOT-PROVEN (no live call yet)

Whether Go accepts the broker; the allowance unit and per-model vs pooled allowance; billing_source values; the HTTP status at a limit; window anchors. The UI does not show allowance windows yet. Per-token paid routes keep the `COST_UNKNOWN` gap (recorded open in ADR-0080).

author: flowcool
body:
## Intended behavior

Refs #36. Source implementation: flowcool/BillCollector#62.

Allow a declared login phase `submit` chain to end with `fill`. This covers portals that submit when a password or OTP field is filled. The existing durable attempt is reserved before the action. Final session proof still controls success.

```text
reserve durable attempt -> fill once -> wait for final session proof -> settle
```

Click/Enter submission, direct OTP entry, fresh-code resolution, failure limits and no-replay behavior remain covered. There is no database or exit-code change.

## Verification

- Before: terminal `fill` is rejected; preparation cannot safely represent an input-triggered submission.
- After: password/direct-OTP tests prove reservation through a second SQLite connection, one submission, fresh OTP, finalization, failure and interruption settlement.
- Run: `apps/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_bc_login.py -q`.
- Expected: 62 passed.
- Full-suite evidence: 461 passed, 3 skipped, 53 subtests passed. This reuses the prior pinned upstream test run: the complete candidate tree is identical to tested commit `625a6b677f4a1870a28d512644934dd1f99e37ea`.
- Historical command: `apps/.venv/bin/python tests/run_regression.py --ini tests/bc_regression.ini`. Prior identical-tree result: PASS, all 7 pairs and exactly 8 files matched. Initialize the isolated harness Service table with `DatabaseManager` on a fresh checkout, as required by the current harness.
- Ruff 0.17.0 and 0.16.9 pass. Bandit 1.9.4 reports no findings in the changed login module.

## Recovery

Revert this focused commit. The schema remains unchanged.

## Coordination and ownership

We advanced this feature independently in our fork to continue our collection work. This PR offers that implementation for upstream review. It does not presume agreement on the proposed contract. If the contract changes, we will adapt the code and its tests to the agreed interface. The maintainer retains the architecture decision and integration.

The branch starts directly from public `main` at `d9362b3b68d7f9aa54b070c5f8a86708102e1cff`. It contains only this contribution, without the fork CI or dependency updates. Validation uses isolated synthetic state and browser fixtures. No provider, vault, production or consumer service was contacted.

## AI assistance

Codex assisted with implementation, adaptation and verification. I remain responsible for the contribution and its review.

author: stevekrenzel
body:
## What

Part 4 of 4 of keeping Elwood's teardown off Codex's shared app-server daemon, stacked on #369. It is split from #341.

**The race.** The Codex TUI forks the daemon as a `codex` group leader of its own, then `exec`s it. A path read can come between those two steps and find no daemon yet, and the walk can then stop the group after the `exec`.

**The fix.** A stopped process cannot `exec`, so the kill pass decides by the latest read. It resumes a group with SIGCONT, and never SIGKILLs it, when that read shows either of these in it:
- a process holding the daemon;
- a process not shown stopped that could still become the daemon.

A resume refused with anything other than `ESRCH` fails the walk.

**The leader exiting.** A leader killed by something else while the walk holds that group leaves the stopped daemon under PID 1, out of the leader's reach. So each group the walk stops is a root of its own for the path reads. Part 3 already roots the scope there; this part relies on it.

The sweep ops gain `continueGroup` (SIGCONT), and the sweep state keeps the latest table.

**Spec:**
- PRD §5.3 now says "never killed: the walk may stop its group, but then resumes it". This answers #341's round-4 minor about "never signaled".
- C-LIFE-10 has the resume clause.
- `docs/cli-behavior.md` explains why the resume is needed, and its walk-mechanics paragraph now says that a group holding the daemon is resumed rather than SIGKILLed. That paragraph is the stale description flagged in round 4.

## Evidence

**`tests/unit/shared-daemon-real.test.ts`** (real processes, macOS). Node cannot `exec`, so the fixture's process stands in for the daemon by taking the daemon's path as its title, which macOS `ps` reads as `comm`. It checks two cases:
- A group stopped just as its process became the daemon is resumed, and is still the tree's own process, running.
- The same group is still resumed after the leader is SIGKILLed while the walk holds it and the leader's exit leaves the group under PID 1.

**`tests/unit/detached-sweep-daemon.test.ts`** (scripted). It checks:
- a group whose latest read shows the daemon is resumed, not killed;
- a candidate not shown stopped is resumed while a hook is killed;
- a stopped group with the daemon's shape that no read marks is killed and not resumed. This is the test #341's round 4 asked for.
- an already-gone group needs nothing, and an `EPERM` fails the walk.

**`tests/unit/process-tree-ops-real.test.ts`**: the real ops stop and then resume a detached process's group on every platform. **`tests/unit/reap-tree-inert-seam.test.ts`**: the inert resume sends no real signal.

**Break-the-fix:**

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| Kill pass never resumes | 5 tests fail: the 3 resume tests in `detached-sweep-daemon.test.ts` and both real tests |
| Scope roots set to the leader alone | The real PID-1 test fails |
| Kill pass resumes a stopped, unmarked candidate | The new killed-not-resumed test fails |
| Code restored | All pass |

**Gate:** `npm run check` passed at this head, with lint, types, and the 200-line cap: 978 test files, 5601 tests passed and 1 expected fail (the existing `test.fails` on main), and coverage of statements 100% (12906/12906), branches 100% (7833/7833), functions 100% (3495/3495), lines 100% (10973/10973).

author: seiyafunaokajp
body:
## Summary

Over SSH, renames and edits in the project panel showed up late or not at all when a large tree (here, a whole home directory with Yocto build output) was open.

**Cause:** on Linux the fork keeps Zed's inotify watches to a quarter of the user's limit (ADR-F43) and polls every other directory in a round-robin sweep of 20,000 stats every 2 s. One round therefore takes (entries ÷ 10,000) seconds, which is minutes for a home directory. The scan is breadth-first, so the directories the user actually works in (deeper ones, or ones created after the budget filled up) end up polled.

**Fix (ADR-F104):** the client tells each worktree which directories the user is looking at, and the watcher keeps those on native watches.
- **What counts:** directories expanded and visible in the project panel, including a hidden root and the folded parts of a folded row, plus the parent directory of every open buffer.
  - The two are combined per worktree in `project::watch_priority`, open-file directories first.
  - The set is capped at 1024, debounced by 250 ms, and sent only when it changes.
  - The panel hook is a single call after `update_visible_entries` installs its state.
- **Local worktrees:** the set reaches the background scanner's watcher through `fs::Watcher::set_priority_paths`, using the paths the scanner registered (canonical paths for external directories). It is re-sent after a scanner restart.
- **Remote worktrees:** a new `SetWorktreeWatchPriority` message, best effort. The server checks each path with `RelPath::from_unix_str` and caps the list at 4096. Collab guests don't send it.
  - `JP_ENHANCE_WIRE_REVISION` goes to 3. The server binary's name carries the revision, so without the bump release clients would keep reusing the older server already on a host and never get the fix.
- **`OsWatcher` (fs):** keeps one priority set per `FsWatcher` and acts on their union.
  - Priority directories get native watches outside the 1/4 share, up to 1024 per process. They are counted separately, so the share decisions stay coherent.
  - Trimming and yielding take ordinary watches first and never the ones held beyond the share.
  - No new beyond-share watches are added while other programs are about to run out (yield).
  - Directories the kernel refuses are polled on every pass instead of waiting for the sweep.

On Windows and macOS native watches are recursive and there is no budget, so the call does nothing there.

## Testing

**Real host** (Ubuntu 26.04 over SSH, `max_user_watches` 65536, 20,000 directories, dev client plus the musl release server at revision 3):
- **Before the fix:** a rename in a polled directory took about 3 s to appear, against under 0.5 s in a natively watched one.
- **After:** a directory created once the budget was full was polled. After I expanded it in the panel it went native within 1–2 s, and the native watch count rose by exactly 2. Renames in it then showed within 0.4 s.
- **Control:** an unexpanded directory created alongside it was still polled 40 s later.
- **How I checked native or polled:** I compared each directory's inode with the `inotify ino:` lines in `/proc/<server pid>/fdinfo`.

**Automated tests:**
- **fs** (in `fs_watcher.rs`): promotion beyond the share; trimming and yield keep the priority directories; refused directories are polled every pass; a directory registered after the share is full gets a native watch; the cap; no beyond-share watches under yield; an unchanged set requests no maintenance.
- **worktree:** the set reaches the watcher with internal and external (canonical) paths, and again after a restart.
- **project:** the panel set and open-file directories are combined, debounced, deduplicated, capped and not resent when unchanged; save-as and close update the set.
- **remote_server:** the set reaches the server worktree; unchanged sets are not resent; the server rejects `..`, absolute and non-normalized paths and applies its cap.
- **project_panel:** expanding and collapsing update the set; hidden roots and folded directories are included.
- Each new test was checked with mutations: break the code, confirm the test fails, restore.

**Suite results:**
- fs 88, worktree 15 + 101, project integration 530, remote_server 183, project_panel 148, remote `wire` 15.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- --deny warnings` (debug) on the touched crates and `cargo fmt --check` are clean.

**Notes for reviewers:**
- `./script/clippy` (release) could not run on this machine: `wasmtime-c-api` failed to build because cmake isn't on PATH for that target.
- `cargo test -p proto --test jp_enhance_numbering` fails 2 tests (`GetAgentServerCommand.approve_update`, `GetTerminalShell`) on `main` already; this change doesn't touch them.
- **Known limits:**
  - A set sent during the initial scan takes effect once that scan finishes.
  - An external directory that hasn't been loaded yet takes effect on the next request.
  - Open buffers (including ones opened by search or diagnostics) can fill the 1024 cap ahead of the panel's directories.

## Self-review

- [x] I've reviewed my diff for quality, security, reliability, and performance.
- [x] UI changes follow the [checklist](https://zed.dev/docs/development/ui-checklist).
- [x] Tests cover the new or changed behavior.

Release Notes:

- Improved file change detection over SSH on Linux: folders open in the project panel, or holding open files, now pick up renames and edits right away even when the host's inotify watch budget is used up.

**Inventory F0, part A (ALPHA-CODE-INVENTORY §1): move the pieces the alpha uses out of legacy giants, so each legacy family can be deleted in one PR without touching the program path. Merge after tonight's W8 check, on a green build with no new test failures.**

## What changes, for the person

Nothing visible. This is a verbatim move with no change in behaviour. It is the first step towards Paul's ruling that "the alpha is, at its core, completely new code". The program's save path no longer loads the Living Model's context reader or the legacy draft replacement module.

| Piece | Was in | Now in |
|---|---|---|
| `readSaved`, `SavedRead`, `isSavedRead`, `NO_MODEL_YET`, `isNoModelYet` | `path-b/tools/context-tool.ts` (the Living Model reader; it loads `resolveRunAdmission`, `livingViewOf` and run facts) | `model-program-turn/saved-read.ts` |
| `approvedGraphHeld` (and its two helpers) | `agent-lane/runtime/draft-replacement.ts` (720 lines of legacy draft replacement) | `model-program-turn/saved-read.ts` |
| `InternalDispatch` (type) | `agent-lane/runtime/agent-capabilities.ts` (12.7k lines) | `core-route/internal-dispatch.ts` |
| `NOTE_NODE_KINDS` | `path-b/tools/note-on-item.ts` | `core-route/turn-request.ts` (its alpha reader) |

- **Switched to the new homes:** `program-save.ts`, `core-write.ts`, `turn-read-cache.ts` and `turn-request.ts`.
- **Kept working on re-exports:** the old modules re-export each piece for their legacy callers.
- **Waiting for part B:** importers in files that today's open PRs change. Those are `core-turn.ts`, `core-route/deps.ts`, and `turn.ts` and `program-tools.ts` in `model-program-turn`. They switch in part B, after #3791, #3792 and #3793 merge.

**Part B** (second commit, after #3791 and #3792 merged):
- `present.ts` took `comparatorWords`, `displayRoundingFor` and `sayDisplayedPct` from three legacy goal-target modules. `goal-chance-driver.ts` loads the coaching and unified-pipeline code, and `goal-targets-joint.ts` loads the retained-limit and cohort readers. The three helpers move verbatim to `model-program/present/display-words.ts`, and the old modules re-export them.
- `program-tools.ts` reads through `saved-read.ts`.
- `turn.ts`, `program-tools.ts` and `core-route/deps.ts` take `InternalDispatch` from `core-route/internal-dispatch.ts`.
- `goal-target-basis.ts`'s second `COMPARATOR_WORDS` lookup now calls `comparatorWords`, which gives the same result for every input.
- **Left out:** `core-turn.ts`'s importers wait for #3793. author: kprovorov
body:
## Summary

Arnold shipped undici versions with known high-severity advisories. eve and guarded-fetch pin undici to exact vulnerable versions, so this PR overrides both pins. The `ai` path has a range and gets a scoped lockfile resolution instead.

```diff
 apps__arnold
   eve@0.80.0 (exact pin)
-    undici 8.10.2
+    undici 8.12.3        # override "eve>undici"
   just-bash > guarded-fetch@0.1.3 (exact pin)
-    undici 7.29.0
+    undici 7.30.1        # override "guarded-fetch>undici"
   ai > @ai-sdk/provider-utils@5.0.61 (^7.29.0)
-    undici 7.30.0
+    undici 7.30.1        # lockfile resolution only
```

- The overrides in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` carry a comment. It names the upstream pins and says to drop each line once eve or guarded-fetch releases with undici ≥ 8.12.2 / ≥ 7.30.1. eve 0.83.2 and guarded-fetch 0.1.6, the latest releases, still pin vulnerable versions.
- The lockfile change is kept scoped because FIT-330 holds the broad refresh. `pnpm update ai` would have re-resolved rollup, babel, @types/node and more, so this PR moves only provider-utils' undici. That moved entry has not been through a re-resolve yet: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` passed on it.
- The eve pin itself is untouched; the optional eve 0.83.2 bump is not part of this PR.

## Evidence

- **Before:** `pnpm audit --prod --json` reported 13 undici advisories on `apps__arnold` paths, 3 of them high: GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c, GHSA-rfgv-xxqx-mfg5 and GHSA-w293-vg96-wgc3.
  **After:** `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 advisories on any `apps__arnold` path.
- `pnpm arnold test` passes: 15 files, 233 tests. `tsc --noEmit` passes too.
- `pnpm arnold build` passes. The bundled `_libs/undici.mjs` is built from `eve/node_modules/undici`, which is 8.12.3, and the traced `node_modules/undici` is 7.30.1.
- `pnpm arnold eval show-my-plan` ran one real model turn through AI Gateway on the overridden undici and passed 5/5 gates.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

Reverting the commit restores the old pins.

**Blast Radius:** Arnold

eve's undici moves from 8.10.2 to 8.12.3, a minor version within the same major. Every outbound call goes through it (AI Gateway, RevenueCat, the Library API). The overrides apply to the whole workspace, but only eve and guarded-fetch consume these pins.

author: fortunesayspump
body:
New private-project setup requires a strong user-chosen password and a separately confirmed random backup code. Either unlocks the same random vault key after account sign-in. An unlocked version-2 vault can also add an optional WebAuthn PRF recovery passkey from Help. Enrollment verifies the password, creates a passkey, requires a successful PRF assertion, then saves only a ciphertext wrapper, credential ID and random salt. On another browser, the same available passkey can unlock the vault. Unsupported passkeys leave password/code recovery intact.

Existing code-only vaults remain readable and can upgrade through the enrolled-browser replacement flow. Replacing password/code preserves project keys and reports but clears the old passkey wrapper; the owner can add a new passkey afterward. Wallet sign-in alone never derives a missing vault key. No new method retroactively recovers a vault that has lost all prior unlock methods.

The broker accepts version-2 password/code ciphertext wrappers and its existing passkey-only compare-and-swap update path. Browser-only PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 (600,000 iterations, unique salt) protects the password wrapper. WebAuthn PRF output is processed in the browser, derives an AES-GCM passkey wrapper with HKDF, and is never sent to the broker. Tenant/vault context is authenticated. Help, recovery docs, discovery and llms.txt are updated together. Public Hub API/MCP contracts and fees are unchanged.

Release in order: deploy fd874fe8 to both private brokers with DRNIB_REQUIRE_PRIVATE_PASSWORD unset; verify existing version-1 reads and version-2 validation. Then deploy the frontend/docs including 8966ee77 on both networks and verify the live unlock and passkey UI. Finally enable DRNIB_REQUIRE_PRIVATE_PASSWORD=true on both brokers to reject new code-only enrollments. Do not rotate existing vaults automatically or claim a real passkey is enrolled without an owner completing the browser ceremony.

Validation: 436 private broker tests, 14 browser-crypto/passkey tests, 11 broker route tests, frontend and docs production builds, frontend typecheck and changed-file lint passed. The passkey browser API was exercised with a synthetic assertion; a real passkey and cross-device recovery still require live acceptance. No paid worker, model call, transaction or live vault rotation was used.

author: ernescz
body:
Addresses #99.

## Why

The database grows without bound: every input version wrote every fact again, every Transition kept its full briefing uncompressed, and nothing was ever removed except ten-day observation detail. On a reporter-shaped database that is about 0.8 GiB a day.

## What

**Store less per change**
- A Transition's briefing is stored apart and compressed (largest one: 634 KiB to 82 KiB, 12 ms to compress, 5 ms to read).
- A fact is written only when its content changes; a head per (Situation, kind, subject) names the row that holds the current content.
- Coverage is kept only for each Situation's current assessment, the only one read.
- Existing data moves to the new shape in the background after the upgrade (resumable cursors, short transactions).

**Bound what is kept**
- Memory is kept forever: every Situation, its journal, its current state, its final record, verdicts and annotations.
- The working record (past briefings, superseded facts, observation evidence only past decisions cite) expires after `storage.retention_days` (90).
- The audit log expires after `storage.audit_retention_days` (365). An anchor entry records the last removed entry; `verify-audit` and `alertint_verify_audit` verify from it.
- A size limit, `storage.retention_size_percent` (80% of the volume) or `storage.retention_size`, shortens both, oldest first whatever the kind, until the database is back under 95% of the limit.
- `0` turns any limit off. Maintenance runs a minute after start and hourly; each step is isolated, so one failing step does not stop the others.
- `/health` reports used/file/limit/volume bytes and how far back each record reaches; a warning is logged once a day when the size limit shortens history or the volume has under 10% free.

## Invariants this relaxes (please check)

- **Observation refresh cursors are deleted** once their run's detail has expired and they are past the cutoff (0027 said they are never deleted). Such a cursor already reads as no cursor.
- **Old observation cycles are trimmed per plan** to the runs something still needs (current heads, live references, reuse sources), instead of being kept whole while any run in them is referenced.
- **Evidence pinned under an assessment call's ID at dispatch is released** with its attempt's evidence: when the attempt is released (unless a protected attempt shares the work attempt), or, for a call with no attempt, once its Situation moved past that input or ended.
- **Open preparation cycles nothing can resume are removed** after the cutoff (input moved on, Situation ended, or the generation already passed).
- Situation transitions, attempts, facts, coverage and references can now be updated/deleted through retention only: each trigger requires a retention marker row and refuses anything protected (current, pending, cited).

## Upgrade cost

- Migration 0048 adds about 15-20 s before ready on a database with about 2 GB in use (measured: 17-18 s vs 0.5 s on 0.15.7).
- The first maintenance pass (about 5 minutes on 2 GB) roughly doubles Situation update time while it runs; afterwards update times match 0.15.7. Both grow with the database. Noted in the CHANGELOG.
- Under the chart's default 256Mi limit the upgrade completes; the agent's own memory stays under 80 MiB and the rest is reclaimable file cache.

## Not in this PR

- Capping the briefing's lists: `ended_work` and the alert list feed materiality, so a cap needs its own design.
- Shrinking the file (VACUUM): freed pages are reused, so a full-size database stops growing.

## Verification

- **Copies of two reporter-shaped databases** (about 1.9 and 1.6 GiB in use), 1 CPU:
  - upgrade pass 202-229 s, then nothing left to do on the next pass;
  - every Transition reads the same before and after (0 of 2,246 and 0 of 2,039 changed);
  - after 100 days 152 / 132 MiB in use, after 400 days 41 / 36 MiB; the steady hourly pass takes 0.4 s;
  - longest single store hold under 250 ms; `verify-audit` passes from the anchor; integrity and foreign-key checks clean.
- **Size limit at 50% of the volume:** 742 -> 317 MiB (limit 371) in one pass, oldest first across kinds.
- **Agent under steady traffic vs 0.15.7:** main Situation update p50 +5%; no WARN/ERROR; no `/ready` or `/live` failure.
- **Under the chart's 256Mi limit:** first start and backlog pass complete, no OOM kill or restart; anon memory peak 76 MiB.
- **New tests:** compression round trip, fact heads and replay conflicts, each expiry step, protected rows refused by the triggers, audit prune and verify from the anchor, size walk, maintenance loop.
- **Local checks:** `go test -race` on `internal/store` and `cmd/alertint`; golangci-lint (darwin + linux) and gosec clean; docs validate OK.

## Checklist

- [x] Tests were added or updated where behavior changed.
- [x] Documentation was updated where user-facing behavior changed.
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` was updated for a notable user-facing change.
- [x] Every commit includes a DCO `Signed-off-by` trailer.

author: jabbera
body:
When the UI's API token (`_token`) expires while the FAB session is still valid, the UI redirects to `/auth/login/?next=<deep link>`. FAB 5.2.2's DB, LDAP and OAuth login views then see an authenticated user and redirect to the index page, so `next` is dropped and the user lands on the home page instead of the page they opened. Clicking the link again works because the redirect issued a fresh token.

This adds `CustomAuthDBView` and `CustomAuthLDAPView`, and overrides `CustomAuthOAuthView.login`, so an authenticated user is redirected to the safe `next` URL (via the existing `get_safe_url`). The provider's `redirect` sets the fresh `_token` cookie on that response. Anonymous users still get the parent login flow, and remote-user auth already honors `next`.

Flask-AppBuilder fixed this upstream in dpgaspar/Flask-AppBuilder#2479 (5.3.0), but that release also changes authenticated-but-unauthorized requests to return 403. This keeps the provider on 5.2.2 and fixes only the login redirect.

Tests:
- `test_views_login.py`: end-to-end against the FAB app with a logged-in DB user, checking the redirect to `next`, the `_token` cookie, the fallback to the index, and rejection of an external `next`. The `next` test fails without this change.
- `test_auth_login.py`: unit tests for the helper and the DB, LDAP and OAuth views.

author: bbbstyyy
body:
## M5 / ADR 0162 — real HTTP CONNECT IPv4 localhost through Rule / Direct / Selected

**Rebased after PR #38 merge.** PR #38 exact head `376225fa` passed ordinary CI with Go Race 4/4, Managed Core Integration, and native amd64/arm64 Core Provenance. It was squash merged into `feat/m0-m1-foundation` as `2472acf3`. The intended six-file ADR 0162 diff has been rewritten as a single commit **`b8262299`**, directly based on that exact development head, retaining the improved Daemon stopped-readiness guard and crash-stage diagnostic protections.

This PR remains **Draft** pending new exact-head ordinary CI including Race 4/4, Managed Core integration and both native architectures. Earlier runs on superseded stacked commits (including one failed amd64 pre-HTTP lifecycle) are not acceptable evidence for this new head. No changes to stable `main` or release Draft PR #1.

### Missing contract
T22 requires HTTP in addition to SOCKS. Prior native airgap probes cover real SOCKS5 numeric-localhost CONNECT on Rule 2080, Direct 2081 and Selected 2082, but do not exercise the HTTP CONNECT parsing path of those **same existing mixed inbounds**.

### Implementation and safety
- Inside the *same sixth real Daemon and fourth existing* native read-only, nonroot UID 10001, `docker --network none --cap-drop ALL` container, after ADR 0161's bounded 24×3 SOCKS5 reconnects, issue **three actual HTTP/1.1 CONNECT** requests only to `127.0.0.1:<existing transient echo port>` with strict numeric Host header. No external network, DNS, credentials, new port, process, capability or TUN.
- Read a bounded (≤1024 bytes) HTTP/1.x status header **without consuming tunnel bytes**; only status 200 is accepted. Exchange the exact synthetic binary echo over the HTTP CONNECT tunnel, one at a time through Rule/Direct/Selected. Verify the same approved Core PID, config+declaration revision 2 and Applied=LKG generation before/after.
- Require exactly **one** extra synthetic Selected-node SOCKS upstream dial, zero cross-routing from Rule/Direct and no new node rejection. Failure to complete any header/echo or PID/route check preserves the existing unconditional explicit Core stop and cold restarted-Daemon stopped audit.
- Add offline Python negative fixtures for rejected/partial/oversized/malformed HTTP responses, invalid port/payload, echo mismatch, stale/replaced PID, Selected bypass or Rule crossing. Update native final Selected successful count from 51 to **52**, and append only on native success `T22_AIRGAP_HTTP_CONNECT_IP=ok` with explicit `T22_HOSTNAME_AND_UDP_VERIFIED=false`.

### Explicit non-claims
This proves **only numeric localhost HTTP CONNECT over mixed inbounds**, not HTTP absolute-form, SOCKS domain/hostname, UDP, auth, external DNS/proxy, real CN 28-group/five-layer SRS resources, licensed offline tar distribution, T15/T23 real power-loss restore, T20 1,000 reconnects, T25 72h/7d/30d soak, double rollback or full T22 acceptance. Release/Restore/GC/core distribution and CN bundle gates remain CLOSED; no subscription/ISP routing layer.

author: bbr111
body:
Closes #4502

## Summary

New source `cbbo_it` for the comuni served by CBBO (Brescia), including Capriano del Colle (the request).

- **Data:** each comune's yearly *Ecocalendario* PDF, linked from its page on https://www.cbbo.it/.
  1. `GET /`: `lookups.link_pick` resolves the comune in the site's comuni block.
  2. `GET` the comune page: the first `Ecocalendario….pdf` button.
  3. `GET` the PDF.
- **Parsing:** the shared `MarkerCalendarParser` reads the coloured waste icons in the month grids. The year comes from the file name (`Ecocalendario_2026…`).
- **Shared component change (`service/PdfMarkerCalendar.py`):** two small opt-in additions, each with a unit test. Existing callers are unchanged.
  - `placement="below"`: the icons sit under the day number in each cell, so each icon binds to the nearest day number above it.
  - `page_headings=True`: a month heading standing alone on a page is used as a month band if at least 28 day numbers lie below it.
  - `doc/contributing_source.md` mentions both.
- **Parameters:** `comune`, as listed on cbbo.it. An unknown name raises `SourceArgumentNotFoundWithSuggestions`.
- **Waste types:** `ORGANIC`, `GENERAL_WASTE`, `PLASTIC`, `PAPER`, `GLASS`, `GARDEN_WASTE`. *Tessili sanitari* (nappies, on request) maps to `GENERAL_WASTE` and keeps its raw label. Street sweeping and "centro di raccolta chiuso" markers are ignored.
- **HOWTO:** English, with an Italian hint.

## Coverage

All 2026 calendars were run through the parser offline. Jan–Dec gave consistent weekdays for each waste type, with outliers only on printed holiday shifts.

- **Supported (16):** Acquafredda, Calvisano, Capriano del Colle, Carpenedolo, Castenedolo, Flero, Ghedi, Isorella, Mazzano, Montichiari, Montirone, Nuvolento, Nuvolera, Poncarale, Remedello, Visano.
- **Not supported:**

  | Comune | Reason |
  |---|---|
  | Barbariga | A3 single sheet with day rows, a different layout. It raises `SourceArgumentNotFound`; the HOWTO explains why. |
  | San Zeno Naviglio | Oct–Sep season calendar with vertical month headings; the published one (2025/26) has expired. It raises `SourceArgumentNotFound`. |

## Verification

- Live (`test_sources.py -s cbbo_it -l`):

  | Case | Entries |
  |---|---|
  | Capriano del Colle | 366 |
  | Flero | 304 |
  | Acquafredda (CMYK icons) | 184 |
  | Remedello (smaller paper icon) | 249 |

- Cassettes: one per `TEST_CASES` entry plus two `ERROR_TEST_CASES` (unknown comune; Barbariga).
  - The PDFs are recorded whole, about 1.6–2 MB per cassette.
- `pytest tests/`: 26682 passed, 4 skipped.
- `pre-commit run --files …`: green.

author: gabrielhom
body:
## Por quê

O Treino só tinha os próprios erros e os puzzles. Para estudar uma abertura, o jogador precisa repetir cada variação dela até saber de memória, e ver o que já aprendeu.

## O que muda

- Uma aba nova, "Aberturas", no Treino. Ela traz as 327 famílias da base aberta do Lichess, com busca, agrupadas pela mesma regra do relatório de pontos fracos.
- A tela de cada família, por cor, mostra quantas variações você aprendeu, quantas voltam hoje e as variações agrupadas pelo nome. Cada variação pode ser estudada sozinha, e cada grupo também ("Estudar só estas").
- O treino de uma variação vai do primeiro lance ao último. O adversário responde sozinho. Uma variação nova mostra seta em cada lance seu. Depois ela volta de memória nas caixas de Leitner do treino de erros.
- Durante o treino, um lance de outra variação da mesma família é teoria e não conta como erro. O app diz o nome dela. Qualquer outro lance é erro, e a seta mostra o lance certo.
- O progresso fica no IndexedDB (versão 4 do banco) e vai no backup, ficando com a resposta mais recente. O relatório de pontos fracos e a tela inicial levam às aberturas.

## Escopo

- Uma variação é uma linha que nenhuma outra linha da mesma família continua. A Siciliana tem 259. Duas linhas que só mudam o último lance do adversário contam como duas variações.
- Uma ordem de lances que transpõe para a mesma posição conta como erro, a não ser que a base traga essa ordem na família.
- A agenda de Leitner foi para `src/training/schedule.ts` e `family()` foi para `src/openings`. As aberturas usam as duas sem criar um ciclo de importação com a análise.

## Riscos

O `lines.json` (79 kB com gzip) só é baixado quando alguém abre as aberturas. O livro por FEN que a revisão usa sai do mesmo script e ficou idêntico byte a byte.

## Verificação

- Cada um dos 9 commits passa `tsc -b`, `oxlint` e `vitest`. No topo: 492 testes passaram, contra 447 na `main`.
- `playwright test e2e/openings.spec.ts` passa. O teste estuda a Caro-Kann de pretas: a seta da variação nova, a teoria de outra variação sem erro e um erro que acende a seta.
- A bateria `npm run e2e` inteira rodou num Chrome sem interface por CDP. 4 testes passaram e 13 falharam no tempo limite com "Avaliação pendente". Todos dependem do Stockfish WASM no navegador. Um deles falha igual na `main`, então a causa provável é o ambiente, não este branch.

author: atenai
body:
## 概要
アニメーションの細かい部分を5点直しました。

1. ハンドガンを両手で構えた時に、銃口が少し下を向いていたので上げました
2. 両手構えと C.A.R. 構え（敵が近い時の構え）の切り替えを速くしました
3. ショットガンのダッシュで、右手で持ち上げる銃を少し下げました（アサルトライフルも同じ位置に下げました）
4. ダッシュしたままステージを移ると、右手が上がったまま残っていたので、ステージを移る時は立ち姿に戻すようにしました

## 修正内容
| 修正 | 変更前 | 変更後 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ① ハンドガンの両手構えの銃口 | 弾の飛ぶ向き（カメラの正面）より 3.5° 下（見下ろす時 4.1°、見上げる時 2.7°） | 0.1°（見下ろす時 0.6°、見上げる時 −0.8°） |
| ② 両手構え ⇔ C.A.R. の切り替え | 0.2秒で約66%、終わるまで約0.8秒 | 0.2秒で約87%、0.4秒でほぼ終わる（戻る時も同じ速さ） |
| ③ ショットガンのダッシュの右手 | アサルトライフルと同じ位置 | 9cm 下げて、銃口の高さをアサルトライフルとそろえた |
| ③ アサルトライフルのダッシュの右手 | ダッシュ中の右手の高さ（平均）1.29m | 9cm 下げて 1.20m（ショットガンと同じ位置。ショットガンは 1.21m） |
| ④ ダッシュしたままステージを移る | ロード中も、銃を持ち上げた右手が残る（右手の高さ 1.55m） | 立ち姿に戻る（1.26m） |

### コード
- `HandIK`：ハンドガンを両手で構えている時（近距離の構えも含む）は、銃口を 3.5° 上げます（`HandGunTwoHandAimRaiseAngle`）。片手で狙う時は変えていません
- `PlayerManagerPresenter`：近距離の構えの割合が追いつくまでの時間 `CloseQuarterAimDampTime` を 0.2秒 → 0.1秒にしました
- `ReSurvivorPlayerModel2.prefab`：ショットガンの `dashRightHandPosition` を (0.12, 0.05, 0.25) → (0.12, −0.04, 0.25) にしました。アサルトライフルの `dashRightHandPosition` も、同じ値に変えました（364fa92d）
- `PlayerCharacterView.ResetMoveAnimation`：ダッシュの割合 `f_dash` と構えている割合 `f_aim` も 0 に戻すようにしました
  - ステージを移る間（ロード中・次のステージのフェードイン中）は、`InGameManager` から毎フレーム呼ばれています

## 地雷を置くアニメーションを MineAnimation に分けた（f4fc7cdb）
`GunAnimation` と同じように、地雷を置くアニメーションの設定と処理を、新しいクラス `MineAnimation` にまとめました。動きは変えていません。
- `MineAnimation`（`PlayerCharacterView` が持つ）：アニメーターのレイヤー・再生位置の定数、アニメーションを進める処理 `UpdateAnimation`・立ち姿に戻す処理 `ResetAnimation`、左手を銃から離す割合、地雷を置いている間の手をずらす量（右手 `rightHandOffset`・左手 `GetLeftHandOffset`）
- `PlayerCharacterView`：`UpdatePlaceMineAnimation`・`ResetMoveAnimation` は `MineAnimation` を呼ぶだけにしました
- `HandIK`：地雷を置いている間の手の位置を、`MineAnimation` から受け取るだけにしました
- `GunAnimation`：地雷を置いている時の右手のずらし量 `placeMineRightHandOffset` を外しました（3丁とも同じ値だったので、`MineAnimation` の1つの値にまとめました）
- 確認：3丁で地雷を置く動きを動かし、腰・両手・右肘の位置が変更前と1フレームずつ完全に一致することを確かめました（306フレーム）

## 確認したこと
- ①：銃身の向きと弾の飛ぶ向きの差を、カメラの上下の向き 3 通りで測りました
- ②：敵を 6.5m → 2.2m → 6.5m と動かして、近距離の構えの割合の変わり方を測りました
- ③：ダッシュ中の銃の体へのめり込みは 0 です。頭とのすき間は、ショットガン 2.3cm・アサルトライフル 2.9cm です
- ④：ダッシュ中と構え中に、ロード中と同じ処理（毎フレームのリセット）を始めて、右手の高さと胸の前傾を測りました
- 変更前と変更後を、横からとゲームのカメラから録画した比較動画で確認しています
- コンパイルエラーはありません

## 注意点
- ④の修正で、構えたままステージを移った時に上半身が前に曲がったまま残る問題（胸の前傾 12.5°）も一緒に直っています
- アサルトライフルとショットガンは、構えた時に銃口が弾の飛ぶ向きより約 5° 上を向いています。今回は変えていません

author: vlsi
body:
The `automerge` preset merged only minor, patch, pin, and digest updates, so every major waited for a reviewer, including majors of the actions GitHub publishes, such as `actions/checkout` or `github/codeql-action`. A PR-triggered workflow runs every action it uses, so a green PR has already run the new major, and these majors are mostly runtime moves such as a Node.js bump.

`automerge` now also merges majors of `actions/**` and `github/**` from the `github-actions` manager. Renovate automerges a grouped branch only when every update in it automerges ([`generate.ts`](https://github.com/renovatebot/renovate/blob/719bd35cb7b3/lib/workers/repository/updates/generate.ts#L473)), so `github-actions` moves these majors out of `major third-party GitHub Actions` into a group of their own, `major GitHub-published Actions`. Otherwise a `docker/build-push-action` major in the shared group would hold them for review. Without `github-actions`, `actions/**` majors already sit in the inherited `actions org` group, which holds nothing else.

The checks do not run release, scheduled, or push-only workflows, so an action used only there merges without having run. The README says so and points to `matchFileNames` for a repository that wants those files reviewed.

## User-visible changes

- With `automerge`, a major update of an `actions/*` or `github/*` action merges once the required checks pass.
- With `github-actions`, those majors open in the `major GitHub-published Actions` group.
- Not changed: majors of every other dependency, other third-party actions included, still wait for review.

## Verification

`assertGitHubPublishedActionMajors` in `test-presets.mjs` (new) applies the inherited config with `automerge` alone and with `github-actions` plus `automerge`. It fails on `origin/main` for the four `actions/checkout` and `github/codeql-action` major cases. The `docker/build-push-action` major and the `actions/checkout` minor controls pass there and here. `renovate-config-validator --strict` accepts both presets.

This came up while enabling automerge in [vlsi/issuecrawl#1](https://github.com/vlsi/issuecrawl/pull/1), and replaces the skill-only change in [Netcracker/qubership-ai-packages#193](https://github.com/Netcracker/qubership-ai-packages/pull/193).

author: constantfold
body:
## Why

Competing alternative to #125. Both answer the same question: is this agent on a subscription or on a metered API key? Today the account snapshot cannot answer it for Claude Code. An API key set in `settings.json`, an `apiKeyHelper`, a Console ("Claude Platform") login and Bedrock/Vertex all leave `oauthAccount` looking the same. Codex pointed at OpenRouter through `config.toml` is also invisible.

#125 reads the missing inputs, then **decides in the shipper**: it emits an `<agent>.auth` record with `billing: subscription|api|cloud|local|unknown` under a new `agent-auth/v1` schema. Most of that record repeats what the snapshot already ships. Cursor's record is built entirely from `cursor.local.account`; Codex plan, account and paid-until all come from `id_token_claims`; Claude's account block comes from `oauthAccount`.

This PR ships **only the missing inputs**, as stored, and leaves the decision to the ETL (`account_probes.sql`):

- **No duplication.** Each fact ships once, in the record named after where it is stored.
- **Rules change without a release.** A new `billingType` value, a new Codex provider or a new Claude env flag becomes an ETL fix that also applies to past snapshots. With #125 it is a client release rolled out to the fleet, and old snapshots keep the old verdict.
- **No new format to keep stable.** No `agent-auth/v1` schema.
- **Smaller.** 106 lines of code against #125's 226 lines plus a schema.

## What

Both new records are additive lines in the existing account snapshot file. No new source, no new file, no new network call, no config change.

| Record | Field (as stored) | Ships |
|---|---|---|
| `claude.local.config` (new) | `settings.json:apiKeyHelper` | `true` when set |
| | `settings.json:env.CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK` / `_VERTEX` / `_FOUNDRY`, `env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | value |
| | `settings.json:env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` | `true` when set |
| | `.claude.json:primaryApiKey` (Console login key) | `true` when set |
| | `.claude.json:customApiKeyResponses` | count of approved / rejected keys |
| | credentials `claudeAiOauth.subscriptionType`, `rateLimitTier`, `scopes` | value |
| `codex.local.config` (new) | `config.toml:model_provider` (top level) | value |
| `codex.local.account` (existing) | `auth.json:OPENAI_API_KEY` | `true` when set (new key, other keys unchanged) |

Selection rule: ship the value as stored, unless the value is a credential. Then ship only that it is present. Identity data (email, account and org ids) is not touched; it already ships raw in `oauthAccount` and `id_token_claims`. A test plants a credential in every credential-bearing input and fails if it reaches the snapshot.

Breadth is a superset of #125: it uses every input #125 uses. Additions:
- the `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` value, which shows the gateway (OpenRouter, LiteLLM, a proxy)
- `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` presence
- `rateLimitTier` and `scopes`
- `customApiKeyResponses` counts. `approved > 0` means Claude Code has used an API key from the shell environment, which neither PR can otherwise see.

## Examples

Validated on a real macOS machine (Claude Team, Codex ChatGPT login):

```json
{"source":"claude.local.config","body":{
  ".claude.json":{"customApiKeyResponses":{"approved":0,"rejected":3}},
  "credentials":{"claudeAiOauth":{"rateLimitTier":"default_claude_max_5x","scopes":["user:file_upload","user:inference","user:mcp_servers","user:plugins","user:profile","user:sessions:claude_code"],"subscriptionType":"team"}},
  "settings.json":{}}}
{"source":"codex.local.account","body":{"auth_mode":"chatgpt","id_token_claims":{"...":"..."}}}
{"source":"codex.local.config","body":{}}
```

Claude Code on Bedrock with an API key in settings (from the tests):

```json
{"source":"claude.local.config","body":{
  ".claude.json":{"customApiKeyResponses":{"approved":1,"rejected":2},"primaryApiKey":true},
  "credentials":{"claudeAiOauth":{"rateLimitTier":"default_claude_max_20x","scopes":["user:profile"],"subscriptionType":"max"}},
  "settings.json":{"apiKeyHelper":true,"env":{"ANTHROPIC_API_KEY":true,"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL":"https://openrouter.ai/api","CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK":"1"}}}}
```

Codex on OpenRouter with an API key:

```json
{"source":"codex.local.account","body":{"OPENAI_API_KEY":true,"auth_mode":"apikey"}}
{"source":"codex.local.config","body":{"model_provider":"openrouter"}}
```

The ETL decision table from #125 then becomes SQL over these fields. In Claude Code's order: cloud flag → `apiKeyHelper` / `env.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `primaryApiKey` → `subscriptionType`. For Codex: non-`openai` `model_provider` → `auth_mode`.

## Compatibility

- Additive. Existing records keep their shape; `codex.local.account` gains one optional key. A reader that expects an exact record count sees one more (engine and sources tests updated for that).
- The comparison bytes change, so every Claude and Codex account ships once more after upgrade.
- A missing `settings.json` or `config.toml` ships an empty object. An unreadable one ships `store_unreadable`, as other local records do.
- Golden outputs are unaffected; they do not record account snapshots.

## Not covered (by either PR)

- A key set only in the user's shell environment leaves nothing on disk. The `customApiKeyResponses` counts are the only trace.
- On macOS, a Console login may keep its key in the Keychain, not in `primaryApiKey`. Unverified; needs a test with a Console login.
- Codex `profile`-scoped `model_provider` and Claude managed/project settings, as in #125.

author: jsbcannell
body:
Adds host commands and SDK methods for the machine-override API that shipped in the webserver (vast #6050, HOST-1091).

- `vastai set machine-override FIELD VALUE` → `POST /api/v0/machines/overrides/set/`
- `vastai clear machine-override FIELD` → `POST /api/v0/machines/overrides/clear/`
- SDK: `set_machine_override(...)`, `clear_machine_override(...)`

Fields: `geolocation` ("Region, CC", e.g. `"Guangdong, CN"`), which hosts can set, plus `inet_up` / `inet_down` (Mbps), which only admins can set. `--ids` narrows the change to specific machines; without it the change applies to all of the host's machines. `--host-id` and `--reason` are for admin/support use; the server requires a reason for any admin write. The response lists the machines set, `locked_machine_ids` (an admin value the host can't change) and `skipped_machine_ids` (ids that aren't the host's).

Request fields and value types are checked against the merged server model (`SetMachineOverrideParams` / `ClearMachineOverrideParams`): `field`, `value`, `machine_ids`, `host_id`, `reason`.

Tests: `pytest tests/cli/` → 608 passed (adds 5 in `tests/cli/test_machines_commands.py`).

Docs: vast-ai/docs branch `HOST-1091-machine-overrides-docs`.

author: kingsleyh
body:
The curator asked the model for the whole page, so replies grew with the page: `cli.mdx` hit the 8,000-token cap, and the cut-off page would have been opened as a PR. Re-typing also corrupts text: asked to copy a 4.7 KB section verbatim, DeepSeek v4 Pro changed it 3 times out of 3.

**Now:** the model changes the page through tools.
- `edit` replaces one exact passage and applies only if that passage occurs exactly once. A misquote fails rather than corrupting the page, and text no edit names is never re-typed.
- `append` writes new pages.
- `finish` or `keep_page` ends the edit.

**Fail-closed at every stage:**
- A reply that reaches its token cap is discarded, never applied.
- A page's edits are written only on `finish`.
- A notes reply that reaches its cap has its chunk halved and read again.

**Also:**
- OpenRouter reports a tool call cut off mid-arguments as `tool_calls`, so a reply that spent its whole allowance is now reported as `MaxTokens`.
- `[curator]` gains `notes_max_tokens` and `max_turns`, and its `Default` now matches its serde defaults.

Draft until a live run on `cli.mdx` from this branch shows only the changed passages differ and the docs build passes.

author: ugurcl
body:
## Summary
Adds `/rule pick`: users SELECT rules from a catalog by number instead of writing `--check` specs. The existing `/rule add|list|supersede|forget` behavior is unchanged (pick is intercepted before `rule_command.parse`).

## Usage
```
/rule pick             → print the grouped, numbered catalog
/rule pick 1 3 5       → add the selected rules as ENFORCED
/rule pick 1 3 in app/ → scope the picked code rules to app/ (default: whole repo)
/rule pick 7 src/core  → freeze a path
```

## Catalog (v1 — each maps to an existing, proven check)
1 no console.log → `forbid:console.log` · 2 no new comments → `added:no_comment` · 3 no TODO/FIXME/XXX → `no_todo` · 4 no eval → `forbid:eval` · 5 no "Co-authored-by: Claude" in commits → `message:forbid_any_case:co-authored-by` · 6 no "Generated with Claude" → `message:forbid_any_case:generated with claude` · 7 freeze a path → `frozen --in <path>`

## Design
- **`src/protocol/rule_catalog.zig`** (new): one data-driven catalog table + a pure, unit-tested `plan()`. `pick()` calls the SAME `rule_command` add path — no ledger logic duplicated.
- **Whole-repo by default** (no hardcoded `src/`); an optional trailing `in <path>` scopes the picked code rules. Message rules and item 7's own path are never affected by the batch scope.
- **Freeze-path guard**: item 7 takes the next token as its path only if it is not a bare integer.
- `prompt_hook.zig` delegates `pick`; `rule_command.zig` usage now lists `pick`.

## Tests
`zig build test-unit` (all unit tests, no e2e): 1937/1973 passed, 36 skipped, 0 failed, 0 leaked. CI runs the full suite incl. e2e as the merge gate.

## Scope
Just the pick feature. Follow-ups: an interactive visual checklist (`emetgate rules`), an `emetgate.rules` file, a cross-agent MCP tool.

body:
Closes #849. 운영자 결정(2026-10-26): 보관함 **안 D**, 내 풀이 화면 **안 A**. **운영자 승인(2026-10-26)**: 머지 · 궁합 두 화면도 같은 꼴 · 새 문구 둘 — 캡처(아티팩트)로. #853 을 merge 해 맞췄다.

## 무엇이 참이 되는가

- **풀이 보관함(안 D)** — 폰 · 넓은 화면 모두 한 열의 줄이다. 줄 왼쪽에 작은 책 표지(일간 색 · 등 · 천간 그림, 궁합은 두 얼굴과 점수), 오른쪽에 이름 · 요약 두 줄 · 날짜. 전체 칸은 **인연 궁합 → 사주풀이 → 궁합풀이** 묶음(머리는 제목 + 설명 한 줄, 묶음 안은 DB 가 준 최신순), 아직 도는 것(한 사람 풀이 · 궁합풀이 · 인연 궁합)은 묶음과 상관없이 칩 · 찾기 바로 아래 **「만드는 중」** 에 종류 글자와 함께 모인다. 칩 하나를 고르면 묶음 머리 없이 그 종류만 서고, 그 종류의 만드는 중인 것이 그 목록 맨 위다.
- **#849** — 인연 궁합 줄(다 된 글 · 만드는 중 둘 다)에 상대가 채워 주는 **받는 기운** 그림 + 이름과 균형 한 줄이 선다. 데이터가 기운을 문장 대신 **값**으로 넘긴다(`InboxMatch.elementsToMe` · `balanceShort`, #848 의 `knownElementsOf` 꼴). 인연 기록의 「만드는 중」 편지(`MakingShelf`)도 같은 값으로 고쳤다 — 같은 결함이었다.
- **내 풀이 화면(안 A)** — 「공유 링크 복사」 · 「사주풀이 다시 받기」가 **글 끝**에 반반으로, 그 아래 의견이 「이 풀이는 어떠셨어요?」 한 줄로 접혀 서고 누르면 그 자리에서 펼친다. 머리의 공유 아이콘 · 다시 받기는 걷었다. **수정 전 글이면 다시 받기는 머리의 주 단추 그대로**다(읽기 전에 정하는 일). 풀이권 문구 · 확인 창은 지금 코드의 글자 그대로다 — 새 약속 없음.
- `panel.tsx` 는 한 사람 풀이 · 궁합 · 인연 궁합이 함께 쓰는 칸이라, **직접 본 궁합 화면도 같은 꼴**(글 끝 행동 · 접힌 의견)이 된다. 인연 궁합은 공유 · 다시 받기가 원래 없어 의견만 접힌다.

## 잰 값

- 고치기 전: `shelf.tsx:281` 이 `ELEMENTS.find((one) => one === match.suppliedToMe)` — `suppliedToMe` 는 「나에게 부족한 토(土) · 금(金) 기운을 이 사람이 채워 줘요.」 문장이라 늘 `null`. 로컬 계정(보는 쪽 土 · 金 없음, 상대가 가짐)으로 열어 그림이 안 서는 것을 봤다(전 그림 `shelf-all-phone.png` 의 윤슬 편지).
- 같은 계정 · 같은 데이터: 풀이 3(나 · 엄마 · 동생) · 직접 궁합 5 · 인연 궁합 2(봄비 — 글 있음, 윤슬 — 만드는 중) · 만드는 중인 한 사람 풀이 1(아빠). 폰 390 기준 보관함 전체 길이 2,307 → 2,250 CSS px(표지 2열 → 줄 한 열, 「만드는 중」 묶음이 늘었는데도). 요약이 2열 표지에서 넷째 줄 「…」로 잘리던 것이 두 줄 안에 다 든다(이 데이터의 요약 25~40자).
- 내 풀이 화면 전체 길이(폰 390) 4,903 → 3,800 CSS px — 늘 펼쳐져 있던 설문이 한 줄로 접혔다.

## 돌린 것

- main(#853) merge 뒤 다시: `npm test` 4,249 통과 · 11 건너뜀, typecheck · lint 통과, 보관함 · 내 풀이 · 공유 e2e(signed-in -g) 31 통과 · 1 건너뜀, match.spec 관련 6/6.
- 첫 회: `npm test` — 293 파일 · 4,259 시험 중 통과(첫 회 `scripts/ci-plan.test.ts` 5건이 붉었다 — 이 PR 의 e2e 정규식 `/^복사했(습니다|어요)$/` 의 「습니다」 조각을 배포 판정 시험이 「시험이 글자 그대로 찾는다」로 읽었다. `/^복사했/` 로 바꿔 160/160 통과).
- `npm run typecheck` · `npm run lint` — 통과.
- `npx vitest run app/me/requests/inbox.test.ts app/me/matching/history.test.ts` — 16/16.
- e2e(로컬 스택 · `PLAYWRIGHT_PORT=3140` 의 ui-dev 재사용):
  - `e2e/match.spec.ts -g "받는 기운|요청을 보내 수락하면 같은 결과 화면|키보드만으로"` authed-desktop · mobile — 6/6.
  - `e2e/signed-in.spec.ts` 전부 authed-desktop · mobile — 169 통과 · 3 건너뜀 · 6 붉음 → 고친 뒤: 「저장한 사람의 풀이는 그 사람의 화면에서」(책장 줄이 같은 요약을 들어 `exact` 가 둘을 잡음 → 글의 `blockquote` 로) 2/2 통과. 남은 4 붉음은 「로그인 · 가입이 목적지를 든다」의 로그인 전 사주 문단 둘(3780 · 3892) — 재사용한 ui-dev 서버에 시험용 HMAC 비밀(`TASTE_*`)이 없어 문단이 안 선다. 로그인 전 화면이라 이 PR 이 닿지 않는다 — CI 의 제 서버가 잰다.
  - 공유 시험은 단추가 글 끝이라 재기 전에 굴려 두게 고쳤다(8/8).
- 전후 그림(같은 계정 · 데이터, 폰 390 · 데스크톱 1280, 커밋 안 함): `/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kyunglee-Documents-projects-saju/ef65a074-203e-48b4-b3bc-987307a94382/scratchpad/next-round-build/{before,after}/` — `shelf-all` · `shelf-chip-saju` · `shelf-chip-match` · `shelf-empty` · `reading-end`(+ `-view` 글 끝) · `reading-feedback-open`.

## 잠금이면 일부러 어긴 것

- #849 e2e(「풀이 보관함의 인연 궁합 줄에 받는 기운 그림과 균형 한 줄이 선다」): 줄의 기운을 옛 비교(`elementsToMe.filter((one) => one === match.suppliedToMe)` — 문장과 견줌)로 되돌리면 `Expected substring: "받는 기운"` 으로 붉다. 되돌려 초록.
- 단위(`inbox.test.ts`): `matchOf` 가 `elementsToMe` 를 안 실으면 타입부터 붉다 — 값이 문장이 아니라 오행 글자 목록인지 · 모르는 글자를 버리는지 잰다.

## 문서

결정 여부: **있음** — 결정 점검표 「볼 수 있는 것 · 할 수 있는 것」(보관함 묶음 · 차례 · 풀이 화면의 행동 자리) · 「화면 문구」. **운영자가 답했다**(2026-10-26 안 D · 안 A · 궁합 두 화면도 같이 · 새 문구 둘, 캡처 아티팩트). ADR 0133 「2026-10-26 덧」.
