body:
## 변경 내용

Core가 대화 시작 전·종료 후에 부르는 Luna(Responses API) 호출의 사용량을 활동별로 저장합니다. 기존 회원·활동·결과 테이블은 변경하지 않고 전용 사용량 테이블(`core.core_ai_usage`, V12)을 추가합니다.

| 목적 | 언제 | 연결 대상 |
|---|---|---|
| `SCENARIO_GENERATION` · `SCENARIO_REVIEW` | 연습 장면 생성·검수 | 연습 준비 ID(준비 성공 시 같은 ID로 활동 시작, 실패하면 시작 실패 비용) |
| `RESULT_TEXT` · `GOAL_CANDIDATES` · `REJUDGMENT` | 종료 후 결과 작업 | 활동 세션 ID |
| `SEED_GENERATION` | 목표 후보의 지식 시드 생성 | 후보가 나온 활동 세션 ID |

- 공통 호출부 `CoreLunaClient`에서 실제 전송한 시도마다 한 행을 남깁니다. 재시도·스키마 재요청도 각각 기록하고 `call_id`로 묶습니다. 업무 응답이 거절·검증 실패여도 받은 사용량은 기록합니다.
- 토큰: 입력·출력·캐시 읽기(`cached_tokens`)·**캐시 쓰기(`cache_write_tokens`, 별도 단가)**·추론 토큰. 미확인 값은 NULL로 유지합니다.
- 활동 연결은 서버 내부 값(`AiUsageScope`)으로 넘기며 공급자 요청 본문에 넣지 않습니다. 기존 게이트웨이 시그니처를 바꾸지 않으려고 작업 진입점 3곳(결과 작업·장면 생성·시드 생성)에서 열고, 실행기로 넘기는 3곳(`ResultTextGateway` · `TextAiGateway` · `ScenarioDeadline`)에서 함께 전달합니다.
- 전용 유한 큐와 저장 작업 하나로 비동기 저장합니다. 큐 포화·저장 장애가 결과 작업·연습 시작을 막지 않습니다.
- 계정 삭제 참가자(순서 50)를 추가했습니다. 보호자 외래 키로 삭제 뒤 늦은 저장을 막습니다.
- 수집 스위치 `MUJOONG_CORE_AI_USAGE_ENABLED`(기본 false, Realtime 스위치와 별개)를 `application.yml`·ECS·`render-env`에 연결했습니다.
- main(JIRA-271)을 반영해 `timing.md`의 `mujoong.timing.ai-usage.*` 행을 소유 앱 `realtime · core-api` 한 행으로 합쳤습니다. 계약 문서(`ai-io.md`)와 RUNBOOK 19절을 추가했습니다.

관리자 인증·조회 API·화면·단가 계산과 제브 사용량은 이 PR에 포함하지 않습니다.

## 확인한 내용

증거 종류를 나눠 적습니다(R-M11).

**테스트 대역(가짜 공급자 · 시험 DB)**
- 사용량 관련 시험 통과: `ResponsesUsageTest` · `AiUsageRecorderTest` · `AiUsageScopeTest` · `CoreLunaUsageTest` · `AiUsageRepositoryIT`
- `CoreSchemaIT`, core·realtime `ConfigKeyContractTest`, `LunaConfigurationTest`, `Neo4jIT` 통과
- core 전체 검사(`:core-api:check`, main 병합 전): 1,894건 중 1,892건 통과. 실패 2건(`ReportPdfColdStartTest` · `ReportPdfTest`)은 로컬 Windows에서 하위 Java 프로세스 명령줄 길이 제한(`CreateProcess error=206`)으로 실행되지 못한 것으로, 3회 재시도 모두 같은 원인입니다. 리포트 PDF 코드는 변경하지 않았으며 CI(리눅스) 결과로 확인합니다.

**실제 API · 실제 대화(로컬 실키 스택, main + JIRA-271 + JIRA-277 합친 이미지)**
- 자유대화: 종료 후 `RESULT_TEXT` · `GOAL_CANDIDATES` 행이 해당 활동 ID로 `COMPLETE` 저장
- 연습: 시작 시 `SCENARIO_GENERATION` · `SCENARIO_REVIEW`, 종료 후 `REJUDGMENT` · `RESULT_TEXT` · `GOAL_CANDIDATES` 행이 같은 연습 활동 ID로 저장. Core `LUNA_CALL` 로그 9건과 사용량 행 9건 일치(결과 작업 재시도분 포함)
- 결과 수준 `INSUFFICIENT` 대화는 AI 호출이 없어 행이 생기지 않음(정상)
- 연결 미확인(`session_id` 없음) 행 없음
- 캐시 쓰기 토큰 저장은 실호출 확인 이후에 추가해, 실제 응답 값 확인은 하지 않았습니다(대역 시험만)

## 남은 확인

- CI 전체 검사(특히 리포트 PDF 2건)
- `SEED_GENERATION` 실제 호출 경로 확인(후보가 기존 기술 밖일 때만 호출되어 이번 실대화에서는 발생하지 않음)

Feedback-ID: cmvo361cj000djn072k6f84uw

## Reported request
Add a memorization section with different memorizations throughout the year and individual children's scores.

## Implemented
- New Sunday School Memorization workspace and navigation entry; servants create their own class/year-scoped items rather than choosing from a fixed list.
- Title, optional instructions and UTC calendar date; create/edit/archive without deleting recorded scores.
- Per-child whole-number 0–100 scores and optional notes; blank clears a score, zero is scored, and class summaries exclude unrecorded children.
- Database-derived AuthorizationContext checks active tags, enabled-account status and year-bound assignment scope. Assigned servants/coordinators and authorized admins/priests can write; Prep roles alone cannot. No guardian contacts or production records are included.
- Additive Prisma models and explicit SQL migration with foreign keys, unique child/item scores and database score-range constraint.
- Validation/API/navigation regression tests and feature/rollout documentation.

## Assumptions and limitations
- Items belong to the class and therefore its ministry/academic year. Existing assignment scope and business-data write permissions apply.
- Integer scores out of 100; notes are optional and removed when a score is cleared. Scores remain attached to the original class item when a child moves.
- Current/open-year active classes only in the UI. Archived records are preserved and accessible through the authorized API, but archive browsing/restoring and historical-year selection are not in this first version.
- No parent/student score self-service, notifications, or fixed memorization catalog.
- The durable role/year/assignment backfill must be reconciled per the authorization compatibility workflow before rollout.
- Draft for human review. Nothing has been merged, deployed or marked Completed; no public feedback reply was posted.

## Validation
All development database work used only this feedback's isolated databases on openclaw-feedback-dev; browser fixtures were synthetic.
- bun install --frozen-lockfile and bun db:generate: passed.
- TypeScript --noEmit: passed using the managed wrapper and node --max-old-space-size=1536 node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit. The wrapper's default 1 GiB Node heap exhausted memory after Next generated development types; the bounded 1.5 GiB retry passed.
- bun lint via database.py run: passed.
- bun test:run via database.py run (two workers): 280 files / 2,396 tests passed; 6 files / 58 existing opt-in integration tests skipped.
- Migration: pushed the unchanged release schema to the isolated shadow DB, executed the checked-in migration there, and ran prisma migrate diff from that shadow DB to the feature schema with --exit-code: passed, no difference. Feature migration is also applied to the isolated task DB.
- Playwright/Chromium against the local app: create item, save score/notes, reload score persistence, edit, invalid score rejected with HTTP 400, and archive passed; no browser page errors.
- git diff --cached --check: passed.
- The restart interrupted an earlier validation run; only the subsequent completed run above is counted. A production build/Vercel preview was not run.

## Release considerations
Apply 20261026140000_sunday_school_memorization explicitly under the normal reviewed backup/migration procedure before releasing the feature. Builds never apply it. Application rollback can retain the additive tables and recorded scores. No production migration or deployment was attempted.

## Unsent feedback reply draft
Thank you for this lovely suggestion! A Memorization section is prepared for review, where servants can add different memorizations for their class throughout the year, with optional instructions and a date, then record each child’s score out of 100 and optional notes. It also keeps scores when an item is archived. This is still in progress and has not been released yet.

author: 0blom
body:
Centralised update management, wave 29: the `ccd-*` sweeps read their operator settings from `~/.ccrc/ccrc.env` through ccrc's own reader, so a setting written there survives a reboot.

Plan: https://github.com/Synapsium-Labs/ccrc-pwa/blob/main/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-26-centralised-update-w29-sibling-settings-read-ccrc-env.md (before merge: https://github.com/Synapsium-Labs/ccrc-pwa/pull/1578/files). Follows #1237 (wave 24), whose ruling 9 carried this class to "a later wave with a shared reader file".

## The rule

Six settings the fleet box's sweeps read are now read the way ccrc reads its own (#1237): a nonempty process environment wins, else a plain `KEY=value` line in `~/.ccrc/ccrc.env`, else the default.

| Setting | Sweep | Default | Accepted |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CCRC_GRAPH_BUDGET` | `ccd-graph-sweep` | 8 | 0 to 999 |
| `CCRC_GRAPH_MAX_WORKERS` | `ccd-graph-sweep` | 4 | 1 to 99 |
| `CCRC_KEEPALIVE_MODEL` | `ccd-telemetry-keepalive` | `haiku` | any |
| `CCRC_KEEPALIVE_PROMPT` | `ccd-telemetry-keepalive` | `Reply with the single word: ok` | plain, or one whole pair of quotes |
| `CCRC_KEEPALIVE_FRESH` | `ccd-telemetry-keepalive` | 1800 | ASCII digits, representable by bash decimal integer comparisons; zero and leading zeros allowed |
| `CCRC_USAGE_SWEEP_DAYS` | `ccd-usage-sweep` | 7 | 1 to 999 |

Their units have no shell, no `EnvironmentFile=` and no `Environment=`, so until now only the user manager's environment reached them, and a reboot lost a setting unless an `environment.d` file was written. `EnvironmentFile=` was refused again for #1237's reasons: systemd's parse instead of the one reader, every secret in `ccrc.env` exported into the sweep and its children, and a set environment could no longer win.

## The shared reader: generated, not moved, and not #1404's mechanism

- `ccd/lib/ccrc-settings.sh` is generated by `deploy/gen-settings-lib.mjs`: the `BOX_ENV_FILE=` and `CCRC_SETTINGS=` lines and the eight functions of `_ccrc_knob`'s closure, copied whole out of `ccd/ccrc`. `server/test/ccrc-settings-lib.test.ts` holds it byte-equal (W29-L1), closed over what it calls (L2), inert when sourced (L3), and answering exactly as `ccd/ccrc` does over sixteen fixture cases, including a setting inside an unrelated multi-line quoted value (L4). `node deploy/gen-settings-lib.mjs --check` names the first differing line.
- It is not a move: moving `_ccrc_knob` and the `_box_*` model out of `ccd/ccrc` would shift every line citation and the slices that lift `_box_env_value` by name, and break #1237's census.
- It is not #1404's pinned-library mechanism, which fits one fixed library pinned into ccd's stamped body, not three unstamped timers. This PR touches neither `ccd/ccd`, nor #1404's `lib/` directory, nor any backup-set row. An integrity pin for this file is a follow-up once #1404 merges.
- Placed 0644 at `~/.local/libexec/ccrc/ccrc-settings.sh` by `_inst_bins` on every OS and role (above the sweeps it serves), by `deploy.sh`'s agent arm after ccd's pair, and removed by `_uninst_tree_bins` in a statement of its own. W29-I1 to I4; the D-6051 census now reads `_inst_bins`' placements outside `~/.local/bin`.
- Each sweep sources it beside itself first (how the repository's suites run), else from `~/.local/libexec/ccrc`, with one two-line loader spelled identically in each.

## Refusals

A setting the reader cannot read (a line it does not take, an unreadable file), a value out of range, or a missing or broken library stops the pass with exit 1, and never runs a default. The graph sweep and the keepalive stop before their lock; the usage sweep stops after its pause check, so a paused sweep stays paused, and before its lock. The stderr line, which the unit's journal keeps, names the setting, where it came from (`the environment` or `~/.ccrc/ccrc.env`) and what was refused. `ccrc doctor`'s `box-settings` reports the six like ccrc's own, on every role; on a server-role box, where no sweep runs, a sweep setting the file sets, including an empty/default value, says so.

## The census's sibling half

`ccrc-settings-census.test.ts` grows a W29 describe over the bash executables `_inst_bins` places (derived) plus `ccd/ccrc-models-probe`, and over the `.mjs` helpers `ccd/ccrc` names:
- S1: each setting is read once, in the knob shape, never expanded with a default;
- S2 and S3: every other `CCRC_` name a sweep or helper reads is a reasoned exception (`call-bound`, `fixture-path`, `handshake`, `constant`, and a new class, `tuning`), and every exception is still read;
- S4: siblings have no direct box-env reader (quoted `~/.ccrc/ccrc.env` messages are allowed); the helper half catches only a literal `ccrc.env` beside a direct fs opener on the same line, not the indirect history role-reader seam;
- S5: one loader spelling; S6: the units give no shell, no `EnvironmentFile=` and no `CCRC_` environment; S7: no sweep assigns the reader's names; S8: the example's budget block names the unit's `TimeoutStartSec`; S9: the doctor's list of the sweeps' settings equals what they take.

## Residue folded

- **R38** (W29-A1, A2): the validators of values read from outside spell their ten digits (`cmd_wrappers`, `_acct_candidates`, `_codex_port_ok`, `_upd_deadline_ms`, `_upd_watchdog_probe_gap_s`, `_upd_sweep`, the keepalive's knob loop). Measured: under `en_US.UTF-8`, `[0-9]` takes `²`, `٣` and `５`.
- **R45** (W29-Y1 to Y6): `ccd-update-sync`'s mask covers userinfo after one or more scheme slashes and with no scheme (which curl takes as http), under local `LC_ALL=C`, including invalid UTF-8 bytes. Its header says which rules it applies.
- **R46** (W29-T1 to T3): a counted backup data set from before a schema migration is the pre-migration keep, so no fourth set is kept for it. **This changes backup retention.**

## Residue carried

- **R48** and **R50**'s first and fourth bullets (the bootstrap's release-host defences, SHA256SUMS held to one line, the watchdog on an undecided deadline): out of this wave by the coordinator's ruling, to an issue.
- R37 (server inventory), R41 (macOS install), R42 and R50's fifth bullet (test teardown), R43 (test hygiene), R44 (text and pin nits), R50's second bullet (needs a server change): carried as the plan's "Not in this wave" lists. R36, R39, R40, R47 and R49: closed there, with reasons.

## Growth

`ccd/ccrc` +5 net code lines (the placement and the removal); every other edit there is in place. No other listed file changed.

## Pins changed on purpose

- `keepalive-freshness-parity.test.ts`: its broad and narrow patterns move from `: "${CCRC_KEEPALIVE_FRESH:=N}"` to `_ccrc_knob CCRC_KEEPALIVE_FRESH N && …`, keeping the two-tier count.
- `ccrc-settings-census.test.ts`: the SCOPE paragraph; C2 and C4 read the sweeps' calls too.
- `install-census.test.ts`: the D-6051 spine reader reads `_inst_bins`' non-PATH placement.
- The inherited-env scrub lists and the three sweep harnesses drop the six names.

## The operator's migration

This PR asks no act on any box. After it reaches the fleet box: write each sweep setting you rely on as a `~/.ccrc/ccrc.env` line, read `ccrc doctor`'s `box-settings`, then remove any drop-in or `environment.d` line for these names. A set environment still wins over the file.

Deviations D-6979 to D-6985 are defined in the plan's ledger; D-6986 is spare.

author: trungdong
body:
The PROV-XML reader no longer reads a name whose prefix is not declared as a local part of the default namespace. A typo or a missing `xmlns:` declaration such as `prov:id="zz:x"` used to land silently in the default namespace when the document declared one. It is now refused through the model's one rejection, as every other reader refuses it, with a `ProvXMLException` that names the element and the line and carries the model's error as `__cause__`. The writer stops relying on that fallback, so `prov`'s own output reads back under the stricter reader.

What changes:

- The writer spells a default-namespace local part holding `:` under a prefix bound to the default IRI, `dn:a:b` or the prefix the document already binds, in a record or bundle `prov:id`, a `prov:ref` and `xsd:QName` text, as it already did in `xsi:type`. It used to write the bare `a:b`, which only the reader's fallback read back, and which read back as another IRI when the document also declared a prefix `a`.
- The reader resolves a name through the element's `nsmap` first and sends every name the `nsmap` does not resolve to the model. The model resolves a prefix the document has already registered, including `prov` and `xsd`, and reads an empty prefix as a name with no colon. Anything else is refused: "its prefix 'zz' is not declared", #675's reason for a value equal to the default namespace IRI, and "it has no prefix and no default namespace is declared" for a name with no colon and no `xmlns` in scope. The positions are a record or bundle `prov:id`, a `prov:ref`, `xsd:QName` text, `xsi:type`, an attribute element in no namespace, and a reference given as element text.
- A reference given as element text (`<prov:entity>ex:e1</prov:entity>`) resolves through the element's `nsmap` as a `prov:ref` does. 3.2.3 resolved it against the names registered so far, so it compacted a full IRI and rejected a prefix the document element declared that no earlier name had used.
- Whitespace around a name in `xsd:QName` text and in reference text is stripped, as `xsd:QName`'s whitespace facet reads it. An empty `xsd:QName` element, which raised a bare `TypeError`, is a `ProvXMLException`. An attribute element's escaped local part is resolved in the namespace its tag carries and never split at `:`.
- A file 3.2.3 wrote with `xsi:type=":t"` or `":a:b"` now reads back with the datatype in the default namespace.

Why: the fallback that read `prov`'s bare spelling back was the same branch that misread an undeclared prefix, so neither could be fixed alone. A reader-only fix broke `prov`'s own round trip of a default-namespace local part holding `:`, which is why the writer and reader change together. A file 3.2.3 wrote with such a local part in a `prov:id`, a `prov:ref` or `xsd:QName` text is now refused like any undeclared prefix. `HISTORY.md` says how to fix it: declare a prefix for the default IRI and write the name under it. `HISTORY.md` lists the reader's refusals under "Rejected input" and the writer's spelling under "Fixes", and the 3.3.0 preparation guide gains a table row and the reader's error for PROV-XML.

Closes #677.

author: tvxsha
body:
## What this adds
An optional learned importance score that retrieval can use instead of the hand set blend. It is off by default, so the running system and the demo behave exactly as before.

## Why
In the previous PR (learned importance model), a model trained on LoCoMo predicted which turns will be needed later and ranked evidence better than similarity alone. That model used position features (session number, position in the conversation), which a live chat does not have. This PR adds a version that uses only features of the message text, so it can run inside the real pipeline.

## How it works
- memory_engine/importance_model.py: computes 7 text features (word count, character count, has photo, has digit, capitalised words, has question mark, starts with first person) and returns the probability that a message will be needed later. If the model file is missing it returns None and nothing breaks.
- memory_engine/config.py: two new settings. USE_LEARNED_IMPORTANCE (default 0) and LEARNED_IMPORTANCE_WEIGHT (default 0.15).
- memory_engine/retrieve.py: when the flag is on and the model exists, items are ranked by similarity + 0.15 * learned score. Otherwise the original 0.7 * similarity + 0.3 * score blend is used, unchanged.
- evaluation/train_text_importance.py: trains the text only model on all 10 LoCoMo conversations and saves memory_engine/models/importance_text.joblib.
- evaluation/importance_nested_weight.py: new --text-only option to evaluate the text only features.
- tests/test_importance_model.py: 5 new offline tests (feature values, missing model fallback, unchanged behaviour with the flag off, reordering with the flag on, fallback when the flag is on but the model is missing). All 86 tests pass.

## Results (text only features, weight chosen without peeking, 1,535 questions)
- All evidence in the top 5: 0.349 (similarity only) to 0.387, gain +3.8 points, 95 percent CI [+2.5, +5.3]
- At least one evidence turn in the top 5: 0.443 to 0.514, gain +7.1 points, 95 percent CI [+5.5, +8.7]
- Better than similarity only in 8 of 10 conversations, tied in 2, worse in none
- The chosen weight was 0.15 in 8 of 10 folds, so 0.15 is the default

Dropping the position features costs little: ROC AUC for predicting importance goes from 0.785 to 0.770.

## Limits
- These results come from ranking all turns of a conversation. The live system stores only some turns, so the end to end effect still has to be tested with the ablation experiment.
- The importance label comes from benchmark questions, so it is a proxy for what a user would need.

## How to try it
python evaluation/build_importance_data.py
python evaluation/train_text_importance.py
Set USE_LEARNED_IMPORTANCE=1 in .env to turn it on.

author: burak-bayir
body:
## What this changes

`pnpm check`, which `bin/check-local` runs, now fails any change that drops type coverage below 100% or adds a type escape hatch.

- `pnpm typecheck` runs `tsc --noEmit` and then `type-coverage --strict --at-least 100`. Strict mode counts `any`, unsafe `as` casts and `!` assertions as uncovered.
- The new `pnpm lint` runs ESLint with inline config off. It bans every type assertion except `as const`, every `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-expect-error` and `@ts-nocheck` comment, and every `type-coverage:ignore` comment. A `// eslint-disable` comment becomes a warning, and `--max-warnings 0` fails it.
- ESLint fails any `.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs` or `.cjs` file, so every file is TypeScript that `tsc` checks.
- `tsconfig.json` includes every file, sets `erasableSyntaxOnly` so Node can strip the types of each script, and drops `skipLibCheck` and its exclude list.
- `esbuild.config.mjs` and `scripts/check-reproducible.mjs` move to TypeScript. Node strips their types and runs them with no build step.
- `src/worker.ts` narrows tool params, config and response bodies with record checks instead of casts. Non-object params now get the missing-parameter error or a default request, where main threw a `TypeError`. A new test covers that case.
- type-coverage needs the TypeScript 6 compiler API. `typescript` points at `@typescript/typescript6`. `tsc` still runs TypeScript 7 from `@typescript/native`.
- ESLint loads `eslint.config.ts` with its `unstable_native_nodejs_ts_config` flag, which ESLint 10.13.0 lists as active, so the repository needs no `jiti` dependency.

## Measured

| Measure | main | this branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `type-coverage --strict` | 99.55%, 10 of 2,248 identifiers uncovered in `src` and `tests` | 100.00%, 0 of 2,557 across every file |
| Type casts other than `as const` | 10 | 0 |
| JavaScript files | 2 | 0 |
| Files outside the type check | 3, the 2 `.mjs` scripts and `vitest.config.ts` | 0 |
| `skipLibCheck` and tsconfig excludes | 1 and 2 | 0 and 0 |

## Red proof

A scratch copy got 1 escape hatch at a time in `src/constants.ts`, then ran `tsc --noEmit`, `type-coverage --strict --at-least 100` and the ESLint step.

author: firasletaif-ctrl
body:
## Ce que fait cette PR

Ajoute une **corbeille pour les congrès** : un congrès supprimé n'est pas détruit tout de suite, il reste restaurable **30 jours**, puis il est effacé définitivement avec ses données.

## Côté desk

- **Mettre à la corbeille** (administrateur) : *Mes congrès* → ⚙ du congrès, ou *Paramètres* depuis le desk. Une fenêtre rappelle les inscrits, les arrivées et le montant encaissé avant validation.
- Le congrès disparaît immédiatement de la liste, du sélecteur du haut, des badges, des rapports et des exports ; l'API ne le sert plus et les postes encore ouverts basculent sur un autre congrès (leur cache local de ce congrès est purgé).
- **Section « Corbeille des congrès »** en bas de *Mes congrès* : nom, date, nombre d'inscrits/arrivées, auteur de la suppression, **compte à rebours** (rouge à 3 jours ou moins).
- **Restaurer** (tous les comptes) : retour exact de l'inscrits, arrivées, paiements, grille tarifaire et modèles de badge.
- **Effacer définitivement** (administrateur, case de confirmation) : suppression irréversible du congrès et de tout ce qui s'y rattache.

## Côté serveur

- Colonnes `events.deleted_at` / `events.deleted_by` (migration douce, aucune perte sur une base existante).
- `POST /api/events/<id>/trash` (admin), `POST /api/events/<id>/restore` (tous), `POST /api/events/<id>/purge` (admin).
- Purge automatique des congrès expirés au démarrage et à chaque consultation de `/api/events` — aucune tâche de fond à installer.
- `GET /api/events` renvoie la liste active + `trash` (avec `daysLeft` / `purgeAt`) + `trashCount`.
- Un congrès en corbeille est refusé partout : participants, tarifs, badges, sync, modification.
- Sauvegarde ZIP **v6** (`deleted_at` / `deleted_by` dans `01_events.csv`) ; les ZIP **v5 et antérieurs restent restaurables** (congrès tous actifs).

## Vérifications

- Parcours API complet testé : création → suppression → liste → 404 sur les données du congrès → restauration → purge → expiration automatique (30 jours antidatés).
- Sauvegarde/restauration testée en v6 **et** en v5 simulée.
- Démo mise à jour : un congrès en corbeille depuis 4 jours (26 jours restants) pour voir la fonctionnalité en direct.
- `README.md` : nouvelle section « Supprimer ou restaurer un congrès (corbeille, 30 jours) ».

author: davidmrgaona
body:
## Causa

En las páginas del enlace del correo (cancelar y confirmar la inscripción), cada fila de la tarjeta de datos era un `flex justify-between` sin separación. Cuando el valor ocupaba más de una línea en un móvil, se comía todo el ancho: la etiqueta quedaba pegada («MesaPrueba…», «Fechalunes…») y el texto partido se alineaba a la izquierda.

## Cambios

En las 10 filas de `CancelRegistration.vue` y `ConfirmRegistration.vue`:

- fila: `gap-4`
- `<dt>`: `shrink-0`, para que la etiqueta no se parta cuando el valor es largo
- `<dd>`: `text-right` y `min-w-0 break-words`, para que un título largo sin espacios se parta dentro de la tarjeta en lugar de desbordarla

Además, los dos botones del pie («Volver» y la acción) se apilan por debajo de `sm` (`flex flex-col gap-4 sm:flex-row`, como en `MyTables.vue`). Uno al lado del otro, a 375 px cada uno tenía unos 130 px y «Cancelar inscripción» se partía en dos líneas. «Volver» queda arriba, en el mismo orden que el DOM, así que el tabulador y el lector de pantalla siguen el orden visual.

## Pruebas

- A 375 px, en `/mesas/cancelar/{token}` con un título largo: la etiqueta y el valor quedan separados y el valor partido sale alineado a la derecha. Con una palabra larga sin espacios, la tarjeta no desborda ni aparece desplazamiento horizontal.
- A 375 px los botones quedan apilados, a ancho completo y de 44 px de alto; a 768 px siguen en fila.
- ESLint y Prettier del core sobre los dos ficheros.

Closes #140

author: luojiaxuan
body:
## Motivation

With `max_concurrency > 1`, `SimpleScheduler` ran each compute call through `asyncio.to_thread`, on the event loop's default executor, which the 50 ms inbox poll also uses. That pool hands work to whichever thread is free and keeps spawning threads up to `min(32, cpu_count + 4)`, so over a long run a stage's compute drifts across a growing set of threads. Every thread that runs a CUDA stage keeps its own cuBLAS/cuDNN handles and a 32 MiB cuBLAS workspace for the life of the process.

Measured on an H200 Qwen3-Omni session server built without #3111 (audio encoder at the default four workers): the `audio_encoder` process grew in steps of exactly +32 MiB allocated and about +104 MiB in nvidia-smi, 32 steps in all (the pool's cap), +3.1 GB after a C1 → C2 → C4 → C8 ramp versus +0.56 GB for C8 on a fresh server, and nothing came back after the sessions closed. 12 of the steps happened during C1 with one session open, so it follows uptime, not concurrency. With the config preallocating ~94% of the GPU, C8 after the ramp failed twice with `CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED`.

On main the Qwen audio encoder runs at `max_concurrency=1` since #3111, so it no longer hits this, but every other GPU stage on the concurrent path does (e.g. the zonos2 speaker encoder at 4 workers, the dots_tts reference encoder at 8).

## Modifications

- `run_workers` owns a `ThreadPoolExecutor` of exactly `max_concurrency` threads for compute, with the context still copied into each call as `to_thread` did. Per-thread CUDA state is bounded by the configured concurrency instead of by uptime.
- Nemotron ASR's session scheduler no longer resizes the loop's default executor to `max_concurrency + 1`; that only existed to bound its compute threads, which the scheduler now does.

## Tests

- New case in `tests/unit_test/pipeline/test_simple_scheduler_concurrent.py`: with `max_concurrency=2`, a barrier and 40 requests, compute runs on exactly 2 threads. Failed 30/30 on main, passed 30/30 with the change.
- `pipeline/test_simple_scheduler_concurrent.py` + `nemotron3_5_asr`: 57 passed; the 3 `test_websocket_stage_final_drain_and_cleanup` failures also fail on main on this Mac.

author: alexandrapaiz
body:
## Skill seat, 2026-10-26 (hook, capacity returned): `skill-library-engineering` retrofitted to 113 lines, unmeasured, and two of its own numbers were wrong

**The option I chose, named at the top as the org rule asks.** My seat had two
open pull requests. I **merged #587's branch into this one in my first turns and
supersede it**, because this run appends to `docs/ideas.md`,
`docs/research/reading-queue.md` and `skills/_validation/results/`, which are
exactly the files #587 touched. The supersede proof,
`git log --oneline origin/alexandria-skill/2026-10-26-message-prompts-hold ^HEAD`,
printed nothing before I closed it, and I closed it myself rather than leaving it
for the owner. **#582 is deliberately not merged here**, because it is held under
section 10's Tier B path check on `prompts/skill-extract.md` and merging it would
take a second pull request into that hold. **Merge order: #582 first, then this
one.** The two diffs share no file under `skills/`, and the two register files
they both append to will want a trivial textual resolution in that order.

**Chain depth: two.** #587 was the first link from `main` since #464, and this is
the second. Not a chain, and no seat is blocked on merges because of it.

**This event was not already answered.** The payload said a provider limit
refused my last run and has now reset. #587 is a completed run with a finished
retrofit in it, not a refused one, so this is a genuine new run rather than the
duplicate-wake class that `INC-2026-10-24-one-event-wakes-two-runs...` records. I
checked before assuming.

**No database and no eval key, verified rather than assumed.** `NEON_RO_URL` is
absent, so this run surveyed no cluster and extracted nothing, which is what the
charter prescribes. For the gate I ran both arms to see the refusal rather than
quoting the charter: the subject refuses with `kimi-k2.6: not listed by moonshot
for this key` and the judge with `openai/gpt-oss-120b: not listed by groq for
this key`. No key of either kind is in this environment. So this retrofit is
**unmeasured**, in that word, and `status` moved from `active` to `provisional`.

---

## The work: the last entry in the chair's retrofit queue

`skill-library-engineering` is the fifth and final skill in the 2026-09-29 ADR-38
retrofit queue (`docs/ideas.md:7564`), after `context-window-engineering`,
`evaluation-integrity`, `recursive-harness-self-improvement` and
`self-improving-post-training-loops`. **Maintenance was checked first and nothing
fired**: the only consumer report in the library is still
`harness-engineering/reviews/2026-09-29-ursa-chair.md`, so no ADR-38 trigger
exists, and with no database there is no graph to survey.

**Rule 4, length.** `wc -l` **337 to 113**, including frontmatter. Nine prose
sections became six deltas. Four of the nine merged rather than were cut: set
selection folded into the boundary delta, where it belongs because both are about
telling neighbours apart, and cross-model transfer folded into the
stop-at-grounding delta, where it is the reason the grounding cost amortizes.
The checklist moved first, seven lines, one per delta plus the no-skill-baseline
line.

**Rule 2, thresholds.** Every delta ends in a numbered procedure with numbers in
it: 30 candidates on 50 held-out examples, threshold 0.6 approached downward,
three revision rounds, one owning file per failure class.

**Rule 1, deltas rather than restatement.** Each *Validation:* tag now names what
this run expects a bare subject to supply already and what it does not, so the
bare-first screen has something to test against when a key arrives. Delta 3's tag
is the sharpest: a bare model will say "write a clear, specific description", and
is unlikely to say that showing the router the full body leaves 29 percent of
picks wrong at twenty times the context.

### ADR-35: all five papers read in full, and two statements did not survive

Read this run through the arXiv HTML, method, results, ablations and limitations:
`2609.05824` (Beyond Top-k), `2609.11682` (COBRA-Skills), `2609.15982` (The
Router Within), `2609.17653` (Reflect, Revise, Reuse), `2609.21749`
(GraphSkillEvo). None was paywalled and none was skipped. Roughly thirty numbers
in the file checked out exactly. Two statements are wrong against the papers, and
**the paper wins in both**.

| the skill said | the paper says |
|---|---|
| an expert-written and a model-written skill "both left an agent slightly worse off on average than no skill at all", over "four to five benchmarks on two OpenAI models" | net negative in **one of three** model-harness configurations. Codex harness on GPT-5.4: 67.23 and 67.21 against 67.97. No harness: **+2.14 and +2.13** on GPT-5.4, **+7.39 and +8.42** on GPT-5.4-nano |
| loose matching is "more than twice as costly" as strict matching | 14.3 points against 2.8. **Five times** |

The first is the one that matters, and it is worse than #587's equivalent because
this skill is the one the library writes itself under. It was an overstatement in
the skill's own favour, on the finding the skill leans on hardest, used to justify
the procedure it asks of every reader. **The replacement finding is narrower and
more useful**: on SpreadsheetBench a hand-written skill was net negative in all
three configurations, -1.31, -0.48 and -7.50, and a described-from-the-task one
too, -3.57, -2.39 and -9.28. So the harm is task-shaped rather than model-shaped,
and delta 1's procedure is now "report the delta per task family, never as an
average", which is a rule a reader can execute rather than a warning they can
only believe.

**That is three consecutive runs finding paper-level errors by reading.** #582
found four attribution figures that appear nowhere in their paper, #587 found four
contradicted statements, this run found two. Ten corrections across three skills,
every one surfaced by reading rather than by any gate the pipeline runs. The
ledger entry says plainly that this is now a rate, and proposes the sampling duty
as a standing one.

The reading also made the skill better rather than only shorter. Four facts the
old version did not carry are now decision rules: that placing the twenty
shortlisted full bodies in the menu does not close the routing gap (correct body
present for 92 percent of queries, another skill chosen on 29 percent, median
prompt 1.3K tokens to 28K to 52K, 26 to 124 seconds of prefill), that a naive
similarity penalty cut multi-skill full coverage 0.424 to 0.254, that the same
skills held their lead under Claude Code and Codex, and that trajectory-driven
mutation is worth 17 points against crossover's 5.

### The eval suite

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| tasks | 11 | 12 |
| hard checks, scored with no judge | 3 | **4** |
| rubric criteria tied to a certificate | 0 of 32 | **32 of 32** |
| rubric tasks shipping an exploit | 0 of 8 | **8 of 8** |
| conformant suites in the library | 8 of 9 | **9 of 9** |

- `sections` repointed at the six delta headings. Every delta is exercised and
  `--check` reports no coverage gap for this skill; the library's two remaining
  gaps are other skills' "What this file no longer carries" sections.
- `sle-t10` added as a `tests_pass` hard check with no judge in it. `router.py`
  ships with delta 4's two defects planted, a 0.4 reuse threshold and a raw-cosine
  redundancy penalty. **The reference implementation passes 6 of 6 and the file as
  shipped passes 2 of 6**, which I verified by running both arms. A
  threshold-only fix still fails the two complementary-pair tests, so the task
  cannot be half-answered.
- Two anchors restated against the papers: `sle-t1` now demands the configuration
  behind the net-negative result and its anchor 1 names the unconfigured version
  as the overstatement this library carried, and `sle-t4` says five times rather
  than twice.
- Library certificates rose **68 to 100 of 265**, the whole increase from this
  suite.
- `suite_version` stays 2. It is the format contract `tools/skill_eval.py`

author: ayushcodes10
body:
Every number in `docs/BENCHMARKS.md` is about this system with no baseline beside it. `eval/external.py` had `ingest()` and the query wired straight to `write_episode` and `query_memory`, so there was nowhere for another system to go.

This is the seam, the scoring work that makes a cross-system comparison honest, and the first competitor through it.

**Not the whole of #147.** Still to come: Zep, Letta and cognee adapters, the CLI wiring, the judged QA pass, and any real run on either corpus. Landing this separately because the scoring decisions below are the part worth reviewing on their own.

## The decision that makes or breaks the comparison

`score_question` matched results to gold turns by reading a turn key out of provenance. A backend that cannot supply one would have had every key read as `""`, matched nothing, and scored **0.000** on MRR, recall@k, hit@k and session@k.

That is the number that would have made this dishonest: it reports a competitor that retrieved exactly the right content, and merely could not name its source turn, as having retrieved nothing. Understating a rival, in our favour, in the one direction a reader of our own benchmark has most reason to suspect.

So `attributed=False` records `None`, `means()` drops `None` instead of averaging it in, and the report carries the reason. `statistics.mean` over a list holding `None` raises, which is the right failure: the choice has to be made, not coerced. The test that matters asserts both halves at once — null turn-keyed metrics **and** `answer_words@5 == 1.0` for the same result — so "not computable" cannot be misread as "found nothing".

## Three things the live API said, all contradicting what I assumed

| assumed | measured |
|---|---|
| `add` is synchronous | returns `status: PENDING`; ~5s before the memory is queryable |
| `search` takes `user_id=` like `add` | raises; needs `filters={"user_id": ...}` |
| `metadata` is lost in extraction | `turn_key` survives even with `infer=True` |

The first is why `settle()` is on the protocol rather than hidden in the adapter: a harness that ingests then queries immediately scores Mem0 at zero. It waits for the memory count to stop moving, because it cannot wait for a count it cannot predict.

The third means Mem0's results *are* attributable, so the `attributed` flag is not needed for it. The work was still right; it just applies to a different backend than expected.

## And one the smoke test found, which matters more than any number

Attribution can be **present and wrong**. The fixture run returned `attribution_rate` 1.0 with `recall@k` 0.000 and `session@10` 0.750 — right sessions, wrong turns. A memory Mem0 synthesised from several turns carries *one* of their keys, so a result whose content answers the question can be keyed to a sibling turn and score as a miss.

`attribution_rate` measures whether a key was there, not whether it was the right one, and nothing outside Mem0 can tell the difference. So the turn-keyed metrics understate Mem0 by an unmeasurable amount. That belongs in the writeup, not a footnote. Four questions on a twelve turn fixture say nothing statistically; the mechanism was what was being checked.

## Other notes

- `external.ingest()` now delegates to `EchoBackend.ingest` instead of holding a second copy. Those assume-new assertions have been found the hard way twice (without the utterance one, 419 turns became 18; without the speaker one, 344 of 680 were silently deferred) and two copies of that is one that goes out of sync.
- `EchoBackend` is the old behaviour moved behind the protocol unchanged. A comparison where our side ran one code path and theirs ran another is measuring the harness.
- `infer` stays at Mem0's default `True`. `infer=False` skips the model and would be a faster, cheaper Mem0 that nobody buys.
- **`mem0ai` is deliberately not in `pyproject.toml`.** The backend SDKs pull heavy, mutually incompatible trees and belong in a separate environment.

## Verified

- 455 unit tests pass, including 28 scoring tests, 5 of them new and covering the null-not-zero behaviour
- 14 integration tests pass, including the resume and write-refusal paths, which are the two that would catch a wrong delegation
- one live end to end Mem0 run through the harness: ingest, settle, score, render

Refs #147

author: huancheng65
body:
Step 2 of the auth consolidation, last kind: questions and answers. It follows #4881 (teams), #4885 (spaces) and #4892 (problems), and checks itself against the step-0 question matrix from #4879. With it, every team, space, problem, question and answer route asks one `can()`, and the old role tables are gone.

## What changes

- `app/domain/questions/permissions.py`: what changes a question is its asker's. That covers editing or deleting it, setting a bounty, accepting an answer or taking the acceptance back, and withdrawing an invitation.
- `app/domain/answers/permissions.py`: editing or deleting an answer is its author's.
- A question or answer that was deleted, or never existed, gets 404.
- `can()` learns both kinds. These routes declare `needs(...manage)`:
  - the six question routes: `accept_answer`, `unaccept_answer`, `update_question`, `delete_question`, `set_question_bounty`, `delete_invitation`;
  - the two answer routes: `update_answer`, `delete_answer`.

## What is deleted

- The eight author checks in `QuestionsService` and `AnswersService`, and the `user_id` parameters only they read.
- The role × action × resource checker, which no route uses any more:
  - `app/auth/domains/` (the question and task tables; team and space went in the earlier PRs);
  - `require_permission`, `PermissionChecker` and the start-up `register_all_permissions()`;
  - `Action`, `Resource`, `Role`, `Permission`, `RoleHierarchy`, `PermissionRule` and `PermissionConfig` from `app/auth/core.py`, along with `AuthUserInfo.domain_roles`;
  - `tests/unit/test_permission_checker.py`, the tests of that deleted code.
- `get_auth_user`, `require_auth_user`, `AuthUserInfo` and `SystemRole` stay.

## Fixed

Step 0 left two refusals out because they looked like bugs.
- `GET /questions/{id}/followers` listed follower ids to anonymous callers, though the question itself needs sign-in. It now needs sign-in.
- `DELETE /questions/{id}/accept` on a question that does not exist answered 403. It now answers 404, as accepting does.

Both regression tests are in `test_who_may_act_on_a_question.py`. `prove-regression.py --without origin/main` shows each fails on `main` and passes here.

## Tests changed

- `test_questions_service.py`, `test_answers_service.py`: removed the cases that asserted the service refused a non-author. The service no longer judges the caller, and the step-0 matrix asserts those rules over HTTP. Deleting an invitation on a deleted question now raises "not found" where it raised "forbidden", and that assertion is updated.
- `test_task_indexes.py`: it used the deleted task role lookup to exercise the claim index, and now uses the claim lookup itself.
- The refusal-key baseline is lowered.

## Deferred from the plan, and why

The plan's step-2 row also says to refuse new `ROUTE_DECIDES` declarations. That is not in this PR. `needs()` resolves a signed-in person only, through `get_auth_user`. Project and channel routes are reached by AI teammates' and 芝士's credentials, through `ActorResolver`, which cannot declare `needs()` today. A ceiling now would block every new project route for nothing. It belongs with step 3, where every credential becomes one caller that `needs()` can read.

`TaskVisibilityService._is_space_admin` also stays (noted in #4892): it reads the admin relation inside the visibility query that the list pages share.

## Hands-on check

On dev:
- As a question's asker: accept an answer, then take the acceptance back.
- As someone else: try the same on their question; it is refused.
- Signed out: open a question's followers list; it asks you to sign in.

The four step-0 matrices (team, space, problem, question), the question and answer unit tests, the index test and the refusal-key guard all pass: 310 tests on the merged head. `pyright` on the changed files, the import contracts and the manual anchor check pass.

Fixes: N/A

### What was the problem/requirement? (What/Why)

uv-backed Hatch environments do not include a `pip` executable. Repositories using plain `pip` commands in `hatch.toml` could therefore install dependencies outside the Hatch environment and fail at test time.

### What was the solution? (How)

Add cross-platform `pip` shims to the runner `PATH` that forward existing commands to the pinned `uv pip` installation. The shims use exact Unix and Windows line endings and do not install pip into Hatch environments.

### What is the impact of this change?

Repositories using the shared Python workflow can retain their existing Hatch commands while installing dependencies into the correct uv-backed environment.

### How was this change tested?

- Verified against an unchanged `deadline-cloud` `hatch.toml` containing plain `pip install` commands.
- Confirmed a fresh Hatch environment could import both `deadline` and `pytest`.
- Verified exact Unix and Windows shim bytes using Python 3.9.
- The shared repository checks pass on Ubuntu, Windows, and macOS.

### Was this change documented?

No documentation change is required; comments in the workflow explain the compatibility shim.

### Is this a breaking change?

No.

body:
<!-- Use this template only when the primary intent is to restore broken behavior. -->

## User impact

Anyone editing a table in `RichTextEditor` (GFM tables are on by default) who pastes into its cells, with the caret in a cell or a range of cells selected:

- **A pasted table with a merged cell empties cells.** Pasting `x1 | merged` (where `merged` spans two columns) with the caret in `d1` of the row `d1 | d2 | d3` leaves `x1 | merged | ` — `d3` is gone. A cell spanning rows does the same to the cell below, and so does pasting over selected cells.
- **A table copied with other content is discarded.** A paragraph and a table, as a web page copies them, pasted into a cell: nothing happens, with no message.
- **Part of an uneven table is dropped.** A pasted table whose first row is shorter than a later row loses that row's cells past the first row's width.

After this change no paste is dropped, and no cell loses its text to a paste that does not fill it.

## Problem and solution fit

1. **Why it occurs.** Lexical's `TablePlugin` answers `SELECTION_INSERT_CLIPBOARD_NODES_COMMAND`. A table pasted alone goes through `$insertTableIntoGrid`, which merges the cells under a merged pasted cell and replaces their content, and sizes the paste by the pasted table's first row. Any other paste that holds a table is refused when nested tables are off, as they are here: the handler returns `true` without inserting anything.
2. **Why it harms the task.** `RichTextEditor` mounts `TablePlugin` with `hasCellMerge={false}`, so the unmerge transform splits the merge again into new empty cells. The paste deletes the text of cells it never filled. A refused paste does nothing, so the person has to notice that their content is missing.
3. **Why that matters.** The editor's value is its Lexical editor state (spec:AST-061/DEC-7). A cell emptied by a paste is saved empty, and a dropped paste never reaches the value.

The fix is one internal plugin. It answers the same command ahead of `TablePlugin`, and only for a paste that holds a table, made with the selection in one table's cells. Any other paste goes on to Lexical as before.

## Expected behavior and authority

- `spec:AST-061/DEC-7`: RichText is a form-field editor whose value is Lexical editor state. A paste is an edit to that value, so it must not silently discard what the cells held or what was pasted.
- `spec:AST-061/DEC-8`: RichText's public surface is Lexical's, kept small. The fix adds no prop, type, or export. It is an always-on internal plugin on Lexical's own clipboard command, beside the editor's other table plugins.
- `spec:AST-061`, *Platform support*: a construct a surface cannot show as a structure appears as text and is never dropped. A cell holds no table here, because nested tables are off, so a table pasted with other content goes into the cell as text.

## Smallest restoration

- New `packages/richtext/src/TablePastePlugin.tsx`, internal and not exported, rendered by `RichTextEditor` after `TablePlugin` at `COMMAND_PRIORITY_LOW`. `TablePlugin` runs at the editor priority. `RichTextView` is read-only and is unchanged.
- **A table alone** pastes cell by cell from the top-left selected cell (the caret's cell). It adds rows and columns as needed and stays inside a cell selection, as Lexical's paste does. Each pasted cell replaces the content of the cell it lands on. A merged pasted cell fills only the cell where it starts. The rest of its span, like the missing end of a short row, leaves the cells under it as they were.
- **A table with other content** goes into the selection through Lexical's own `selection.insertNodes`. Each table becomes text: a paragraph per row, with tabs between the cells. With the caret in a cell, it goes into that cell. Over selected cells, Lexical puts it in the focused cell.
- Supporting: one sentence in the tables guidance of `RichTextEditor.doc.mjs`, and a `[fix]` changeset.
- No new API, default, styling, or interaction model. A table that keeps merged cells is out of scope, because `RichTextEditor` splits merged cells today.

## Evidence

- **Reproduction before the change.** The new test file was run on the untouched tree, with only the test file added: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/richtext/src/TablePastePlugin.test.tsx` → **6 failed, 2 passed**. Failing assertions:
  - merged cell over the caret's row: expected `d3`, received `""`
  - cell spanning rows: expected `e1`, received `""`
  - uneven rows: expected `t`, `u`, received `e2`, `e3` (the pasted cells were dropped)
  - table with other content, caret in `d2`: expected `d2intro/t1\tt2/t3\tt4`, received `d2` (paste discarded)
  - merged cell over selected cells `d1:e2`: expected `d2`, received `""`
  - table with other content over selected cells: expected `intro/t1\tt2`, received `e2` (paste discarded)
- **Result after the change.** The same command: 8 passed.
- **Representative unchanged paths.** Both pass before and after the change:
  - "grows the table for a pasted table that reaches past it": a plain table, same result as Lexical's paste.
  - "leaves a paste without a table to the editor": paragraphs pasted into a cell.

  The whole RichText suite passes: 36 files, 605 tests.
- **Mutation-sensitive proof.** Without the plugin, 6 of the 8 tests fail (the run above).
- Pastes are driven through `PASTE_COMMAND` with `text/html` clipboard data in jsdom. A real browser's clipboard was not exercised, and no rendering was seen. This is not a visual change.

## Scope

- [x] One defect is restored.
- [x] Separable contradictory or unsettled tagalongs were removed or split.
- [x] No new public API, visual representation, default, or interaction model is hidden under the bug-fix label.
- [x] Public text and artifacts contain no internal Meta context.

## Testing

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/richtext/src/TablePastePlugin.test.tsx packages/richtext/src/RichTextEditor.test.tsx`: 2 files, 122 tests passed
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/richtext/src`: 36 files, 605 tests passed
- `pnpm -F @astryxdesign/richtext typecheck`: passed (after building core and richtext)
- `pnpm -F @astryxdesign/richtext lint`: 0 errors. The 34 warnings were already there, none on changed lines.
- `pnpm exec prettier --check` on the changed files: passed
- `pnpm check:changesets`: passed
- `pnpm check:repo`: passed

## Interplay with #8578

If this and #8578 (`hasCellMerge`) both land and `hasCellMerge` is on, pasting `p | q` onto a merged cell keeps only `q`. The fix is a three-line rule in `TablePastePlugin`: the first pasted cell replaces a merged target cell's content, and later cells append to it. That fix goes into whichever of the two PRs lands second.

author: jaavander
body:
## Description

Releases are now signed with Sigstore keyless signing. The release workflow signs `SHASUMS256.txt`, which lists the checksum of every release asset including the install scripts, and every container image by digest. There is no signing key to manage or leak: a signature proves a file came out of `release.yml` on `main` of this repository, and Sigstore's public transparency log records it. The release notes show how to verify both with cosign. Images are now built before the release is published, so a release can no longer go out without its images.

`xinity up` and `xinity update` verify the signature before they use any checksum, and refuse a release whose signature is missing or invalid. Releases from before signing are still installed after the checksum check, with a warning. The trust data the check needs is updated from Sigstore when the machine is online, and otherwise taken from the last cached copy or the one built into the CLI, so air-gapped installs keep working. A CLI pointed at a fork expects that fork's release workflow as the signer.

`install.sh` and `install.ps1` still only check the checksum, since verifying the signature would need cosign on a machine that has nothing installed yet. They now refuse to install when the checksum list cannot be fetched or does not list the download, where they used to warn and carry on. A new docs page explains what is signed, what each tool checks and how to verify by hand.

Container images are signed but not verified automatically, so Docker Compose installs pull them as before. Their signatures use the cosign 3 format, which podman and skopeo signature policies cannot read.

Closes #127

## Type of change

New feature

## Testing

The signing steps ran in a private test repository, signing a checksum list and an image on GHCR, and that real signature is the test fixture. New tests cover accepting it, rejecting modified checksums and another repository's signer, each trust data fallback, and the CLI refusing a signed release without its signature or checksums. The compiled check ran on Linux, macOS and Windows against online, cached and built-in trust data. `install.sh` installed the current release and refused one without checksums or without its entry. The first signed release will be the first run of the full workflow in this repository.

Working directly on the existing branch requested by the repository owner: `agent/backend-platform-hardening-2026-10`. This is a Draft validation PR only; do not merge automatically.

- IDE execution fails closed with HTTP 503 if quota enforcement cannot be verified due to database errors; no Runner call is made.

author: saanidhi-git
body:
### Summary
Fixes a user experience issue on the homepage (`/`) where touch scrolling got trapped or stuck when dragging over the "Fragments of Becoming" (`ShipTheseusIllusions`) card grid on touchscreens and mobile viewports.

---

### Root Cause
* Invisible overlay containers (`.theseus-illusions__overlay` at `opacity: 0`) were intercepting pointer/touch gestures even when inactive.
* The inner card copy container (`.theseus-illusions__copy`) was set to `overscroll-behavior: contain`, preventing vertical swipe gestures from propagating to the main window scroll.

---

### Key Changes
* **Pointer Events:** Added `pointer-events: none` to `.theseus-illusions__overlay` by default so background touch drags pass directly to page scroll, enabling `pointer-events: auto` only when active (`.is-open`, `:hover`, `:focus-visible`).
* **Scroll Chaining:** Replaced `overscroll-behavior: contain` with `overscroll-behavior-y: auto` on `.theseus-illusions__copy` to allow smooth parent scroll chaining.
* **Touch Action:** Added `touch-action: pan-y` to `.theseus-illusions__card` and `.theseus-illusions__copy` for immediate vertical gesture recognition on touch viewports.

## Summary

Codex terminal failures currently reach the server as display text while their structured error category and HTTP status are discarded. This makes upstream failures, provider helper failures, and local network policy failures hard to distinguish in logs.

body:
## Summary

Moves CI and the repo to Node 24, brings every dependency to its current release (including the majors that are safe today), and applies the refactors that the newer React / TanStack / Supabase / Vite versions make possible. Fixes the `Node.js 20 is deprecated` warning in the deploy workflow.

### Platform and tooling
- **Node 24**: `engines` `>=24.15` (jsdom 30), `.nvmrc`, `node-version-file` in CI. `npm` 12.2.1 locally; CI uses the npm bundled with Node 24.
- **GitHub Actions** (all SHA-pinned): `checkout` v7.0.1, `setup-node` v7.1.0, `setup-cli` v3.0.1 (Supabase CLI 2.122.0, kept in sync with `package.json`), `wrangler-action` v4.1.3, `codeql-action` v4.39.1. `setup-deno` v2.0.5 already runs on Node 24.
- **Majors**: ESLint 10 (with `fixupPluginRules` + a root `overrides` for `eslint-plugin-react@7.37.5`, which does not declare ESLint 10 support yet — drop both when it does), Vitest 5, jsdom 30, jest-dom 7, globals 17, `@hookform/resolvers` 6, `pdfjs-dist` 6.4.299. Removed the unused `eslint-plugin-tailwindcss`.
- **Minor/patch**: React 19.3.1, Vite 8.3, Tailwind 4.3, supabase-js 2.118, zod 4.6, TanStack Query/Router, react-hook-form 7.91, chart.js 4.6, Prettier 3.9, Supabase CLI 2.122 and the rest. `npm audit`: 0 vulnerabilities.
- **Build**: `heic-to` (`heic-to/csp`, no `unsafe-eval`) and `tus-js-client` load on demand; Rolldown `codeSplitting` groups. Entry chunk 448 → 22 kB, `photo` chunk 3.2 MB → 64 kB, Chart.js no longer on the first load.
- **Dev experience**: one root Vitest run via `test.projects`, shared test setup/helpers, `eslint --cache`, Query/Router devtools in dev only, `.gitattributes` (`eol=lf`) + `format:check` in PR checks, `@tanstack/eslint-plugin-query` and `-router`.

### Behaviour fixes and refactors
- **Bug fix — stale `/stats`**: receipt mutations never invalidated `['stats']` (5 min `staleTime`), waste items or packaging candidates. One shared `invalidateReceiptDerivedQueries` is now used by save / update / delete / stub / reassign-payer / purchase-correction.
- **Data layer**: `keepPreviousData` on filter-driven queries (old data dimmed instead of a loading flash), `useCategoryNames` / `useProductNames` via `select`, `queryOptions` + `skipToken`, `.abortSignal` and `.overrideTypes`, one shared reference-counted auth listener (no `/auth/v1/user` call on load), `queryClient.clear()` on sign-out / user switch, `parse-receipt` surfaces the Edge Function error body and has a 140 s client timeout, `usePrefetchQuery` on the home page.
- **Navigation**: `useBlocker`-based `useLeaveGuard` for dirty forms, unsaved photo/pending batches and uploads in progress; non-optional `validateSearch` schemas with `.catch(undefined)` and functional `search` updates with `replace`; `defaultNotFoundComponent`; Cancel returns to the filtered list.
- **React**: labels bound to controls with `useId`, `SubmitEvent` instead of deprecated `FormEvent`, `forwardRef` removed, `useWatch` / `compute` so a keystroke no longer re-renders every item row, `useObjectUrl`, `<Activity>` in the batch carousel (edits survive switching cards), `useModalDialog` shared by all dialogs, `useSyncExternalStore` for stats preferences, per-route `<title>`, chart `aria-label`s and stable options.
- **React Compiler 1.0** (own commit `a42e1b6`, easy to revert): 188 functions compiled, 8 skipped by the compiler's own limits (e.g. `try/finally` without `catch`). Babel 7 pinned on purpose (the compiler depends on `@babel/types` 7).
- **Static hardening**: `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` on the **Report-Only** CSP only; `preconnect` to Supabase in `index.html`.
- Docs refreshed (`project-status.md`, `setup.md`, `architecture.md`, `extending.md`, `deploy.md`, `CLAUDE.md`).

## Deferred (not in this PR)
- **TypeScript 7** — `typescript-eslint` does not support it yet (its peer range is `<6.1`); a dry run showed `tsc -b` passing with ~3x faster builds. Bump once TS 7.1 + typescript-eslint support land.
- **Auth/session**: `flowType: 'pkce'` (needs a manual test of the magic link in mail-app/in-app browsers) and `getClaims()` (depends on whether the project uses asymmetric JWT keys).
- **Router**: loaders + router context with query prefetching and `beforeLoad` auth redirect replacing `<RequireAuth>` (large, touches the sign-in flow).
- **Features**: infinite scroll on `/recent` (currently capped at 30 rows).
- **Zod** (`packages/domain`, `supabase/functions/_shared`; left alone because of in-flight local work): remaining `.finite()` no-ops, `z.iso.date()` / `z.iso.time({ precision: 0 })` instead of the regexes that accept `2026-02-31`, Ukrainian locale (`z.locales.uk()`).
- Background import worker does not invalidate stats/receipts; they refresh when their `staleTime` expires.
- Not done on purpose: `useTransition` / Suspense / `use()` / `useActionState` / `useOptimistic` (no use case here), `useEffectEvent` refactors, `persistQueryClient` (would persist RLS-protected data in browser storage).

## Needs a manual check in the browser (not verifiable without a login)
- [ ] `/manual`, `/edit/$id`: clicking a label focuses its field; product-name suggestions still appear.
- [ ] `/photo` batch: edit a card, move to another and back (edits kept), save mid-batch (auto-advance works), leave with unsaved cards (confirm prompt).
- [ ] Open/close every dialog, including Esc and backdrop click (category, store/product link, delete confirm, JSON import, statement import, purchase correction, stub receipt).
- [ ] `/stats`: switch period and filters, reload, change them in a second tab (should sync); click a category bar to open its details; charts have accessible names.
- [ ] `/recent`, `/waste`: filter changes dim the old list, Back leaves the page instead of stepping through filters; a hand-edited invalid URL parameter is ignored, not an error page.
- [ ] Save a receipt, then open `/stats` immediately: it must include the new receipt.
- [ ] Sign out and sign in as another user: header and route guard switch without a loading flash; no previous user's data visible.
- [ ] Photo upload: thumbnails, PDF badge, HEIC conversion (heic-to is now a separate lazy chunk), a >6 MB resumable upload (tus is lazy too); packaging import page previews.
- [ ] Typing speed on a long receipt, and Fast Refresh in `npm run dev` with the React Compiler on.
- [ ] Browser console on the deployed site: Trusted Types violations reported by the Report-Only CSP (pdf.js, heic-to, Chart.js) — informational only.
- [ ] After the first CI run on this PR: the `deploy-backend` job (setup-cli v3) and `wrangler-action` v4 only run on `main`, so watch the first deploy after merge.

## Verification
`npm run lint` (0 errors, 0 warnings), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run test` (1115 Vitest tests, 4 PGlite SQL scripts, `check:edge-domain`), `npm run build`, `npm run format:check`, `deno check` for all three Edge Functions and `deno lint supabase/functions` all pass locally on Node 24 / npm 12.

body:
## Summary

Moves `eslint-config-scratch` to ESLint 10. ESLint 9 reached end of life on 2026-08-06 (https://eslint.org/version-support/). This targets the `v15` branch, which publishes `15.0.0-next.N` prereleases so consumers can try the upgrade before it reaches master.

- Peer dependency `eslint: ^10.0.0`; dev dependency `eslint` 10.13.0; `@eslint/js` 10.0.1.
- eslint-plugin-react 7.37.5 and eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y 6.10.2 still call `context` methods that ESLint 10 removed, so eslint-plugin-react crashes with `context.getFilename is not a function`. Their rules are wrapped with `fixupPluginRules` / `fixupConfigRules` from `@eslint/compat`. Both helpers cache their result, so every config shares one wrapped plugin object and ESLint doesn't see conflicting plugin definitions.
- Neither plugin's peer range includes ESLint 10 yet. `overrides` keep this repo's install clean. Consumers see npm `ERESOLVE overriding peer dependency` warnings, which the README explains.
- ESLint 10 uses the config file nearest to each linted file. The nested `test/*/eslint.config.mjs` files would have taken over the fixtures and ignored the root config's `globalIgnores`, so they are renamed to `fixtures.config.mjs`. The tests pass them explicitly, as before.
- `eslint:recommended` gains `no-unassigned-vars`, `no-useless-assignment`, and `preserve-caught-error`, and `no-shadow-restricted-names` now reports `globalThis`. The bad fixture covers the first two. The resolved-config snapshots show these changes; the rest of their diff is ESLint 10 listing default rule options explicitly. Lint-message snapshots drop `nodeType`, which ESLint 10 no longer reports.
- README: install line and an "Upgrading to v15" section (eslint-env comments, new rules, nested configs, and making sure only one ESLint is installed in a monorepo).

This supersedes scratchfoundation/eslint-config-scratch#386.

## Resolves

- N/A

## Testing

- `npm test` passes, and `scripts/check-fresh-install.sh` installs the packed package into a clean project with ESLint 10 and lints the good fixtures.
- With the shim, every fixture produces the same error and warning counts on ESLint 10 as on ESLint 9.
- Linted real consumers on ESLint 10 with a prototype of this package. Errors added: scratch-blocks 0, scratch-desktop 0, scratch-storage 1, scratch-render 2, scratch-vm 23, scratch-gui 34, scratch-paint 53. Nearly all come from the new recommended rules (mostly `let defaultState;` in reducer tests and initial values that are always overwritten) and from `eslint-env` comments. None of the hits sampled were real bugs.

author: yabgu
body:
# chore: derive the record stride from the declaration

Finishes the record-writer cleanup PR #26 started, and records why the rest of it
is not mechanical.

**Base:** `origin/main` @ `f1a0a90`.

**Process note (rule-2 override).** The user authorized this branch, commits,
push and PR in the current request, overriding the standing rule-2 (no branch,
commit or push without explicit per-turn authorization). No merge, no force-push,
no rebase, no squash.

**Branch name.** `refactor/struct-field-writes` could not be created: a local
branch named `refactor` (`6f86283`, not on `origin`, not in `main`) owns that ref
namespace, and git cannot nest `refs/heads/refactor/...` under it. Left alone;
this branch is `chore/struct-field-writes`.

## The plan changed on measurement

The brief scoped converting raw `store<>` calls in `bones.ts`, `motion.ts` and
`skin.ts`. **Two of those three files were already done.**

```
grep -n "store<" assembly/ogre/bones.ts    → no matches
grep -n "store<" assembly/ogre/motion.ts   → no matches
grep -n "store<" assembly/ogre/skin.ts     → 6
```

PR #26 (`62b4da1`, squash-merged as `31a6626`, an ancestor of `main`) converted
them. The report showing fifteen raw stores in `bones.ts` was read from a
checkout on `build/optimize-level` at `1c663ed`, which predates #26.

What was genuinely left in the writers: the stride was still the hand-copied
`BONE_SIZE` / `MOTION_SIZE` while the field writes went through the declaration.
That is this PR's one code change.

## Three commits

| Commit | Change |
|---|---|
| `5a41050` | stride derives from the declaration: `sizeof<T>()` in the three write paths |
| `98a069b` | `skin.ts` TODO: the 32-byte record, its known shape, and the one unknown |
| `75b71a1` | CHANGELOG + `docs/session-findings.md` (new in this repo) |

`BONE_SIZE` / `MOTION_SIZE` remain exported: they are the wire's published
stride, and `index.ts`'s region checks, the `BONE_TABLE_OFFSET` /
`PROCEDURAL_BASE` arithmetic and `tests/guest-physics-units.ts` still read them.

## Byte-identity: proven, not assumed

`tension-framework`'s `index.wasm` at `-O3` (`--runtime incremental --target
release --optimizeLevel 3`):

```
before    ff42c221527bacfaf3215d6610402586   65628 bytes
after     ff42c221527bacfaf3215d6610402586   65628 bytes
```

The **wat** is byte-identical too, so `sizeof<T>()` folds to exactly the constant
it replaced rather than merely costing the same bytes.

The reason this is free, measured: a probe writing four fields by raw store and by
field assignment was **deduplicated by the compiler into a single function
symbol**. Not equal output — one function. The accessor tax that once justified
the raw stores is gone at `-O3`.

## What is *not* in this PR, and why

### The size-binding check strengthening — held

`ogre/wire.ts` binds record sizes with
`offsetof<X>("pad2") + 4 != <constant>`. That catches a field moved *before*
`pad2` and **misses one appended after it**: the record grows, the constant still
matches the offset arithmetic, and the table stride silently disagrees with the
slot size. Replacing the constant with `sizeof<T>()` closes it — probed with an
appended field, the old form returns `true` (sees no problem), the new form
returns `false`.

It cannot land under the byte-identity gate. Those check functions are **live
wasm exports**, so a stronger body is a different module:

```
with the check strengthened:   65627 bytes, e1427710762d9c22464711dfbf8277f0
```

One byte under. The diff is confined to the three offset-check functions and a
`~lib/string/String.__eq` the compiler no longer needs; **all three record
writers remain byte-identical**, and the full framework suite, the four OGRE
fixtures and the three drift cells all pass with it.

So the two goals are mutually exclusive, and the strengthening is left out rather
than described as free. If you want it, the honest commit message is: *one byte,
confined to the offset-check functions, no behaviour change for any program
without an appended field.*

### `skin.ts` — 6 sites, blocked on a measurement

No `SkinUpdate` declaration exists anywhere, and `SKIN_SIZE = 32` is a bare
constant. The TODO records the known shape and the gating unknown: `@4` is
written from `this.used`, a running byte offset, but whether the adapter reads it
as an offset or a usage counter has not been checked — and that answer names the
field. Declaring it wrong would be worse than leaving it raw. Filed as
`skin-record-undeclared`.

### `solver.ts` (25) and `physics.ts` (16) — not record writers

Addresses over a flattened `f64` state vector (`dyPtr + (base + i) * 8`), whose
slot meanings depend on a runtime `config.dim`. Field assignment needs named
fields; expressing this as a struct means a fixed dimension (contradicting the
variable-dim contract) or a per-call layout. A design question. Filed as
`state-vector-declarations`.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `index.wasm` sha256 | `ff42c221527bacfaf3215d6610402586` (unchanged) |
| Framework suite (`tests/run.sh`) | **exit 0**, `all fixtures OK` |
| OGRE at `-O3`, NULL renderer | motion **5/5**, skinning **6/6**, angular **8/8**, physics **9/9**, `all cases passed` |
| Drift cells | refuse OK · partial `guest 144 != host 128` then OK · fixed aborted exit 1 |
| `offsetof` checks | 128 field-arg + 2 no-arg, all pass (unchanged — `wire.ts` declarations untouched) |
| `layout_hash` | **786288195** |

## Scope

3 files changed: `bones.ts`, `motion.ts`, `skin.ts`, plus `CHANGELOG.md` and
`docs/session-findings.md`. No declarations added, no `wire.ts` change, no Zig,
no `tension-core`. `docs/session-findings.md` is **new in this repo** — the brief
named that path, but the file lives in TensionScript, which this PR must not
touch, so the Tension tree gets its own scoped to what Tension owns.

## What could not be measured

- **Windowed OGRE cases** (windowed, skin-matrices, noskel) — skipped without a
  display; the NULL-renderer structural clauses cover the same paths.
- **The host binary is `target/debug/tension-core` from 2026-10-21**, older than
  `origin/main`. It is the prebuilt artifact the tree has; its hash matching
  `session.json` is what makes `layout_hash` meaningful, but it was not rebuilt
  at `f1a0a90`. The primary checkout holds unrelated uncommitted work and was
  not touched.
- **The `@4` skin field's semantics** — the follow-up's first task, unmeasured
  here by design.
- **CI:** the Tension repo has no workflows, so there are no checks on this PR;
  the local suite above is the verification.


---

## Update — the strengthened check landed; the helper did not

Three further commits, and one of them was attempted and reverted.

| Commit | Change | `.wasm` |
|---|---|---|
| `4aed560` | strengthened size-check, both records | `e1427710…` (65 627) |
| `8de644a` | declaration comments: unmanaged pointer views | `e86f41c6…` (65 627) |
| `a4d052d` | array-views + recordAt follow-ups | unchanged |

### The check (landed)

Both records now assert `offsetof<T>("pad2") + sizeof<f32>() != sizeof<T>()`
instead of comparing to a copied constant. Proven with a probe: with a field
appended after `pad2`, the old form folds to `true` (passes) and the new form
folds to `false` (catches it). Both fold at compile time — which is the point:
the old check optimised itself away in exactly the case it existed to catch.

The delta is confined to the diagnostics path. In `tension-framework`'s
`index.wasm` the wat diff touches three functions
(`checkOgreMotionOffsets`, `checkWireOffsets`, `~lib/string/String.__eq`) and
nothing else.

**A correction to my own earlier evidence.** The previous turn reported
`BoneBatch#write` and friends as "IDENTICAL" across a change. That comparison was
worthless: the framework barrel `index.ts` tree-shakes every writer out, so the
build it compared had no writers in it, and two absent names compared equal. Re-measured
against the real guests that instantiate the classes:

```

author: kingimann
body:
## Summary

IK/animation plan PR 2b, the animation half of smooth stance transitions. It's rebased onto main, which has 2a (#364), #370 (`Quat::ToEuler`, the get-up clip needs it) and #380 (the one-shot fade-out fix this PR used to carry).

On the default humanoid graph:
- The crawl goes four ways.
- Prone → stand gets up through hands-and-knees and a kneel; standing still → prone drops down the same way.
- On the move, the stride blends straight into the crawl and back.
- Every stance crossfade takes the Animator's stance times (N19).

## Changes

- **Directional crawl**:
  - `HumanoidMotion` state 7 now reads `travelYaw`: crawling sideways, the arm on that side reaches wide, the other tucks in, the chest bends toward the travel and the near knee draws up higher.
  - The library bakes `Crawl` (forward; it keeps the name scenes saved since 1b use), `Crawl_B` (the cycle reversed), `Crawl_R` and `Crawl_L`.
  - Prone is now a still `Prone` pose plus a `Crawl` state: a 2D tree on `gaitX`/`gaitZ` with `matchSpeed`.
  - The Character feeds the travel direction while prone too (it was zeroed outside walk/run/crouch-walk).
- **GetUp / Drop**:
  - A new `HumanoidMotion::KneelPose` gives hands-and-knees and a kneel on the right knee, with the hips' height.
  - `GetUp` is prone → hands and knees → kneel → standing, and `Drop` is the reverse. Both are baked one-shots with a root track, so the hips follow a real path instead of lerping through the floor.
  - Standing still, going prone plays Drop and standing up plays GetUp. Changing your mind mid-way blends out from the live pose.
- **On the move**: walk/run → prone blends into Crawl; crawling and standing up blends into Walk/Run. Crouch-walk → prone goes to Crawl.
- **N19 timing**: `HumanoidLibrary::ApplyStanceTimes` sets the default graph's stance crossfades from `stanceTimes`:
  - stand↔crouch;
  - crouch↔prone;
  - the whole way up or down on the move: prone→stand, and stand→crouch plus crouch→prone going down;
  - GetUp and Drop playback speeds.
  - `DefaultGraph` calls it, and so does the inspector when the times change.
- **IK**: foot IK is off in Prone, Crawl, GetUp and Drop (state IK weight 0); it stays on while crouched.

body:
## Summary

Replace the selected local worker's Unix socket with one authenticated loopback HTTPS transport on Linux, macOS, and Windows. The parent creates a fresh loopback listener, server certificate, and bearer token for each direct worker. The worker receives the certificate and token through bounded startup stdin, pins the server, and sends the token only to that origin. The server authenticates before decoding protocol bodies.

Reuse the existing bounded HTTP Job, Status, Result, and callback routes. Remove the Unix socket endpoint, socket paths, runtime directory, and platform restriction. Keep the direct child lifecycle and accepted callback drain.

Use one offline publication and restart test across all three operating systems. Cover the HTTPS direct child's Main and Critic calls and persisted paid receipts.

## Verification

- `go test -count=1 -timeout=20m ./...` on Linux
- Focused HTTPS endpoint and direct child race tests on Linux
- `go vet ./...`, formatting, and diff checks
- Cross-compilation of cmd/minion test binary for Windows amd64 and macOS arm64
- Native Linux/macOS/Windows CI on the final head before merge

## Review disposition

The review identified a local resource regression: loopback TCP is reachable by other local accounts, while the old Unix socket was inside a private directory. A small 16-connection bound now limits pre-authentication sockets. It bounds Minion's resource use, although another local process can still occupy all slots and interrupt the selected worker.

The first native CI run exposed three acceptance-test fixture failures on macOS and Windows; the helper lifetime, Windows Git proxy configuration, and fake Codex debug command are fixed. A later review identified a missing child-start cleanup test and an unclear provider-credential comment; both are fixed. The final whole-PR review at `5aceb86` found no actionable findings. Native CI at that head remains the merge gate.
