author: alejogm
body:
Hoy, durante un rato, `espbench benches` devolvió `[]` y cualquier comando con `<dev>` daba `'NVC3@dev' no está en ningún bench (benches encontrados: ninguno)`, con los dos benches online y contestando por IP (con `ESPBENCH_HOST` andaba). Coincidió con el DNS de Tailscale (MagicDNS) fallando en la Mac. Un rato después el discovery volvió solo: sondeo de sensipi03 en 0,04 s. **No se pudo reproducir**, así que esto no arregla la causa: arregla dos cosas que la empeoraban y la dejaban sin diagnóstico.

## Qué cambia

- **Un scan vacío no se cachea.** Se guardaba 30 s como cualquier otro, así que un mal momento de Tailscale o de la red dejaba "ningún bench" pegado aunque la red ya hubiera vuelto (`ls`, `pick` y `props` leen la caché; `locate` re-escaneaba solo si la placa no estaba).
- **Cuando no hay ningún bench se dice por qué** (`benches.diagnose`): `tailscale status --json` no respondió, Tailscale no está instalado, la tailnet no tiene peers online, o ningún peer (con sus nombres) o host del config contestó como espbench en `timeout_s`. Y apunta a `ESPBENCH_HOST=<ip>` para saltear el discovery. Sale en el `message` de `benches`, en el `not_found` de `props` y en el de cualquier comando con `<dev>`.

```
$ espbench who NVC3 --json
{"ok": false, "error": "not_found", "message": "'NVC3': no se encontró ningún bench. ningún host del config (10.255.255.1) contestó en 1 s. Para saltear el discovery: ESPBENCH_HOST=<ip del bench>"}
```

El diagnóstico solo corre cuando el scan vino vacío: es una llamada más a `tailscale status`, nada en el camino normal. `lib.Benches` lo recibe inyectable (`why=`), como ya recibía `scan=`, para que los tests no llamen al Tailscale real.

## Verificación

- `master/.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests`: 847 pass, 1 skipped. Nuevos: un scan vacío no se cachea y el siguiente encuentra el bench; `diagnose` para cada causa; `locate` sin benches trae el diagnóstico.
- A mano: con un config que apunta a un host que no existe, `benches` y `who` dan el mensaje de arriba. Con la tailnet real, `benches` lista dev y sensipi02.

author: chadmueller
body:
A sideloaded test build can now keep its own saved data, so a tester can sign it in to a lab Jellyfin or Emby server without signing the store copy on the same TV out of its real server. Release builds keep exactly the same registry and cache names as today.

**Why.** Every app signed with one developer key shares one registry. So the sideload `scripts/deploy.sh` installs and the store beta read and write the same sign-in, packages and settings. That blocked device checks that need a small library (#60) or a server with BoxSets (#70).

**What changes**
- `NX_TEST_DATA=1 scripts/deploy.sh` stamps `nx_data_ns=nxtest` into the build's manifest. That build opens its registry sections as `nxtest-guide`, `nxtest-plex` and so on, and keeps its saved library, guide, pools and caches under `cachefs:/nxtest`. Settings' VERSION line ends in TEST DATA.
- `source/util/Values.brs`: `NxRegSection(name)` and `NxCacheRoot()`. With no `nx_data_ns` in the manifest they give the old names (`guide`, `cachefs:`). All 21 registry sections and every cache path go through them.
- `scripts/stamp-manifest.sh` (new) writes `nx_build`, and `nx_data_ns` only with `--test-data`. Both `deploy.sh` and `release.sh` stamp through it. `release.sh` uses the plain call and refuses a staged manifest that has `nx_data_ns`.
- `tests/run.sh` fails on any `roRegistrySection` or quoted `"cachefs:` outside `Values.brs`, so nothing new opens shared data by accident.

**Tests**
- `tests/stamp-test.sh`, run by `tests/run.sh`, checks:
  - the repo manifest has no `nx_data_ns`;
  - release.sh's stamp never writes it, even with `NX_TEST_DATA=1` set;
  - the test-data stamp writes it with the same build hash;
  - release.sh keeps its single plain call and its guard.

  It fails on main.
- `tests/VersionTests.brs`: a build without the key keeps `guide`, `cachefs:`, `cachefs:/nostalgex-library` and the plain VERSION line.
- The full suite passes off the TV. Static analysis is clean.

**Not on a TV yet.** The tester has the stick next. The plan:
1. A plain deploy stays on the existing sign-in.
2. A test-data deploy opens at the connect screen and says TEST DATA.
3. The store copy keeps its own sign-in throughout.

Not measured: whether `cachefs:` is also shared between the sideload and the store copy. This keeps them apart either way.

**Merge order for 1.0.6.** This one goes first. #60's PR and #105 are rebased on top of it. Against #103 and #104 it conflicts only in `docs/DEVLOG.md`; keep every entry. Anything that lands after it opens saved data through `NxRegSection` and `NxCacheRoot`, and the `run.sh` check says so. PR #106 adds two `roRegistrySection "player"` calls that will need that change.

@tydude001 heads up: this touches a line in most files that save data. If you're mid-change in one, `NxRegSection("player")` replaces `CreateObject("roRegistrySection", "player")`.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Wide persistence-layer refactor across sign-in, guide, and sign-out paths; release naming is unchanged but mistakes could still affect shared store/sideload data.
> 
> **Overview**
> **Test-data sideloads** can keep Plex/Jellyfin sign-in, guide settings, and `cachefs` caches separate from the store app on the same TV. `NX_TEST_DATA=1 scripts/deploy.sh` stamps `nx_data_ns=nxtest` via new `scripts/stamp-manifest.sh`; registry sections become names like `nxtest-guide` and files live under `cachefs:/nxtest`. Settings’ VERSION line appends **TEST DATA**. Plain deploys and `release.sh` builds behave as before—no namespace key, and release refuses a manifest that includes `nx_data_ns`.
> 
> **Implementation** routes all saved state through `NxRegSection` and `NxCacheRoot()` in `Values.brs` (replacing direct `roRegistrySection` / hard-coded `cachefs:` paths). `NxCacheRoot` uses global `CreateDirectory` instead of `roFileSystem` so sign-out cache clearing works on the render thread (fixes a crash on test builds).
> 
> **Guardrails:** `tests/stamp-test.sh` and expanded `VersionTests.brs`; `tests/run.sh` fails if persistence is opened outside the helpers or if `Values.brs` uses `roFileSystem`. `docs/DEVLOG.md` and `roku/README.md` document the workflow.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit cd8f783986ea2f38af52d36b21fc5a95d2a7cf94. Bugbot is set up for automated code reviews on this repo. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

Fixes #319.

Both OwnTracks paths in `includes/sync/class-owntracks-checkin-sync.php` (`create_checkin_from_location` and `create_checkin_from_transition`) called `wp_insert_post()` without `post_author` and set `post_date` to `gmdate( $tst )`.

- **Time:** the UTC epoch landed in the site-local `post_date` column, off by the site's UTC offset.

Fix:
- **Author:** `Import_Manager::resolve_author_for_post_type( 'post' )`, the call the Foursquare and Untappd syncs use. If no user qualifies, the location path returns a `no_author` `WP_Error` and the transition path returns false.
- **Time:** `post_date_gmt` is the UTC time and `post_date` is `get_date_from_gmt()` of it, as in the Foursquare sync.
- **Duplicate check:** compares its UTC window against `post_date_gmt`. It used to compare against `post_date`, which, with only the time fix, would miss duplicates on any non-UTC site.

Tests in `OwnTracksCheckinSyncTest`, all run through `handle_webhook` with Nominatim stubbed and the timezone set to America/New_York:
- **Author, both paths.** Before the fix: "Failed asserting that 0 is identical to 2".
- **Date, both paths.** Before the fix: expected `2026-07-15 09:00:00`, got `13:00:00`.
- **Duplicate detection on a non-UTC site.** This one guards the `column` line: it fails with the time fix applied and that line removed.

The OwnTracks, Foursquare, ImportManager and NoColorLeakage filters pass: 148 tests.

The issue notes no OwnTracks-imported posts exist on dev, test or live, so no backfill is needed.

author: tamnd
body:
Closes #241.

This PR adds `FS_IOC_GETFSMAP` on ext4, as fs/ext4/fsmap.c of Linux. The ioctl gives the map of the used and free space of the file system.

- The map has the superblocks, the group descriptors, the reserved descriptor blocks, the two bitmaps and the inode tables of each group, with the ext4 owner codes of Linux. Then it has the runs of free blocks, joined across the groups. The other blocks have the owner "unknown".
- A block that a change freed after the last commit is not free in the map, as Linux.
- The VFS part checks the header as Linux, uses the low and high keys, continues after the last record of the call before, counts the records when the count is 0, and sets `FMR_OF_LAST` on the last record.
- The map does not need a write transaction, so it also works on a read only or frozen mount.

### Tests

- ext4/027 and ext4/028 pass on rukernel on ext4 on a release kernel.
- One new ext4 unit test checks the full map of the test image, the map on a read only mount and the free space after a write. Five new VFS unit tests check the keys, the empty result and the device number.
- The boot tests `init blk busybox initramfs` and `alpine` pass with the user programs, except `init with UEFI` and `initramfs with UEFI`. These two also fail on main, and #272 tracks the fix.
- The full gate did not run.

### Motivation

iOS equivalent of https://github.com/RevenueCat/purchases-android/pull/4451. The backend now supports per-screen soft and hard gating. RevenueCat-rendered checkpoint workflows need to enforce hard gates without changing the public checkpoint API.

- Entitlements are only trusted for the app user they were read for. After a `logIn`/`logOut` the gate fails closed until info for the new user arrives, and info read for another user is ignored.
- Soft, ungated and non-checkpoint workflows behave as before.
- Update `CheckpointTester` so the checkpoint callback unlocks content. I haven't compiled this one.

Known gaps: a stale purchase on an earlier soft step, with an identity change mid-purchase and an enforced gate later, can still auto-dismiss. Android blocks that case.    - **GST:** added on the base after the coupon, at the rate already configured for GoKesari's registration fee (Admin → Statutory, `PLATFORM_FEE_GST`: 18%). ₹999 → GST ₹179.82 → **₹1,178.82**. GoKesari's fee invoice already reads a paid registration fee as GST-inclusive, and the split matches to the paisa (unit-tested).
   - **On the form:** before Submit the owner sees the fee, a coupon box (checked by the server), GST and the total. After Submit they go to the payment page, which shows the same breakdown.
   - **On the server:** `registerShop` prices it all again. The coupon is locked and its limits rechecked inside the registration transaction, so two registrations can't both take the last use (tested, and `touchSellerRow` for the split layout). The breakdown is snapshotted on the shop (`registration_fee_base/discount/gst_paise`, `gst_rate_bp`, coupon id and code); `registration_fee_paise` is the total payable. A fee sent from the browser is ignored. An operator's fee override is taken as the total (no coupon, no GST added).
   - **Turnover tiers kept, switched off:** rule `registrationFeeByTurnover` (up to ₹2 crore → ₹999, above → ₹4,999) is off by default. Switched on in Admin settings, the form asks for the turnover and the tier becomes the base fee (still less coupon, plus GST).
2. **Fee payment step.** After Submit the owner lands on the new `/shop/registration-fee` page and pays online. It reuses the existing payment-intent + capture handler (`SHOP_REGISTRATION_FEE`, the same one the operator fee request uses), which writes the shop's immutable ledger:
   - one open checkout is reused (a double tap charges once);
   - a failed payment can be retried;
   - a paid fee refuses a new charge;
   - returning from the gateway re-checks the payment.

   The owner's "next step" guidance now points here. Approval already required the fee to be settled (existing check), so a shop reaches final approval only once it has paid.
3. **Submit stays off while a registration is pending.** On the form, every field and the button ("Waiting for approval") are disabled, with a link to pay the fee if it is due. On the server, `registerShop` refuses a second, different shop under a per-owner advisory lock (409 `REGISTRATION_PENDING`). Duplicate detection for the *same* shop is unchanged, and operators registering for an owner are exempt.
4. **Professional and office types.** New shop types: *Professional office — CA, CS, advocate, tax consultant*, *Doctor / clinic*, and *Consultancy and other services*. They are added to both the `shop_type` and `department` enums. 34 professional categories are seeded, each with a new **group** heading:
   - *Finance and legal*: CA, CS, CMA, tax/GST, auditor, advocate, notary.
   - *Medical — doctors and clinics*: 16 specialities.
   - *Consulting and services*: 11 types, including "Other consulting".

   Groups are editable in Admin → Shop categories. For these types the form hides delivery and says "practice / office", and the picker lists the matching group first.

## Speed (each screen was slow on mobile)

Measured before any change:
- Both GoKesari Neon databases (prod and test) are in **AWS us-east-2 (Ohio)**. One round trip from India measures **~280 ms**, against **~9 ms** to AWS Mumbai.
- Computes scale to zero: the first request after idle took **10.8 s** on gokesari.com and **18.8 s** on test.
- Warm pages: home took ~1.8 s of server time, which is about six sequential database rounds.

Code fixes in this PR (fewer sequential round trips per page):
- Root layout (wraps every page): its reads go out in **one parallel batch** instead of a chain of about four. The cart total is chained behind the count only.
- `/shop/register`: three sequential reads plus a client-side category fetch after load become **one parallel batch**; the category list is passed to the picker.
- `listShopsForOwner` is memoised per render, so the seller layout and page share one query.
- Category pickers no longer compute a per-category shop count.
- `src/app/shop/loading.tsx` shows a skeleton instantly on every seller page.

The biggest remaining win is infrastructure and needs the owner's decision (not in this PR): move the Neon projects to **aws-ap-south-1 (Mumbai)**, and turn off scale-to-zero on production.

## Migrations

- `0097_professional_shop_types` (`-- split: both`): enum values only, not used in the same file.
- `0098_professional_registration` (`-- split: seller`): the turnover column with a check, `shop_categories.group_name`, and seeded categories (insert-if-absent). Safe to rerun.
- `0099_registration_fee_coupons_gst` (`-- split: seller`): `registration_fee_coupons` and the fee breakdown columns on `shops`. Safe to rerun.

## Questions for the owner

- **GST rate and SAC:** taken from Admin → Statutory (18%, SAC 998599, already marked "CA to confirm").
- If the turnover tiers are switched on later, confirm the boundary (₹2 crore as built, or ₹1 crore): it is `thresholdRupees` in the rule.
- The referral-code self-registration (`/shop/join`) and its own fee plans are untouched.

## Tests

Run locally against PostgreSQL 18:
- New `tests/unit/registration-fee.test.ts` (rule off by default, tiers, boundary, parsing, rule schema, professional types; GST and coupon maths, and the invoice's inclusive split matching to the paisa).
- New `tests/integration/registration-fee-coupons.test.ts`: ₹999 + GST = ₹1,178.82 with the breakdown stored; base fee change applies to new shops only; only an admin manages fee and coupons; flat, capped-percent and 100% coupons; unknown / off / expired / not-started coupons refused next to the field; total and per-owner limits; two registrations racing for the last use; operator override; the form's quote endpoint; Submit with a coupon and pay the total; admin create / list / switch off.
- New `tests/integration/registration-fee-turnover.test.ts`:
  - flat ₹999 by default, whatever turnover is sent; the API asks no turnover and ignores a client fee;
  - with the turnover rule on: fee tiers, no turnover, admin change, override, API requires turnover;
  - second pending shop refused; professional type accepted;
  - full sandbox payment → PAID; retry after failure; another account gets 404.
- Category group tests; existing tests updated for the one-pending rule.
- Full suite (latest run): **2,706 passed**. Failing: the 3 spreadsheet-import tests that fail identically on unchanged `origin/staging` (unrelated); two GST-amount expectations (registration-fees §25.11, operator-limited payment links), since updated to the GST-inclusive total and passing (29/29); and the migrate-on-build / split-migrate setup hooks, which timed out under the full run's load and pass 11/11 alone.
- The migrate-on-build and split-layout migration tests pass.
- Typecheck and lint are clean.
- Checked by hand at 375 px on a local dev server (base ₹999, a ₹200-off test coupon): the form shows ₹999 + GST ₹179.82 = ₹1,178.82; a wrong code shows "That coupon code isn't valid." (Enter applies, it does not submit the form); LAUNCH200 → ₹799 + ₹143.82 = **₹942.82**; Submit as a dental clinic → payment page with the same breakdown → "Pay ₹942.82 now" → sandbox succes

author: johnnyclem
body:
## Why

On a device, Google sign-in ended on the website's login page inside the sign-in sheet ("A stale sign-in cookie was blocking the final step"); signing in there signed only the sheet's web view in, and the app never got the code.

What I found, checking the live project with a made-up token (nothing signed in or created):

- Supabase's Redirect URLs list does not include `hypervault://auth/callback`; for that address it falls back to the Site URL (`https://www.claudedamnit.com`), exactly as for an unknown host.
- `05156ac` already moved the app to the right design: return through `https://<server>/auth/callback?client=app`, which Supabase accepts on every host I tried, and have the website's callback hand the code on to `hypervault://`.
- `main` of the website has no `client=app` handling, so with a Git deployment of `main` the callback tries a cookie exchange with no PKCE verifier (the app's is on the phone), fails, and sends the browser to `/login?reason=verifier`. That is the screen in the report. The website half is [hypervault#181](https://github.com/johnnyclem/hypervault/pull/181).
- **Production today already has a handler** (a CLI deployment from 18:32 UTC that is not on `main`), so the handoff may already work on your phone with the build you have. That handler is lost the next time `main` deploys unless #181 is merged first.

This PR is the app's half of making that failure impossible to miss and impossible to get stuck in.

## What changed

- **`AppHandoff` (Kit).** Owns the return address (moved from `SignInController`, which keeps `oauthRedirect(on:)` as a forwarder so the existing test still holds) and `check(returnURL:transport:)`: it asks the page to bounce a made-up code, without following the bounce, and reads where it would send the browser. A redirect to `hypervault://auth/callback` is `ready`; any other answer is `missing`; offline, 408, 429 or a 5xx is `unknown`. Nothing is signed in or written, and no credential is sent.
- **`HTTPTransport.sendWithoutRedirect`.** A new requirement with a default (`send`), so existing transports and the mock are unchanged. `URLSessionTransport` implements it on Apple platforms with a session whose delegate refuses redirects; Linux takes the default (its tests use `MockTransport`).
- **`SignInController`.** Before opening the sheet, Google sign-in runs the check. `missing` says why in words (and announces it for VoiceOver) and does not open the sheet; a second tap goes ahead regardless, so a wrong probe cannot lock Google out; `unknown` goes ahead silently. The sheet is now a closure the tests can replace, so the whole Google path (check, authorize URL, sheet, token exchange) is tested.
- **Docs.** The README and `docs/DEVICE_TEST_PLAN.md` told you to add `hypervault://auth/callback` to Supabase's Redirect URLs, which is not what the app does any more. They now say what it does and give a one-line `curl` that shows whether a deployment has the handoff.

## Tests

`AppHandoffTests` (Kit): the return address, ready for every redirect status, case-insensitive `Location`, the exact request sent (made-up code only, no credential), an address that already has a code, that it reads the first answer and not the last, every kind of not-ready answer, and the no-answer cases (offline, 408, 429, 5xx). `GoogleHandoffTests` (app): a site that hands back opens the sheet at the right authorize URL and signs in; a site that cannot says so and opens nothing; a second tap goes ahead; no answer goes ahead without a warning.

The Linux Kit job compiled and ran these (one name collision in a test double, fixed in `0d951e8`); the macOS job is the first compile of the controller and its tests. An independent read of the Swift (Swift 6 mode on Linux, Xcode 26) found no compile problems. The Apple-only redirect-refusing `URLSession` is run by no automated test, so step 2 of the device test plan is its only check; if iOS did not return the 302 the check would fall to `unknown` and sign-in would still work, only without the warning.

## Before this works on your phone

1. Merge [hypervault#181](https://github.com/johnnyclem/hypervault/pull/181) **before** the next merge to the website's `main`, then deploy `main`. Production is a CLI deployment of an older checkout that already answers the handoff; a Git deployment of `main` without #181 would replace it and bring the failure back. The same deploy brings #178 to #180 (the keys, pairing, invite and admin screens need #180).
2. `curl -sI 'https://hypervault.store/auth/callback?client=app&code=x'` should show `302` and `location: hypervault://auth/callback?code=x` (it does today).

author: danielmschaves
body:
Implements step 13 of the Ledger implementation.md: a complete Brazilian Portuguese version of the site under `/pt/`, switched by `LanguageToggle`.

This replaces #32, which closed when its base branch (step 12, #31) was merged. It contains the same 9 commits, now based on `main`, plus a terminology pass from review: keep the English word where Brazilian teams actually say it in English.

## What changed

**Routing**
- Every page moved under `app/[lang]/` and is statically generated for `en` and `pt`.
- `middleware.ts`:
  - rewrites unprefixed paths to `/en`, so every English URL is unchanged;
  - passes `/pt` through;
  - redirects `/en/*` (308) to the unprefixed URL.
- `<html lang="en | pt-BR">` is set per language.
- Unknown paths get a localized 404 through an `app/[lang]/[...rest]` catch-all.

**Strings**
- `dictionaries/en.json` and `pt.json` come from the DS `ui-strings.json`. `pt` is typed against `en`, so a missing key fails `tsc`.
- `lib/i18n.ts` exports `getDictionary`, `href(lang, path)` (which every internal link goes through), `localeHref`, `pageMetadata` and `resumePdf`.
- `LanguageToggle` (EN | PT) sits before the theme toggle. Its options are real links with `hreflang`, `lang` and `aria-current`, and the `#hash` carries over.

**Content, all translated**
- `data/en/` and `data/pt/`.
- All six case studies, prose and every chart label, via `{ en, pt }` in `components/projects/*.copy.ts`. These are type-checked, so `pt` can't miss a key.
- The six figures: frame labels, captions, alt text and the words drawn inside them.
- Some chart layout fixes made for Portuguese also tidy the English charts:
  - the Cloud Migration risk legend and escalation wire;
  - the DW gateway lines and escalation label;
  - the e-commerce dependency-rule column.

**Metadata**
- Canonical and hreflang alternates (`en`, `pt-BR`, `x-default` = English), plus `og:locale`.
- The sitemap lists both languages with their alternates.
- Portuguese pages reuse the English OG images.

**Form and email**
- The form posts a hidden `lang`. Validation, CAPTCHA and success/failure messages answer in that language.
- The notification stays in English, with a "SENT FROM /pt/contact/" line for Portuguese submissions.
- Fields are validated before the CAPTCHA.
- **Bug fix (pre-existing):** the Resend client is now created per send. A missing `RESEND_API_KEY` used to crash the action before validation.

**Résumé PDF:** `siteConfig.resumePdf` is `{ en: "/DMC-17-05.pdf", pt: null }`. For now `/pt/` links the English file, labelled "Baixar PDF (inglês)". When you add the Portuguese PDF to `public/`, set `pt` to its path.

## Kept in English (review feedback)
The sentence is in Portuguese; the term stays English where that's what the market says.
- **enterprise:** "programas enterprise de dados e IA", "contas / clientes / projetos enterprise", "modernização enterprise", "rollout enterprise".
- **delivery** (the discipline): "Delivery & liderança", "Delivery de IA & GenAI", "liderança de delivery", "org. / time / engenharia de delivery", the "DELIVERY" credential group, "DELIVERY · DADOS · IA". The verb *entregar* and *entregável(is)* stay in Portuguese.
- **Titles as published:** Program Manager (hero and résumé eyebrows too), Project Manager and Project Analyst (CERTI), Data & AI Delivery Manager.
- **batch, runtime, in-process, throughput, storage / object storage.**
- **sponsor(s), steering committee.**
- **surrogate key / foreign key, and "poor man's data lake".**
- **Q1–Q4** for quarters. The word "trimestre" stays in prose.
- **Already in English:** pipeline, dashboard, data lake / warehouse, backlog, sprint, dailies, kick-off, lift-and-shift, pathfinder, hypercare, parking lot, gate, cutover, stakeholders, tech lead, head de dados, dbt layer names, Raw / Bronze / Silver / Gold, tool, method, certification and client names.

**Kept in Portuguese** because it reads naturally: entregáveis, engenharia de dados, gestão de projetos/programas, cronograma, controle de mudanças, destino (for "sink"), fato/dimensão, currículo, competências, estudo de caso.

## Still open (please check)
- **CERTI:** I used "Fundação CERTI – Centro de Energia Sustentável". Please confirm the official name.
- **PUC Minas entry:** "PUC Minas" / "Pós-graduando em Engenharia de Dados". The English is "Data Engineering Bootcamp (PUC-MG)" / "Data Engineering Graduate Student".
- **"Gateway"** → "gate contratual". The alternative is "marco contratual".
- **Spotify quote:** "the one you can actually *afford to run*" → "o que dá para *manter rodando*". This loses the cost nuance; "*bancar*" keeps it.
- **OG taglines:** "Spotify, refinado em quatro passadas." · "Valide uma vez, grave em qualquer lugar." · "Um warehouse, reconstruído sob contrato."
- **"Trading company"** → "trading".

## DS vs. what we built
- **404:** in Next 14, `not-found.tsx` gets no params. It renders both languages, and a CSS rule keyed on `<html lang>` shows the right one. Unknown `/pt/…` paths return 404 with the Portuguese text.
- **`LanguageToggle` uses plain links** (full page loads), because `<html lang>` changes between languages.
- **Additions to `ui-strings.json`** (worth adding to the DS asset): `sections.skills`, `hero.ctaResumeFallback`, `resume.downloadFallback`, `services.eyebrow`, `notFound.caseText` / `allWork`, form CAPTCHA and failure messages, `meta.*`, `footer.place`, `langNames`, and `accountsLine` as label + items.
- **The DS pt strings now use enterprise, delivery and PROGRAM MANAGER** where `ui-strings.json` had "corporativos", "entrega" and "GERENTE DE PROGRAMAS".
- **Mobile metrics row on Portuguese case pages:** values like "18 meses" wrap to two lines at 360px.

## Verification
- `tsc`, `npm run lint` and `npm run build` are clean. Every page is SSG in both languages.
- e2e: **112/112** passing (desktop and mobile Chromium) against `next start`. The checks cover:
  - both languages per page, with `<html lang>`, hreflang and canonical;
  - the toggle keeping the page and `#work`;
  - the `/en/*` redirect, and `/pt/` links staying inside `/pt`;
  - the PDF fallback label, the Portuguese 404 and Portuguese form errors;
  - the chart rules and the 360px header in both languages.
- **No English left on `/pt/`:** a crawl of every page checked visible text, SVG labels, aria and alt text, title and description. Apart from the agreed English terms above, the only hits are false positives: FLUENTE, INTERMEDIATE, ContactType, and the Portuguese verb "for".
- All 30 Portuguese charts were re-measured at 1280 and 390 after the terminology pass: rendered text is at least 12px, no round shapes, no overflow. I looked at every chart whose labels changed.

author: amarshaked
body:
Closes KAB-35.

## The bug

Every job in `pre-release.yml` targets a **GitHub larger-runner** label inherited from upstream Vibe Kanban:

| label | where |
|---|---|
| `ubuntu-latest-m` | `bump-version`, `package-npx-cli`, `upload-to-r2`, `create-prerelease` |
| `ubuntu-latest-x64-l` | `build-frontend`, and 3 `build-backend` matrix entries |
| `ubuntu-latest-arm64-l` | `build-backend` / linux-arm64 |
| `macos-15-xlarge` | `build-backend` / macos-x64, macos-arm64 |

Larger runners are configured per-org/enterprise. `AmarShaked/kablan.dev` is owned by a **user** account (`gh api repos/AmarShaked/kablan.dev --jq .owner.type` → `User`) and has **zero** self-hosted runners registered (`gh api .../actions/runners` → `total_count: 0`). Nothing can pick these labels up.

The workflow is `workflow_dispatch`-only and has never been dispatched, so it has never failed — it would have **queued forever**. Same failure mode `test.yml` had with its Blacksmith label before KAB-29, and the reason that one went unnoticed too: a job waiting on a label nobody owns never reports an error.

`pre-release.yml` was the last workflow with this problem. The other seven (`pages`, `publish`, `release`, `remote-deploy-dev`, `remote-deploy-prod`, `remote-release`, `test`) are all on GitHub-hosted labels.

## The fix

Every label → a GitHub-hosted one, free on a public repo. Adopts `test.yml`'s `RUNNER_LABEL` anchor so the next copy-paste from upstream is easy to spot.

| was | now |
|---|---|
| `ubuntu-latest-m`, `ubuntu-latest-x64-l`, `ubuntu-latest-arm64-l` | `ubuntu-latest` |
| `macos-15-xlarge` | `macos-15` |

**The arm64 Linux host is dropped, not replaced with `ubuntu-24.04-arm`.** `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` is built by `cargo zigbuild` — a cross-compiler — so an x64 host emits the same artifact. Three of the four Linux matrix entries were already cross-compiling (`cargo xwin` for the MSVC targets). This keeps the change pure CI plumbing and leaves "do we advertise ARM64" where it belongs: a release-scope call, not a runner-label one.

`macos-15` is arm64 exactly as `macos-15-xlarge` was, so the macOS jobs still build arm64 natively and cross-compile x86_64 with the SDK Xcode ships.

## Verification

Not a structural read — I ran it, on a temporary probe workflow that used the labels and toolchain pins this file now specifies.

**[Run 40384248898](https://github.com/AmarShaked/kablan.dev/actions/runs/40384248898)** — `ubuntu-latest`, `nightly-2025-12-04`, `BloopAI/setup-zig@main` 0.15.2, `cargo-zigbuild` 0.20.1:

```
host arch=x86_64 os=Linux image=ubuntu24
target/aarch64-unknown-linux-musl/release/probe: ELF 64-bit LSB executable, ARM aarch64, version 1 (SYSV), statically linked, stripped
target/x86_64-unknown-linux-musl/release/probe:  ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64,      version 1 (SYSV), statically linked, stripped
```

An x86_64 host produced a genuine aarch64 binary. That is the claim the dropped arm64 runner rests on, and it holds.

**[Run 40383467565](https://github.com/AmarShaked/kablan.dev/actions/runs/40383467565)** — `macos-15` job: success. Picked up 3s after dispatch, built `aarch64-apple-darwin` natively and cross-compiled `x86_64-apple-darwin`.

Every probe job was scheduled within seconds instead of queueing, which is the thing the old labels could not do.

The probe branch has been deleted; the run logs remain.

## Side finding — the nightly pin is load-bearing (friction)

Probe round 1 used `stable` rustc instead of the pinned nightly and `aarch64-unknown-linux-musl` failed to link:

```
error: unsupported linker arg: --fix-cortex-a53-843419
```

Current stable rustc passes `--fix-cortex-a53-843419` for aarch64; zig 0.15.2's linker rejects it. So the arm64 Linux build works *only* because of the `nightly-2025-12-04` pin — it is not host-arch related and would fail on an arm64 runner too. A future toolchain bump will break that target until `cargo-zigbuild`/zig catch up. Filed against KAB-32 (ARM64 release verification) rather than fixed here.

## What this PR does *not* do

A real `pre-release.yml` dispatch pushes a version-bump commit, pushes a **tag**, and creates a **public GitHub prerelease**. That is Shaked's call, not mine, so KAB-35's second acceptance criterion ("one triggered run reaches a real pass/fail") is escalated rather than self-served. The probe is the strongest evidence available without minting a public release.

## Not a conflict with #9

KAB-35 flagged a possible collision with #9 (`release/arm64-targets`). There isn't one — `gh pr diff 9 --name-only` returns only `.github/workflows/release.yml`. #9 never touches `pre-release.yml`, so these land independently.

author: zsaplan
body:
## Summary

Session-approved Slack threads currently bypass repeat confirmation prompts, but the agent cannot see the active grants and is instructed to post only when explicitly asked. This makes users repeatedly ask for investigation updates even after approving the destination.

Supply a fresh, request-local snapshot containing only approved thread destinations before each model call. Keep stable posting policy in tool guidance and the publishing skill. Guide the agent to post concise updates for clearly relevant new evidence, changed conclusions, meaningful investigation blockers, and final outcomes without another posting request. Explicit user limits and draft-only requests still take priority; ambiguous destinations require clarification.

The snapshot uses the existing session and verified workspace/bot/API boundaries, reflects revocation, and excludes Canvas grants and non-interactive runs. Global confirmation bypass settings are not proactive posting permission. No automatic publisher is added, and execution-time approval checks are unchanged. Proactive guidance covers non-broadcast replies only—not unsolicited uploads, edits, Canvas changes, deletes, or top-level posts.

Existing sessions need `/reload` after installation. Existing active thread grants then become visible to the agent under this guidance.

## Validation

- [x] `npm run verify --workspace slack`: lint, typecheck, and all 110 tests passed.
- [x] Added checks for current grant visibility, revocation, reload, session isolation, workspace/bot/API isolation, missing credentials/identity evidence, Canvas exclusion, and non-interactive/global-bypass boundaries.
- [x] `git diff --check` passed.
- [x] Complete repository-wide `npm run verify` passed in the feature worktree, including workspace verification and live-config checks. Generated the task-assistant build output needed by its typecheck before running. Its existing real-clock 150-second intake test remains skipped by the suite.
- [ ] Live acceptance: in an interactive session with an approved investigation thread, confirm that a substantive finding leads to a concise relevant reply while routine progress and draft-only work stay private, then revoke the grant and confirm proactive replies stop. No live Slack posts were made during development.

## Limitation

Posting judgment is prompt guidance, not a deterministic classifier. Automated checks verify the permission snapshot and existing safeguards, not whether every model will choose the right update cadence.

The higher-class-number route needs a bound on the primes whose determinant factors cannot be demanded. This PR integrates the actual-Gram excluded-prime assembly into production and proves the canonical conversion from their prefix count B to weighted loss. The arithmetic count remains an assumption.

Phase61 proves 2p F(R,S,p) ≤ R(R−1)S and uses the decreasing kernel log(p)/p with Mathlib finite summation by parts. The public theorem `TenthDiscriminant.ExcludedPrime.excluded_prime_budget_log_div` retains the original prime, nonsquare and radius guards; callers no longer provide a kernel, its signs/monotonicity or a separate weight bound. The original matrix, derivatives and normalization stay fixed. The Phase59 core is transported under a production namespace; all old production proofs, tools, certificates, pins and CI gates are unchanged. README stays61 lines.

Validation at b4cff273f620ead13fc60097222fac01cce4ab67: protocol fad0eac precedes source. Three capped target builds: FAIL98.8740729s (cast-definition proof), PASS39.3685823s, PASS44.6006691s (EOF-only formatting cleanup). All nine new theorem types/guards are unchanged; all attempts are archived. Local full root,34-input exclusions (final closure48263),168-module structural coverage,250 source endpoint pairs and compiled audit4821 logical/4071 theorem/16978 runtime pass. author: pedroklein
body:
Second part of ADR 0041, on top of #390.

## Before

An assignment carried the Profile's content (packages, three markdown files, MCP servers, settings), and the runner rebuilt five files from it on every start. Anything else in a Profile folder never reached a Session.

## After

- An assignment carries the Profile's id and a hash of its files. The runner downloads the files from `GET /agent/sessions/:id/profile` only when the hash differs from its copy's, so `skills/`, `prompts/`, `extensions/` and any other file Pi reads now work.
- The runner installs new packages first, then replaces each file whole and removes the files the Profile dropped. Packages it already installed stay.
- The server leaves out `profile.json`, `auth.json`, `models.json`, `sessions/`, `git/`, `npm/`, `tmp/`, `node_modules/` and anything that isn't a regular file, so a link can't hand runners a file from elsewhere on the server.
- A Profile over 20 MB fails the Session with "Profile X is over 20 MB".
- Plugin Profiles such as the meta one go through the same path, built from their content.
- The runner protocol goes to version 4, so runners need updating with the server.

## How

`folderFiles` and `contentFiles` in `@pi-cloud/profiles` build the files and hash. `Sessions.profileFiles` picks a plugin's Profile or the folder, and `syncProfile` in the session host writes them and keeps `.pi-cloud-profile.json` with the hash and paths it wrote.

author: kayrmac23-droid
body:
## What

`npm run eval` generates full natal readings for a 12-chart fixture and records per-section quality and cost. It exists to check whether the one-chart production numbers from 25 Oct generalise to other charts: a ~28% first-pass clean rate, 4 sections failing even after repair, and generations running long past their word bands.

- `scripts/eval-readings.mjs`: the launcher. It parses the flags, reads `.env.local`, sets the `AXIS_EVAL=1` opt-in and runs the harness under vitest. Usage and the output format are documented in the file header.
- `scripts/eval-readings.harness.ts`: the harness. It has its own vitest config and is not a `*.test.ts` file, so `npm test` and CI never collect it.
- `scripts/eval-readings.request.ts`: builds the request the route sends.
- `scripts/eval-charts.json`: 12 charts, one per axis: unknown time, Sun on a cusp, the 1962 Aquarius stellium, Ushuaia 54.8°S, Tromsø 69.6°N, Quito, 7 retrograde planets, Mars at station, Dublin 1903 (local mean time), plus 3 controls. `--verify` recomputes each chart and fails if it no longer hits its axis.

Modes:
- default: generation only, Sonnet calls.
- `--gate`: also runs the real `gateForCache` per section.
- `--verify` and `--dry-run`: make no API calls.

Outputs go to the gitignored `eval-output/`:
- the prose of each section
- `sections.jsonl` / `sections.csv`
- `calls.jsonl`
- `summary.json`, with aggregates per chart, per section and overall

## src changes (no behaviour change, no prompt change, version not bumped)

- `GateForCacheResult.firstPass`: the evaluator's verdict on the first pass. The result's `scores` holds the repair's re-score once a repair runs, so before this field the first-pass scores were not recorded anywhere.
- The unknown-time angle notice moved from `route.ts` to `lib/unknown-time-notice.ts`, so the harness imports it instead of copying it.
- `eval-harness-parity.test.ts` drives `/api/reading` through two whole readings, one with a known birth time and one without, with the SDK mocked. It asserts that every request equals what the harness builds. I mutated the builder to confirm the test fails on drift.

## Verification

- `npm test`: 401 passed, 2 skipped (the two live-API tests).
- `npm run lint` and `tsc --noEmit` are clean.
- `--verify`: all 12 charts hit their axis.
- `--dry-run` was run across charts.
- `--gate` was run end to end against a local mock of the Messages API. Call counts reconcile (Sonnet 54 = 40 generations + 14 repairs; Opus 50 = 36 evaluations + 14 re-scores), and the cost arithmetic was checked by hand.
- A 401 aborts the run after one call.
- No real API call has been made.

author: goyaldarwin
body:
## 1. One writing standard for every verse
The owner's decisions are applied to every work by one module, `tools/text/standard.py`. Every exporter writes through it (`jsonio.dump_library`). The build fails on any verse, transliteration or meaning that differs from the standard.

- ॥ (U+0965) everywhere, in verses and meanings; numbers compact (॥१॥).
- Sanskrit verses follow Pāṇini:
  - ॐ;
  - the class nasal inside a word (सङ्कल्प, सम्भव);
  - म् at a pause and before a vowel.
- ꣳ before श ष स ह र in the Yajurveda's works (Rudram, Kaṭha, Īśā); ं elsewhere.
- Transliteration in ISO 15919, made from the verse, with Vedic accents on the vowel. The Sukhmani Sahib keeps its own Gurmukhi transliteration.
- The Mānas chhands show their number on the verse.
- Word lookup folds the spellings the standard chooses between (गङ्गा · गंगा), in the app and the build. The smoke test checks that both apply the same rule.
- The old per-work transliterators and the unused `t` in `text.json` are removed. The docs state the standard.

## 2. Śrī Rudram audio
- **The owner's times by ear are applied.** They came in issues #48 and #49, from the owner's second account `darwingoyal`, which the timing workflow skipped. That is 300 starts and ends, in `owner.json`. The source is published (`checked`).
- **The śānti no longer loops.**
  - Cause: a recording's `first..last` came only from the automatic matches. The owner timed the Namakam's śānti after its last matched verse, so the śānti lay outside its recording. When the recording ended, the player went on with "the next verse": the śānti again.
  - Fix: `make_timings.py` and the app now stretch a recording over every verse timed on it. `library.py` refuses a verse timed outside its recording.
- **Namakam u8 begins at प्राणानां**, as recited and as the owner gave it. `settle.py` drops the extra opening line (`DROP_LINE`); the meanings and `reconciliation.md` follow.

## 3. Timing workflow
`timing.yml` applies issues from both owner accounts, `goyaldarwin` and `darwingoyal`.

## Tests
- `build` and `regen_check` pass.
- Smoke, UX: the first commit passed both locally (772/772) and in CI. They run again in CI on this push.

author: creampelt
body:
## Summary

`pls run` could only start a script on one card, so a multi-GPU training run on a held SLURM node had to be launched by hand.

`pls run --on <node> --gpus N` now claims N free cards on that one node (host or host:job), sets `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` to their UUIDs, and starts the script with `python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc_per_node=N`. The runner checks each card is visible before launch and checks all of them when it drains. The lease heartbeat, detach record and release cover every card together. `--gpus` without `--on` (with `--any` or `--lease`) and on box cards is refused with a message. `res._choose` gains `within` and `one_host` so the N cards come from a single node; when no node has N matching free cards it reports that.

Tested live on a 2-card Horizon node: an NCCL all_reduce across both ranks returned the expected sum, and both leases were released.

- [x] Changes fit within this repo's scope — workspace tooling, Ray/cluster, and docs. Task or env
      code belongs in `hcrl_isaaclab` / `*_tasks`.
- [x] If `workspace.yaml` / `resolve_workspace.py` / `src/hcrl_cli` changed, `pls resolve` (and
      `pls setup` if touched) still produces a working workspace.
- [x] No secrets or cluster-specific absolute paths committed.

author: gtapps
body:
## Problem

The core plugin's `claude plugin eval` suites were gitignored (`plugins/hermitd/.gitignore` had `evals/`), so they existed on one maintainer machine only. Helper worktrees never saw them, and the cases' copies of live text drifted without review: the task-policy copy in all 33 channel-routing cases was stale. Delegation decisions (which subagent to keep, which to fold or merge) had no end-to-end baseline at all.

This PR has four parts, in commit order. Nothing in it runs in an installed hermit except the one-line residency change in `startup-context.ts`.

## 1. Track the suites and add a chain-shaped baseline (`337dc598`, `a3c58bf7`)

- **Tracked suites.** `evals/` is tracked; only `evals/results/` is ignored. The files ship inert in the plugin tree (the runner reads `evals/` below the plugin root).
- **Real hooks instead of hand copies.** `startup-context.ts` treats `EVAL_HERMIT_RESIDENT=1` like `HERMIT_RESIDENT=1`, since only `EVAL_*` variables reach an eval run; the registry incumbency check still applies. Channel-routing cases scaffold `.hermit/` from the live `TASKS.md` template, so the real SessionStart hook supplies the task policy.
- **Drift test.** `tests/evals-drift.test.ts` fails when a remaining copy goes stale: agent bodies and the resident prompt passed as `append_system_prompt`, and the channel reply reminder and responder nudge (hermitd's mod drops a `<channel>` envelope submitted from a non-channel origin, so the UserPromptSubmit pipeline never runs on an eval prompt).
- **`chains` suite (11 cases).** One case per agent chain that runs together in production, plus must-not-break rules: reflection-judge verdicts and fail-closed on a blind gate, the reflect quick gate chain, background task-worker dispatch, the waiting-record answer path, proposal-create triage, helper report relay, and the evolve-runner template conflict.

## 2. Port the generators to Bun/TypeScript (`7b368aa6`, `8f48dffc`)

`evals/_generators/{lib,gen-triage,gen-heartbeat,gen-chains}.ts` replace the Python scripts. Regenerating all three suites from deleted directories reproduced the Python output byte for byte, file modes included. `lib.ts` holds the helpers the generators share with the drift test.

## 3. Fixture JSON as the scripts write it (`dc966b26`, `633bc7ee`)

The Python-compatible JSON encoder is gone. Fixtures use plain `JSON.stringify`: compact for script stdout, indented for the state files and `config.json` the scripts write indented. The case diff is whitespace and `\u` escapes only (every changed file compared with whitespace removed and escapes decoded).

## 4. Heartbeat `run-*` cases as real resident ticks (`38d447d4`, `d2410de1`, `2e7e4f6a`, `0d907bf1`)

Seven heartbeat `run-*` cases failed the same graders on every run: the handler dispatched the evaluator and never reached alert-state. The cases carried a drifted hand copy of `prompts/resident.md`, used old `tick`/`alert-state` output shapes, and scaffolded no install, so the real evaluation subagent found no `HEARTBEAT.md`.

- Each `run-*` case now appends the real resident prompt, sets `EVAL_HERMIT_RESIDENT=1`, and is a seed (config, `HEARTBEAT.md`, state files, an optional queued record, the evaluation return). The generator writes the seed to a temp install, runs the real `heartbeat.ts tick`, `alert-state`, `ack-queue`, `task.ts list` and `cost-tracker.ts --mark-budget-notified` there under a fixed-clock preload, and scaffolds the same install, so the files on disk agree with the stand-ins.
- Generating the stand-ins exposed two fictions in the hand copies: a `task.ts show` verb that does not exist, and an `alert` result for an already-reported finding, which the script reports as `ok`.
- The review of that commit found the same drift elsewhere, now fixed: every channel-routing case showed the retired pipe format of `proposal-micro match`, and two chains cases showed an impossible thread key and invented `[task thread]`/`[waiting task]` lines. Those now come from the real scripts and the real prompt pipeline.

```
BEFORE                                            AFTER
evals/ on one machine, untracked                  evals/ tracked, ships inert in the plugin tree
channel-routing: hand copy of TASKS.md policy     real SessionStart hook injects it
reminder / nudge / agent bodies: unguarded        guarded by tests/evals-drift.test.ts
0 cases for task-worker, judge, evolve, relay     evals/chains/: 11 cases
Python generators                                 Bun/TypeScript, sharing lib.ts with the drift test
heartbeat run-*: drifted resident excerpt,        real resident prompt; stand-ins printed by the
  hand-copied stand-ins, no install                 real scripts against the scaffolded install
  (7 cases failing every run)                       (0.996)
```

## Measurements (sonnet, main-loop effort low, `--runs 3`)

- chains: 0.862 at first, 0.875 ($2.24) after the JSON change; chains-write 0.908, then 0.836 ($1.55), no per-case flips beyond one-run variance. `reflect-tier3-chain-shop` stays near 0: quick mode rarely sends a current-session external-content candidate through both gates.
- heartbeat, first per-case baseline: `eval-*` all 1 except two single misses. `run-*` went from seven cases failing every run to 0.981 as resident ticks, then 0.996 ($4.56) with real-script stand-ins.
- channel-routing: 0.925 before the move to real hooks, 0.889 after; flips listed per case in the README.
- Not re-measured after the last fix (`0d907bf1`): channel-routing and the two changed chains-write cases. The README marks those numbers as predating it.

## Known gaps

- Bash cannot run in eval runs on the maintainer host (Ubuntu 26.04's `bwrap-userns-restrict` AppArmor profile blocks the sandbox's seccomp step; the documented bubblewrap profile does not lift it). So the worker reaching `done`, the helper launch, and a real `evolve-runner` dispatch are untested; script output is stood in.
- Generated stand-ins are not drift-checked by a test; regenerating picks up a script change, but nothing fails if nobody regenerates.
- `settings-model-change` asks for the run model, so it fails on sonnet runs; it needs a different requested model.

## Validation

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`: exit 0
- `bun run test`: exit 0 (all 8 suites), after every part
- `bash scripts/plugin-validate.sh`: exit 0
- Privacy scan over `plugins/hermitd/evals` for personal names, hostnames, home paths, keys and emails: no matches; all ids are synthetic
- Generators: two consecutive regenerations produce identical files
- Each part reviewed with `/simplify` (Sonnet reviewers) and `/code-review high --fix` in a fresh-context subagent (Opus 5.5); applied fixes are in the `fix(hermitd): address review findings…` commits, skipped findings listed in each commit or the README

author: maxktz
body:
## Description

Shared pieces for tables of chart numbers, pulled out of Platform's Gateway Query view (mastra-ai/platform#3890) so other cards and pages can use them:

- **`MetricsTable`**: one row per series or group, with lines between rows that fade at the ends (a hovered row covers its neighbours' lines). Columns set their own cell, grid width, alignment and sort value; sort can be controlled (e.g. kept in the URL) or left to the table. With `onRowHover` / `onRowClick` / `isRowDimmed` it acts as a chart's legend; without them it's a plain data table for the numbers under a chart, where a strip chart doesn't fit.
- **`SeriesMark`**: ties a row to its series: a small color square, or an icon (e.g. `ProviderLogo`) drawn in the series color on a square tinted with it. Shaped so legends like `MetricsShareList` rows can use it later; this PR doesn't change them.
- **`Sparkline`**: a tiny trend line for a row.
- **`ChartCard`**: `href` (and `LinkComponent`) make the title a link to a fuller view of the chart, marked by an expand icon.
- **`DropdownMenu.RadioOptions`**: `closeOnSelect` closes the menu on a pick (Base UI's `closeOnClick`), for menus that hold only that choice. Default unchanged.

Nothing existing changes how it looks.

| `MetricsTable` as a chart legend | `MetricsTable` as a data table |
| --- | --- |
| ![MetricsTable as a chart legend](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ab510f9b-4dd8-4ae7-9095-9064d3932bd5) | ![MetricsTable as a data table](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/caaffeaa-cf2d-4660-8f05-ddcaaf989c34) |

| `ChartCard` with `href` | `SeriesMark` |

| ![ChartCard title link](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d13d096b-e3bc-48af-bbd8-8fde85e69ec9) | ![SeriesMark with provider logos and a plain square](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b14641ca-5ae1-45a8-83cd-28971a8fa266) |

Snapshot for Platform: `0.0.0-chart-table-drawer-20261027104130` (from `max/chart-data-table-snapshot-2`: this PR's commits on top of `e94c2e3`, the commit Platform's current pin was built from). mastra-ai/platform#3890 uses it.

## Related issue(s)

Part of PLTFRM-2841 (Gateway usage Query view). Platform PR: mastra-ai/platform#3890.

## Type of change

- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

- [x] I have addressed all Coderabbit comments on this PR


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->
<!-- coderabbit-ai-generated:v1 -->

## ELI5

This PR adds reusable components to display metrics in tables and small trend lines. It also lets chart titles link to more details and gives radio menus an option to close after a selection.

## Changes

- Added `MetricsTable` with configurable columns, sorting, empty-state content, and optional row hover, click, keyboard activation, and dimming. Clicks on controls inside a row do not activate the row.
- Added `SeriesMark` to show a colored square or an icon on a tinted square.

Charter pillar: autonomy. Issues: agent_issues 1000393 (a: github_repo_read marks a path miss not_found; closes on its code-probe), 1000394 (b: logToolEvent records a not_found result as status ok), 100437 (TOOL-FAILURE github_issue_get: GitHub 404 for the D1 issue id 100350), 1000443 (TOOL-FAILURE web_search: `q required` for `{"query": ...}`), and 1000115 (web_fetch self-fetch refusal). Evidence for 1000405 (git_op) and 1000115 was already green on their own probes (closed by autoclose at 18:08 and 18:31Z).

## What was wrong (live qnfo-audit, 2026-10-26)
- An existence lookup that misses is an answer, not a tool malfunction, but `githubRepoRead` returned `{ok:false}` and `logToolEvent` recorded every `!ok` as `status error`, which files TOOL-FAILURE and `[self-heal]` issues and pushes the 24 h error rate over its limit: 5 of the last 14 `github_repo_read` errors were paths that do not exist.
- `github_issue_get` got a GitHub 404 for the number 100350 (a D1 `agent_issues` id): 1 call, 1 error, 100 percent in the 24 h window of its probe.
- `web_search` read `args.q` only: a call with `{"query": ...}` was answered `q required` (1 of 4 calls, 25 percent).
- The self-fetch refusal of `web_fetch` (a correct refusal by design) was logged as an error.

## What this changes (qnfo-ops 2.59.2, patch, mirror identical)
- `githubRepoRead` 404 branch and `githubIssueGet` 404 return `{ok:false, not_found:true, error:...}` (same text and hint).
- `logToolEvent`: `res && (res.ok || res.not_found) ? "ok" : res && res.rejected ? "rejected" : "error"` (the edit specified in 1000394). Meta still carries `resultOk:false` and the error text, so nothing is hidden and the calibration join on `meta.resultOk` is unchanged. Only these two lookup tools produce the flag; only `logToolEvent` reads it.
- `webSearchTool` accepts `query` as an alias of `q` (`q` wins when both are given; neither still answers `q required`).
- The self-fetch refusal of `web_fetch` is `rejected:true` (the status `rejected` is what refusals use; no caller reads it except `logToolEvent` and the deploy result).
- `qnfo-ops/tool-miss-not-failure.test.mjs` (new, 27 checks, no network): lookups, status mapping for ok / not_found / other failure / rejected / not_found+rejected / undefined, alias behaviour, flag counts. `d1-caller-reject.test.mjs` and `d1-query-caller-reject.test.mjs` pinned the old status expression and follow it.

author: agent-smith-ddp
body:
Ticket: OPEN-426.

## What
Four tests in `tests/test_classify_motion.py` failed on `main` (two Utah, two Michigan). I checked each against the real stored votes: **the rules are right and the tests were stale**, so this changes the tests, not `motion_classification.yaml`. It also runs that test file in CI, which is why they rotted unnoticed.

## Why the rule is right (real data)
Commit 807fa5785 (2026-07-03) deliberately made these `passage`: a chamber's concurrence, a conference report's adoption/final passage, a combined 2nd-and-3rd-reading passage under suspension, and a failed passage vote. The tests still expected the old behaviour.

| Check | Utah (all 1,917 stored votes) | Michigan (all 1,279) |
|---|---|---|
| Stored classification equals today's rule | **1,917 of 1,917** | **1,279 of 1,279** |
| Stored equals the pre-807fa5785 rule | 1,396 | 1,262 |
| Votes that would change if the rule were reverted to match the old tests | **521** (230 Senate "passed 2nd & 3rd readings/ suspension", 214 concurrences, 51 "failed", 26 conference final passage), all `[]` to `passage` | **17** (9 concurrences, 8 conference-report adoptions) |

Random api-v3 sample (seed 426, 800 bills each): same result (UT 1,483 votes, MI 238 votes: stored equals today's rule every time). Every concurrence vote in the data has a real tally and voters (UT 214 of 214, MI 9 of 9) and result `pass`; no vote text says "not concur".

**What the broker needs.** I ran the broker's own `compute_eligibility`, unchanged, with each state's real config (migrations 0056 and 0057) on those bills' votes and actions. With today's rules 1,141 of 1,483 Utah votes are scorecard-eligible; with the old rules only 795. **Reverting would drop 346 eligible Utah votes (264 of 572 bills' sets change), including real final-passage votes**, and 2 Michigan concurrences. So flipping the rule to satisfy the tests would have been a regression.

## The four tests
* `test_ut_passage[Final Passage]`: bare "Final Passage" appears in 0 of 1,917 real Utah votes (the real shape is "... Conference Committee - Final Passage", 26 votes). The case is replaced by the real shapes.
* `test_ut_not_passage[Senate/ concurs with House amendment]`: it is passage (214 real concurrence votes). Moved to the passage test with the other real shapes. The not-passage test keeps the real "passed 2nd reading" (361 votes) and adds two look-alikes ("substitute adoption failed", "floor amendment").
* `test_mi_not_passage[... CONCURRED IN ...]` and `[Conference Report adopted ...]`: passage (17 votes). Moved to the passage test. The third case in that test ("SENATE CONCURRED WITH HOUSE AMENDMENTS") is not a text that exists in the data (0 votes), so the whole `test_mi_not_passage` is removed.

## CI
`lint.yml` gets one step: `pip install pytest pyyaml` and `pytest tests/test_classify_motion.py` (132 tests, 0.2 s; verified in a bare venv with only those two packages). I did **not** add the whole `tests/` directory: the other files import `openstates`, `lxml` and `requests` and need the full dependency install, which would slow the job and could turn the fork's CI red for reasons unrelated to classification. On the merge of this branch with the OPEN-401 catch-up branch the file also merges clean.

## Not changed
No YAML change, so **no backfill is needed** (stored data already matches the rules). Edge cases found while sampling are separate tickets: OPEN-439 (5 of 7 Michigan votes whose text says "defeated"/"not adopted" are stored with result `pass`) and OPEN-440 (86 Michigan roll calls with a bare "roll call" text, including 16 resolution adoptions, have no classification).

## pm-review (one pass)
Verdict was "needs revision", all medium or low. Taken: the bare "Final Passage" case is kept as an explicit not-passage case with the reason; a comment on the failed-vote cases says "passage" describes the vote, not its outcome, so nobody flips them again; CI uses `python -m pip` / `python -m pytest`. CI on this branch passed with the new step (the `motion classification tests` step ran). Declined: keeping the removed Michigan test's third text ("SENATE CONCURRED WITH HOUSE AMENDMENTS ROLL CALL # 200") as a pinned `[]`: it is not a text Michigan emits (0 votes), and the two real texts from that test are kept as positive cases; pinning an invented text would make a future rule change look like a regression.

author: cyr-ch
body:
Stacked on #7. IntentOS as an MCP server, with the policy review as an MCP Apps widget.

## `intentos mcp`
- **Model-visible tools**: `explain(repo, task)` returns the evidence pack (text + structured), `policy(repo)` the approved invariants, rules and decisions with sources, `review_start(repo, …)` loads the last `suggest` run into a review session. `review_start` carries `_meta.ui.resourceUri = ui://intentos/review.html`, so hosts that render MCP Apps show the review inline; a client that does not declare the UI extension gets the token-protected local URL in the result instead, and the approval still happens in a browser the model does not control.
- **App-only tools** (`_meta.ui.visibility: ["app"]`): `review_session`, `review_state`, `review_decide`, `review_finish`. Hosts do not offer them to the model, and they also require the session's widget token, which only `review_session` returns. A model-initiated approval is refused twice over; the model-visible result never contains the token.
- **The widget** is the existing review page in `widget` mode: the apps browser bundle is inlined as a classic script that leaves its exports on `globalThis.__mcpApps`, the page connects to the host over `PostMessageTransport`, fetches the token from `review_session`, and routes state/decide/finish to the app-only tools. One page, two transports, same approval code (policy block with real id, hidden test file, policy-notes section, feedback and re-index on finish).
- `intentos mcp --print-codex-config` prints the `codex mcp add` line; `.intentos/mcp.log` records what the client declared and every tool call.

## Dependencies
`@modelcontextprotocol/server`, `client`, `core`, `node` (SDK v2) and `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` 2.0.3.

## Tests
`tests/integration/mcp.test.ts` (4): tool visibility and the resource (bundle and page compile as classic scripts); UI-capable client → `ui: "widget"`, no token in the result, approvals without or with a wrong token refused and the policy untouched, approval with the session token lands INV-001 with its hidden test, finish; client without the extension → `ui: "link"` with a working token-protected page; CLI registration command. The real stdio process was driven with the SDK client (7 tools, resource served). Full suite: 18 vitest files / 107 tests, pytest 30, typecheck clean. Docs: README ("Using IntentOS from inside Codex"), architecture, policies, status.

## Headless Codex run (layer 2)
`codex exec --approve-for-me` with Codex CLI 0.154.0 against the real stdio server on demandlib: the client (`codex-mcp-client`) declared `elicitation: {form, url}` and no MCP Apps UI extension, so the widget is not rendered by Codex today. It listed exactly `explain`, `policy`, `review_start` (app-only tools hidden), got the evidence pack from `explain`, received `ui: "link"` with the token-protected URL from `review_start`, and when told to approve a candidate itself reported that `review_decide` was not visible. Elicitation support points at the next step: approvals through Codex's own form prompts.

author: jaybeeuu
body:
## Problem

Delegated agents (ralph, pipeline workers) started with **no tools at all** and reported the `task` tool — plus every other tool — as missing.

Root cause: `bin/installers/pi.mjs` rendered the generated `tools` frontmatter as one space-separated scalar:

```yaml
tools: "bash read grep find task read_agent wait_for_agents"
```

pi's `parseFrontmatter` returns that as a single string and every consumer splits it on **commas**:

- `extensions/subagent/agents.ts` → `["bash read grep find task read_agent wait_for_agents"]` (one bogus name) → `pi --tools "<bogus>"` → allowlist matches nothing.
- `extensions/agent-modes/discover.ts` flat fallback couldn't read the scalar form at all, so it fell back to `DEFAULT_TOOLS` — lifting the restriction instead of applying it.

Reproduced end to end before the fix:

```
pi --tools "bash read grep find task"   →  none — no tools are listed
pi --tools "bash,read,grep,find,task"   →  bash, read, grep, find, task
subagent(pipeline-worker)               →  ctx_* only (MCP), no built-in tools
```

## Fix

- **Renderer** (`bin/installers/pi.mjs`): emit `tools: "bash, read, task"` — the comma-separated form `parseFrontmatter`, the subagent extension, and `pi --tools` all agree on.
- **Parsers**: `parseToolList` (subagent `agents.ts`) and `splitToolList` (agent-modes `discover.ts`) accept comma- **or** whitespace-separated lists, so a future renderer change can't silently zero out a tool list; the flat fallback now reads the scalar form instead of dropping to `DEFAULT_TOOLS`.
- **Docs**: `agents/README.md` records the rendered-tools contract.
- **Tests**: a render→parse round-trip in `test/pi-installer.test.mjs`, parser tests in `extensions/subagent/agents.test.ts` (wired into that package's test script), and flat-frontmatter cases in `extensions/agent-modes/discover.test.ts`.

After re-running `agent-cortex install pi`, `subagent(pipeline-worker)` resolves its declared tools (`bash, edit, read, write, grep, find`).

Closes bead `agnt-ctx-rpm3`.

## Checks

- `pnpm lint` — pass
- `pnpm test` — 189 pass, 0 fail

author: stephennmiller
body:
Closes #712
Closes #713
Closes #728

## Causes and fixes

**#728: tm-core timeouts in repo-summary.spec and merge-driver.test.** tm-core tests ran git with the machine's global config. On a machine with `commit.gpgsign=true`, every `git commit` in a test runs the signing program. The merge-driver tests make 4 commits each, so on this machine signing took about half the run time of the two files (5.4s down to 2.7s with the global config ignored), and it slows down further under full-suite load or with a slow signing agent. `packages/tm-core/tests/setup.ts` now sets `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL` to the null device and `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1`. Tests that commit already set their own identity, because CI has no global identity. Timeouts are unchanged.

**#713: "builds without caching outside git" sees a repository.** After each commit, git runs auto maintenance, which takes a lock file in `.git/objects`. Newer git versions run that maintenance in a detached background process, so it can race the test's `fs.rmSync(root/.git)`. On Node 24, which CI uses, `rmSync` returns without an error when a file disappears in the middle of a recursive delete, and it leaves `.git` partly in place. `git rev-parse HEAD` then succeeds and the summary gets cached. I reproduced the silent leftover on Node 24.22.1 with a background loop that creates and deletes a lock file. Node 22.22 throws `ENOTEMPTY` in the same case. The setup now also sets `maintenance.auto=false` through `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`.

**#712: `readTrace` read a line the fake was still writing.** The failing run (`e3101e6`) predates the fix now on main: `readTrace` drops the unfinished last line, and the fake already writes each line with one `appendFileSync`. That fix had no test, so this PR adds one: a complete line followed by an 8192-byte partial line. Without the fix, the test fails with the same `Unterminated string in JSON at position 8192` error as CI.

## Stability

- repo-summary.spec + merge-driver.test: 20 runs, 4 at a time, all passed
- full `@tm/core` suite: 4 runs, all passed (192 files, 3029 tests)
- fake-claude.test.ts: 10 runs, all passed
- typecheck, knip and format-check: pass

author: samuelstefano
body:
## O que muda

Relay endurecido, além do roteamento selado (T5) já nesta branch.

- **Root também preso por id** (`COCKPIT_ROOT_USER_IDS`): com a lista preenchida, root exige e-mail na allowlist E `sub` na lista. Barra o cadastro novo com um e-mail root ainda não registrado (cai pra admin/fellow). Vazio = comportamento atual.
- **Allowlist de origem** (`DECK_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`): `/ws` e `/agent` rejeitam (403) `Origin` fora da lista; sem `Origin` passa (agente não é browser). CORS de `/pair/new` só reflete origem listada. Barra página de terceiro abrindo socket com o token do usuário. Vazio = qualquer origem, com aviso no boot.
- **Limites de conexão**: teto de sockets por IP (`DECK_MAX_SOCKETS_PER_IP`, 64; IP = último `X-Forwarded-For` se o peer é loopback) e de abas por conta (`DECK_MAX_TABS_PER_ACCOUNT`, 20; a nova fecha 4429). Barra exaustão de sockets/memória.
- **Guarda de tamanho pré-auth no /agent**: frame > 16 KB antes de autenticar fecha 4413. Pós-auth segue sem esse limite. Barra despejo de dados por peer não autenticado.
- **JWT por subprotocolo WS**: `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol: deck.v1, bearer.<JWT>`; o relay seleciona `deck.v1`. `?token=` continua como fallback e perde pro subprotocolo. Tira o token do access log do Caddy (SPA ainda não migrou, fica pra outra PR).

## Não incluído

`email_verified` só do claim de topo: o GoTrue não emite esse claim no topo do JWT (só em `user_metadata`), então a mudança quebraria o login root. Ficou de fora; a alternativa segura é o `COCKPIT_ROOT_USER_IDS` acima.

## Novas envs

`COCKPIT_ROOT_USER_IDS`, `DECK_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`, `DECK_MAX_SOCKETS_PER_IP`, `DECK_MAX_TABS_PER_ACCOUNT` (em `.env.example`, `relay/deploy/README.md`, ARCHITECTURE.md).

**Ordem de deploy:** este relay precisa ir pro ar ANTES da PR do canal selado (SPA+agente). É compatível com o SPA/agente atuais.

author: aschoch
body:
Prueba para simplificar la app: «Últimos días» pasa al Calendario, que queda como una sola lista de días. Arriba están los días que ya pasaron y abajo los que vienen.

**Cómo se enciende**
- En Ajustes hay un nuevo interruptor: «Calendario con los días pasados (prueba)».
- Se guarda solo en ese móvil y por defecto está apagado. Quien no lo encienda no ve ningún cambio.

**Lo que cambia con el interruptor encendido**
- **Hoy** se queda con la fecha, el botón de hoy y el total de Misas. Desaparecen «Últimos días» y «Ver más».
- **Calendario** muestra los 30 días anteriores encima de hoy. Cada día pasado lleva «He ido», «x de 12» y los puntos de siempre, con la leyenda arriba.
  - El swipe funciona igual que en el resto de la lista: a la derecha marca que fuiste y a la izquierda lo quita.
  - «Días anteriores» añade otro mes por arriba sin mover lo que estás viendo.
- El calendario se abre en hoy, con la fila marcada como «Hoy». Volver a tocar la pestaña también vuelve a hoy.
- Las filas pasadas usan el mismo marcado de asistencia que Hoy (`attendanceRows`/`queueAttendance`). Funcionan también para días en los que no fue nadie.

**Sin cambios en la base de datos.** El historial que devuelve `estado()` ya trae cualquier día pasado.

**Tests**
- Test nuevo que recorre todo lo anterior: interruptor, Hoy sin «Últimos días», 30 días pasados, abrir en hoy, «He ido», swipe a los dos lados y «Días anteriores» sin salto.
- Chromium completo: 88 en verde. Unitarios: 12 en verde.
- Service Worker `misa-v24`.

author: ifiokjr
body:
An Anchor IDL could supply a huge fixed-array length that bypassed the decoder's item limit, allowing zero-byte elements to expand without consuming input. Validate fixed-array lengths when their IDL type is parsed and enforce `maxItems` at decoder construction, before byte-size calculations or element reads.

The parser and decoder share the one-million-item default through `defaultMaxArrayItems`. Regression tests cover invalid schema lengths, zero-byte items, empty arrays, and custom decoder limits. Package documentation and a changeset describe the new checks.
