author: vitopio-prete
body:
## What

Phase 3, third part: tool UIs and human-in-the-loop approval.

- **Tool UIs (`@ngx-assistant/angular`):**
  - `provideToolUi({ toolName, component })` and `provideToolUi({ fallback })` declare the component that renders the calls of a tool, in the `providers` of the app, a route or a component. A tool name is looked up from the nearest injector level up to the root before any fallback is used; within a level the first declaration wins.
  - Each runtime provider has a registry for UIs registered at runtime (`injectToolUiRegistry().register(...)`, which returns its dispose). A runtime registration comes before the UIs declared at its level, and a nested runtime provider still sees the outer UIs.
  - `*nxaMessageParts` renders a `tool-call` part with the UI of its tool, else the fallback, else its own template. A change of registration creates the row again with the new UI; a UI row keeps following its `toolCallId` when the parts are reordered.
  - `injectToolCall()` (`NXA_TOOL_CALL`, provided by every `tool-call` part scope): `part`, `args`, `result`, `status` and `approval` as signals, plus `addResult`, `resume` and `respondToApproval`, which always rejects when the runtime refuses the answer.
- **Approval primitives:**
  - `nxaToolApprovalRoot` holds the request of the nearest tool call and the state of its controls (`state`, also `injectToolApproval()`), with `data-nxa-approval`, `data-nxa-display`, `data-nxa-submitting`, `aria-busy`, `data-nxa-error` and `data-nxa-confirming` on its host.
  - Controls: `nxaToolApprovalApprove` / `nxaToolApprovalDeny` for a decision, `nxaToolApprovalOption` with its confirmation step (`nxaToolApprovalConfirm`, `nxaToolApprovalConfirmCancel`), `nxaToolApprovalText` and `nxaToolApprovalSubmitText` for typed answers, `nxaToolApprovalDismiss` for a dismissible question, and `*nxaToolApprovalQuestions` with `nxaToolApprovalQuestionOption`, `nxaToolApprovalQuestionText` and `nxaToolApprovalSubmitAnswers` for a questionnaire.
  - A request is pending only while its call requires action. Once an answer is sent the controls stay locked until the request settles; a refused answer unlocks them with the error, and a late refusal of a previous request is dropped. The draft, choices, confirmation and error start afresh with each new request. A settled request gives a receipt (outcome, option, notes, questionnaire answers).
- **Docs:** "Tool UIs" and "Tool approval primitives" sections in `packages/angular/README.md`, and `injectToolCall()` in the scopes table.

## Why

Phase 3 of the roadmap: a tool call can be rendered by the app's own component, and a call gated by an approval request can be allowed, denied or answered from headless controls.

## How it was verified

- [x] `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run format:check`
- [x] `pnpm run test`: engine 131 files / 2538 tests, Angular 25 files / 660 tests
- [x] `pnpm run build`
- [x] `pnpm run e2e`: 15/15 checks on the demo
- Tool UIs: registered UI over the template with the call and its actions; `addResult`, `resume`, `respondToApproval` and recorded interactions reach the external store adapter; live swap on register and dispose; other tool names; first declaration wins; runtime registration before declarations; fallback and named UI swapping; names that only `Object.prototype` has; nearer level wins and lookup through every level; app-level declarations; two assistants side by side; nested assistant scope; UI rows following the call id, recreated for a new id or a part that becomes a tool call; calls sharing an id
- Approval: decision with and without note; lock until settled; cancelled run; thread that cannot answer; option order, known and custom kinds, confirmation step; no allow or deny for questions; typed answers, empty answer, note on a decision; dismissal only when declared; questionnaire with single and multiple choice and a `__proto__` id; synchronous and asynchronous refusals; reset on a new request; late refusal dropped; receipts
- Breaking the first-registration rule, the name-before-fallback lookup, the late-refusal guard, the reset per request or the custom-kind approval makes the tests fail
- `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run smoke` and `pnpm run security:check`
- commitlint over all commits and the PR title: no errors or warnings

## Checklist

- [x] Tests added or updated for the behavior that changes
- [x] Commits follow Conventional Commits

author: aidanallchin
body:
## Problem In multi mode a workspace could connect GitHub with a personal access token. That token is one person's long-lived, unscoped credential, and it gets sealed whole into every claim's credential bundle. An App's installation token lasts an hour and covers only the installation's repositories. A token workspace with no deployment App on its host also has no OAuth client, so its members can't link a GitHub identity once TFAC-1104 drops token identity capture. An imported App with no client secret leaves the same gap. This is hardening: no multi deployments exist yet, so no token workspaces need migrating. ## Change In multi mode, a workspace's GitHub access is always an App. Local mode is unchanged. - **Token routes 404 in multi.** `PUT …/github/pat`, `POST …/github/pat/switch-to` and `POST …/github/pat/preflight` call one helper, `refuseWorkspaceTokenInMulti`, before authorization. It does the same thing the deployment-App routes do in local mode. `DELETE …/github/pat` stays available in both modes. - **Import requires `client_secret` in multi.** If it is absent or blank, the import returns 400 `MISSING_FIELD` on `client_secret`. The missing-field checks now accumulate (`httpx.Validation`), so an empty body names `app_id`, `pem` and `client_secret` together. A rejected secret is still 422, and an inconclusive check still stores the secret unvalidated. - **Removed the managed-App guard from the PAT bind.** The deployment App exists only in multi and the bind only in local, so the guard could never fire. Its tests in `github_managed_disconnect_test.go` change to match: - the PAT-bind case now asserts the 404; - the "no live row is not in the way" case now runs through the register launch; - `TestManagedDisconnect_RacesAPATBind` is deleted along with the route it raced. Disconnect racing an import or registration still takes the same lock, but nothing tests that race now. - **Discard's 409 message.** For a live App it now points at the disconnect, which exists in both modes, instead of "switch the org to a PAT". - **Frontend, multi only:** - The wizard hides the access-method step and seeds the method as App, so the URL step leads straight to the App source step. - Settings shows no way to add, replace or switch to a token in any state. A workspace that holds a token keeps "Switch to GitHub App…". - The import form shows the client secret as a required field instead of a collapsible optional one. - **Out of scope:** identity linking (TFAC-1104), any operator setting to re-enable tokens (deliberately none), and migrating existing token workspaces.
Scope / verification - `./scripts/lint.sh`: all checks passed. - `go test ./...`: all packages pass. Docker was available, so the pgtest-backed multi-mode tests ran rather than skipped. - `pnpm run test:run`: 130 files, 1291 tests pass. New tests: - `github_app_only_multi_test.go`, full multi stack on Postgres: - the three token routes 404 and never call GitHub; - `DELETE` still removes a seeded token; - import without a secret (absent, empty, blank) returns 400 on `client_secret`; - an empty body reports all three missing fields; - a rejected secret returns 422; - an import with a secret succeeds. - `steps.test.ts`: multi has no mode or token step, and `loadOrg` seeds App even when the workspace holds a token. - `GitHubAccessControl.test.tsx`: no token affordance in any multi state. - New `GitHubAppImportForm.test.tsx`: the secret is required in multi and optional in local. - The existing local-mode tests pass unchanged.
Line breakdown From `./scripts/pr-lines.sh` (blank lines excluded: +39/-5). | Kind | Added | Removed | | ------------- | ----- | ------- | | Code | 203 | 129 | | Tests | 339 | 68 | | Documentation | 10 | 9 | | Code comments | 123 | 67 | | Test comments | 24 | 13 |
## Docs - `docs/self-hosting/install.md`: every place that offered "its own App or a PAT" now says a workspace uses an App, with one sentence on why. - `docs/concepts/github-app-installations.md`: the PAT bind is no longer listed as a managed-guard door. Resolves [TFAC-1205](https://linear.app/sky-ai-eng/issue/TFAC-1205)

author: dshechter
body:
Four changes, none touching the data.

## 1. Zenodo DOI for every version (10.5281/zenodo.22696798)
This DOI opens the most recent version, and Zenodo lists every version with its own DOI. It doesn't change between releases, so nothing in the repository needs updating when a release is archived.
- **README:** one badge under the title; the Cite section asks readers to add this DOI for the data.
- **Website:**
  - a two-part header badge (DOI | 10.5281/zenodo.22696798), in plain HTML;
  - a footer line ("archived on Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.22696798");
  - the archive named in the Versions note and How to cite (`ARCHIVE_DOI` in `docs/assets/explorer.js`).
- **CONTRIBUTING.md:** set the version in `.zenodo.json` and `CITATION.cff` before tagging. There is no step after Zenodo archives the release.

## 2. Protein pages open with the protein map alone
- **New protein:** only the Protein map is open; every other section is closed, showing its one-line summary and small picture.
- **Same protein:** the reader's choices stay through a redraw, for example a filter change.
- **Next protein, Back or a reload:** starts afresh. Old saved section states are ignored, and protein sections are no longer saved in the browser.
- **Links still work:** `#Q13148/p-3d` opens 3D structure, and `#Q13148/R293` shows the site's card under the map.
- **3D viewer:** it starts when its section is opened and scrolled into view, so a protein page no longer downloads the 3D library and model unless someone opens 3D.

## 3. Visit counts with GoatCounter (site code `shechterlab`)
GoatCounter sets no cookies and keeps nothing that identifies a visitor.
- **What counts:** one count per page, a tab or a protein (`#overview`, `#Q13148`, titled by its gene), only on shechterlab.github.io.
- **Excluding a browser:** opening `#toggle-goatcounter` stops counting that browser, and opening it again restarts it.
- **Disclosed:** the About text says visits are counted.

## 4. Two wording fixes from the scientific review
- **The PRMT5 knockdown of Li et al. 2021 lists only its decreased sites**, so "385 of 385 (100%)" read as a response rate. The response table now shows "385 listed", with no bar (and the row no longer sets the bars' scale), and the increased column says "not listed". The Overview tile and the section summary give the count without a denominator. Every other row keeps its share.
- **Curated experiments:** the note now says how much the curation holds: "6 experiments from 3 papers, last curated 2026-10-25". This sits beside the existing "a protein without rows has not been curated, not shown to lack experiments". The figures are computed from the curation table, so they update as it grows.

## Checks
- `node --check docs/assets/explorer.js` passes. The asset version is bumped to `20261027b`.
- **Protein page folds:** 10 browser tests and the breadcrumb regression tests pass. The 3D viewer draws once opened, with internet access.
- **Counter:** 8 browser tests on the site served at its real address pass, covering counts, no double counting, the toggle, and nothing counted from a local copy.
- **Review fixes:**
  - the PRMT5 KD row reads "385 listed" with no %, and the other 14 rows keep their shares;
  - the METTL14 page shows the curation scope;
  - no page errors.

author: drabdanoo
body:
Fixes from the first real-world case (an STL sent from Android, on the 1.0.0 store build). Everything here is **JS-only** for the app, so it can ship to 1.0.0 as an **OTA update**. It also needs a **web deploy** and a **storage rules deploy**.

## 1. STL never reached the lab, and the case was sent several times
- **Duplicates:** the app created the case, then uploaded the scan. If the upload failed, the code fell into a generic "Failed to send" error, so every retry created a new case. Now the created case is remembered. A retry ("إعادة رفع الملف" / "Retry file upload") only re-uploads the file to that case, and the dentist is told the case itself was sent. A ref also blocks double taps.
- **The Android upload itself:** the scan was read with `fetch(uri).blob()`, which is unreliable for large binaries on Android. It now reads with `expo-file-system` (`File.arrayBuffer()`, already in the 1.0.0 binary) and uploads raw bytes with an explicit content type.
- **Size:** checked when the file is picked, before any case is created.
- **`storage.rules`:** the `orders_files` limit goes from 60 MB to **150 MB**.

## 2. Lab couldn't see the scan on the website
The website only showed `fileUrl`, which the apps never write; they store `filePath`. `OrderInvoiceModal` and `IncomingOrderRxModal` now download the scan by path via `CaseFileLink`. Storage rules are checked against the lab at click time.

## 3. Lab didn't notice new cases
- **Web:** the bell only showed a silent badge. New notifications that arrive while the page is open now show a toast, a chime, and a desktop notification when the tab is in the background. Permission is asked on the first bell click.
- **App:** push tokens were only saved from the Notifications screen. They're now registered once per signed-in user. Actually *sending* pushes (Cloud Function plus APNs/FCM credentials) is a separate follow-up.

## 4. Rx → add medicine: fully black screen on Android
The sheet avoids everything known to break Android modals:
- no RN `KeyboardAvoidingView` "height" resizing on Android
- a definite sheet height, so the `FlatList` virtualizes instead of laying out all ~177 rows and images
- no `removeClippedSubviews`
- `resizeMethod="resize"` for the remote images

**Not verified on a device.**

## Deploy steps (each needs sign-off)
1. `firebase deploy --only storage` (150 MB limit)
2. Web deploy (scan download + alerts)
3. `eas update --channel production` from this branch (runtime 1.0.0, reaching iOS build 4 and Android versionCode 7). Test on a preview channel or a single device first; OTA hasn't been used on this app before.

## Testing
- [x] `tsc` passes (native; web only has an existing unused-import error in `IncomingOrderRxModal`)
- [ ] Android: send a case with a real STL. One case, a progress bar, a success screen; turning off Wi-Fi mid-upload shows "Retry file upload" and doesn't duplicate.
- [ ] Web (lab): open the case and download the STL from both case views.
- [ ] Web (lab): with the dashboard open, send a case from the phone. A toast, a chime, and a desktop notification if backgrounded.
- [ ] Android: Rx → add medicine opens normally.

Unlike the private owner note, the review is shared: the pet's owner reads it under the pet room, and other sitters read it on the pet card of a request or booking (the existing sitter Booking details card, under the Life Record fold). No new screen.

| Step | What | Commit |

| 1 | DB: `pet_reviews` (`015u`): one review per (booking, pet). RLS: only the stay's sitter writes or edits, only after Returned and only for a pet of that stay; the pet's owner and any sitter read; nobody deletes. Stay dates filled by a trigger. SQL smoke | 18d7b99 |

| 3 | App: per-pet review card on the sitter's finished stay (under the medals), reviews list under the owner's pet room and on the sitter's pet card (this stay's own review left out there), e2e `pet-review` | 86c0e07 |

body:
**Needs Theo:** this row has a ✓ (`tools/balance/**`: the balance matrix). It is P1-15e2b, the row Theo chose on 2026-10-27 (option 1: the held chase from a named balance scenario), before P1-15e3. Its base is `main`: #242, the base its Decisions name, has merged.

## What changed

The balance matrix's tools only. **The game is exactly the same.**

The balance matrix must show that a hero's chase can be held up by a battle that hasn't ended. Until now it waited for its 12 scripted games to show this, and they only did by luck: about four times a set. P1-15e3's games, which give the spare heroes their own orders, never do. So the matrix failed for reasons that had nothing to do with the change being tested.

**Now `npm run balance` stages the held chase on purpose, first, in 20 short runs (about 3 seconds).** An enemy king besieges a province that two weak hosts hold. The siege can't end in Spring. Our king rides after the enemy king. In every run, his chase must wait in Early Summer, because the ground is still a battlefield. In most runs it also waits in Spring, the moment he catches the enemy king. If either hold stops happening, the matrix fails and says which one, in how many of the 20 runs.

The 12 scripted games still count the held chase and print it. A set no longer fails when they don't meet it. A set still fails when they never give Encounter Character.

## Rulings

None.

## Staging

Not needed, because only the balance matrix's tools and tests change (`site/` is byte-identical but the build stamp). Nothing here is something a player or the GM can try. The proofs below cover the risk: both sets play exactly as before, and each hold, planted out of the engine, turns the run red.

---

## What it is

**By hand:**
- `tests/balance/scenarios/a-chase-held-by-an-unresolved-battle.ts` (new): the scene above, as the scoping's sketch stages it. There are three Human realms: 0 and 1 at war, 1 and 2 at war. Realm 1's king (12 Elite Heavy Infantry) besieges a province of realm 2's. Realm 2's king and a hero hold it, with one Green Light Infantry each. The province is flagged `_battleUnresolved`, and every land province beside it belongs to realm 0. Realm 0's king (4 Veteran Heavy Infantry) is given Encounter Character on realm 1's king in Spring. Every Spy is 0, every duel stance is `refuse`, and every other hero is unarmed.
  - It runs 20 times. Its figures are `chases: waited for a battle`, its two slices (`| when: on the catch in Spring`, `| when: in Early Summer`: the hunter's own "the reckoning must wait" and "the chase after … must wait" lines in those seasons) and `chases: caught`.
  - It requires the Early Summer hold in every run, and the hold on the catch in some run.
  - Its staging check throws "could not stage" when Spring's first battle (the siege's round) is not more than four to one. That is the fortune of battle's bound. It also throws when a Spy counts as anything but 0.
  - The sketch's `process.env` settings and its trial-only figures are not in the row.
- `tools/balance/scenario.ts`: `Scenario` gains an optional `requires` (`ScenarioRequirement`: a figure, `'every run'` or `'some run'`, and its words). `whatAScenariosRunsMissed(scenario, runs, failedRuns)` is a pure function that returns one line for each failed run and for each requirement missed, with how many runs showed it.
- `tools/balance/run.ts`: before the sets, `npm run balance` plays every scenario that has `requires`, on this site or `KC_SITE`'s, with `--jobs` runs at a time (every core by default). It plays it once with `--update`, which plays both sets. It does not play it with `--only` or when a scenario is named. It prints one line, for example `Required scenario "a-chase-held-by-an-unresolved-battle": 20 runs in 2.9 s: every requirement met`. A miss or a failed run fails the run.
  - `CASES_A_REQUIRED_SCENARIO_GIVES` (`battleChase` → the new scenario) takes that case out of the "never happened" check, which is now a pure function, `theScriptedCasesThatNeverHappened(cases)`.
  - The run also fails if a scenario on that map isn't there or requires nothing.
  - The header comment is updated.
- `tools/balance/play.ts`: the `Cases` comment only (where the held chase is required). The counting is unchanged, so `matrix.json`'s `cases` and every game stay identical.
- `tools/balance/labels.ts`: the `when` slice, which labels the two new figures.
- Docs: `tests/README.md` ("The balance matrix": the scripted realm's sentence about the armed hero after an armed enemy in an unresolved battle is gone, because it only happened by luck; "Named scenarios": required scenarios and the new one; `balance-scenario`'s row), `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` (named scenarios: the required one is played in CI's balance job), and `CLAUDE.md`'s `npm run balance` line ("and the scenarios it requires").

**Generated:** nothing. The baselines are unchanged.

**Workflows:** none changed. CI's balance job already runs `npm run balance` when an engine path changes, and `tests/balance/**` is an engine path. The mutant scorer's balance stage plays the scenario too.

## The proof

Run on this branch (`882ef76`, base `main` at `6e49094`, whose tree is #242's head `53264f8`). Planted copies are `git archive` copies of the branch with `node_modules` symlinked. The scoping's figures (on `53264f8`) are in brackets.

| | Set A | Set B |
|---|---|---|
| The required scenario | 20 of 20 held in Early Summer, 15 of 20 on the catch: every requirement met (20, 15) | the same 20 runs: met |
| Games identical to the baseline | 60 of 60 (60) | 60 of 60, `noise.json` (60) |
| Every realm's report identical | 60 of 60, 5,772 reports (5,772) | 60 of 60, 5,903 reports (5,903) |
| The games' scripted cases (printed, unchanged) | Encounter Character 36, held chase 4 (36, 4) | 31, 4 (31, 4) |

- **Over 1,000 runs** (runs 1 to 1,000, 14 at a time, 72 s): **1,000 of 1,000 held in Early Summer**, 657 held on the catch in Spring. No run is without a hold, and there are 0 errors (1,000 and 657). If the dice shifted, the chance that 20 runs would give no hold on the catch is 0.3^20, about 1 in 30 billion.
- **Planted copies, each hold taken out of `advancePursuit` alone**, `KC_SITE=<copy>/site npm run balance -- --set A`:
  - **The first hold** (`meArmed &&` read as `false &&`): `MISSED: the chase held by the battle in Early Summer: in 0 of 20 runs`, exit 1. Also, 57 of 60 games are identical, and the games' held chase is 0. (Scoping: 0 of 20, 57 of 60.)
  - **The second hold** (the "reckoning" branch never taken): `MISSED`, held in Early Summer in 5 of 20 runs, on the catch in 0 of 20, exit 1. **Set A's 60 games stay identical.** With the base's tools, the same copy exits 0 with 60 of 60 identical: today's matrix can't see this hold at all. (Scoping: 5 and 0, 60 of 60.)
- **Time**, `npm run balance` from a copy each (it builds its site first), base and row alternately:

  | | Base `6e49094` | This branch | Difference |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Set A | 41.6, 45.5, 44.7, 45.8 s | 47.4, 49.0, 48.8, 48.7 s | +5.8, +3.5, +4.1, +2.9 s (mean +4.1) |
  | Set B | 41.9, 43.0, 43.3 s | 46.6, 46.4, 46.5 s | +4.7, +3.4, +3.2 s (mean +3.8) |

  The required scenario's own line says 2.9 to 3.1 s every time. The games' half and every realm's report took the same time on both, within the noise (for example, set A run 4: 23.8 and 20.7 s on the base, 23.6 and 20.7 s here). The Decisions bound is "within 4 s" (the trial measured +2.5 s). The B mean is within it. The A mean is 0.1 s over, because of the first pair's +5.8 s.
- **On CI's runner** (4 jobs): the required scenario took 13.3 s. The balance job took 6 min 19 s on this branch and 6 min 31 s on #242 (`53264f8`). The games' half took 174.3 s here and 178.2 s there, and every realm's report 167.5 s and 166.3 s, so the runner's noise hides the scenario.

author: privaloops
body:
**Stacked on #344 → #343 → #333: merge those first, in that order.** Until then this PR's diff also shows their commits; this PR's changes are the last three: `37c07bd`, `93ad0af`, `154dcdb`. It targets `main` so that CI and the e2e run against the preview cover it.

Decodes in a Web Worker in `@hevcjs/mediabunny-plugin`, with `registerHevcDecoder({ workerUrl })`, and keeps the page's thread responsive when there is no worker.

## Why

Decoding flat out froze the page: the plugin decodes synchronously, and Mediabunny chains `decode()` through promises only, so nothing gave the browser a task boundary. Reported on a 300 MB file; reproduced on a 60 s 1080p file (Chromium, Apple M4 Pro, 2026-10-26): 4 animation frames in 17.8 s of decoding.

## Plan

1. `decode-worker.ts`, bundled on its own as `dist/decode-worker.js` (IIFE, 13 KB, no mp4box): loads the glue with `importScripts()`, decodes, packs each frame (I420 / I420P10, or 10-bit scaled to 8) and sends it back transferred. Messages are handled one at a time, in order.
2. `worker-client.ts`: the page's side. One worker per track. At most 4 packets in flight — `decode()` waits past that, and Mediabunny awaits it before the next packet. Errors from the worker reach Mediabunny through `onError`. A cross-origin worker is fetched (HTTP status checked) and started from a blob URL, revoked once the worker answers.
3. Timing stays on the page: each worker answer carries the pictures the packet suppressed, then the frames it released, fed to the same `OutputTimestamps` as before.
4. Without `workerUrl`, decoding stays on the page's thread and now yields to the event loop about every 50 ms.
5. Demo: decodes in the worker unless `?worker=0` (new toggle), and drops its own yield since the plugin yields. New script `build:demo:mediabunny-worker`; `demo/mediabunny-decode-worker.js` is committed like the other demo bundles and rebuilt by CI before deploying.
6. Tests — Node: a stand-in worker runs the real worker handler and the real WASM, asynchronously both ways (Node has no Web Worker); the end-to-end assertions are shared with the page-thread test (`test-utils.ts`). E2E: every case runs in the worker and on the page's thread, plus a responsiveness case per mode on the longest gap between animation frames.
7. Docs: plugin README (worker setup, page-thread mode, options, trusted sources and CSP), root README, CHANGELOG, changeset (`minor`).

## Interpretations

- **Worker opt-in through `workerUrl`, page thread by default**: like the Shaka plugin's `workerUrl`. A default worker would need a URL the plugin cannot know without bundler-specific code.
- **Default glue and binary next to the worker**: the three files are served side by side, as the other plugins' setup does.
- **Yield every 50 ms on the page's thread**: keeps paint gaps around 70 ms on a 720p stream; the cost on throughput is within run-to-run noise.

## Results

Measured on 2026-10-26, Apple M4 Pro, Chromium (Playwright), 60 s 1080p HEVC file (x265 ultrafast, 132 MB, 1 500 frames), decoding flat out:

| | Decode time | Animation frames during it |
|---|---|---|
| Before (page's thread, no yield) | 17.8 s | 4 |
| Page's thread, yielding | 20.2 s | 811 |
| Worker | 17 s | 2 044 |

- **Unit tests**: `pnpm -r typecheck` clean, `pnpm -r build` clean, `pnpm test:unit` 205/205 (mediabunny 19). Mutation: without the backpressure wake-up, the worker test hangs.
- **E2E** (`local-chromium`): 11/11. Mutation: without the plugin's yield, the page-thread responsiveness case fails with a ~1 s gap. (Its first version missed that: a frozen page runs no animation frame, so the gap only shows at the first frame after it; the case now waits for two before stopping.)
- **Other engines**, Playwright Docker image `v1.62.0-noble`, demo page in the worker: Firefox 153 — 250/250 and 10/10 frames; WebKit 26.5 (Linux), forced — 250/250 and 10/10. **To look at**: in that WebKit, BBB 720p took 4.8 s in the worker against 1.6 s on the page's thread in an earlier run; Chromium shows no such gap (0.94 s vs 1.1 s). Not checked on Safari.
- **Cross-origin worker**: page on `localhost`, worker, glue and binary on `127.0.0.1` (the repo's CORS server): 250/250 frames; a missing worker reports `HTTP 404` instead of running the error page.
- **`/mdma-review`**: security — no dependency change, `pnpm audit --prod` clean; findings applied: HTTP status checked and blob URL revoked for a cross-origin worker, README note that worker, glue and binary must come from trusted sources, with the CSP directives. Lint — no linter configured. Bundle — worker 13 KB; demo bundle 386 KB minified.

author: shyamsharma23
body:
This PR fixes the intermittent failure in `e2e/integrated/10-load.spec.ts` that has been dropping PRs from the merge queue.

### Cause
`growClient` copied units until the client had 10,000 instances counted across every year. Every read in the journey, including the final `count=true` check at line 208, asks for `fy=2022-23`.

When earlier journeys leave instances in other years, a single copy of each unit is enough to pass 10,000 overall but not within the year. Queue run 40385424693 shows exactly that:
- The whole client grew from 5,049 to 10,098 (×2).
- FY 2022-23 grew from 1,899 to 3,798 (×2), which is the "total 3798" the check got.

So it is not a read-before-commit, a replica or a cache. The count was right; the journey grew the wrong number. It passed on the PR's own CI because that base had fewer out-of-year instances, so several copies were made.

### Fix
`growClient` now counts instances that are not archived and are due between 2022-04-01 and 2023-03-31. That is the window `fyRangeOf('2022-23', 4)` gives the register. It grows until the year holds 10,000 and returns that number, and the log line says "in FY 2022-23". Budgets and checks are unchanged.

### Checked on main 6f3a28f
- Full integrated suite run locally: 49/49 pass.
- The load journey grew the year to 10,128 in 971 ms. Alone, the slowest reads were 688 ms for the overview and 968 ms for the count. With 10 users, p95 was 6.1 s for the overview and 5.9 s for the count, within the 10 s budgets.
- ESLint, Prettier and the e2e `tsc` are clean.

author: kantagesolutions
body:
Adds full lifecycle management for organizations and staff in the admin portal, every action audited.

## The rule: delete only when there is nothing to keep

Dental records must legally be kept for years, and the audit trail must outlive what it describes. So:

- **Nothing to keep → Delete permanently.** An organization with no patients, records, staff or activity (like the `ssss` test organization in production), or a staff member who has never acted.
- **Anything to keep → Archive.** Hidden from the lists, all access cut, every record kept, restorable at any time. The portal explains exactly why, e.g. *"It holds 2 staff accounts, 1 patient record, 1 booking request and 10 logged actions, which must be kept."*

The portal asks the server what must be kept **before** offering either option. The database enforces it independently too: every foreign key into organizations, clinics and staff is `NO ACTION`, and the delete functions refuse when anything remains.

| | Active | Suspended | Archived |
|---|---|---|---|
| Organization | Suspend · Delete | Restore · Delete | Restore · Delete |
| Staff | Edit · Suspend · Delete | Edit · Restore · Delete | Restore · Delete |

## Details

- **Permanent delete** removes the organization with its clinics, configuration and tenant registry entry, which retires its booking links. The registry is written before commit, so a registry failure leaves everything in place.
- **The audit trail survives a delete**: earlier entries keep the name with the reference cleared (`ON DELETE SET NULL`), and the deletion itself is recorded.
- **Archived organizations take no bookings**; the booking functions already require an active organization.
- **Totals count only live organizations**, so archiving visibly changes them.
- **CORS now allows `DELETE`.** Without it, every browser would have blocked the request before it reached the server.

## Verification

- All 17 migrations applied in order to a fresh database: **27 of 27 tests pass**.
- Migration 016 exercised as the restricted request role: an empty org deletes with its clinic and keeps its audit entry; an org with a patient refuses and keeps the patient; archive and restore work; idle staff delete with their roles; staff with activity refuse and keep their history.
- **Backward compatible**: the statuses the currently deployed API uses still work.
- Every state previewed with fictitious data. Two layout issues found and fixed in preview: action buttons stacking vertically, and totals counting archived organizations.

## Merge note

Merge this on its own and let its deploy finish before merging anything else. Merging two PRs close together previously deployed an older commit last and rolled production back.

body:
The bundle read the engine's raw argv and dropped every `--quiet`, `--batch`, `--no-color` and `--verbose` in it, wherever it stood, so `sh -c 'echo $0 $1' --quiet --batch` lost them.

Both launchers now start the engine as `x-bin OPTION... -- ARG...` (x.sh since x-lang#934; x-os since jonruttan/x-os#55), and `(Sys args 'program)` answers the engine's path and what follows that `--`. `run.x` hands `(rest (Sys args (lit program)))` to the main, which now takes the operands; the filter and its `*-argv` export go. Both launchers swallow a user's first `--` themselves, so the bundle's "drop one leading --" only ever removed the launcher's own.

The `ash-operands` spec becomes one showing those words reach `$0` and `$1`, BusyBox ash's reading.

**Verified:** the bundle through v0.39.0's `x -l` from this branch, with arguments the filter used to eat. Ten bundles' branches in one directory, all ten ok.

author: jeromebanks
body: Closes #683 Part of #682 ## Decision needed (owner) **Why this PR exists:** Anthropic's plugin directory needs an icon before we submit pscat (#682), and the portal reads the icon only once, at the first save or submit. So this PR has to merge before the first portal submission. It touches owner paths (`plugin/.claude-plugin/`, `plugin/plugin.json`, `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`), so it's tier (c) and an agent won't merge it. **Steps:** 1. Look at the images below: the 1024 px icon, the 48 px render, and the old vs new 512 px. A good result is a cream page with cat ears, a folded corner and a readable `%!` on mustard yellow, still legible at 48 px. 2. #778 (exact-area fill coverage) merged while this PR was open. `main` is merged in and all three PNGs are re-rendered with it, so the shipped icon matches the 0.7.0 renderer. Only edge antialiasing changed, and the result is visually identical. If the renderer changes again before you submit, re-run the three commands at the top of `art/logo/pscat-logo-d.ps`. 3. Merge this PR (squash). 4. Go to https://claude.ai/directory/manage, then **Submit new**, then **Plugin bundle**. Enter Repository `PSCatLabs/pscat`, Plugin path `plugin`, Branch `main`. Select **Validate**. A good result is no **Blocking** findings and no icon warning. Then **Save/Submit**. The directory takes the icon from this first save. ## The icon 1024 px, `plugin/.claude-plugin/icon.png`: 48 px at actual size, `art/logo/renders/pscat-logo-d-48.png`: ### Old (2026-10-23, candidates branch) vs new (this branch), 512 px | old: `6b74021` | new: this PR | |---|---| | | | **Before #778 the renders were byte-identical, and so were the 48 px ones.** The brief expected #757 (embedding the standard 35) to change the `Courier-Bold` `%!`. It didn't, because `Courier-Bold` was already one of the 12 Liberation builtins (`LiberationMono-Bold.ttf`, `src/font.rs`). #757 embedded only the other 23 names. So D needed no tuning, and it's unchanged apart from header comments. After #778 merged, the renders differ only in edge antialiasing: 680 of 9,264 raw bytes at 48 px, and 0.3% at 1024 px. The images above are the post-#778 renders. ## Summary - Brings over only candidate D: `art/logo/pscat-logo-d.ps` (CC0, render commands in its header) and its 512 and 48 px renders in `art/logo/renders/`. The rejected A, B and C candidates and the contact sheet stay on branch `feature/683-plugin-icon-pscat-logo` (commit 6b74021) for history. - `plugin/.claude-plugin/icon.png` is the 1024 px render (`--page 384x384 --dpi 192`). It's 21 KB. - **Where Claude Code expects the icon:** the top-level `icon` field in `plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`, set to a `./` path inside the plugin. - Anthropic's directory reads it for the listing, and Claude Code ignores it at load time. - It is **not** allowed in a marketplace entry, so `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` is untouched. - Source: [Plugin manifest reference, "Directory listing fields"](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins-reference). - `claude plugin validate` (2.1.309) also finds the file by path. Its `ICON_MISSING` warning checks `icon`, then `.claude-plugin/icon.png`, then `assets/icon.png`, and gives the requirements: square PNG/JPEG, 512 to 2048 px, under 2 MB, and read once at the first portal save/submit. The field is set anyway so nothing depends on that fallback. - **Codex:** `extensions.com.openai.interface.composerIcon` and `.logo` in `plugin/plugin.json` now point at the same file. Source: [Codex "Build plugins"](https://developers.openai.com/codex/plugins/build). author: claudio-alvarez
body:
## Context

Found in the end-to-end checks of 2026-10-26 (follow-up to #816 and #817):

- With `AI_ADDITIONS_KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID` or `_SECRET` unset in EthicApp, the connection test reported the token step as `unauthorized` ("AI Additions rejected the EthicApp credentials"), even against a host that does not exist, because no request was ever made. Operators looked for the problem on the AI Additions side.
- While `GET /mng/api/ai-services/catalog` was pending, the Services section showed the loading line together with "The catalog cannot be read…" and the "Allow no services" form.

## What changed

**ethicapp**
- `ai-additions-client.service.js`: new typed `AiAdditionsCredentialsMissingError` (`code: "credentials_missing"`) plus `isAiAdditionsCredentialsMissing`, thrown where the client previously threw a plain `Error` with the same message. Dispatch behavior is unchanged except for the clearer code; nothing on the dispatch path branched on that error.
- `ai-services-catalog.service.js`: new `CREDENTIALS_MISSING` code. The existing pre-request credential check in `readCatalog` and in the connection test's token step now returns `credentials_missing` (logged as `error=credentials_missing cause=MissingClientCredentials`) instead of `unauthorized`. `classifyAiAdditionsError` also maps the typed error, as a safety net.

**management-console**
- Backend: `credentials_missing` is a known code (`AI_SERVICES_ERROR_CODES`) for the catalog and the test steps, so it is no longer collapsed to `invalid_response`.
- Frontend: `credentials_missing` message in `es_CL` and `en_US`, naming both variables and pointing to "AI Services" in `INSTALL.md` (EthicApp's deployment configuration).
- `ServicesSection`: with a connection, the catalog counts as pending while a request is in flight or none has answered yet. Pending shows only the loading state. The error panel and "Allow no services" appear only after a failed request. `catalogLoader.js` (generation/abort logic from #830) is untouched.

**Docs**
- `EXTERNAL.md`: `credentials_missing` in the error table; `unauthorized` no longer covers missing credentials.
- `INSTALL.md` (Enabling AI, step 4): what `credentials_missing` means and where to fix it.

## Risks

- A console older than this PR talking to a newer ethicapp maps `credentials_missing` to `invalid_response` (unknown code). Deploy both together.
- Clients that matched the missing-credentials error by message still work: the message is unchanged.

## Verification

- `cd ethicapp/backend && npm test`: 966 passed. New/updated tests: catalog read and connection test answer `credentials_missing` for unset, empty and whitespace-only id/secret, with a `fetch` that throws if called (`http://ai-additions-missing.invalid` for the test); classifier maps the typed error; client throws the typed error with no request.
- `cd management-console/backend && npm test`: 249 passed (`credentials_missing` passes through for the catalog and the token step).
- Console frontend `vitest run`: 43 passed. New tests cover pending → success and pending → failure (resolved error and rejected request) through the real catalog loader, a pending retry, the idle state with a connection, the `credentials_missing` test-step message, and the presence of the variables and `INSTALL.md` in both locales.
- Console `vite build` (output outside the repo): OK.
- `docker build -f ethicapp/Dockerfile .` and `docker build management-console`: OK (test stages pass); images removed afterwards.
- ESLint (`.eslintrc.yaml`) on touched ethicapp files: no errors (also fixed three pre-existing `key-spacing` errors in `ai-services.node-test.mjs`).
- Not done: a live check against the running dev stack.

Closes #838

body:
## What this adds

**Serving manager and thought log (Tue 27, rung R1).**

- `app/serve/serve_on_host.py`: runs on nelly inside one fleet GPU booking. Starts llama-server with Muse Glimmer 30B Q4_K_M and the official DFlash drafter, two 32K slots (`-np 2 -c 65536`), the fixed alias `muse-glimmer-30b`, `--jinja` with `reasoning_strength: minimal` as the default, and `--slot-save-path /data/afterglow/slots`. llama-server binds only `127.0.0.1:18611`. With `--lora`, it loads the adapter and turns off the RAM prompt cache, because that cache does not track adapters. It writes `/data/afterglow/serve/current.json` (weights and adapter hashes, flags, state). If either process exits, it stops both.
- `app/serve/trace_proxy.py` (stdlib): the public endpoint, on the tailnet address `100.96.31.41:18610`. It forwards every method and path unchanged and streams response bytes as they arrive. For each chat completion, it appends one JSONL record to `/data/afterglow/traces/<YYYY-MM-DD>.jsonl` (JST date). The record holds the request time and id, the client address, the requested model, the messages, the reply model, `reasoning_content`, `content`, tool calls, finish reason, usage and timings, and the done time. This is the "what it thought overnight" log.
- `app/serve/glimmer_server.py`: the Mac-side `start | stop | health [--deep] | endpoint | status`. `start` books nelly with `fleet run --detach` and a hard 14 h `timeout`, then waits for health. Health checks the proxy from the Mac and llama-server on nelly's loopback. `--deep` adds a non-streamed and a streamed chat on slot 1 and checks that the reply model is the alias in every frame.
- `app/serve/test_trace_proxy.py`: 6 tests against a fake llama-server on the Mac, no GPU needed. They cover byte-identical non-streamed and streamed bodies, unbuffered SSE, trace fields, untraced pass-through of other paths, a client disconnect that closes the upstream, a 502 when the upstream is down, and the wildcard-bind refusal.
- `app/serve/check_passthrough.py`: the same byte-identity proof against the real server on nelly.

## Verified (27 Oct, JST)

- 04:45: booking `1027-044508-86d9` on nelly, ready in 10 s. `/v1/models` = `[muse-glimmer-30b]`. A request naming `any-other-name` got the reply model `muse-glimmer-30b`, non-streamed and in all 25 SSE frames.
- `check_passthrough.py` on nelly, against the real llama-server: bytes the client received == bytes llama-server sent, for the non-streamed (948 B) and the streamed (24,084 B) call. The trace records hold the reasoning and the content.
- `python3 app/serve/test_trace_proxy.py`: 6/6 pass.

No pre-existing scripts are called. The pinned weight hashes come from the lead's `verify_weights.sh` check (26 Oct 20:51).

author: unknownhackerworld
body:
## Description
`fillSizeDifference` in `src/diff-snapshot.js` marks the area added to a smaller image (when the received image and the snapshot differ in size) with semi-transparent black, so those pixels count as different. Its check was:

```js
const inArea = (x, y) => y > height || x > width;
```

The added area starts at `x = width` and `y = height` (pixel coordinates are 0-based), so the first added column and the first added row were skipped and left fully transparent. This PR changes the check to `>=` so the whole added area is filled.

## Motivation and Context
`alignImagesToSameSize` pads both images to the larger size, and the new pixels start out as transparent (all zeros). pixelmatch blends a transparent pixel onto white before comparing, so a transparent pixel reads as white. With the off-by-one, the first padded row and column only count as different when the other image happens not to be white there.

Example with `allowSizeMismatch: true` and a 2x2 white snapshot:

| Received (white) | Pixels outside the snapshot | `diffPixelCount` before | after |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 3x2 | 2 | 0 (passes with `failureThreshold: 0`) | 2 |
| 2x3 | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| 4x4 | 12 | 7 | 12 |

So a size mismatch is undercounted, and a 1 pixel wider or taller image with a white edge can pass a zero-threshold comparison. The `percent` threshold type is affected the same way, since it uses the same count.

Tradeoffs: images with a size mismatch now report a few more differing pixels (the full added area). Users who rely on `allowSizeMismatch` with a tight pixel or percent threshold could see a comparison that used to pass start failing, but only because the old count was wrong. No API change.

Alternatives considered: filling the padded area in `alignImagesToSameSize` itself, or counting the size difference separately from pixelmatch. Both are larger changes to the same behavior; the one-character fix keeps the existing design.

## How Has This Been Tested?
- Added a `diffImageToSnapshot with a size mismatch` block to `__tests__/diff-snapshot.spec.js`. It unmocks `fs`, `pixelmatch` and `glur`, writes a real 2x2 white PNG snapshot to a temp dir, and compares 3x2, 2x3 and 4x4 white images with `allowSizeMismatch: true`. Each case checks `pass === false`, `diffSize === true` and the exact `diffPixelCount`.
- Without the fix, the three new tests fail (0, 0 and 7 differing pixels). With the fix, the full suite passes: 107 tests on Node 20 and Node 22 (`npx jest`).
- `npm run lint` and commitlint pass.

## Types of Changes
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to not work as expected)
- [ ] Documentation (adding or updating documentation)
- [ ] Dependency update

## Checklist:
- [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation and I have updated the documentation accordingly.
- [x] My changes are in sync with the code style of this project.
- [x] There aren't any other open Pull Requests for the same issue/update.
- [ ] These changes should be applied to a maintenance branch.
- [ ] I have added the Apache 2.0 license header to any new files created.

## What is the Impact to Developers Using Jest-Image-Snapshot?
With `allowSizeMismatch`, the padded area is now always counted as different, so `diffPixelCount` and the diff ratio match the real size difference. A received image that is only one pixel larger no longer slips through a zero threshold when its new edge is white.

AI disclosure: this change was found, written and tested with help from an AI assistant.

Each product page's "Compare with other products" section now leads with a **Head to head** group listing the comparison pages that product appears in. It is derived from the `COMPARISONS` pairs, not listed by hand, so adding a pair adds the links on both product pages automatically.

The pair resolution moves ahead of the products loop, since the product pages now need it. The comparisons block uses the same `pairs` list it did before.

author: fr9rx
body:
## Summary

Stage 1 v2. It adds three things:

- **Install-script scanning.** The root `package.json` is reduced to its `preinstall`, `install` and `postinstall` commands and scored like a file.
- **A faster scanner with identical results.** A 64 KiB LZMA dictionary, a thread pool and an inverted LZJD index.
- **The v2 malware set.** 6,500 packages with a ratio tuned by experiment instead of v1's fixed one.

**Results improved on both accuracy and speed:**

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| AUC on new malware (diverse / random tests) | 0.623 / 0.631 (v1-style: no install scripts) | **0.697 / 0.662** |
| v1 detailed test, total time (195 packages) | 108 s | **68 s** (scan 67 s → 25 s) |
| v2 ratio tests, scan time (964 packages) | 613 s | **265 s** |
| Install-script-only malware in the reference set | 0 (v1 dropped 2,970) | **952** |
| Reports changed by the speed work | | **0 of 195** |

Full write-ups: `experiments/v2/README.md` (v2), `experiments/v1/README.md` (v1), `dataset_index.md`, `docs/v2-suggestions.md` (what's next).

## 1. Install scripts (`src/manifest.c`)

- **What it scans.** Many npm attacks have no JavaScript at all, only a command like `curl … | sh` in `preinstall`. The scanner now reads the root `package.json`, keeps only the three commands npm runs on install, one per line, and scores that text like any other file. A `package.json` deeper in the package is skipped, since npm never runs it.
- **How references store it.** References keep no `package.json`, as before. They store the same text as `install_scripts.txt`. Commands that only launch a local `.js` file (`node index.js`) are not stored, because the file itself is kept and the command alone would match benign launchers.
- **Correctness.** The C extractor and a Python copy of it give byte-identical output on 29 edge cases: escapes, surrogates, BOM, duplicate keys, broken JSON and nesting up to 10,000 levels (`tests/install_scripts_test/`).

| Measured on the v2 time split | Without install scripts | With install scripts |
|---|---|---|
| AUC, `mal_shape` (300 diverse new packages) | 0.623 | **0.690** |
| AUC, `mal_stream` (200 random new packages) | 0.631 | **0.656** |
| Benign packages with install scripts scoring ≤ 0.30 | 0/64 | **0/64** |

The lowest benign script scored 0.462 while about 10 malicious scripts scored below it. So a separate threshold for script text (about 0.45) is the next step (suggestion 3).

## 2. Speed: 64 KiB dictionary, thread pool, inverted LZJD index

- **64 KiB dictionary.** It still holds a whole 16 KiB reference plus a 16 KiB target; a `_Static_assert` keeps it at least 2 × the split threshold. The encoder shrinks from 12.6 MiB to 1.9 MiB per thread, so it fits in the CPU cache.
- **Thread pool.** Threads are created once per run instead of for every pass (two passes per chunk). Packages are scanned in batches of 64, and each thread scores whole chunks on its own. A single small package still splits its 256 candidates across all threads, in blocks of 16.
- **Inverted LZJD index.** Profiling showed that about 60% of the scan was ranking: each chunk's digest was compared with all 69,249 reference digests and the whole list was sorted. The digests now form an index from digest value to references; v1 has 60.4 million values but only 2.1 million distinct ones. A chunk only touches references that share a value with it, and the top 256 are picked with quickselect. The order is exactly that of a full sort, checked on 1,500 candidate lists in `tests/lzjd_top_test/`.

v1 detailed test, 195 packages, WSL with 4 threads:

| Build | Load | Scan | Total | Peak memory | Reports identical |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Before (1 MiB, threads per pass, full comparison) | 41 s | 67 s | 108 s | 1.28 GB | |
| 64 KiB + thread pool | 33 s | 61 s | 94 s | 1.27 GB | 195/195 |
| **+ inverted index (this PR)** | 43 s | **25 s** | **68 s** | 1.74 GB | **195/195** |

The index costs about 10 s at load and 0.5 GB of peak memory while it is built.

**Safety checks on the new code**, recorded in `docs/memory-safety.md`:
- **Sanitizers.** AddressSanitizer with LeakSanitizer and UBSan: 0 reports in 11 runs. ThreadSanitizer: 0 data races in 11 runs.
- **Valgrind.** Helgrind: 0 errors. Memcheck with full leak check: 0 errors, 0 bytes leaked.
- **Builds.** No warnings with GCC `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wshadow` or with the zig Windows build.
- **Mode identity.** Batch mode and split mode give identical reports (`tests/score_chunks_test/`, plus the 195 v1 packages).

## 3. v2 malware set (`data/v2/`)

- **Source.** All 23,825 DataDog npm `malicious_intent` zips of 1 MiB or less were downloaded and indexed: 22,907 usable, 14,218 with distinct content, 2,928 install-script-only.
- **The ratio experiment.** References came from malware published before 2026-04-01 (19,872 packages). Tests were malware published after it:
  - `mal_shape`: 300 packages, one per random code shape.
  - `mal_stream`: 200 random packages.

  False alarms were measured on 400 popular npm packages (`ben_general`) and 64 popular packages with install scripts (`ben_scripts`). 11 reference settings were compared.

| Setting | Refs | Load | Peak memory | Recall ≤ 0.19 (shape / stream) | AUC (shape / stream) | Benign ≤ 0.19 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **1 per shape, 3 per name, newest first (chosen)** | 5,411 | **28.5 s** | 1.22 GB | 10.3% / 12.0% | **0.697 / 0.662** | 10/400, 0/64 |
| 3 per shape, 3 per name, earliest first (v1 rule) | 6,419 | 39.7 s | 1.29 GB | 10.3% / 12.0% | 0.690 / 0.656 | 10/400, 0/64 |
| 1, 2, 5 or 10 per shape (earliest first) | 5,401–7,233 | 35–40 s | 1.17–1.36 GB | 10.3% / 12.0–12.5% | 0.690 / 0.656 | 10/400, 0/64 |
| No shape cap | 8,468 | 40.7 s | 1.39 GB | 10.3% / 12.5% | 0.692 / 0.657 | 10/400, 0/64 |
| No name cap | 9,431 | 58.9 s | 2.04 GB | 10.3% / 12.0% | 0.698 / 0.662 | 10/400, 0/64 |
| No caps | 11,968 | 57.4 s | 2.16 GB | 10.3% / 12.5% | 0.699 / 0.662 | 10/400, 0/64 |

**Analysis**
- **More examples per code shape added no detection.** A code shape is the same code with different strings, so one example gives NCD everything it needs; extra copies only cost memory and load time.
- **Newest first gave the best AUC for its cost.** Recent variants are closer to the next ones, and it matched the AUC of removing every cap at about half the memory.
- **Recall on post-cutoff malware is low (10–12%)** because almost all of it came from new campaigns: only 9 of the 300 `mal_shape` packages share a code shape with older malware. Keeping the reference set updated daily with new attacks closes that gap; the ratio cannot.
- **Prefilter against brute force on v2 data:** 22 of 24 packages got exactly the brute-force score. One malicious package was 0.0074 higher (0.873 against 0.866) and one benign package 0.0105 higher, both far above any threshold (`experiments/v2/results/prefilter_vs_bruteforce.csv`).
- **Benign false alarms come from two places:** compiled-TypeScript stub files of 44–200 bytes, and libraries copied by typosquats (`supertest` matched `eslint-supertest` at 0.030). Ignoring JavaScript chunks under 256 bytes halves them (10 → 5 at 0.19, 24 → 8 at 0.30). It is now suggestion 1.

**The v2 set**
- **Contents.** 6,500 packages in 6,500 code shapes, 38,623 files, 654 MiB, 16 encrypted zips of 123 MiB in total (password `infected`, the largest is 10.6 MiB).
- **Integrity.** All 16 zips pass the CRC test, with no `package.json` and no executable file.

## v1 results (still valid: the new build reproduces every v1 score)

| v1 detailed test, threshold 0.19 | Flagged | AUC |
|---|---|---|
| Known malware | 50/50 | 1.000 |
| Renamed clones | 32/35 | 0.985 |
| New versions of known packages | 23/35 | 0.886 |
| Family left out of the references | 12/50 | 0.833 |

The bundle read the engine's raw argv and dropped every `--quiet`, `--batch`, `--no-color` and `--verbose` in it, wherever it stood, so an infocom operand lost them.

Both launchers now start the engine as `x-bin OPTION... -- ARG...` (x.sh since x-lang#934; x-os since jonruttan/x-os#55), and `(Sys args 'program)` answers the engine's path and what follows that `--`. `run.x` hands `(rest (Sys args (lit program)))` to the main, which now takes the operands; the filter and its `*-argv` export go. Both launchers swallow a user's first `--` themselves, so the bundle's "drop one leading --" only ever removed the launcher's own.

author: ciaranra
body:
C4-Helix slice 3a: one code-agnostic reader for abstract measurement-result references, and one measurement-layout certificate built on it, so the Helix Guppy programs of the next slice can be certified through the same reader as the surface code. Surface behaviour is unchanged.

## Change

- `pecos.qec.measurement_layout.abstract_result_refs(abstract_tc, new_classifier, *, family)` owns everything that is not label vocabulary: the tick and gate-batch walk, the measurement gate types, the single-qubit check for every measurement gate, and the agreement check with `measurement_emission()`. A code family supplies its labels as a classifier. `new_classifier` is a factory called once per walk, so a classifier with state (the surface one counts per-round ordinals) always starts fresh. `family` names the code family in the reader's own errors.
- The surface rules (`sx`/`sz` with `syndrome_round`, `init` for negative rounds, `final[i]`) move into `_surface_result_classifier`. `_surface_abstract_measurement_result_refs` keeps its name, its callers, and every error message.
- `certify_measurement_layout(program, abstract_tc, new_classifier, *, family)` replaces `certify_surface_measurement_layout`. It calls the shared reader itself, so every certified layout has passed the reader and its emission check, and a caller cannot certify a hand-built reference list.

## Verification

- A fixture generated from the pre-refactor reader (surface memory, d 3 and 5, X and Z, 1 and 2 rounds, plus d 3 with `ancilla_budget=2`, whose walk order interleaves the tags) is reproduced exactly.
- An independent review ran the old and new reader side by side on 150 surface configurations and error cases (distances 3, 5, 7; 0, 1 and 3 rounds; ancilla budgets; typed annotations on and off): outputs and error messages are byte-identical, and certificates (layout and digest) are byte-identical for `make_surface_code` and `make_surface_memory`.
- New tests cover the generic walk and metadata, multi-qubit rejection before classification, classifier errors propagating unchanged, emission disagreement (reader and certificate, with no certificate left behind), and the certificate layout and digest formula. Mutations of the reader (shared ordinal state, classifier before the single-qubit check, wrong gate index, removed emission check, dropped MPZ, missing-label default) each fail a test.
- `import pecos` still does not load guppylang.
- `pre-commit`, `python-ci-lint`, and the `qec-guppy` and `qec-surface` shards.

body:
Refs samanyudas/miri#72

## Summary

Engine PR #39 made the dragged window's centre pick the drop column.
Two rules from samanyudas/miri#72 had no test that grabs a window away from its centre.
This PR adds those tests and changes no engine code.

- `a_stack_member_grabbed_near_either_edge_and_dragged_down_reorders_it` replaces the right-edge-only test and runs the same full drag for a left-edge grab.
- `the_pointer_not_the_windows_centre_starts_an_edge_hold` checks that a pointer at the edge with the centre inside scrolls, and a centre at the edge with the pointer clear of it does not.
- `drag_from` is `press_and_drag` with a chosen grab point. `press_and_drag` now calls it.

## Evidence

Each test fails when its rule is broken. I broke each rule with a temporary engine edit, then restored the engine:

- `hit_test` with the centre ignored: the left-edge case fails with a vertical line at x 0 to 3 instead of a horizontal one. The right-edge case still passes.
- `held_edge` given the centre instead of the pointer: the edge-hold test fails at `grab_right=true`.

`cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, and `cargo test --all-targets` pass. The suite passed 1035 tests with 0 failures.

Sol round 1 found that the left-grab case put the window's centre at the display's exclusive right bound, so it passed even with the edge hold following the centre. `908ca5c` moves the centre inside the edge band, and each case now fails on its own under that mutation.

Reviewed with sol-loop: 2 rounds with gpt-6.1-sol. Sol verdict: approved

author: mablr
body:
Makes `AccountHandle::mark_created` public and adds `mark_created_keeping_storage`.

When a transaction continues on a fresh overlay, whether in a nested EVM or after suspend/resume, the new overlay must inherit the accounts it already created, or EIP-6780 `SELFDESTRUCT` stops deleting them. Since #731/#734, `mark_created` also discards the storage baseline. That is correct for a fresh creation but drops writes the database already holds for a resumed one. The keeping variant only skips that discard.

Rules that follow: the first creation mark in a transaction decides whether the baseline is kept, so a rolled-back later mark leaves it alone. An EIP-8246 survivor that keeps its baseline is wiped rather than zeroed. Note that this overlaps #562's `storage_is_reset`: whichever lands second should use `discards_storage()` there.

Context: needed to move Foundry onto evm2 without a fork, see foundry-rs/foundry#17541.

author: uglygameface
body:
## One active task: conservative event-driven battery optimization on-watch

Physical stock Watch3 SDB power readings are now verified (71% -> 68% in ~35 min), but longer testing is optional, and that test does **not** prove UgLy|OS battery savings. The user requested live battery diagnostics in Watch Settings and automatic reversible adjustments instead of repeatedly running Termux.

### Existing execution path and design
- Reuse pinned upstream AsteroidOS Settings, `Nemo.Configuration` and Mce battery/charger signals, no fork.
- Add **Settings > Battery & Power**, showing live battery reading, AOD/tilt states, adaptive mode and a stop/restore control.
- Add the actual event-driven controller in pinned **resident launcher MainScreen**, *not* a transient Settings screen or new daemon.
- Opt-in default Off. At 20% or less while discharging, save previous AOD/tilt state before disabling those controls when supported. At 30% or higher, charging or opting out, restore changed controls conditionally.
- Respect Solo Saver and nightstand ownership. Never disconnect Bluetooth/Wi-Fi, disable tap-to-wake, start power polling, execute a shell or bypass hardware controls.

### Required validation
- Pinned Settings patches 0001-0005 and launcher notifications + adaptive patch applied in order with `git apply --check` and final `git diff --check`.
- Host tests exercise the **actual QML reconcile function** via Node VM and mocked battery/charger/manual override/sleep capabilities, plus source/permissions checks.
- Restore compatibility with existing standalone Solo Saver and notification controls.

### Important nonclaims
No real R08 UgLy|OS boot, native Qt package proof in this slice, battery savings, wake/driver verification, or safe Samsung flash/recovery demonstrated. Do not flash. A single stock Tizen 34-minute sample cannot establish optimized endurance.

**Draft until all CI/compatibility tests pass and final diff is inspected.**

author: jackhorrordevscl
body:
## Qué cambia

`recoverMfa` lleva el código de recuperación a su forma canónica (`a1b2-c3d4-e5f6-a7b8-c9d0`) antes de verificarlo contra el hash: acepta mayúsculas, sin guiones o con espacios. Un valor que no tiene la forma de un código emitido (20 hex) pasa tal cual y no puede matchear ningún hash.

Sugerencia del issue #487: «Los códigos de recuperación se comparan exactos (mayúsculas y guiones)».

## Por qué

El código se muestra con guiones y se hashea esa forma exacta. Quien lo copia a mano en mayúsculas o sin guiones quedaba rechazado justo en el momento en que perdió su dispositivo.

## Verificación

- Unit `auth`: 232/232 (casos nuevos: mayúsculas, sin guiones, espacios, y forma no canónica sin transformar).
- E2E `mfa-recover` contra base local descartable: 10/10 (`--testTimeout=60000`), con un caso nuevo en mayúsculas y sin guiones.
- `eslint` y `tsc --noEmit` limpios.

Risk: none (el único cambio es la forma del texto que se compara; no cambia el throttle, el consumo atómico ni los mensajes de error).

Refs #487

## Revisión nativa

Aprobada (riesgo y fiabilidad), sin bloqueantes. Aviso informativo: la variante con espacios solo está probada en unit (el e2e cubre mayúsculas y sin guiones); el DTO limita a 64 caracteres y la variante con espacios mide 26, así que no choca con la validación.

author: plateau-worker[bot]
body:
Routes the slowest required-path jobs (unit shards + integration) to the Hetzner self-hosted runners (`[self-hosted, hetzner, we]`) for `merge_group` and `push` to main only. `pull_request` / `workflow_dispatch` keep the GitHub-hosted jobs.

**Stacked on #6002** (branch `lane/ci-speed`): both PRs edit `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (shards/checkout), so this is based on that head. Retarget to main after #6002 lands.

- New `.github/workflows/hetzner-jobs.yml` (`on: workflow_call`): `test-shard` (1..10) and `integration`; WE checkout pinned to `ref: ${{ github.sha }}` (the merge-group / push commit, not main); same artifact names (`coverage-shard-N`, `timing-unit-N`).
- `ci.yml`: new `hetzner` job; hosted `test-shard`/`integration` run only on pull_request/workflow_dispatch; `coverage-merge` and `test` read the effective result (`needs.hetzner.result` on merge_group/push, else the hosted job). Unused path is skipped and never counted as success; active path fails closed.
- Deviation from the brief: `uses: ./.github/workflows/hetzner-jobs.yml` (local ref), not `...@main`. A same-repo `@main` ref fails the whole run while the file is absent from main (this PR's own run) and would test main's copy instead of the tested commit. Same behavior once on main; say if you want `@main` after merge.

**Required check names unchanged.** Ruleset 24930207 requires `test`, `smoke`, `daemon-soak`, `soak-replay-gate`, `merge-gate`; none is moved. They stay jobs in ci.yml on `ubuntu-latest`. Called jobs report as `hetzner / test-shard (N)` and `hetzner / integration`, which are not required contexts (before: `test-shard (N)` / `integration` were also not required; `test` already gated them). Verified by `scripts/ci/__tests__/ci-hetzner-routing.test.mjs` (asserts ids, `runs-on`, and that hetzner-jobs.yml defines no required name) plus executed shell-gate tests for all four events.

**Baseline (GitHub-hosted, last 10 main pushes, successful jobs):** test-shard avg 986s / max 1473s (n=50, pre-#6002 4-5 shard layout); integration avg 879s / max 1010s (n=10). Compare after merge-group runs on Hetzner.

Tests: red first (17/18 failing), then green; scoped suites scripts/ci/__tests__ + ci-*.test.mjs: 287 passed. Workflow edit: needs human review (review:human). Runners are persistent, no sudo/docker; setup-node supplies Node.

author: catalyst-cloud-connector[bot]
body:
## Summary

`coppa rx` and `coppa listen` were two different receivers in one binary: `rx` streamed
audio through `CoppaCore::push_samples` (the `StreamingReceiver` path the daemon and FFI
use), while `listen` re-ran the batch `CoppaCore::decode` over a growing window on every
read, with its own flags and its own (unescaped, SNR-less) output format. Users couldn't
tell which to use, and `listen`'s loop re-decoded the whole buffered window on every read.

This PR makes `coppa rx` the only receiver and folds `listen` into it as a hidden,
deprecated alias, per Tony Hagale's 2026-10-15 decision comment on the ticket.

## What changed

- **`coppa rx` gained `listen`'s flag surface**, via one shared `clap::Args` struct
  (`RxArgs`) used by both the `Rx` and `Listen` subcommand variants, so the two cannot
  drift apart:
  - a bare positional `FILE` argument (`coppa rx cq.wav`), alongside the existing
    `-i/--input` (clap rejects both at once with `ArgumentConflict`)
  - `-d/--duration <SECONDS>` (0 = no limit): caps a file read to its first N seconds, or
    stops a live capture after N seconds of wall clock
  - `--callsign <CALLSIGN>`, echoed only under `--verbose` (same no-op-otherwise behavior
    `listen` had)
- **`stream_decode` gained a stop rule for live sources** (`deadline: Option<Instant>`,
  checked every iteration including empty reads, so a stalled device still stops on time)
  and caps file reads to the `--duration` limit instead of always reading to EOF. The
  `TRAILING_FLUSH_SAMPLES` trailing-silence flush — previously file-only — now runs on
  every normal stop (file EOF, file duration cap, or live deadline), so a frame ending
  right at a live `--duration` cutoff can still complete.
- **`coppa listen` is now a hidden, deprecated alias of `rx`**: it parses into the same
  `RxArgs`, prints a stderr warning unconditionally (even under `--quiet`, matching this
  file's other `WARNING:` lines) before anything else, then dispatches to `cmd_rx`. It no
  longer appears in `coppa --help` but still answers `coppa listen --help` and
  `coppa help listen`.
- **`cmd_listen` and its batch re-decode loop are deleted**, along with the 5-second `.`
  liveness dots and the duplicated device-resolution block. `CoppaCore::decode` now has
  exactly one CLI caller left (`cmd_loopback`); FFI v1 (`coppa_decode`) is the only other
  caller workspace-wide.
- **One output grammar for both commands** (COP-13's, unchanged): valid UTF-8 prints as
  `Decoded: "<escaped text>"  (SNR: x.x dB)`, anything else as `Decoded (hex): <hex>  (SNR:
  x.x dB)`; `--hex` forces the labeled hex form; `--raw` prints only lowercase hex, one
  line per frame. `listen`'s old output (unescaped `print!`, no SNR, nothing printed for
  binary payloads) is gone — this also closes a real sink COP-13's validation had flagged:
  `listen` used to print received-frame text to the terminal unescaped, which the security
  review confirms was a terminal-escape-injection vector.
- **Docs updated to describe one receiver**: `README.md`'s CLI examples use the bare-path
  form and add a live-receive example; `docs/tutorials/getting-started.md` gains a
  "Receiving Live Audio" section; `ARCHITECTURE.md`'s subcommand list drops `listen` and
  notes it survives one release as a deprecated alias.

## Deviation from the plan (declared, accepted during validation)

The plan computed the `--duration` file cap using the engine's fixed 48 kHz
(`core.config().sample_rate`). The implementation uses the WAV's own sample rate
(`source.sample_rate()`) instead: `WavSource` doesn't resample, so for a file recorded at
any other rate, capping against the engine's rate would decode the wrong number of seconds
and print a wrong header. Both expressions agree for 48 kHz files — the only rate `coppa
tx` ever writes, and the only rate every pre-existing test uses — so no previously-tested
behavior changes. A new test (`rx_duration_counts_seconds_at_the_files_own_sample_rate`)
exercises an 8 kHz file to pin this down.

## What this deliberately does not do

- **Delete `coppa listen`.** Per the decision comment, it stays one release as a hidden
  alias before removal. The three items to delete at that point (the `Listen` variant,
  `LISTEN_DEPRECATED`, and its dispatch arm) are marked with a `COP-56` code comment. A
  follow-up ticket for that removal needs to be filed — this run has no ticket-system
  credential to do so itself.
- **stdin (`coppa rx -`) and raw-PCM streaming.** Only the bare-path half of the relevant
  review finding is in scope here; the `-` / raw-PCM half is separate follow-up work.
- **Any liveness/progress output, Ctrl-C handling, or an end-of-run summary.** `listen`'s
  5-second `.` dots are dropped, not ported; that's separate follow-up work.
- **Making `--callsign` do anything** beyond echoing under `--verbose` (validating it,
  putting it on the wire) — separate follow-up work.
- **Closing `StreamingReceiver`'s full-band sync-sensitivity gap.** Moving `listen` onto
  the streaming receiver trades batch decode's better full-band-noise sensitivity for
  streaming's cost efficiency. Measured on throwaway probes: on SSB-filtered audio (what a
  real rig produces), the two decoders perform within noise of each other at the SNRs that
  matter; on unfiltered full-band white noise, streaming is meaningfully worse. This is a
  pre-existing, documented gap (`rx_golden.rs`'s module doc), not something this PR
  changes, and it's the right tradeoff for what `coppa rx` actually receives in practice.

## Testing

- `cargo test --workspace --features cpal-backend,websocket` (CI's full suite): all 46
  suites pass, including `coppa-cli`'s 49 unit tests (40 pre-existing + 9 new), `rx_golden`
  (2, unchanged), `rx_text` (2, unchanged), and the new `rx_one_receiver` integration suite
  (7 tests) covering the bare path, the FILE/`-i` conflict, `--duration` on a file, the
  `--callsign` echo, and the `listen` deprecated-alias behavior (identical stdout to `rx`,
  warning on stderr, hidden from `--help` but still answers its own `--help`).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` and
  `cargo clippy -p coppa-cli --all-targets --features cpal-backend -- -D warnings` (the
  latter is the only lint pass that covers the cpal-gated live-capture code; CI's own
  clippy job doesn't enable that feature) — both clean.
- `cargo fmt --all -- --check` — clean.
- `cargo check -p coppa-cli --no-default-features` and `--workspace --no-default-features`
  — only pre-existing warnings remain, strictly fewer than on the base branch.
- `cargo +1.85.0 check -p coppa-cli --features cpal-backend --all-targets` (MSRV) — clean.
- Manual verification against the real binary, including live capture on ALSA's null
  capture device (`--device Discard`): bare path, `-i` conflict, `--hex`/`--raw`,
  `--duration` on a file and live (`exit 0` after ~2.4 s wall clock, correct
  `Stopped listening after N s.` footer), and the `listen` deprecation warning plus
  identical downstream output. Full transcripts are in the validation report.
- Independent code-review and security-review passes (5 review lenses) returned no
  findings at their reporting thresholds; one informational LOW note (a predictable test
  temp-file path, matching this repo's existing test convention) does not block.
- `cargo check --workspace --all-features` could not run in the validation container
  (missing `libudev` system library pulled in by an unrelated `coppa-radio` feature); every
  `coppa-cli` feature combination was checked individually instead, all clean. This diff
  touches no `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`.

Fixes https://linear.app/hagale-technologies/issue/COP-56

author: jthorare
body:
Part of #1206. Phase M-0 of the model-pick spec: one real Jev call on a 100,000-character input, to check the cap before M-2 relies on it.

## Result: the 100,000-character cap stands

Calls to `POST https://api.typesafe.ai/v1/systemone`, model `jev-1.13.0`, in the real request shape: `state` is a `ModelPickInput`-shaped record with synthetic lorem-ipsum files (no repo content), four candidates `m1`..`m4` cheapest first, and a prompt that names keys and paths only.

| Call | `state` chars | Request bytes | Status | Time | Input tokens | Answer |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| control, ends with "answer m3" | 2,002 | 2,419 | 200 | 340 ms | 906 | `m3` (0.55) |
| **full, ends with "answer m3"** | **100,002** | **100,473** | **200** | **348 ms** | **19,153** | **`m3` (0.56)** |
| full, no instruction | 100,000 | 100,471 | 200 | 332 ms | 19,148 | `m1` (0.89) |

- **Accepted:** 200 at 100k, no 413.
- **In budget:** ~350 ms against the question's 20 s.
- **Read to the end:** the last two rows differ only in the final 110 characters, and that flips the answer from `m1` to `m3`. A truncated input would have stayed on `m1`.
- **Cost:** about 19,000 input tokens and 50 output tokens per 100k pick. That's the number §15.8's cost rule prices against the tokens saved.
- **Side finding for §4.5:** the planted instruction moved Jev only to 0.56 confidence, below the 0.6 threshold, so a real pick would have fallen back to rules instead of obeying the file.

Request ids: `req_01a17a425ae276e088cc497913b4e40d` (control), `req_01a17a425ce17b3dbbb15e7fefc47d27` (full).

## What's in the PR
- Spec §1 M1 and §4.3 amended with the result (the table above).
- `tests/fixtures/judge/model-pick-m0-100k.json`: the exact 100k request body (no key). The script that sent it was a throwaway and isn't shipped, as the spec says.

No code, so no build or tests.

author: fernandorff
body:
Closes #227

## Why

- Fernando's decision (26/10, issue #227, approved proposal): every item gets 3 upgrade levels, each level at the item price.
- Same batch (26/10): the Scourge becomes a free item again, like the game until 21/10, and frees a spell slot.
- Proposal with the per-item choices: https://claude.ai/artifact/Ua2MMwwrju8QQDk119i2ip

## What changes

- **Items with 3 levels** (existing levels keep their strength):
  - Ring of Life 100/190/270 health; Lifesteal 9/17/24% (levels 4 to 6 removed).
  - Cursed Ring level 3: +300 health, 7% less knockback, slows 35% longer.
  - Pocket Watch −35/−45/−50%; Lava Boots 18/30/40%; Rune of Affliction 5/10/20%.
  - Helmet 15/20/24% less knockback, spell range always −10%.
  - Shock Boots 3/4/5 s; Wind Boots wait 5/4.5/4 s for +25/+29/+33 speed.
  - Aegis: each level is one save; a save spends 1 level (was: breaks entirely).
- **Scourge as an item:** free at level 1 for everyone, 3 levels (80/100/120 damage, 7 gold each), Protection section of the shop, takes 1 of the 6 item slots, active button in the item grid. Key **1** (its own key also in Q W E R D F mode, rebindable in Launch) and **LT** on the controller. The free level does not sell. Spells: 5 bought besides Fireball (was 4).
- **Inside:** the Scourge still fires through the spell path (cast, cooldown, protocol, animation); its level lives only in `items.scourge` and `newWorld`/`refit` copy it into the wizard. `priceOf('scourge')` is always `null`, and lists of spells a player can own use `BAR_SPELLS`. No active-item code from #236 came back.
- **Saved rooms:** a Scourge spell becomes the item (up to level 3); items above level 3 drop to 3.
- Pact stays a spell; the Redirector stays out.
- **Campaign:** the Aceso starts with the Scourge item at level 1; night cards do not upgrade it yet (question for Lucas on #227).
- Docs: two rows in `docs/DECISIONS.md`, README and `src/shared/CLAUDE.md`. Test names and comments of the edited test files translated to English (tests/CLAUDE.md rule).

## Screenshots

Local test at 1280×720 (localhost, branch `feat/itens-3-niveis`): shop with the Scourge in Protection (key 1, "1 of 6 items"), bar with the Scourge in the item grid; key 1 cast it in a round and the button showed the cooldown. The PR environment link is posted by the pipeline for Fernando's test.

## How I tested

- [x] `npm run typecheck` (client, server and scripts)
- [x] `npx vitest run` (1460 tests; new: 3 levels for every item, saved-room migration, Aegis charges, Scourge not buyable as a spell, Shock Boots and Wind Boots level 3)
- [x] `npx vite build`
- [x] Played in the browser (`npx wrangler dev`) on PC: shop, bar, Launch keys, controller map, key 1 cast; `scripts/smoke.mjs` OK
- [x] New text in Portuguese and English (`t('pt', 'en')`)
- [x] Non-obvious decision with a 1-line English comment explaining why

## What changed

`FileOrderTests.testTheSidebarFollowsTheSelectedNoteOnlyIfItWasOnScreen` failed every time while the Mac's display was asleep. Three tests in `packages/svelte` failed on `main`.
