author: stelizhenets
body:
## Bear traps R6: a trap that goes off under a body is heard by its enemies, like its steps (switched off)

Stacked on R3 (`claude/traps-react3`, itself on R2); the diff of this PR alone is `git diff claude/traps-react3 claude/traps-react6`. **Switched off** (`traps.react.hear` false, independent of `traps.react.on`): no state is kept, no sound is made, the bots hear exactly what they heard.

**What existed first.** Nothing: the bots' ears (`view.sounds`) are made only from players' inputs (shot, reload, switch, use, jump) and held keys (sprint); the footstep rule (`sense.step_m` 8 m) needs an enemy walking upright. A trap's snap reached no bot at all, though the players hear it (the client plays `sound_fired`; there is no disarm sound, PROVEN in the client's trap data). So the owner's "hear it like any sound" is a small piece of code, not a test of an existing path.

- **The sound** (`SoundKind::Trap`, `view.rs`): `Tracker::snap(victim, at, time)` puts a `Sound` of the body that set the trap off at the trap's place; `sense.rs` gives it the range of the footsteps (`tuning.step_m`, times the bot's `hearing`), one arm in the existing range `match`. It is heard by the *enemies* of that body only (the existing team test), as a `Heard` percept with an error that grows with distance, not `busy` (a shot is). No new tuning number beyond the next.
- **The trigger** (`Bots::hear_snaps`, from `traps_from_world`): a trap that the previous world showed armed (within 1.5 m, `MATCH_M`) and this one shows *fired*. The victim is the alive body nearest the trap within `snap_near_m` (3 m, a GUESS; the world names nobody). A trap that is **disarmed makes no sound** (by hand or by a shot): no false "stuck bot" chase. A fired world seen twice, a trap never seen armed, and one with nobody near it make none. `Bots::snaps_heard()` counts them for the bench.
- Shared-file hunks: `view.rs` (`SoundKind::Trap`, `nearest_body`, `snap`), `sense.rs` (one arm), `mod.rs` (two fields, the hook, `hear_snaps`), `tuning/traps.rs` (`hear`, `snap_near_m`), tests.

**Root cause.** A catch is loud for the players (the trap's snap, and the victim's cry) and silent for the bots: a bot that sets a trap, or any bot near one that catches an enemy, learns nothing of it, where a player turns to the sound. The sound is the cheapest of the human cues the server already knows, and it does not need the trap to be noticed.

**Best practice.** Noise as an event with a place and a loudness, heard by an agent only within its hearing range scaled by the loudness, and only by the agents that are hostile to the source ([Unreal `ReportNoiseEvent`](https://docs.unrealengine.com/4.27/en-US/BlueprintAPI/AI/Perception/ReportNoiseEvent/index.html)); here the loudness is the footsteps' and the hostility test the sense's own. Merged off, the bench turns it on ([Fowler, Feature Toggles](https://martinfowler.com/articles/feature-toggles.html)).

**Latency, and why there is no earlier source (PROVEN, read in the code).** The server learns of a game only from what the clients send: inputs (action bits and view), hashes, time replies and the patched client's world uploads (`match_msgs.rs` ids 0xD8-0xDF, the 0xE0 upload, `upload.rs`). There is no damage, hit or trap event message; a leg hit and a trap's state come only inside a world (`driven.rs` `observe_driven`: `Hurt::of` and `traps_from_world` both read the same uploaded world). While the server's bots play the clients are asked for a world every `PLAYING_REFRESH` = 2 s (`driven.rs:65`), and an upload is the uploader's event-horizon item, about 500 ms old (`game.rs:45`). So a snap reaches the ears **0.5-2.5 s after it happened (mean about 1.5 s)** in a live bot match; the 3.4 s median is the human recordings' gap, not the bots'. The sound carries the world's time (sounds are kept 3 s). The only faster ways are a shorter refresh (more uploads of up to 32 KB per client) or a prediction from the dead-reckoned body against the armed trap (noisy: a sound where nobody was caught); neither is in this PR, and the counter `snaps_heard` is the one source.

**Limits.** It helps the hunt, not the first reaction; and a trap fired by a body farther than `snap_near_m` from it at the world that shows it is silent. The bench look reports `snaps_heard` against the catches (`own_trap_counts().fired`).

**CPU.** Off: one flag read per world. On: one scan of the world's traps (<= 26) and, per newly fired one, a scan of the bodies (<= 12); nothing per think.

Checks (Windows, OpenSSL 3): see the comment on the PR for the suite counts. New tests (2): the sense test (a snap under an enemy is heard within the steps' range times the hearing, not beyond it, not a mate's, not `busy`); the game-loop test (armed then fired gives one sound of the nearest body at the trap; the same fired world twice, a disarmed trap, a trap with nobody near it and the switch off give none).

author: thejackshelton
body:
**TLDR:** each converted page now loads only the library ports its own markup can use, instead of every port the whole site uses. On the shadcn 20-page port, the tabs page drops 7 of its 17 ports from its first-click code (slider, tooltips, Base UI menu, toggle, form, panel motion); its preloaded JS goes from 846 to 819 kB raw (132.1 to 126.9 kB brotli).

## What was wrong

Every page's root delegate (`onClick={(event) => behave(event)}` and friends) imported `lib/parts/index.ts`, which imported `lib/parts/registry.ts`, which imported every port the site uses. Markless preloads the code each control needs on first use, so a page with one tab list preloaded the slider, both tooltip ports, the Base UI menu, the toggle port, and so on. The sidebar's `onVisible={() => mount(...)}` pulled the same registry in at load.

## What changed

Convert now records which routes each port is emitted for:

- markup emitted for a page (its own tree, the layers it portals, fragments a plan writes for it) belongs to that page;
- a region several pages share belongs to every page that renders it (`factor` reports the region's pages as it emits it);
- a port a plan needs (toggle, panel motion, roving focus for Base UI tabs, switch, charts, scenes, forms, clock, calendars) belongs to the pages whose markup that plan binds, or to every page if none is found;
- anything else (the document, the body's shared children) belongs to every page.

Each distinct set of ports gets one module, `lib/parts/registries/<hash>.ts`, which calls `use(SITE_PARTS, { ...ports })` and exports `behave`, `listen` and `mount`. A page imports `behave`/`listen` from its own registry and gets root handlers only for the events its ports take. `mount` always comes from a small registry of the site's parts plus the ports that export `mount`, so the sidebar's visibility hook no longer pulls every port in at load.

`parts/index.ts` keeps one list of parts across the registries a session has loaded: the site's parts first, then the ports sorted by module name (the order the single registry used). A page reached later by client navigation adds its ports without reordering the others; `listen()` runs `idle` once per part, including parts added later.

`waste` now names `lib/parts/registries/*` as the parts registry (and still knows the old `registry.ts`).

## Measured: shadcn 20-page port (Markless packs with #285 and #286)

Both sides converted from the same captures, built with the same Markless packs, served with the node server. Downloaded bytes of the page's modulepreloads (raw / brotli 11):

| Page | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| /docs/components/base/tabs | 846.0 kB / 132.1 kB | 818.9 kB / 126.9 kB |
| /docs/components/radix/accordion | 942.1 kB / 138.1 kB | 919.0 kB / 134.4 kB |

The parts chunk on the tabs page goes from 166.7 kB / 36.2 kB to 133.9 kB / 28.8 kB, plus a 6.2 kB / 2.3 kB chunk for the Base UI select its demo uses. What stays on every page is what the shared header and search palette use: cmdk and its option table (`choices.ts`, 26.7 kB raw), the command menu, the Radix dialog engine, the dropdown and popover ports.

Slow network, `markless-migrate network`, 5 cold loads a cell, before and after pages interleaved in one run (medians; the machine's 1-minute load ran from 9 to 62 during it, mostly 35 to 50 in the second half, so small differences are within noise):

| Browser, profile | Page | First click answered | JS downloaded by the answer |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chromium, 2G | base/tabs | 10.44 s to 10.20 s | 148 kB to 142 kB |
| Chromium, 2G | radix/accordion | 10.71 s to 10.63 s | 156 kB to 152 kB |
| Firefox, 2G | base/tabs | 10.59 s to 10.40 s | 181 kB to 175 kB |
| Firefox, 2G | radix/accordion | 10.93 s to 10.95 s | 188 kB to 185 kB |
| Chromium, 3G | base/tabs | 3.50 s to 3.46 s | 148 kB to 142 kB |
| Chromium, 3G | radix/accordion | 3.61 s to 3.59 s | 156 kB to 152 kB |
| Firefox, 3G | base/tabs | 3.70 s to 3.65 s | 181 kB to 175 kB |
| Firefox, 3G | radix/accordion | 3.89 s to 3.79 s | 188 kB to 185 kB |

JS executed by the answer (Chromium) is unchanged on the tabs page (382 to 383 kB) and 448 to 439 kB on the accordion page on 2G: the runtime dominates what runs. WebKit's cells are left out: on 127.0.0.1 its loads did not go through the throttling proxy (time to first byte 0.01 s).

A smoke run on both builds (11 pages: a tab, a disclosure, a checkbox, a switch, a slider key, the search palette on Cmd+K) gave identical results and no page errors.

## Not changed, found on the way

`parts/cmdk.ts` imports `navigate` from `@markless/router`, whose root module reaches the client render path. Every page still reaches cmdk (the header search is on every page, and `lib/site/parts.ts` imports `configure` from it), so that render code stays preloaded. Proposed fix, not in this PR: have the router export `navigate` from a subpath that does not import the render path, or let cmdk navigate by clicking a real link so the router's own link handling does it.

## Tests

- `test/convert-page-parts.test.ts` (new): converts pages shaped by three seeds, each with its own random set of ports and two sharing a factored region that holds another port; every page's registry holds exactly its own ports and its shared region's, never a port only other pages use, and its root listens only to those ports' events. Red on main: every page loaded every port.
- `test/parts-registries.test.ts` (new, browser): a second registry adds its ports in module order after the site parts, runs only the new parts' `idle`, and binds the same runtime.
- The browser tests that served a hand-written `registry.ts` now serve the generator's own `registryModule`.

author: nvorkinn
body:
Stage 2 of slimming countdown-core (after #304, #307 and #306): everything that draws moves out of core into countdown-renderer, so core holds only what the providers and the render pool share.

## Why

Before this, the render pool reached 97% of core and the providers 23%. Core was the renderer in all but name: 12,400 of its 15,200 lines were panels, layouts, styles, the clients that read the store to build panels, and the render itself. The providers only ever needed the store, the API models, the fetch clients, logging and i18n.

## What moved

90 modules (12,443 lines), plus `fonts/` and `images/`, from `countdown_core` to `countdown_renderer`, keeping their subpackage names, with one exception: `countdown_core.core.{abstract_client, api_registry, moment, panel, rotation, style}` sit at the top of `countdown_renderer` rather than in a second `core` subpackage. `countdown_core.core` keeps `device_name`, `http_session` and `log_format`.

- `render.py`, `rendering/` (layouts, registry, screen, encoding), `system_screens/`, `newspaper/`, `departures/`, `utils/` (fonts and drawing helpers, `scaled_draw`, `clock`).
- The render halves of `developer/`, `glow/` and `spotify/` (clients, panels, styles). Their `models.py` stay in core: the store modules `developer`, `energy` and `music` are built on them.
- The render halves of `entur/`, `tfl/` and `weather/` (panels, stored sources, `weather_client`, `weather_forecast`). Their API clients and models stay.
- The render half of `notices/`: `notice.py` (Notice, Severity, NoticeSource), `calendar`, `floods`, and the `tfl`, `norway`, `met_office` and `entur` sources, plus `notice_board_client`, the notice panels and styles. The `*_feed` modules, `location` and `models` stay, as #307 arranged.

What core keeps: 42 modules, 2,835 lines. `store/` in full (the Redis contract between every process), the pydantic models, the TfL, Entur and Open-Meteo clients, the postcode lookups, `http_session`, `log_format`, `device_name` and `i18n` with its catalogues.

## Dependencies and packaging

- `countdown-core`: the `render` extra from #306 is gone; Pillow and qrcode are now plain dependencies of `countdown-renderer`, which also declares `countdown-api` since it imports its models directly. Babel stays with core, where `i18n` lives.
- `babel.cfg` extracts from both `core/src` and `renderer/src`, since the texts marked for translation now mostly live in the renderer while the catalogues stay with `i18n` in core.
- `renderer/Dockerfile` pre-downloads the Material Symbols font from its new module; `.gitignore` and `dev/snapshots.sh` follow the font directory.
- Both wheels were built and inspected: the renderer wheel carries the 12 fonts and 3 images, the core wheel the locale.

## Verification

- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `ty check`: clean. `deptry src` in core/, renderer/ and providers/: clean.
- `pytest -m "not snapshot"`: 2719 passed; the 13 failures on this Mac are the Raqm-dependent parity tests, the same 13 that fail on main here (CI has libfribidi).
- `dev/snapshots.sh test` (the pinned Linux image CI draws the goldens in): 163 passed, so no pixel changed.
- Every provider main imports with neither `PIL` nor any `countdown_renderer` module in `sys.modules`; `tests/test_provider_imports.py` now asserts the latter.

author: hlindset
body:
A cache write's own bytes counted against the cache's pending limit (256 MiB, or `max_size_bytes / 20` when that is smaller). So an entry larger than the limit was dropped as `:pending_limit` even with nothing else pending. A 100 MB cache, for example, never stored an image over 5 MB, and regenerated it on every request.

`Writers.reserve/3` now passes a write that is the only one pending, whatever its size. Concurrent writes are still held to the limit, so the backlog is bounded by the limit or one entry, whichever is larger. Admission still rejects an entry that doesn't fit in `max_size_bytes`.

- Tests: a lone oversized write is stored, and a second write is still dropped while another is pending.
- Docs: `docs/cache.md`, the `max_size_bytes` option doc, and the changelog.

Found while working on image_plug-sole (tuning the writer's limits). Production logs from a 0.4.0 deployment showed no drops of any kind, so this doesn't change that bead's conclusions.

author: ajit-zer07
body:
## Summary

Wave 5 P1.1: an optional, normative way for a runtime to issue signed decision receipts (RFC-MACP-0013 Appendix A, `macp-receipt/1`) and publish the keys that verify them. Modeled on the WhatIfReplay precedent (#226): optional RPCs, capability-gated, `UNIMPLEMENTED` when not advertised, authorized exactly as `GetSession`, rate-limit SHOULD.

- **RFC-MACP-0013 1.4.0-draft**: new §13 *Receipt Issuance (optional)* with requirements (1)–(11). Names `receipt_010_wire_match` as the reference issuance shape. No new vector.
- **core.proto**: `DecisionReceiptCapability {get_decision_receipt, signed}` as `Capabilities.decision_receipt = 8`; `GetDecisionReceiptRequest/Response` (`receipt_json`), `GetReceiptKeysRequest/Response` (`jwks_json`); RPCs appended after `WhatIfReplay`. No message is named `*Payload`, so envelope coverage is unaffected. Synced to proto-npm and proto-rust.
- **RFC-MACP-0006 1.8.0-draft**: §3 listing plus new §3.9. **RFC-MACP-0001 1.5.0-draft**: capability-table row.
- **Registries**: `RECEIPT_UNAVAILABLE` (409 / `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, **provisional**, added to the 409 sentence); `application/macp-receipt+json` (provisional).
- **New schema** `schemas/json/macp-receipt-keys.schema.json` (kid and kty required; an OKP key is Ed25519 with `x`; `d` forbidden on every key; other `kty` allowed), the example `examples/discovery/receipt_keys.json` (the A.5 key), and the negative corpus `schemas/json/tests/invalid-receipt-keys/` (6 fixtures plus a README with the measured grid), wired into `scripts/validate-json.sh`.
- **`scripts/check-receipt-vectors.py`** (stdlib only): asserts that the published key set yields exactly `{example-1: TDVzkxaSf6_Oxu7mmn5TbCkF80s8Ulh33qKQsi0gnZM}`, and that vector 010 verifies as attested against it.
- **Docs**: `docs/security.md` (Decision Receipts subsection), `docs/transports.md` (RPC section), and the README (version census, schema tree, capability list, RFC-0013 posture line).

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Met.** The service ends `WhatIfReplay, GetDecisionReceipt, GetReceiptKeys`, and RFC-0006 §3 lists the same RPCs in the same order. Prose-check #9 passes.
2. **Met.** `Capabilities` field 8 is `DecisionReceiptCapability decision_receipt`, which has exactly the two booleans `get_decision_receipt = 1` and `signed = 2`.
3. **Met.** RFC-0013 §13 contains requirements (1)–(11) as a numbered list.
4. **Met.** `registries/error-codes.md` lists `RECEIPT_UNAVAILABLE` as 409 / `FAILED_PRECONDITION`, provisional. `schemas/parity/contract.json` is unchanged and `make parity-contract` passes.
5. **Met.** `make receipt-vectors` reports "all 12 receipt vectors match" plus the key-set line. A mutation test that changed one character of `x` made the check fail. `gen-receipt-vectors.py` regenerates the vectors with no diff.
6. **Met.** Measured by schema mutation: each fixture passes only when its own keyword is removed. `missing_keys` keys on root `required`; `key_missing_kid` and `key_missing_kty` key on their own member of `$defs.jwk.required`; `okp_private_d` on `properties.d`; `okp_missing_x` on `then.required`; `okp_wrong_crv` on `then…crv.const`. `validate-json.sh` also checks that each fixture is rejected for exactly one reason.
7. **Met.** `make validate` is green on all 15 targets, including `check-proto-sync` after `make sync-protos`.

Release: tag `proto-v0.1.13` after merge.

### What was broken

In the sidebar, the **Add Menu** pages of the Geometry Nodes, Shader and Compositor editors went nowhere, for example *Geometry Node Editor › Header › Add Menu › Utilities*. 34 pages were hit.

### Why

When the pages were reorganised, the old pages were archived but kept their web address. The new page couldn't take that address, so Webflow quietly added a random ending (`…-utilities-05321`). The sidebar still pointed at the clean address.

While checking, I also found 16 doubled pages in the 3D Viewport section (for example the Sculpt Sidebar page existed four times). They came from the website sync retrying when Webflow was slow.

- 🗄️ The 16 doubles and one leftover old page are archived (not deleted, so nothing is lost).

👉 **To fix the live site, publish to bforartists.com** once you've had a look at staging.

### What this PR changes, so it can't happen again

`docs2/tools/sync.py`:
1. A slow *create* is no longer sent twice. The sync looks the page up first.
2. If an archived page holds an address, the sync moves it aside before creating the new page.
3. A live page always wins over an archived copy with the same name.

author: kutasinaelena
body:
## What

Four regression cases for [VCST-6536](https://virtocommerce.atlassian.net/browse/VCST-6536). In that bug, an `OR` clause in the storefront order-list search let a buyer read other customers' orders. X-Order prepended the caller's `customerId`/`organizationId` to the search keyword, and the search grammar's `OR` turned them into alternatives. The fix is vc-module-x-order#57 (XOrder 3.1017.0, hotfixes 3.1014.1 / 3.1005.2).

| Case | Suite | Asserts |
|---|---|---|
| ORD-104 | `014-orders-frontend` | A buyer with no orders searches `OR status:"Processing"` and `OR` on `/account/orders` and gets the empty state; GetOrders `totalCount` is 0 |
| ORD-GQL-015 | `050c-graphql-xorder` | `orders` with `OR` filters returns no row with a foreign `customerId`, and `totalCount` ≤ the caller's own total |
| ORD-GQL-016 | `050c-graphql-xorder` | `organizationOrders` with `OR` filters returns no row outside the requested organization, and `totalCount` ≤ the organization's total |
| SR-GQL-157 | `050m-graphql-sales-rep` | `salesRepCustomerOrders` / `salesRepOrders` with `OR` input stay inside the rep's served organizations |

All four carry `Catches:VCST-6536` and BL-AUTH-006. Ids, totals and organization ids are captured at runtime; nothing is hardcoded.

## Evidence

- **Run:** `REG-2026-10-27-0036` on vcst (XOrder 3.1017.0-pr-57), 4/4 PASS, then promoted Draft → Automated with `tc:promote`.
- **The cases would fail on the bug:** on the pre-fix build the same requests returned 2269 / 2378 orders that were not the caller's (orchestrator probe, same accounts).
  - SR-GQL-157 has no pre-fix baseline. Mechanical negative controls (a wrong caller or organization id) fail it as expected.
- **Corpus check:** the existing order-search rows (ORD-015/022/025/056, 050c, the 050m order rows) were triaged and stay as they are. No REPAIR or RE-BASE.

  - `suites:review`: 0 Blocker/Critical on the new rows.
  - `td:validate` and `suites:lint` pass.

author: stephen-wang24
body:
`str()` of the ACP params models included `request`, which holds the `x-*` headers FastACP forwards to the agent. Those headers can carry end-user credentials such as `x-user-oauth-credentials`. The `default`, `temporal` and `temporal-openai-agents` templates and the Temporal tutorials log the whole `params` at INFO, so the header values were written to agent stdout on every call. ## What changed 1. **Models** (`src/agentex/protocol/acp.py`): `request` is now `Field(repr=False)` on `CreateTaskParams`, `SendMessageParams`, `SendEventParams`, `CancelTaskParams` and `InterruptTaskParams`. `str(params)`, `repr(params)` and `f"{params}"` no longer include it. Attribute access, `model_dump()`, `model_dump_json()` and the JSON schema are unchanged, so handlers, the ADK's header forwarding and the Temporal signal payload still get the headers. 2. **Templates and tutorials**: the 22 log lines that interpolated the whole `params` now log the task id, plus the event id in event handlers: - templates `default` (3 lines), `temporal` (2) and `temporal-openai-agents` (2) - Temporal tutorials 000, 010, 030, 050, 060, 070, 080 and 100 - the procurement demo 3. **Tests** (`tests/test_acp_params_repr.py`): for each model, a canary header value is absent from `str()`/`repr()`, while `.request`, `model_dump()`, `model_dump_json()` and a `model_dump()` → `model_validate()` round trip (the Temporal signal path) still carry it. ```mermaid flowchart LR GW["x-* request headers
e.g. x-user-oauth-credentials"] --> ING["FastACP ingress
puts them in params.request"] ING --> H["Handler / workflow"] H -->|"before: logger.info of the whole params
header values in the log line"| LOG["agent stdout"] H -->|"after: task and event ids only;
str of params omits request"| LOG H -->|"params.request and model_dump
unchanged"| USE["ADK header forwarding,
Temporal signal payload"] ``` ## Before / After | Behavior | Before (`main` @ 7e421c6e) | After (this branch) | |---|---|---| | Stdout of a new `default` agent after task/create, event/send and task/cancel that carry an `x-user-oauth-credentials` header | the header value is printed on 3 lines, one per handler | not printed; each handler logs its task id (and event id) | | Stdout of a new `temporal` agent after the same three calls | the header value is printed once, by the `RECEIVE_EVENT` signal handler | not printed | | Stdout of an agent built from the old templates (which still log the whole `params`) once it runs this SDK | the header value is printed | not printed; the line still prints, without `request=` | | Any `print(params)` or `f"{params}"` in agent code | shows `request={'headers': {...}}` with the values | leaves `request` out | | Headers available to handler code and the Temporal workflow (`params.request`) | yes | yes | ## Proof Ran agents scaffolded from `main` and from this branch with the real `agentex agents run`. Each got task/create, event/send and task/cancel carrying `x-user-oauth-credentials: test-canary-not-a-real-token`, and I counted that value in the agent's stdout: | Agent | Templates | SDK | Canary in stdout | |---|---|---|---| | `default` | main | main | **3** lines: task/create, event/send, task/cancel | | `default` | this branch | this branch | **0** | | `temporal` | main | main | **1** line: the `RECEIVE_EVENT` signal handler | | `temporal` | this branch | this branch | **0** | | `default` | main (old `{params}` lines) | this branch | **0** | | `temporal` | main (old `{params}` lines) | this branch | **0** | The header still reaches the code. A throwaway probe line in the branch's event handlers compared `params.request["headers"]["x-user-oauth-credentials"]` with the canary, and it logged `True` in both the `default` handler and the `temporal` workflow. The event handler's log line, before and after (timestamps replaced by `...`, the middle of long lines trimmed to `…`): ``` # main, default agent ACP: ... INFO - Received task event send rpc: agent=Agent(id='agent-canary', … request={'headers': {'x-user-oauth-credentials': 'test-canary-not-a-real-token'}} # this branch, default agent ACP: ... NRRD files with two domain axes and a list axis (2D+t) with scalar voxels failed to load as a sequence with the error "Unexpected pixel type". For example:

```
dimension: 3
space dimension: 2
sizes: 128 104 5
space directions: (1.15,0) (0,1.15) none
kinds: domain domain list
```

Changes:
- Frames of 2D+t images are now loaded as single-slice 3D volumes. The frame geometry is computed only from the non-sequence axes, with the slice axis orthogonal to the image plane (same as when a single 2D image is loaded). Previously the geometry of 2D+t color and vector images relied on how ITK fills in the list axis.
- Index type and values of the sequence axis are now also read when it is axis 2 (2D+t), not only axis 0 or 3.

Added a test to `vtkMRMLVolumeSequenceStorageNodeNrrdTest` that checks number of frames, frame dimensions, voxel values, IJK to RAS matrix, and index values.

author: mablr
body:
Adds `Version::initial_call_depth` (default 0) and `max_call_depth() = initial_call_depth + 1024`.

Embedders that run a whole transaction inside another one, for example to replay or simulate it while an outer trace is recorded, need the nested root to keep its depth in the surrounding trace while it still gets the protocol's 1024-frame budget. Renumbering depths in an inspector doesn't work, because the bundled inspectors and the tracer arena hard-code `depth == 0` as the root. The depth limit in the interpreter, host and JIT, the CREATE nonce bump, and those inspectors now key off the root depth. Values above `u16::MAX - 1025` are rejected in `with_version`, so depth arithmetic can't overflow.

`Version` is used because the interpreter, JIT builtins and inspectors already read it, so no new host surface is needed.

Context: needed to move Foundry onto evm2 without a fork, see foundry-rs/foundry#17541.

author: stelizhenets
body:
## Bear traps R4: a bot that noticed a trap and does not shoot it walks up and defuses it by hand (switched off)

Stacked on R6 (`claude/traps-react6`, on R3, on R2); the diff of this PR alone is `git diff claude/traps-react6 claude/traps-react4`. **Switched off** (`traps.react.defuse` false, needs `on`): no walk, no USE, no counter.

- **Switch and numbers** (Tuning `traps.react`, `SRP_BENCH_TUNING`): `defuse` (false), `defuse_p` 0.3, `defuse_walk_m` 10, `defuse_walk_s` 8, `defuse_stand_m` 0.85, `defuse_s` 5.0, `use_ok_rad` 0.05, `use_settle_ms` 250. `defuse_s` is the trap's `defuse_time` (PROVEN); `defuse_stand_m` sits between the foot's 0.6 m reach (PROVEN, 565/566) and the use ray (2.0 m from the eye, `usable_objects_detection_distance`, PROVEN; a crouched eye 0.85 m out is about 1.4 m from the trap's centre); `defuse_p` and the rest are GUESSes that become train arms.
- **Two more states of the one transition** (`trap_react::step`): `Walk { spot }` to a stand on the bot's own side of the trap (so the approach does not cross it), then `Defuse` at the stand: crouched, the view held on the trap's centre, USE pressed every tick once the view has settled (`use_settle_ms`) and is within `use_ok_rad`. The hold ends when the world no longer shows the trap armed (`Defused { held_ms }`), or is given up: a fight, an enemy seen, a hit since the walk began, the walk too long, the eye still out of reach after the crouch (1.2 s), or 1.5 s after the 5 s.
- **Start** (`start_defuse`): a trap the bot noticed, not started on by the shot (the shot is off, or had no line, range or weapon), within `defuse_walk_m`, the bot unhurt (health >= 0.4), carrying nothing, no fight; then one roll of `defuse_p` a trap and a life; a stand with a floor under it.
- **One at a time, from observables only.** The same claim as the shot, plus what a player sees of a defuse: a mate standing (<= 0.6 m/s) within 1.4 m of the trap with the view on it (`mate_beside`) holds the walk off (`HeldForMate`). A bot already holding is not moved by a mate who comes (the later one yields). The second hand defuser is counted with the second shooter (`double_shooters`).
- **Never our own team's trap**: `others` excludes the team's list, as for the shot.
- **Counters:** `defuse_started`, `disarmed_by_hand` (the world shows the trap gone after a hold of >= 3 s, the players' own measure; a proxy), `defuse_gave_up`, and the shared `held_for_mate`. Shared-file hunks: `drive.rs` (the hook now walks to a stand and crouches, 10 lines), `tuning/traps.rs`, tests.

**Root cause.** The recordings show that stock players do defuse by hand (30 of the 987 traps had a USE held >= 3 s within 4 m before they were disarmed, 10 by an enemy of the placer); a bot can only do that with a walk, a crouch and a held key, which no play has. Without it a bot that noticed a trap but has no shot, or loses the line, can only avoid it.

**Best practice.** An interaction that takes time is a state with entry guards, a progress timer and abort conditions, one transition function, tested without the game ([the state pattern in game AI](https://gameprogrammingpatterns.com/state.html)); a contended world object is claimed by what the other agents can see of it, not by a shared lock ([attack tokens](https://www.strayspark.studio/blog/attack-token-system-ue5-group-combat-that-feels-fair) as the shape, observation as the claim, as the owner asked). Merged off, the bench turns it on ([Fowler, Feature Toggles](https://martinfowler.com/articles/feature-toggles.html)).

**Calibration.** Target: the other team's traps disarmed by bots, by shot and by hand together, 5-10 %, the hand share about 3 % (the players'), with no extra bot deaths: the arms differ in `defuse_p` (0, 0.15, 0.3) with R1's `p0`. The look reports `defuse_started`, `disarmed_by_hand / defuse_started`, `defuse_gave_up` (and its causes by the trace), the seconds spent crouched at a trap, and the deaths in them. **Not confirmed live:** that the flag the client tests before a use (`[player+0x330]` bit 21 in `use_execute` 0x304F30) is set for a bot as it is for the players. It is read by the battery container's `use_execute` (0x31C780) too, which the bots already use, so it is a general ability, not the skill `can_defuse_traps` (LIKELY, not proven); and that the trap's use volume is met by a ray to its centre from 0.85 m crouched (the stand-in does not model the defuse; the J0/trap stand-in check decides `defuse_stand_m`).

**CPU.** Off: one flag read. On: nothing until a trap is noticed; then one scan of the noticed traps at a think, a grid lookup for the stand at the start, and per tick one step and a scan of the mates (<= 9). Under 1 us a think; the CPU look reports ms/s from the counters.

Checks (Windows, OpenSSL 3): see the comment on the PR for the suite counts. New tests (7): the walk goes to the stand, then crouches and looks; the walk ends (trap gone, a fight, a mate, too long); USE only once settled and on the trap, a mate that comes changes nothing; the defuse ends (gone with the held time, a fight, too long, out of reach after the crouch); a mate beside the trap; the game loop (a trap on the bot's route: the bot walks up, crouches, holds USE for about 5-6 s and gives up when the stand-in does not defuse; with the roll at 0 it does nothing).

author: shiny-code-app[bot]
body:
## Why

An agent that gets UNKNOWN needs to know why, so it can fix the cause or report the gap truthfully. After the desktop route was retired (cbusillo/codex-skills#2804), every gap read "Automatic inspection has no isolated native worker for this selection", and the next step was sometimes wrong:
- A CSS file in VeriReel, a WebStorm repository, got Python-setup advice.
- An empty selection was reported as "no native worker".
- Some messages still pointed at the retired desktop and Qodana backends.

## What changes

- **One reason table.** `UNAVAILABLE_REASONS` in `native_backend.py` maps each existing selection reason code to a plain explanation and a next step that fits it. The cases are:
  - an empty selection;
  - an extension no worker inspects;
  - XML outside Odoo;
  - TypeScript or JSON under a PyCharm-only config;
  - JSON-only or Java/.kts-only selections;
  - nested `projectPath` lanes (#2557);
  - a missing inspection profile (#2540);
  - worker setup problems;
  - a non-macOS host;
  - the host-load pause.

  When nothing can fix the gap, the next step says the coverage is unavailable and should be reported as UNKNOWN. For TypeScript under a PyCharm-only config, the agent is told to ask before recording WebStorm as the IDE.
- **Mixed selections** name the files a worker can inspect and say to run them separately with `--scope files`.
- **Order of checks.** `select_backend` checks for an empty selection and for unsupported file types before it checks worker eligibility, so the reason given matches the files.
- **Unchanged:** the verdict rules, so nothing new can become GREEN.

Removed: the generic message and its `ISOLATED_BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE_HINT` constant, three "existing backend" next steps, and the Qodana paragraph in `references/native-backend.md`. Net lines: about +260. That is about +140 for the reason table and checks, and about +120 for tests.

Refs #2920, #2557, #2540

## Verification

- **Tests:** 12 new tests (26 subtests), one per case. Every one fails on origin/main or the earlier head. All 8 jetbrains-inspection test modules pass (154 native backend tests, 1 skipped).
- **Checks:** typecheck, the comment check, public safety, `quick_validate` and `validate-skill-repo` pass.
- **Native PyCharm inspection** of the changed `.py` files: GREEN, with 0 findings on changed lines. Earlier runs were RED on type warnings and unresolved references, all fixed.
- **Real repositories:** the VeriReel CSS file now gets "no native worker inspects .css". jetbrains-inspection-api's `scripts` file names its nested lane.

## Review by another model

Google, Gemini 4 Argon (Medium), model reported by the CLI. It was required because the change touches `SKILL.md` and `references/native-backend.md`.

- **First review:** three findings, all fixed with tests that fail on the old code.
  - High: mixed selections omitted the files PyCharm could inspect.
  - Medium: a selection re-read failure surfaced as `tool_bug`.
  - Low: dotfiles were handled with inconsistent suffix rules.
- **Rereview** of the fixes, docs and agreement between guidance and code: none.
- **Not fixed here:** a repository whose IDE is WebStorm or IntelliJ IDEA, with no lanes, still routes `.py` and `.yaml` to PyCharm. The explanation now says so accurately. Whether that routing is right is left for a separate decision.

author: strawgate
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"strawgate"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_017RvhsrmxfrCwrkn9wbip3nMN4nHFJCJAkHFm5DJYdtsg)_

Two rough edges from an end-to-end run of the packaged Supervisor against a local Logfire stack.

## What changes

1. **An install that can't connect no longer reports success.** On macOS the Supervisor runs as a root launchd daemon, so it didn't trust a CA that was only in the user's keychain. Every connect failed with `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority`, but `pydantic-opamp-enroll` printed "the Supervisor is running" and nothing pointed at `--ca-file`.
   - `opampsupervisor status` takes `--wait DURATION --since UNIX`. It waits for a Supervisor started since then to connect, then prints the status as before. It exits 0 once connected and 1 when not connected by the deadline. A status left by the previous run doesn't count.
   - The Linux, macOS and Windows enroll helpers record the start time, start the service, then run `status --wait 30s`. If that fails, they print the status (with what to check) and exit 1, saying the service keeps retrying. On success they print "running and connected". `--no-start` is unchanged.
   - `connectHint` takes the error text. An `x509:` failure now says to enroll again with `--ca-file`, or to add the CA to the system trust store, in the log and in `status`.
2. **A remote config the Collector fails on no longer stops the host's telemetry.** The enrolled config turns on upstream's `agent.automatic_config_rollback`. The last config that ran healthy takes the failed one's place. As this fork already does, the failed config's FAILED status stays reported.

## Fork notes

Everything is in our own files: `status_command.go`, `reachability.go`, `status.go` and the packaging scripts. No upstream file changes. The rollback is upstream's own option, turned on by config.

## Spec

No protocol change. A failed remote config stays `RemoteConfigStatuses_FAILED`, with its `error_message`. The rollback's wording ("The last working remote config runs in its place.") is what Platform reads to tell a rollback apart (pydantic/platform#50926).

## Tests

- `go test ./packaging/ . ./supervisor/`
- New tests: `TestEnrollWaitsForTheConnection` (enroll fails when the status says it can't connect, with the hint), `TestStatusCommandWaitsForTheConnection` (a stale status doesn't count, an untrusted certificate names `--ca-file`, a connection arriving mid-wait returns 0), a `--ca-file` case in `TestConnectHintsNameTheSupervisorsSettings`, and `automatic_config_rollback` asserted on Linux, macOS and Windows.
- The Windows helper's wait step is written but not exercised here: its tests all use `-NoStart`. CI's Windows lane runs the same tests.

Reaching hosts needs a Supervisor release after this and #94, then a logfire-cli pin bump.

author: stan4git
body:
## Goal

On Windows, run every muggle hook's script inside the Git Bash shell Claude Code already started instead of starting a second `bash` for it: one fewer process start and MSYS runtime init per hook firing, with no hook timeout raised.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Under Git Bash / Cygwin (`OSTYPE` msys*/cygwin*), every `hooks.json` command runs its script in the invoking shell and launches no `bash` of its own.
- Under any other shell Claude Code may use (`/bin/sh` as dash or POSIX-mode bash), each command still runs its script in its own bash, with unchanged output and spawn counts.
- A gate script still takes its standalone path when it is the hook's own script, executed or sourced, and still does not when `guardrail-dispatch.sh` sources it for its pre-filter.
- Hook output is identical on both paths; no `timeout` changes; `codex-hooks.json` regenerates byte-identical.

## Changes

- **`plugin/scripts/hook-entry.sh`** (new, POSIX sh). Every `hooks.json` command is now `set -- <script> <args>; . "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/hook-entry.sh"`. Under Git Bash / Cygwin it sources the script into the shell Claude Code started; elsewhere it execs `bash "<script>" <args>` exactly as before. Arguments travel through `set --` because a dot command with arguments is a bash extension dash lacks.
- **`guardrail_is_hook_script`** in `guardrail-lib.sh` replaces the 24 copies of `[[ ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} == "$0" ]]`, which a sourced script cannot use: it compares the caller against the path the entry records, or `$0` when bash ran the script.
- **`scripts/build-codex-hooks.mjs`** derives each hook's `bash "<script>"` form for Codex (it starts every command as a process anyway). `codex-hooks.json` is unchanged.
- **Tests:** `hook-entry.test.ts` (in-place under Git Bash and Cygwin, `exec bash` under bash and POSIX `sh`, real build-router output); footprint caps per shell (0 own `bash` launches inside Git Bash at the same no-op spawn ceilings, 1 per command elsewhere); dispatcher cases under both shells; Codex tests keyed through the derived form.
- `plugin/hooks/README.md` documents the entry.

## Measurements (Windows 11, Git Bash 5.2.37, Claude Code 2.1.308)

- Process lifetimes captured across live sessions: a hook was three processes — Git's `bin\bash.exe` launcher, `usr\bin\bash.exe -c`, then the nested `bash <script>`. The nested stage cost 300–1,240 ms under load; the scripts themselves are builtins-only.
- A/B, interleaved, 50 rounds, launched exactly as Claude Code launches hooks: UserPromptSubmit p50 72 → 51 ms, max 2,180 → 1,333 ms, runs over 1 s 4 → 2; Stop dispatch p50 118 → 97 ms, max 2,061 → 1,392 ms. Output identical.
- `claude -p --debug` with this branch's plugin: SessionStart 322 / 353 ms with the same injected context, UserPromptSubmit 52 ms, PostToolUse 60 ms, Stop 202 ms, all status 0.

## Limits

The two remaining process starts belong to Claude Code (launcher → `usr\bin\bash.exe`). Under heavy concurrency each process start on Windows intermittently stalls 0.3–1.3 s, so p90 stays near 450–575 ms and a loaded box can still overrun the 1 s timeout; this change removes the plugin's own share of that cost.

`_wt-posttool-if-gating` holds unpushed edits to `hooks.json`, `guardrail-dispatch.sh` and `guardrail-lib.sh`; whichever lands second carries the `set -- …` command form over.

## Validation

unit-only — plugin hook scripts, manifests and tests; this repo serves no web surface to drive (`NO_WEB_SURFACE`).

author: ablasik
body:
`DoFilleting` ends with `BooleanPostProcess(TRUE)`, which checks every edge of the body. It removes the target's own edges too, so faces of the target on coincident surfaces are merged. On SolidCraft's sphere in six patches (rig case 2752: r 2, cut flat at z = 1, R1 round on the rim) the five patches become one face whose surface no patch's parameterization can carry: loops of the wrong orientation and rails up to half a millimetre off their surfaces, with status success.

Fix: opt-in `Kernel::fixes.fillet_cleanup_keeps_target_faces` (default off, SMLib behaviour), the fork's change tangency-labs/smlib@9ddf4a8. `do_filleting` records the target's edges and faces; `boolean_post_process` skips each recorded edge and each edge whose faces are all recorded. WR-459 in `plan/upstream-issues/`.

Before/after: the six-patch sphere is not built in Rust (analytic patches in six faces), so the test shows the mechanism. A cylinder united with a disc extruded from two half arcs, a round on the disc's top rim: default 5 faces and 1 edge with one face on both sides; with the flag 5 faces and 2 (the disc's wall edge kept). Volume is the same. The sphere's own failure is not reproduced here and nothing was run against C++.

author: zegoverno
body:
Simplifies zenbot. Kept: the tape and context management, Claude Code and Codex on the owner's subscriptions, the tools, System One, and memory and the knowledge records. Removed: the security model, the learning router, skill drafts, the release pipeline and most of the docs. **208 files, +2,402 / −29,253.**

## What changed (one commit each)

1. **Shipping from the checkout.** `scripts/upgrade.sh` builds whatever is checked out and installs it once no session is working. `apply-upgrade.sh` went from 225 to about 100 lines: it backs up SQLite, swaps the binaries, health-checks, and restores both the binaries and the database if the new kernel isn't healthy. CI is a single job on PRs (`scripts/check.sh`). Removed: the edge release, the arm64, Matrix and Postgres jobs, size budgets, the docs/PROGRESS check, and all Postgres migration tooling.
2. **No security model.**
   - Deleted the taint, gate, queue, proxy, fsview, sources, trust, task and session_state modules.
   - `bash` runs on the host in the workspace, without bubblewrap or the egress proxy.
   - Every `AGENTS.md` is followed, and tool results are handed over as they are.
   - System One loses its 7 risk decisions, the caution/grant rules, the owner rung, batches and the learner.
   - The router is gone: a session uses the model you chose or `ZEN_DEFAULT_MODEL`, and a subagent uses its parent's model unless the call names one.
   - `save_skill` writes the live skill.
   - Jobs the agent creates are live at once.
   - **Kept:** the loopback owner token, secret masking in tool output and recorded arguments, and the Matrix device and room checks.
3. **Database.** Migration `0002_simplify.sql` drops the security, router and draft tables, views, triggers and columns. It was tested on a copy of the live database: no foreign-key violations, integrity ok, and the new kernel runs a turn on it. The end-to-end tests now expect the simpler behavior.
4. **One command table** (`zen_client::commands`): `/x` in the terminal app, `!x` in Matrix and `zen x` on the command line are the same command. New on the command line: `new`, `model`, `effort`, `done`, `rename`, `archive`, `steer` (with `-s <id>`), plus `mcp [login]`, `memory [tier|sleep]` and `upgrade [check]`. Queue, approve, deny, trust, tools, policy and skill-review commands are gone everywhere. Tests keep the command line and the table in step.
5. **Docs rebuilt from the code:** `AGENTS.md`, `MAP.md`, `INSTALL.md` and a short `README.md`. Everything else is deleted, and code comments no longer cite decision numbers.

## Checks

`scripts/check.sh` passes in 343s (it took about 450s before): build, unit tests, clippy with `-D warnings`, and the 21 end-to-end scenarios (54–60s, down from 105s). `crates/zen-matrix` passes clippy and its 22 tests. `scripts/matrix-e2e.sh` (Docker) was updated but not run.

## After merging, on the VM

- `zen upgrade`. Migration 0002 runs once, and the database is backed up first.
- Clean-up of leftovers, which are now ignored:
  - `ZEN_SESSION_RISK_CAP` and `ZEN_TRUSTED_REPOS` in `~/.zenbot/env`
  - `~/.zenbot/s1/action_gate.toml`, which System One now reports as a problem because that decision no longer exists
  - `~/.zenbot/trust.toml`
  - the "marked untrusted" line in `~/.zenbot/AGENTS.md`; your copy isn't overwritten, and the new default says to follow every `AGENTS.md`
- Optional: `sudo apt remove bubblewrap`.

author: rhys-looma
body:
**LU-41: benchmark harness.** One command (`npm run benchmark [-- --runs 5] [--live]`) runs the same journeys three ways for both agents, five runs each, and writes `reports/benchmark.md`.

- **(a) Reads pages, no Usher:** the agent labels every page with its model, then acts. No knock, nothing shared.
- **(b) Maps:** on the mock site (an Usher site) by knocking. On httpbin, which doesn't run Usher, by looking the map up in the registry by fingerprint, with no token.
- **(c) Plan, then maps:** the whole journey's data is checked against the plan first.

**Journeys:** the mock site's three steps, submitted (a made-up quote), and https://httpbin.org/forms/post, filled but never submitted (dry run).

Replayed at recorded latency by default. This report includes one live run per model-using configuration, listed separately.

| Journey | Config | Agent | Success | Wall time (median, range) | Model time | Tokens in/out | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mock, 3 steps | (a) | A, Muse Spark | 4/4 | 14.22 s (14.21–14.23) | 13.60 s | 13,702 / 3,190 | $0.0307 |
| Mock, 3 steps | (a) | B, Spark Open | 4/4 | 14.01 s (13.99–14.03) | 13.39 s | 14,155 / 2,408 | $0.0258 |
| Mock, 3 steps | (b) | A | 5/5 | 2.68 s (2.67–2.72) | 0 | 0 | $0 |
| Mock, 3 steps | (b) | B | 5/5 | 2.71 s (2.69–2.75) | 0 | 0 | $0 |
| Mock, 3 steps | (c) | A | 5/5 | 2.69 s (2.68–2.71) | 0 | 0 | $0 |
| Mock, 3 steps | (c) | B | 5/5 | 2.69 s (2.68–2.72) | 0 | 0 | $0 |
| httpbin, 1 page | (a) | A | 4/4 | 11.12 s (11.10–11.12) | 10.59 s | 3,539 / 1,458 | $0.0106 |
| httpbin, 1 page | (a) | B | 4/4 | 9.56 s (9.55–9.62) | 9.03 s | 3,690 / 1,857 | $0.0125 |
| httpbin, 1 page | (b) | A / B | 5/5 | 2.53 s / 2.58 s | 0 | 0 | $0 |
| httpbin, 1 page | (c) | A / B | 5/5 | 2.54 s / 2.58 s | 0 | 0 | $0 |

**Live runs:**

| Journey | Agent | Wall time | Model time | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mock | A | 21.89 s | 21.23 s | $0.032 |
| Mock | B | 16.04 s | 15.40 s | $0.026 |
| httpbin | A | 11.10 s | 10.57 s | $0.011 |
| httpbin | B | 9.54 s | 9.02 s | $0.013 |

Plans add no measurable time over maps on these journeys. Their value is checking the journey's data before starting, not speed.

**Also in this PR:**
- **New agent modes:** without Usher (`noUsher`), registry lookup on sites without a knock lane, and dry run (`dryRun`).
- **A rate-limit fix:** the benchmark showed the per-address limit on writes (120 a minute) also covered site-script session events, which made Agent A's registry lookups fail from one machine. Events now have their own limit (1,200 a minute), writes are at 300, and the benchmark lifts the limits for its single-address run.

With `--config=remote`, Windows clients handed remote Linux genrules their local shell path (`C:/Program Files/Git/usr/bin/bash.exe`). The `rules_distroless` genrule that unpacks Debian 13's `libxcb1` then failed whenever it missed the cache, so every `//kestrel/app` build or test from Windows needed `--shell_executable=/bin/bash` by hand.

- `.bazelrc`: `build:remote --shell_executable=/bin/bash`. Remote workers are always Linux, and builds without `--config=remote` are unchanged.
- `kestrel/tools/network-lab.ps1`: no longer passes the flag.
- `kestrel/todo/testing.md`: the task moves to Done.

A genrule forced to run locally under `--config=remote` on Windows would now get `/bin/bash` as well. Neither the Kestrel tests nor the game build ran into one.

- All 24 `//kestrel/...` tests pass (`--build_tests_only`, which skips the GPU demos that can't build remotely). Most actions hit the cache, so the action keys match the ones the ad hoc flag gave: https://app.buildbuddy.io/invocation/d1b1250e-b14f-42fa-adec-d891da2f600e

author: leaf-admin
body:
## Objetivo
Domínio 4a da saída do RTDB: veículos (`vehicles`, `user_vehicles`, `vehicle_plate_index`), que alimentam o gate de ficar online. A mudança precisa ser cuidadosa por isso.

## Por que um roteador por raiz
O gate de ativação lê `driver_activation`, `users`, `user_vehicles` e `vehicles` juntos, e os veículos são lidos e gravados em ~15 arquivos (com `update` multi-caminho na raiz). Trocar cada chamada à mão seria arriscado. O roteador fica dentro de `firebaseConfig.getRealtimeDB()`, de modo que todo código existente passa por ele sem mudança, e a migração acontece por raiz, controlada por flag:

| Configuração da raiz | Comportamento |
|---|---|
| fora das flags | RTDB puro, como hoje |
| em `RTDB_FIRESTORE_WRITE_ROOTS` | o RTDB segue fonte; cada registro tocado é relido do RTDB e copiado para `rtdb_<raiz>/<chave>` no Firestore |
| também em `RTDB_FIRESTORE_READ_ROOTS` | o Firestore é a fonte; as gravações são aplicadas com a semântica do RTDB numa transação do Firestore, e o RTDB vira espelho |

- Cada registro de topo vira um documento `{ schema, json }` com o conteúdo idêntico ao do RTDB. Isso evita os problemas de arrays aninhados e chaves especiais do Firestore.
- APIs emuladas: `once`/`get`, snapshot (`val`, `exists`, `child`, `forEach`), `orderByChild`/`Key`/`Value` com `equalTo`/`startAt`/`startAfter`/`endAt` e `limitToFirst`/`Last` (ordenação do RTDB), `set`, `update`, `remove`, `push`, `transaction` e o `update` multi-caminho na raiz (um único `update` no RTDB, para manter a atomicidade do lado RTDB).
- Listeners (`on`) em raiz roteada **falham explicitamente**.
- **Sem raízes configuradas, o cliente original é devolvido sem nenhuma mudança.**
- `account-routes` passa a usar o roteador no lugar de `admin.database()` direto.

## Verificação
- **Comparação direta** (`scripts/benchmark/rtdb-root-router-diff.cjs`): a mesma sequência de operações roda no emulador real do RTDB (controle) e no roteador. Cobre `update` na raiz misturando raiz roteada e `users`, `update` com caminho profundo, `set`, remoção de campo e de registro, transações com abort, polígono aninhado e 4 consultas ordenadas e filtradas. Resultado idêntico ao controle em 4 cenários:
  - Firestore como fonte;
  - RTDB espelhado;
  - modo só de cópia;
  - leitura da cópia.

  Um primeiro bug (array virava objeto numa leitura sem filtro) foi pego e corrigido por esse teste.
- `verify-driver-gate-parity.cjs`: para cada motorista, calcula o estado de ativação lendo do RTDB e lendo pelo roteador servido pelo Firestore. **Qualquer diferença bloqueia a troca.**
- `backfill-rtdb-roots-firestore.cjs`: cópia exata por raiz (remove extras), com paridade; simulação por padrão e `--apply` exige `--ref`.
- Novo `rtdb-root-router.unit.test.js` (5 casos).
- `account-routes` (52 testes) continua passando.
- Suíte backend completa: 368 suítes, 3202 testes.
- `governance:check` e `scan-secrets --tracked-only`: ok.

## Fora do escopo
- `driver_activation`, travas e contadores de documentos (domínio 4b).
- `users` (domínio 5): tem um listener de KYC que precisará de tratamento próprio.
- `vehicle_active_assignment` (47 mil registros de teste, nenhum código lê) e `cars` (vazio) ficam para a limpeza.

## Rollback
Esvaziar `RTDB_FIRESTORE_READ_ROOTS` (volta ao RTDB na hora) e depois `RTDB_FIRESTORE_WRITE_ROOTS`.

author: nicholasxu-wq
body:
Refs #838

**Adds `nodes::UsbCameraInput`: open a USB webcam by a stable ID and get decoded frames (NV12 or NV16, captured with no copy) or the camera's raw JPEG frames for passthrough.** Step 3 of the zero-copy USB camera path.

## Summary

```text
                         nodes::UsbCameraInput(opt)
 ┌─────────────────────── at Graph creation (once) ───────────────────────┐
 │ sysfs: camera ID → /dev/videoN                                         │
 │ V4L2 probe on /dev/videoN:                                             │
 │   VIDIOC_QUERYCAP / ENUM_FMT ......... is it an MJPEG capture node?    │
 │   ENUM_FRAMESIZES / FRAMEINTERVALS ... is W×H @ fps listed exactly?    │
 │   S_FMT / S_PARM ..................... set the mode, reject if adjusted │
 │   REQBUFS / STREAMON / DQBUF ......... grab 1 frame → 4:2:0 or 4:2:2?  │
 │   STREAMOFF, close                                                     │
 └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                     │
               ┌─────────────────────┴─────────────────────┐
       output = Frames (default)                     output = Jpeg
               │                                           │
 USB webcam ─► uvcvideo driver ─► v4l2src            USB webcam ─► uvcvideo driver ─► v4l2src
               (kernel)          io-mode=dmabuf-import             (kernel)          io-mode=mmap
                                 writes into the                                     writes into the
                                 decoder's CMA pool                                  driver's own buffers
               │                                           │
         capsfilter image/jpeg, W×H, fps             capsfilter image/jpeg, W×H, fps
               │                                           │
         queue (leaky)                               queue (leaky)
               │                                           │
         neatdecoder (HW JPEG decode)                      ▼
          ┌────┴─────┐                                JPEG frames → app
      4:2:0 cam  4:2:2 cam                            (split → Passthrough + SimaDecode)
          ▼          ▼
        NV12       NV16
```

- **One Node, like `CameraInput`.** `output = Frames` (default) decodes to the camera's native layout: NV12 for 4:2:0 cameras, NV16 for 4:2:2. The model's preprocessing reads NV16 (core#1161), so there is no `ColorConvert`.
- **`output = Jpeg`** returns the camera's JPEG frames for MJPEG passthrough: connect the node to `VideoSender::Passthrough(RtspCodec::MJPEG)` and to `SimaDecode(MJPEG)`, as the high-density detector does with RTSP. The decode branch copies each frame (see Notes).
- **`usb_camera_ids()`** lists stable camera IDs (libcamera's format); **`usb_camera_info()`** says which layout a camera decodes to. Python bindings included.
- Rebuilding a graph after the camera is unplugged or moved fails with "call UsbCameraInput again". `CameraInput` is unchanged.

## Merge order

1. sima-neat/codecs#26, then publish Codecs 0.1.10.
2. sima-neat/scheduler#38, then publish Scheduler (Frames mode needs its `input-pool-buffers`).
3. **This PR**: retarget to `develop` after sima-neat/core#1161 merges. The PR-sanitization check fails until then because of the stacked base.

Track A (core#1161, insight#203, apps#478) does not depend on this PR. An Apps follow-up will move apps#478 onto `UsbCameraInput(output = Jpeg)`.

## Change Type

- [x] Feature

## Risk

- [x] Medium

**Risk notes:** The API is additive; the only shared-code change is one kind name in `GraphComposition.cpp` (live-source fan-in). Creating the node opens the camera once to check the mode and read one frame.

## Test Evidence

- Unit (head `a6942a92`, which merges #1161 `5ed9705c`): `unit_usb_camera_input_test`, `unit_fused_realtime_fast_path_options_test` (NV12 and NV16 USB fan-in), `unit_sima_decode_test` pass. Format, naming and `sima-i18n --require-complete` pass. Codex 👍 on `ee0b1573`.
- DevKit (Platform 3.0 B2121, Logitech C920 4:2:2, with codecs#26 `b6ae1c8` + scheduler#38 fixes, nothing installed): `usb_camera_input_e2e_test` passes at `a6942a92`, including a Jpeg round that runs the real passthrough + decode graph (60 NV16 1920x1080 frames). Jpeg passthrough + decode: 300/300 NV16 frames at 1080p and 720p; Frames mode: 300/300 NV16 at 1080p. Frame rates were about 14–15 fps because the room was dark (gain 255, exposure-driven frame rate); the same code reached 29.7 fps in better light. A combined run of all six USB-camera PRs also passed.
- Not run locally: the Python surface test and full `ctest` (CI).

## Docs Impact

- [x] Docs updated in this PR: USB camera page (5 languages), `node.mdx` row, index card, `architecture.md` note.

## Compatibility and Migration

- [x] Python API or binding changed (additive)
- [x] C++ runtime API changed (additive)

**Migration notes:** None for existing code. Needs a `simaai-scheduler` with `input-pool-buffers`.

## Checklist

- [x] `CameraInput` and its binding are unchanged
- [x] Deterministic pipeline text; element names match `element_names()`
- [x] Options validated before any device I/O

## Notes for reviewers

- **Jpeg mode decodes with one copy.** It captures with `v4l2src io-mode=dmabuf` (the driver exports its buffers as DMA-BUF). `neatdecoder` tries an in-place import; the C920's buffers (`videobuf2_vmalloc`) can't be imported, so the decode branch copies each frame, as an app capturing through OpenCV does today. Zero-copy decode plus passthrough from one camera would need the decoder's pool to reach the camera through the split; that is a follow-up.
- V4L2, not libcamera: Platform 3.0's libcamera has no UVC support. Plan for 3.1: merge into `CameraInput`.
- Known limits: the default 4-buffer pool drops the newest frames under sustained decoder backpressure; `allow_cpu_fallback` has no effect; CI skips the e2e test (no USB camera).
- Pre-existing: hard-coded live-source kinds (`GraphComposition.cpp:39`); camera identity only on `libcamerasrc` errors.

author: mablr
body:
Adds `AccountChanges::touched`.

`AccountChanges` cannot currently tell an account the transaction touched but left unchanged, such as a zero-value call target, from one it only read via `BALANCE` or `EXTCODEHASH`. The flag exists in the overlay, but finalization consumes it for EIP-161 before consumers see the changes. Tools that decide which accounts a transaction interacted with, such as state diffs and tracers, need that distinction. The overlay now remembers the consumed flag, so it survives finalization and `detach`. Reverted touches are not reported, and `StateChangeSink` is unchanged.

Context: needed to move Foundry onto evm2 without a fork, see foundry-rs/foundry#17541.

author: marota
body:
The published map's chat ran from a `nohup` in a terminal, in the checkout used for development. A reboot ended it, a crash ended it, and switching that checkout to a branch — or regenerating its payload mid-curation — changed what the public chat answered from.

## `chat/service.sh`

```bash
chat/service.sh install     # start it at login, and again whenever it stops
chat/service.sh update      # after a merge: move it to the latest main, restart
chat/service.sh status      # what runs, from which commit, whether it answers
chat/service.sh uninstall
```

A launchd agent, `com.marota.hai-chat`, runs the server from **a worktree of its own detached at `origin/main`** (`~/Dev/human-ai-collaboration-live`), never from the working checkout. The published map draws main's `hai-data.js` and the chat must answer from that same file (invariant 17) — so a merge reaches the public chat when `update` runs, and the working checkout can be on any branch meanwhile.

launchd starts it at login and restarts it within seconds if it stops. `install` refuses a port held by a process launchd does not manage, since launchd would otherwise restart into a busy port forever.

## The rest of the chain, checked rather than assumed

| Piece | After a reboot |
|---|---|
| macOS session | automatic login is **on** for `antoine` |
| Tailscale + Funnel | `tailscaled` is a Homebrew boot daemon; the Funnel config (`AllowFunnel` on `:8443`) persists in it |
| Ollama | `Ollama.app` opens at login — started 38 s after boot, 27 s after the session |
| chat server | this agent, at login |

## Verified on this machine

- Installed; `status` shows it running from `cee4004` = `origin/main`.
- **Killed with `-9`** to stand in for a crash: launchd had it answering again in **2 s**, on a new pid.
- From the internet through Funnel afterwards: `/api/health` 200, the map and `.git` still 404.

Once #30 is merged, `chat/service.sh update` puts the off-the-map answers live.

author: dapirian
body:
Five correctness and security issues across the Grype automation workflows, including a condition that silently prevented the remediation-suggestions workflow from ever running automatically.

## `grype-remediation-suggestions.yml`

- **Drop `head_branch` guard** — `workflow_run.head_branch` reflects the branch owning the workflow file (`main`), not the branch checked out internally. The `== 'pre-update-release'` condition always evaluated false for scheduled runs.
- **Fix `workflow_dispatch` run ID fallback** — when `run_id` is omitted, `github.event.workflow_run.id` is empty on `workflow_dispatch` events. Now resolves via API: prefers the most recent successful `Weekly Grype Security Scan` run on `pre-update-release` within the last 7 days, falls back to the absolute latest if none found.
- **Filter PRs from issue search** — `issues.listForRepo` returns both issues and PRs; added `&& !i.pull_request` to prevent accidentally updating a PR body instead of the tracking issue.

## `dependabot-grype-guard.yml`

- **Drop `pull-requests: write`** — the workflow only writes to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` and uploads artifacts; issue/PR creation from scan results is handled by `grype-remediation-suggestions.yml`. Only `contents: read` is required.
- **Scope `underfixed_updates` to High/Critical fixable vulns** — the previous logic false-positived when a package had an unrelated unfixable High vuln alongside a Medium fixable vuln. Added `fixed_high_critical_recommendations()` that filters to High/Critical severity before checking fix state; a package is only flagged underfixed if it was changed *and* still carries a fixable High/Critical finding in the PR image.

```python
# Before: any fixable vuln on the package triggered the check
underfixed_updates = [pkg for pkg in changed if pkg in recs and ("High" in severities or "Critical" in severities)]

# After: only packages with High/Critical fixable vulns are considered
high_critical_recs = fixed_high_critical_recommendations(pr)  # scoped to sev ∈ {High, Critical}
underfixed_updates = [pkg for pkg in changed if pkg in high_critical_recs]
```

author: zmaniacz
body:
## What

- **`fix-legacy-pdf-start-times`** (new, `packages/db`): downloads each PDF-era game's source scorecard from `lfstats-scorecards`, reads the printed header time with `pdftotext -raw`, and rewrites `game.start_time` from it.
  - `--fetch`: download and parse, cached as JSONL so it can resume.
  - `--dry-run`: report the corrections.
  - `--apply`: write them in one transaction.
- **`lib/pdf-header-time.ts`**: the header parser, with tests. It handles both printed layouts, `6:10pm Oct-2-2017` and `7:55pm 10-Nov-2019`.
- **Docs**: `Legacy_Migration_PDF_Games.md` records the correction, the games left unchecked, and the deleted duplicate. Its open items are updated.

## Why

The migration read legacy `game_datetime` with `AT TIME ZONE 'America/Los_Angeles'`. But the legacy importer had stored printed times with a fixed UTC−8, so every DST-season PDF game came out an hour late. A few batches were also imported some other way. The printed PDF header is the source of truth.

## Already applied to the shared database (2026-10-26)

- 4,725 games corrected:
  - 4,542 by −1h
  - 168 by +8h (Syracuse, Loveland and Auckland, Jan–Feb 2020)
  - 11 by −14h15m (Syracuse, 5 July 2015)
  - 4 by +7h (Carmichael, 2016)
- 6,611 games now match their PDFs.
- 540 couldn't be checked:
  - 335 have no `pdf_id`
  - 149 PDFs are missing from S3
  - 52 PDFs are unreadable
  - 4 are blocked by a collision with an unreadable neighbour
- No PDF game is within an hour of a TDF-era game.
- St George legacy 6308 was a duplicate upload of 6311 (identical scorecards) and was deleted. A re-run of `migrate-legacy-pdf-games` without `--reset` would bring it back.

## Reviewer notes

- This is an operational script, and its writes are already live. Merging only adds the script and docs.
- The script needs poppler's `pdftotext` on PATH. A full fetch downloads about 50 GB, because the header can't be read from a partial download.

author: vbreuss
body:
Since #2037, `MatchesPublicApiSnapshot` has one overload per subject with optional options, where `null` means the defaults. `PublicApiDeclarations.GenerateFrom` still had two overloads per subject, one without options and one whose options threw an `ArgumentNullException` for `null`, so the expectation had to substitute a default lambda before calling it.

`GenerateFrom(Assembly, Func<PublicApiOptions, PublicApiOptions>? options = null)` and `GenerateFrom(FileInfo, Func<PublicApiOptions, PublicApiOptions>? options = null)` now replace both overloads, treat `null` as the default options, and the expectation passes its options straight through.

BREAKING CHANGE: `PublicApiDeclarations.GenerateFrom(Assembly)` and `GenerateFrom(FileInfo)` are removed in favor of the overloads with an optional `options` parameter, which now accept `null`. Existing calls compile unchanged, but assemblies compiled against the removed overloads must be recompiled.

author: uniac-dev
body:
This pull request is stacked on #2 (the store), which is stacked on #1 (the contract); it will be retargeted as those merge. It serves the agents' tool set over MCP, the Model Context Protocol, using the official MCP Python SDK.

## What it does

- **One tool per agent operation.** The tools come from the contract's operation list: every operation the contract marks for agents becomes a tool with the same name, its request model's JSON schema as the input schema and its response model's as the output schema. Read-only operations carry the read-only hint. Results come back both as structured content and as JSON text, and refusals come back as tool errors that start with the error code, such as `not_found: ...`.
- **Streamable HTTP at `/mcp`**, mounted in the same app as the API, so it sits behind the same bearer token and the same refusal of browser requests. The server runs in stateless mode: each request stands alone, so a client keeps working across a restart of the service.
- **The caller.** The `Agentorg-Client` and `Agentorg-Client-Session-Id` request headers name the client kind and its session id, as on the API. The stdio proxy sets them; an HTTP client may set them in its configuration.
- **`ask_wait` reports progress.** While the ask stays open, the tool sends a progress notification every 15 seconds, so a client that times out silent calls keeps waiting. It returns as soon as the ask is answered.
- **Instructions.** The server's instructions, the short contract an agent reads on connecting, are in `src/agentorg/mcp/instructions.md`, under the 4,096-character cap of the strictest known client.

## Tests

`tests/mcp/` runs a real server on a free port and connects with the SDK's client, both as a current client and as one using the older `initialize` handshake. The tests cover the tool list and read-only hints, the instructions, the client headers reaching `session_start`, refusals as tool errors, an `ask_wait` that reports progress and returns once the ask is answered through a test stand-in for the page's answer route (answering is a user operation, never on `/api`), and an `ask_wait` that times out with the ask still open.

body:
## Summary
Requested in chat: set up the read-only database role for `/ask` in production. There's no way to run SQL against production from the deploy pipeline, so the bot now creates the role itself, like the tables.

- At every start, `db.init()` checks whether `DATABASE_URL_RO` names a different account than `DATABASE_URL`. If it does, the bot creates that role, or resets its password to the one in the URL, then grants it `CONNECT` on the database, `USAGE` on `public`, and `SELECT` on `items` and `vendors` only.
- The read-only pool now opens *after* this, so its first connections don't fail.
- When both URLs use the same account (development), nothing changes.
- The role name and password can't be bound with `%s` in `CREATE`/`ALTER ROLE` statements, so they're quoted with `psycopg.sql.Identifier`/`Literal`. Nothing is interpolated by hand.
- Rotating the password is just changing the variable; the next start applies it.
- README and `docs/spec.md` updated: no SQL to run by hand, and a new `ASK_RO_PASSWORD` variable referenced by `DATABASE_URL_RO`.

## Test plan

author: cjgimena
body:
Prototype of an **agent mode** for Advantage Ask, off unless `ASK_AGENT=1`. Today the planner writes one plan without seeing a row. In agent mode its first attempt is a bounded tool loop, the way Claude works through the MCP connector, and nothing after the plan changes.

## How it works
- **Loop** (`src/lib/services/ask/agent.ts`): up to 6 tool calls (`finish` not counted) and 12 s. At the limit only `finish` is offered. Tool refusals (`sql_refused: …`, `query_failed: …`) go back to the model as results. A loop that never finishes answers from its last query with rows; with none, it plans the one-shot way.
- **Tools**: the connector's read tools (`list_matches`, `get_match`, `opponent_scouting`, `describe_views`, `run_query`), run by the **same handlers**. These are extracted to `askReadHandlers()` and wrapped by `createAskAgentToolbox()` in `mcp/server.ts`, bound to the scope the route already checked (the model passes no `program_id`). Every SQL string still goes through `checkAskSql()` and `ask_run_query` / `ask_run_team_query` on the question's `createAskDatabase()`. **No new service-role call.**
- **Finish = plan reply**: `finish` takes `ASK_PLAN_REPLY_SCHEMA` plus an optional `query_id`. `askQuestion()` parses it with the existing parser and runs everything after it unchanged: compare/review, soft checks and retries, cell references substituted by `answer-render.ts` (the model never types a number), one `AskVisual`, the save.
- **Adapter**: `getLLMToolTurn()`, one non-streamed multi-turn tool turn on Anthropic and Gemini (OpenAI-compat), with failover. Gemini's own `tool_calls` go back verbatim, thought signatures included.
- **Status**: `AskStatusEvent.detail`, a fixed server sentence per step ("Running query 2"), shown in place of the stage line.
- **Runs**: `ask_runs.route` = `agent` / `agent_server_written` (free text, no migration). Agent turns count in `model_calls` and `plan_attempts`, exploring queries in `query_count`.
- **Eval**: `scripts/ask-eval.ts --mode plan|agent|both`, with a `## Side by side` section. Agent runs are graded without the `modelCalls` / `queries` ceilings, which are the one-shot budget.

## Results (verifier, `scripts/ask-eval-season.json`, `--mode both`)
| Mode | Passed | Median s | Mean s | Max s | Mean queries | Mean model calls |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| plan | 20/21 | 1.7 | 2.1 | 6.8 | 1.0 | 1.4 |
| agent | 20/21 | 2.4 | 2.7 | 6.7 | 1.8 | 2.5 |

Both modes fail the same question (#7: a tree visual where a table was expected). On "What is my best serve placement, by attempts too?" the one-shot plan returned attempts only. Agent mode ran several queries in one turn and answered with points won and attempts per placement. It used all six tool calls, though: 13.5 s against 4.1 s.

Two Gemini traits found live and handled: `finish` fills every field, so a stray `compare` sat beside a written `sql` or a `query_id`. Both are now read as shape A. The eval also records the reply the pipeline parsed, not the raw arguments.

## Not done
- Agent mode is `/api/ask` only. `arrival.ts` and the connector's `ask` tool stay one-shot.
- The season list doesn't measure what agent mode is for. Compound and ambiguous questions should be added before turning the flag on. Next steps are in `docs/ask-improvement-roadmap.md` §1.11.

## Tests
- `tests/ask-agent.spec.ts` (13, offline): loop, budget, deadline, error feedback, `query_id` and stray-`compare` handling, `askQuestion` integration and run record, fallback to one-shot, toolbox guard and team binding, Gemini tool request.
- Full offline suite: 8,459 passed, 0 failed. `tsc` and eslint clean.

body:
## Description

**What was wrong.** The Zendesk test account's trial has expired, so the token request redirects to `/agent/expired-trial` and the "Mint Zendesk test token" step fails. That step runs before the shard's services start. In tonight's nightly the connectors-2 shard therefore stopped there on Neo4j, and GitLab, Jira, Linear, Azure Blob, Azure Files, SMB, Outlook and Gmail never ran.

**What it meant.** One expired account removed the nightly signal for eight other connectors, for as long as the account stays expired.

**The fix and why.** The mint step now has `continue-on-error: true`, so the shard goes on and starts its services. The Zendesk suite then finds no token file. On a run that requires connector secrets (the nightly, or a run that picked Zendesk), it fails with a message that points at the mint step's log and names the three Zendesk secrets. Anywhere else it skips, as for any missing credential (`source_unavailable`). Before, a missing token file raised `FileNotFoundError` from inside a fixture. The shard still ends red while Zendesk cannot be tested, so nothing is hidden.

**What changes going forward.** A Zendesk account problem shows up as failing Zendesk tests with a plain reason, and the other connectors in the shard keep running. The account itself still needs extending or replacing, with `ZENDESK_TEST_SUBDOMAIN`, `ZENDESK_TEST_CLIENT_ID` and `ZENDESK_TEST_CLIENT_SECRET` updated. This PR does not fix that.

### Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How Has This Been Tested?

- New `unit/test_zendesk_access_token.py` (3 tests): a minted token is read from its file; a failed mint fails the suite on a required run with the mint-step message; outside a required run it skips. The last two fail against main's `conftest.py` with `FileNotFoundError`.
- `unit/test_zendesk_prepare_token.py` still passes (9 in total with the new file). Ruff check and format are clean, and the workflow YAML parses.

author: masch
body:
## What

Follow-up to #561, which merged approved with two informational findings. Both were right:

- **`R2-001`** — the exception for the one surviving Leaflet map switched *every* import restriction off for that file, so a raw React Native `Modal` (or `TwButton`) there would have passed unnoticed. The restricted imports are now one definition, and the exception re-declares them **without** Leaflet: it relaxes the deprecation and keeps the rest.
- **`R2-002`** — the source test only matched a single-quoted static import. It now matches double quotes, `require(...)`, a dynamic `import(...)`, subpaths such as `leaflet/dist/leaflet-src`, and the CDN script a WebView loads. The lint rule uses `patterns` so subpaths are refused as well, and its comment states the limit it cannot cross.

## Why

A guard that silently stops covering three of the four ways to reach the package is worse than no guard: it reads as protection that is not there. The frozen map must keep working exactly as it does while every other import rule stays armed inside it.

## Something the review surfaced and this fixes

`no-restricted-imports` in ESLint 10 sees **static import declarations only** — measured with three probe files:

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| `import 'leaflet/dist/leaflet-src'` | ❌ error (restricted pattern) |
| `const a = require('leaflet')` | ⚠️ only `@typescript-eslint/no-require-imports` |
| `() => import('leaflet')` | nothing |

So the lint rule is the first line for the normal case, and the source test is the exhaustive guard. That division is now written where the rule lives instead of being assumed.

## Test plan

- `bun run jest --passWithNoTests --watchAll=false` → 996 tests, 112 suites, all passing.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` → clean.
- `bun --filter @sonora/mobile lint` → 0 errors, 5 warnings (the pre-existing baseline).
- `make doctor-ci` → exit 0.
- RED observed for both, before accepting:
  - `require("leaflet/dist/leaflet-src")` in a throwaway module → the source test failed with one unexpected consumer.
  - `import { Modal } from 'react-native'` added to the frozen map → lint reported `'Modal' import from 'react-native' is restricted`, which the previous exception had silenced.

## Risk

Risk: none. Lint configuration and a test only; the deprecated map keeps its exact behaviour and is still the only file allowed to reach Leaflet.
