author: silasvale
body:
The panel used to end an enrollment with "restart the SummriseLaunch service, then reload this panel", because the app builds its console link at boot. On a supervised install that step is now automatic.

| Aspect | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Supervised | The launcher starts the app with `--release-sha` (its argv carries a verified digest); after a successful `/api/enroll` writes `console.json`/`console-token.json`, the app answers `{id, restarting: true}` and exits after two seconds so the answer reaches the page first. The launcher's restart policy brings it back with the new link. |
| Standalone | No supervisor to return: the app answers `{id, restarting: false}` and keeps running; the page keeps the manual "Restart the SummriseLaunch service" sentence. |
| Hook | `router_with` takes a `RestartHook`; production passes the exit hook, tests pass a recorder. The supervised test proves the hook is asked exactly once and only after the link is on disk; the standalone test asserts `restarting: false`. |
| Page/docs | The panel's success sentence branches on `restarting`; QUICKSTART distinguishes the panel path (automatic) from the command-line path (restart it yourself). |

VERIFIED: device **466 tests** (+1) and 4 integration; `cargo xwin check -p summrise-device --tests` clean; clippy `-D warnings` 0; fmt 0; the console is untouched.

Deliberate: the restart is a clean exit, not an in-process console-link reload — that would need the console task to be reconfigurable while the app keeps serving, and the launcher already supervises an exit (three consecutive restarts, a stable child resets the budget). The two-second delay is the answer's window, not a health check.

author: alongubkin
body:
When a gated Storage is declined, its ComputeCluster node grant survives removal of the resource. Setup preparation then fails because node permissions must name an existing concrete resource.

Extend the shared **pre-mutation** declined-resource cleanup to inline node permission profiles. Frozen declines, Frozen-tied Live declines and off-platform gates remove the target's node grants alongside existing workload/management grants, links and ordering edges. Enabled and unrelated grants remain intact. Empty node profiles retain their platform selector; unrelated invalid references remain available for normal validation.

Mutable Live gates are stripped **after mutations**. That strip retains setup-owned node grants, just as it retains derived ServiceAccount grants, so the saved Frozen config matches the accepted render used by the next update's compatibility checks. Both deployment and the setup-authorization digest projection use the same post-mutation helper. The legacy release fallback follows the same distinction when no prepared stack was saved.

Rebased onto main at `b72c19f97` after #1267 merged. Only the two ALIEN-1976 commits remain; the binary diff against main exactly matches the previously reviewed `1dd72bb7f..ef92a5b01` diff. No generator, API schema or permission-set definitions change.

The Live-gate regression runs update preflights twice with the gate false, then re-enables it, starting from both initially accepted and initially declined storage and with/without a saved prepared stack. Each successful update's pending prepared stack becomes the next comparison baseline. A separate test verifies a Frozen archive addition still needs setup, and a matching re-import authorization succeeds with the same retained node-grant projection. These tests run the real preparation/update preflights; they do not execute cloud controllers.

Final local validation passes: 700 core tests; 10 node-filtered deployment/preflight tests; all 38 ComputeCluster mutation tests; 33 pending-deployment tests; 13 legacy tests; and all 14 Live-node/setup-rerun integration tests. Clippy for the three touched libraries plus the new integration target, targeted rustfmt, and `git diff --check` pass with the repository's existing warning categories.

```sh
cargo test -p alien-core --lib
cargo test -p alien-deployment -p alien-preflights --lib node_
cargo test -p alien-deployment -p alien-preflights --lib mutations::compute_cluster
cargo test -p alien-deployment --lib pending::tests
cargo test -p alien-deployment -p alien-preflights --lib legacy_
cargo test -p alien-deployment --test gated_live_node_permissions --test gated_live_sandbox_setup_rerun_gates
cargo clippy -p alien-core -p alien-deployment -p alien-preflights --lib --test gated_live_node_permissions
```

With only `gated_live_node_permissions.rs` copied onto original head **7eb177e79**, `cargo test -p alien-deployment --test gated_live_node_permissions` exits **101 with all three assertions failing** (no compile failures). Both repeated-update tests reproduce `DEPLOYMENT_SETUP_REQUIRED: Frozen resource 'compute' was modified`; the projection test sees an empty node profile when declined and the retained grant when accepted. All three pass with the fix, including the legacy fallback variants. No cloud controllers run in this proof.

Additional pre-mutation and artifact proof:

- ComputeCluster mutation: 38 tests passed, including a regression covering explicit decline, off-platform removal, and accepted storage; it checks node/workload grants, links, dependencies and the named-permission check.
- Pending-deployment tests: 33 passed; the new regression exercises the real frozen-decline entry point for both recorded answers.
- Enabled AWS storage generator regressions also pass: CloudFormation preserves the bucket and conditional IAM policies; Terraform preserves all conditional storage blocks and passes real validation.
- Clippy for all three touched libraries, targeted rustfmt, and `git diff --check` passed (existing warnings).
- With only new tests copied onto parent `93742a960`, all three regressions fail as assertions (exit 101). The pending regression retains the declined node grant; the core regression retains the declined grant alongside an unrelated invalid target.

Artifact proof uses the built-in AWS storage and service-account generators after shared decline cleanup. Temporary probes run `cfn-lint`, `terraform fmt -check`, `terraform init -backend=false`, and `terraform validate`; the role remains, while the declined bucket and its IAM statements are absent. These probes verify existing companion behavior, so they are retained as proof rather than redundant regression tests. ComputeCluster needs a setup emitter extension in this repository; this artifact proof does not claim to provision a node role. Real AWS end-to-end validation will run separately on staging.

Before/after commands (the parent worktree contains the new tests only):

```sh
cargo test -p alien-core --lib declining_a_node_target
cargo test -p alien-preflights --lib declined_node_targets
cargo test -p alien-deployment --lib frozen_decline_removes_node_grants
```

The parent preflight fails with `STACK_MUTATION_FAILED`: `ComputeCluster 'compute' node permissions must name an existing concrete resource, got 'objects'.` The fixed version passes the mutation and named-permission validation, with neither the declined resource nor its grant/link/dependency present. Gate-on preserves them.

Artifact commands (append the temporary probes below first):

```sh
mkdir -p proof
GATE_PROOF_DIR="$PWD/proof" cargo test -p alien-cloudformation -p alien-terraform \
```

body:
**Tiles keep showing numbers they already have while another range loads.**

Before: any activity fetch (picking a tile, the 5-minute poll, Refresh) blanked every tile. The Today tile shimmered while the PR list beside it already showed the 29 merged PRs it counts.

## What changed

- Every `/api/daily` answer is added to what the page holds (`Loads.hold` in `public/loads.js`), instead of replacing it.
- A tile shows numbers when its days are held, and shimmers only when they are not.
- Picking a tile selects it at once.
- The Custom tile fetches its own range if it reaches past what the picked tile loaded. Before, a "Past year" Custom tile quietly counted only the last 30 days.
- Closed and Merged list counts show loading, not 0, before their days arrive.
- An older answer that lands late cannot overwrite a newer one's days.

## Checks

- `node --test "test/*.test.js"`: 144 pass, 0 fail (2 new regression tests in `test/loads.test.js`).
- Browser, demo mode with `/api/daily` slowed by 4s: after clicking Today, its numbers stayed visible the whole time.
- Browser, Custom = Past year: the 7-day tile filled first, then Custom filled on its own.

Everyone with an active enrollment in a cycle follows every pod in it and every project in those pods: on joining, and whenever a new pod or project is created. An unfollow sticks (each automatic follow is recorded once in `auto_follows`).

- Regional migration `90002`: one new table, three AFTER triggers (on `cycle_enrollments`, `pods`, `projects`), no column or RLS changes. Already applied to the region's database; backfilled: 23 members now follow the 3 C04 pods.
- Verified in a rolled-back transaction: a new pod and a new project each get 23 followers; a member who unfollowed a pod is not re-added after leaving and rejoining the cycle.
- Follows only fill the in-app feed. No messages are sent.
